summary: Notified bodies inform the notifying authority of issued, refused, suspended or withdrawn certificates and approvals, changes affecting notification, requests from market surveillance authorities, and conformity assessment activities; they also inform other notified bodies (Art. 45(2) and (3)).
quote: Notified bodies shall inform the notifying authority of the following

summary: A market surveillance authority that authorises a high-risk system under the derogation informs the Commission and other Member States of each authorisation.
quote: The market surveillance authority shall inform the Commission and the other Member States of any authorisation issued
conditional_on: Authorisation issued under Art. 46(1)

summary: Providers keep the EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk system at the disposal of national competent authorities for 10 years, and submit a copy on request.
quote: keep it at the disposal of the national competent authorities for 10 years
conditional_on: Each high-risk AI system

summary: The EU declaration of conformity states that the system meets Section 2 requirements, contains the Annex V information, is translated into a language understood by authorities, and the provider takes responsibility for compliance.
quote: The EU declaration of conformity shall state that the high-risk AI system concerned meets the requirements set out in Section 2.
conditional_on: Each high-risk AI system

summary: The CE marking is affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly on high-risk systems (digital CE marking for digitally provided systems), followed by the notified body identification number where applicable.
quote: The CE marking shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly for high-risk AI systems.
conditional_on: High-risk AI systems

summary: Before placing on the market or putting into service an Annex III high-risk system (other than point 2), providers or authorised representatives register themselves and the system in the EU database.
quote: shall register themselves and their system in the EU database referred to in Article 71
conditional_on: High-risk AI systems listed in Annex III, excluding point 2

summary: Before placing on the market or putting into service an AI system concluded not to be high-risk under Art. 6(3), providers register themselves and that system in the EU database.
quote: shall register themselves and that system in the EU database referred to in Article 71
conditional_on: AI system the provider has concluded is not high-risk under Art. 6(3)

summary: Deployers that are public authorities or EU bodies register themselves, select the system and register its use in the EU database before putting into service or using it.
quote: deployers that are public authorities, Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies or persons acting on their behalf shall register themselves
conditional_on: Annex III high-risk systems, excluding point 2

summary: Providers ensure AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed so that those persons are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless obvious.
quote: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons
conditional_on: AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons; exception for systems authorised by law for criminal offences

summary: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text ensure outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated.
quote: shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated
conditional_on: AI systems generating synthetic content; exceptions for standard editing and law enforcement

summary: Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems inform the exposed natural persons of the system's operation.
quote: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto
conditional_on: Emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems

summary: Deployers of AI systems generating or manipulating deep fakes disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated, with limits for artistic or fictional works.
quote: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose
conditional_on: Deep fake content, subject to exceptions in Art. 50(4)

summary: Deployers of AI systems generating or manipulating text published to inform the public on matters of public interest disclose that the text is artificially generated, unless human review with editorial responsibility applies.
quote: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest shall disclose
conditional_on: Text published to inform the public on matters of public interest

summary: The AI Office encourages and facilitates codes of practice at Union level on detecting and labelling artificially generated or manipulated content; the Commission may approve them or adopt common rules.
quote: The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level

summary: The Commission adopts delegated acts amending the thresholds in Art. 51(1) and (2) and supplementing benchmarks and indicators.
quote: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 to amend the thresholds listed in paragraphs 1 and 2

summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models meeting the high-impact capability condition notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks, with supporting information.
quote: the relevant provider shall notify the Commission without delay and in any event within two weeks
conditional_on: General-purpose AI model meets the condition in Art. 51(1)(a)

summary: The Commission ensures a list of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk is published and kept up to date.
quote: The Commission shall ensure that a list of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk is published

summary: Providers draw up and keep up to date technical documentation of the model, including training, testing and evaluation results (Annex XI), for provision on request to the AI Office and national authorities.
quote: draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model

summary: Providers make information and documentation available to downstream AI system providers (Annex XII), and publish a sufficiently detailed summary of training content using the AI Office template.
quote: draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training

summary: Providers put in place a policy to comply with Union copyright law, including identifying and complying with reservations of rights under Directive (EU) 2019/790 Art. 4(3).
quote: put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights

summary: Providers cooperate as necessary with the Commission and national competent authorities in exercising their powers.
quote: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall cooperate as necessary with the Commission and the national competent authorities

summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models established in third countries appoint, by written mandate, an authorised representative established in the Union before placing the model on the Union market.
quote: providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union
conditional_on: Providers of general-purpose AI models established in third countries

summary: The authorised representative keeps a copy of the Annex XI technical documentation and the provider's contact details at the disposal of the AI Office and national authorities for 10 years after placing on the market.
quote: keep a copy of the technical documentation specified in Annex XI at the disposal of the AI Office and national competent authorities
conditional_on: Authorised representative of a third-country provider of a general-purpose AI model

summary: An authorised representative that terminates its mandate for provider non-compliance immediately informs the AI Office.
quote: it shall also immediately inform the AI Office about the termination of the mandate
conditional_on: Authorised representative considers provider to be acting contrary to obligations

summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk perform model evaluation under standardised protocols, including adversarial testing, to identify and mitigate systemic risks.
quote: perform model evaluation in accordance with standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art
conditional_on: General-purpose AI models with systemic risk

summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level, including their sources.
quote: assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level
conditional_on: General-purpose AI models with systemic risk

summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk keep track of, document and report serious incidents and possible corrective measures to the AI Office and, as appropriate, national authorities, without undue delay.
quote: keep track of, document, and report, without undue delay, to the AI Office
conditional_on: General-purpose AI models with systemic risk

summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk ensure adequate cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure.
quote: ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the general-purpose AI model with systemic risk
conditional_on: General-purpose AI models with systemic risk

summary: The AI Office encourages and facilitates the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level to contribute to the proper application of the Regulation, covering Art. 53 and 55 obligations.
quote: The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level

summary: The AI Office shall aim to ensure that participants in the codes of practice report regularly on implementation of commitments and measures, including against key performance indicators.
quote: participants to the codes of practice report regularly to the AI Office on the implementation of the commitments
conditional_on: Participants in codes of practice

summary: The Commission may, by implementing act, approve a code of practice and give it general validity within the Union.
quote: The Commission may, by way of an implementing act, approve a code of practice and give it a general validity within the Union.

summary: Member States must ensure competent authorities set up at least one national AI regulatory sandbox, operational by 2 August 2026; authorities must allocate sufficient resources and provide sandbox guidance and written proof or exit reports (Art. 57(7)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level, which shall be operational by 2 August 2026.

summary: National competent authorities must inform the AI Office and the Board of the establishment of a sandbox (Art. 57(15)).
applies_from: from one year after the establishment of the AI regulatory sandbox
quote: National competent authorities shall submit annual reports to the AI Office and to the Board, from one year after the establishment of the AI regulatory sandbox

summary: The Commission must adopt implementing acts on detailed sandbox arrangements; authorities must inform applicants of decisions within three months, keep access free of charge for SMEs, and specifically agree terms of real-world testing within sandboxes (Art. 58(4)).
quote: the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying the detailed arrangements for the establishment

summary: Personal data processed in a sandbox must be kept in a functionally separate, isolated and protected environment under the provider's control, with access limited to authorised persons; other conditions include deletion and monitoring of risks (Art. 59(1)(c)-(h)).
quote: any personal data to be processed in the context of the sandbox are in a functionally separate, isolated and protected data processing environment under the control of the prospective provider
conditional_on: processing of personal data for developing certain AI systems in the public interest in a sandbox

summary: A complete and detailed description of training, testing and validation is kept with the testing results in the technical documentation, and logs of personal data processing are kept for the sandbox participation (Art. 59(1)(h)-(i)).
quote: a complete and detailed description of the process and rationale behind the training, testing and validation of the AI system is kept
conditional_on: processing of personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox

summary: A short summary of the sandbox AI project, its objectives and expected results is published on the website of the competent authorities; excludes sensitive operational data of law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum authorities.
quote: a short summary of the AI project developed in the sandbox, its objectives and expected results is published on the website of the competent authorities
conditional_on: processing of personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox

summary: Before real-world testing of high-risk AI systems outside sandboxes, the provider must draw up a real-world testing plan and submit it to the market surveillance authority (Art. 60(4)(a)).
quote: has drawn up a real-world testing plan and submitted it to the market surveillance authority
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: The provider must register real-world testing with a Union-wide unique single identification number and the information in Annex IX (Art. 60(4)(c)).
quote: has registered the testing in real world conditions in accordance with Article 71(4) with a Union-wide unique single identification number
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: The provider conducting real-world testing must be established in the Union or have appointed a legal representative established in the Union (Art. 60(4)(d)).
quote: has appointed a legal representative who is established in the Union
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: Real-world testing must not last longer than necessary and not longer than six months, extendable once by six months on prior notification (Art. 60(4)(f)).
quote: the testing in real world conditions does not last longer than necessary to achieve its objectives and in any case not longer than six months
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: Subjects of real-world testing must have given informed consent under Article 61; vulnerable subjects must be appropriately protected (Art. 60(4)(g)).
quote: the subjects of the testing in real world conditions have given informed consent in accordance with Article 61
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: Real-world testing must be effectively overseen by the provider and by deployers through suitably qualified persons, and the AI system's predictions or decisions must be effectively reversible and disregardable (Art. 60(4)(j)-(k)).
quote: the testing in real world conditions is effectively overseen by the provider or prospective provider
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: Subjects of real-world testing may withdraw at any time without detriment and request deletion of their personal data (Art. 60(5)).
quote: may, without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification, withdraw from the testing at any time
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: Serious incidents identified during real-world testing must be reported to the national market surveillance authority; the provider must mitigate, suspend or terminate testing and establish a recall procedure (Art. 60(7)).
quote: Any serious incident identified in the course of the testing in real world conditions shall be reported to the national market surveillance authority
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: Providers must notify the national market surveillance authority of the suspension or termination of real-world testing and of final outcomes (Art. 60(8)).
quote: Providers or prospective providers shall notify the national market surveillance authority
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: Freely-given informed consent must be obtained from test subjects before participation, covering nature, conditions, rights, reversal arrangements and the Union-wide identification number (Art. 61(1)).
quote: freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

summary: The informed consent must be dated and documented, and a copy given to the test subjects or their legal representative (Art. 61(2)).
quote: The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative.
conditional_on: testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes

quote: Member States shall undertake the following actions:

summary: The AI Office must provide standardised templates, maintain a single information platform, run awareness campaigns and promote best practices in public procurement (Art. 62(3)).
quote: The AI Office shall undertake the following actions:

summary: Microenterprises without partner or linked enterprises may comply with certain quality management system elements in a simplified manner; this does not exempt them from other requirements (Art. 63(1)-(2)).

conditional_on: microenterprises without partner or linked enterprises

summary: The Commission must develop guidelines on simplified quality management system elements for microenterprises (Art. 63(1)).
quote: the Commission shall develop guidelines on the elements of the quality management system which may be complied with in a simplified manner

summary: The Commission develops Union AI expertise and capabilities through the AI Office, and Member States facilitate the AI Office's tasks (Art. 64(1)-(2)).

summary: Member States must ensure their Board representatives have relevant competences, act as single contact points and coordinate national authorities; representatives adopt rules of procedure by two-thirds majority (Art. 65(4)-(5)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that their representatives on the Board:

summary: The Commission appoints advisory forum members on balanced stakeholder criteria; the forum must prepare an annual report that is made publicly available (Art. 67(3), 67(10)).

summary: The Commission shall facilitate timely access by Member States to scientific panel experts and coordinate support with Union AI testing support (Art. 69(3)).
quote: The Commission shall facilitate timely access to the experts by the Member States

summary: Member States must establish or designate at least one notifying authority and one market surveillance authority, communicate them to the Commission, designate a single point of contact, and resource them adequately (Art. 70(1)-(3)).
quote: Each Member State shall establish or designate as national competent authorities at least one notifying authority and at least one market surveillance authority

summary: National competent authorities must take appropriate measures to ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity.
quote: National competent authorities shall take appropriate measures to ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity.

summary: Member States must report to the Commission on the status of financial and human resources of national competent authorities every two years, with an adequacy assessment (Art. 70(6)).
applies_from: by 2 August 2025 and once every two years thereafter
quote: Member States shall report to the Commission on the status of the financial and human resources

summary: The Commission, with Member States, sets up and maintains an EU database of high-risk AI systems and consults experts on its functional specifications (Art. 71(1), 71(6)).
quote: The Commission shall, in collaboration with the Member States, set up and maintain an EU database

summary: Providers (and authorised representatives) must enter the Annex VIII Sections A and B data into the EU database and keep it up to date.
quote: The data listed in Sections A and B of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the provider

quote: The data listed in Section C of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the deployer who is, or who acts on behalf of, a public authority
conditional_on: deployer who is, or acts on behalf of, a public authority, agency or body

summary: Information in the EU database registered under Article 49 must be accessible and publicly available in a user-friendly, machine-readable manner, excluding the section referred to in Article 49(4).

summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems must establish and document a proportionate post-market monitoring system that collects and analyses performance data throughout the system's lifetime, based on a post-market monitoring plan (Art. 72(1)-(2)).

conditional_on: high-risk AI systems

quote: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred.
conditional_on: high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market

summary: After reporting a serious incident, the provider must without delay perform investigations including a risk assessment and corrective action, cooperate with authorities, and not alter the system in a way that affects evaluation of causes.
quote: the provider shall, without delay, perform the necessary investigations in relation to the serious incident and the AI system concerned
conditional_on: high-risk AI systems; serious incident reported

summary: The Commission must develop dedicated guidance on serious incident reporting by 2 August 2025; the market surveillance authority must take appropriate measures within seven days of notification (Art. 73(7)-(8)).
quote: The Commission shall develop dedicated guidance to facilitate compliance with the obligations set out in paragraph 1 of this Article.

summary: National competent authorities must immediately notify the Commission of any serious incident, whether or not they have taken action.
quote: National competent authorities shall immediately notify the Commission of any serious incident

summary: Member States must designate market surveillance authorities for the purposes of the Regulation, including data protection supervisory authorities for certain high-risk systems, and facilitate coordination among authorities; market surveillance authorities may propose joint activities.
quote: Member States shall designate as market surveillance authorities for the purposes of this Regulation

summary: Market surveillance authorities must report annually to the Commission and national competition authorities on information of interest for competition law and on prohibited practices used.
quote: the market surveillance authorities shall report annually to the Commission and relevant national competition authorities

summary: Providers must grant market surveillance authorities full access to documentation and training, validation and testing data sets, and, on reasoned request, to source code under the conditions in Article 74(13).
quote: the market surveillance authorities shall be granted full access by providers to the documentation
conditional_on: high-risk AI systems; access only where necessary to fulfil tasks

summary: The AI Office has powers to monitor and supervise compliance of AI systems based on general-purpose AI models from the same provider, and must supply information to authorities within 30 days upon reasoned request (Art. 75(3)).
quote: the AI Office shall have powers to monitor and supervise compliance of that AI system with obligations under this Regulation
conditional_on: AI system based on a general-purpose AI model developed by the same provider

summary: Market surveillance authorities must verify compliance of real-world testing under Article 60 within AI regulatory sandboxes and may allow testing in derogation of Article 60(4)(f) and (g).
quote: the market surveillance authorities shall verify the compliance with Article 60
conditional_on: testing in real world conditions for AI systems supervised within a sandbox

summary: By 2 November 2024 each Member State must identify the public authorities protecting fundamental rights, publish their list and notify the Commission and other Member States; market surveillance authorities must organise requested testing.
quote: By 2 November 2024, each Member State shall identify the public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 and make a list of them publicly available.

summary: Authorities and bodies involved in applying the Regulation must put in place adequate cybersecurity measures, request only strictly necessary data, and delete collected data when no longer needed; confidentiality obligations apply under Article 78(1).
quote: They shall put in place adequate and effective cybersecurity measures to protect the security and confidentiality of the information and data obtained

summary: Relevant operators must cooperate as necessary with the market surveillance authority evaluating an AI system presenting a risk, and with national public authorities under Article 77(1).
quote: The relevant operators shall cooperate as necessary with the market surveillance authority
conditional_on: market surveillance authority evaluates an AI system presenting a risk

summary: The operator must ensure that all appropriate corrective action is taken for all AI systems concerned that it has made available on the Union market (Art. 79(4)).

conditional_on: AI system presenting a risk under Article 79

summary: The market surveillance authority must inform the Commission and other Member States without undue delay where non-compliance is not restricted to its territory.
quote: it shall inform the Commission and the other Member States without undue delay of the results of the evaluation
conditional_on: non-compliance not restricted to national territory

summary: A provider of a non-high-risk-classified system found to be high-risk must ensure all necessary action is taken to bring the system into compliance, and corrective action for all affected systems.
quote: The provider shall ensure that all necessary action is taken to bring the AI system into compliance with the requirements and obligations laid down in this Regulation.
conditional_on: AI system classified by the provider as non-high-risk under Article 6(3) found to be high-risk

summary: The Commission must enter into consultation with the market surveillance authority and operators and evaluate the national measure within six months (60 days for prohibited practices).
quote: the Commission shall without undue delay enter into consultation with the market surveillance authority of the relevant Member State
conditional_on: objections raised to a national measure

summary: The provider or other relevant operator must ensure corrective action for all AI systems concerned within the timeline prescribed by the market surveillance authority.
quote: The provider or other relevant operator shall ensure that corrective action is taken in respect of all the AI systems concerned
conditional_on: high-risk AI system compliant with the Regulation but presenting a risk

summary: Member States must immediately inform the Commission and other Member States of a finding that a compliant high-risk AI system presents a risk.
quote: The Member States shall immediately inform the Commission and the other Member States of a finding under paragraph 1.
conditional_on: finding under Article 82(1)

summary: The Commission designates one or more Union AI testing support structures to perform tasks under Article 21(6) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
quote: The Commission shall designate one or more Union AI testing support structures

summary: Deployers must provide affected persons subject to decisions based on Annex III high-risk AI outputs with clear and meaningful explanations of the AI system's role and the main elements of the decision, subject to exceptions in law.

conditional_on: decision producing legal effects or similarly significantly affecting a person, Annex III high-risk system other than point 2

summary: The Commission has exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V obligations of general-purpose AI model providers, entrusted to the AI Office.

summary: The AI Office may take necessary monitoring actions, including checking adherence to approved codes of practice, for general-purpose AI model providers.
quote: the AI Office may take the necessary actions to monitor the effective implementation and compliance with this Regulation by providers of general-purpose AI models

summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models must supply information requested by the Commission under Article 91, through their representative or authorised persons.
quote: The provider of the general-purpose AI model concerned, or its representative shall supply the information requested.
conditional_on: Commission request for documentation or information

summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models must supply information or access requested for Commission evaluations, including API or source code access under Article 92(3).
quote: The providers of the general-purpose AI model concerned or its representative shall supply the information requested.
conditional_on: Commission evaluation of a general-purpose AI model

summary: When requested by the Commission, general-purpose AI model providers must take measures to comply with Articles 53 and 54, implement mitigation measures, or restrict, withdraw or recall the model.
quote: take appropriate measures to comply with the obligations set out in Articles 53 and 54
conditional_on: Commission request under Article 93(1)

summary: The AI Office and Member States encourage and facilitate codes of conduct for voluntary application of requirements to non-high-risk AI systems, including taking account of SME interests.

summary: The Commission develops guidelines on practical implementation, including Articles 8 to 15, 25, prohibited practices, substantial modification, Article 50 transparency and the AI system definition.

summary: Power to adopt delegated acts under listed articles is conferred on the Commission for five years from 1 August 2024, tacitly extended unless opposed; the Commission must consult Member State experts before adopting delegated acts.

summary: When adopting acts on AI safety components under Regulation (EC) No 300/2008, the Commission must take into account the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2.

summary: When adopting delegated acts on AI safety components under Regulation (EU) No 167/2013, the Commission must take into account Chapter III, Section 2 requirements.

summary: When adopting delegated acts on AI safety components under Regulation (EU) No 168/2013, the Commission must take into account Chapter III, Section 2 requirements.

summary: When adopting delegated and implementing acts on AI safety components under Directive (EU) 2016/797, the Commission must take into account Chapter III, Section 2.

summary: When adopting delegated acts on AI safety components under Regulation (EU) 2018/858, the Commission must take into account Chapter III, Section 2.
quote: the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account.
conditional_on: AI systems that are safety components

summary: Amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 require that, when adopting implementing or delegated acts on AI safety components, the Commission take into account Chapter III, Section 2.

conditional_on: AI systems that are safety components

summary: When adopting implementing acts on AI safety components under Regulation (EU) 2019/2144, the Commission must take into account Chapter III, Section 2.

conditional_on: implementing acts concerning AI safety components

summary: AI systems that are components of large-scale IT systems listed in Annex X and placed on the market before 2 August 2027 must be brought into compliance by 31 December 2030.

quote: The technical documentation referred to in Article 11(1) shall contain at least the following information, as applicable to the relevant AI system:
conditional_on: high-risk AI systems

summary: The EU declaration of conformity must contain the listed information, including system identification, provider details, conformity statement, data protection statement, standards, notified body details and signature.
quote: The EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47, shall contain all of the following information:

summary: Under internal control conformity assessment, the provider verifies the quality management system, examines technical documentation, and verifies design, development and post-market monitoring consistency.
quote: The provider verifies that the established quality management system is in compliance with the requirements of Article 17.
conditional_on: internal control conformity assessment procedure

summary: Under the quality management system and technical documentation assessment procedure, the notified body assesses the quality management system, examines technical documentation and carries out periodic audits.
quote: The quality management system shall be assessed by the notified body, which shall determine whether it satisfies the requirements referred to in Article 17.
conditional_on: conformity assessment procedure through a notified body

summary: Providers of Annex III high-risk AI systems must provide and keep up to date the Annex VIII Section A information for registration under Article 49(1), including provider details, purpose, status and certificates.
quote: The following information shall be provided and thereafter kept up to date with regard to high-risk AI systems to be registered in accordance with Article 49(1):
conditional_on: high-risk AI systems to be registered under Article 49(1)

summary: Deployers of high-risk AI systems must provide and keep up to date the Annex VIII Section C information for registration under Article 49(3), including a summary of the fundamental rights impact assessment.
quote: The following information shall be provided and thereafter kept up to date with regard to high-risk AI systems to be registered in accordance with Article 49(3):
conditional_on: high-risk AI systems to be registered under Article 49(3)

summary: Providers must provide and keep up to date the Annex IX information on real-world testing registered under Article 60, including the identification number, participants, plan summary and suspension or termination information.
quote: The following information shall be provided and thereafter kept up to date with regard to testing in real world conditions to be registered in accordance with Article 60:
conditional_on: testing in real world conditions of Annex III systems registered under Article 60

summary: Technical documentation for general-purpose AI models must contain at least the listed general description and development information, as appropriate to the model's size and risk profile; systemic-risk models have additional evaluation information.
quote: The technical documentation referred to in Article 53(1), point (a) shall contain at least the following information as appropriate to the size and risk profile of the model:
conditional_on: general-purpose AI models

summary: Transparency information for downstream providers integrating a general-purpose AI model must contain at least the listed general description, integration information and training data information.
quote: The information referred to in Article 53(1), point (b) shall contain at least the following:
conditional_on: general-purpose AI models integrated into downstream AI systems

summary: The Commission takes into account the listed criteria (parameters, data set size, computation, modalities, capabilities, business users of at least 10 000, end users) when designating general-purpose AI models with systemic risk.
quote: the Commission shall take into account the following criteria:
conditional_on: designation of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk under Article 51

summary: Each Member State must establish Experience and Acceleration Centres for AI, building on European digital innovation hubs, to support AI adoption, upskilling and scale-ups.
applies_from: date of application (entry into force + 1 year)
quote: Each Member State shall establish Experience and Acceleration Centres for AI (‘Centres for AI’).

summary: Member States must establish national cloud and AI strategies with at least the contents in Art. 7(2) (adoption, data centre capacity, AI factories, procurement, open stacks, data access).
quote: The national strategies shall include at least the following:

summary: Member States must notify their strategies to the Commission within three months of adoption and reassess them at least every three years against KPIs.
quote: The Member States shall notify the Commission of their national strategies within three months of their adoption.

summary: The Union and Member States must allocate sufficient AI computing resources to frontier AI priority projects within available capacity; the Union must at least match Member State contributions within its EuroHPC access-time share.
quote: T he Union shall at least match the AI computing resources contributed by Member States to frontier AI priority projects
conditional_on: Project recognised as frontier AI priority project under Art. 8

summary: Member States where data centre capacity is being deployed must designate at least one data centre acceleration zone, considering site size, grid and network capacity, waste-heat reuse, permitting, brownfield preference and sustainability.
quote: Where data centre capacity is being deployed with in the territory of a Member State, that Member State shall designate at least one data centre acceleration zone
conditional_on: Data centre capacity is being deployed within the Member State's territory

summary: Where appropriate, Member States must analyse energy needs and GHG impacts of acceleration zones (reviewed every three years) and ensure TSO and DSO network development plans take that analysis into account.
quote: ensure that the network development plans prepared by transmission system operators pursuant to Article 51 of Directive (EU) 2019/944
conditional_on: Where appropriate to facilitate the development of acceleration zones

summary: Member States must make spatial planning data available to data centre operators, combine SEA and habitats assessments of plans, and involve all relevant authorities, electronic communications operators, TSOs and DSOs when designating zones.
quote: Member States shall ensure that all relevant spatial planning data are available to data centre operators .

summary: When setting sustainability requirements for data centres in acceleration zones, Member States must use the KPIs of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364, and must allocate zone resources on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms without speculative reservation or foreclosure.
quote: Member States shall ensure that the allocation and use of resources within acceleration zones takes place on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms

summary: Member States must designate single information points that assist data centre operators in acceleration zones, on request, with all authorisations over the project lifecycle (operators have a right to this assistance).
quote: For that purpose, Member States shall designate one or more single information points for data centre operators of data centre projects in acceleration zones .

summary: For each acceleration zone, Member States must carry out zone-level assessments and issue an aggregated baseline permit covering the permits needed by data centre projects there, excluding installation-specific permits.
quote: For each designated acceleration zone, Member States shall prepare and issue an aggregated baseline permit authorising the deployment of data centres in that acceleration zone .

summary: Member States must process applications efficiently and decide permits for data centre projects in acceleration zones within 12 months of a comprehensive application, and give them the highest national significance status where national law has one.
quote: Member States shall ensure that administrative applications related to the planning, construction and the operation of data centre deployed in acceleration zones are processed in an efficient, transparent and timely manner.

summary: Data centres in acceleration zones need additional permits only for activities outside the zone's aggregated baseline permit; their projects count as strategic projects under the pending environmental-assessment regulation.
quote: Data centres deployed in acceleration zones shall be required to obtain additional permits only for activities falling outside the aggregated baseline permit referred to in paragraph 2.
conditional_on: Data centre deployed in a designated acceleration zone

summary: Applicants for data centre strategic project designation must supply information showing the criteria are met and substantiating the project's predicted lifetime, which sets the designation's duration.
quote: In its proposal, the applicant shall provide all the necessary and relevant information to demonstrate that the project fulfils the relevant criteria.
conditional_on: Applying in a Commission open call for strategic projects

summary: The Commission must identify and monitor Union compute capacity, demand for data centre capacity and the capacity gap and underserved areas.
quote: t he Commission shall identify and monitor:

summary: The Commission must review Annexes II (assurance criteria) and III (audit evidence) at least every 18 months.
quote: T o ensure Annex II and Annex III rem ain up to date with new legal or technical developments , the Commission shall review them at least every 18 months .

summary: A cloud computing service provider seeking recognition at a Union assurance level must apply to the competent authority of establishment with the required evidence (statement of conformity for level 1; audit report, positive opinion and audit evidence for levels 2-4).
applies_from: date of application (entry into force + 1 year)
quote: A c loud computing service provider that aims to be recognised as offering a Union assurance level , shall submit a n application for recognition to the national competent authority of establishment .
conditional_on: Provider aims to be recognised as offering a Union assurance level (required to supply Union entities and public sector bodies, Arts 16(1), 30)

summary: The evaluating national competent authority must assess applications within 60 days and either notify a draft recognition decision for a 60-day Union review, request more information, or reject after hearing the provider; it must consider objections from other authorities.
quote: t he evaluating national competent authority shall assess the evidence submitted pursuant to paragraphs 3 or 4 and shall either :

summary: On referral of a disputed draft recognition, the Commission must assess it and adopt a binding decision on whether the recognition may be adopted.
quote: T he Commission shall adopt a binding decision determining whether the evaluati ng national competent authority may adopt the recognition decision .
conditional_on: A national competent authority refers a maintained draft decision under Art. 17(10)

summary: Providers seeking level 1 recognition must self-assess against the level 1 criteria and issue an EU statement of conformity, assuming responsibility for compliance.
quote: shall carry out a c onformity self-assessment of compliance with the criteria for Union assurance level 1 set out in Annex II .
conditional_on: Seeking Union assurance level 1

summary: Providers must make their EU statement of conformity publicly available.
quote: The cloud computing service provider shall make the EU statement of conformity publicly available.
conditional_on: Provider has issued an EU statement of conformity (level 1)

summary: Providers seeking levels 2, 3 or 4 must undergo, at their own expense, independent third-party audits by auditing organisations meeting the independence, expertise and ethics conditions of Art. 20(4), meeting all lower-level criteria too.
quote: shall undergo at their own expense, independent third-party au dit s to obtain an audit report and an audit opinion from an auditing organisation .
conditional_on: Seeking Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

summary: Audited providers must cooperate with auditors, give access to data and premises, answer questions, and not hamper or unduly influence the audit.
quote: Audited providers shall refrain from hampering, unduly influencing or undermining the performance of the audit.
conditional_on: Undergoing a level 2-4 audit

summary: Recognised level 2-4 providers must submit the audit report and positive opinion annually for review of continued compliance; the auditor may confirm, update or revoke them.
quote: which shall assess the continued compliance of the audited service with the applicable criteria set out in Annex II.
conditional_on: Holding a positive audit opinion for level 2, 3 or 4

summary: Recognised providers must notify the auditing organisation and the competent authority as soon as possible of any information or material change that may affect the audit opinion or recognition.
quote: the recognised cloud computing service provider shall , as soon as possible , notify the auditing organisation and the national competent authority of establishment.
conditional_on: Provider's service is recognised under Art. 17

summary: Level 1: provider established in the Union; infrastructure and assets (incl. subcontractors') located in the Union and customer data, metadata and telemetry kept exclusively in the Union, unless the public sector body explicitly requires otherwise; traceable out-of-Union support.
quote: the cloud computing service provider is established in the Union;
conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 1

summary: Level 1: state-of-the-art cybersecurity, full transparency and due diligence on subcontractors, and (if third-country controlled) a guarantee that no third-country law requires reporting unexploited vulnerabilities to its authorities.
quote: the cloud computing service provider demonstrates that the service complies with the state-of-the-art cybersecurity standards;
conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 1

summary: Levels 2-4: provider and involved subcontractors established in the Union; infrastructure, assets and personnel located in the Union; customer data exclusively in the Union (for level 4, data identified as sensitive, without the customer opt-out); technical and operational support performed exclusively within the Union (levels 3-4: by Union residents and non-third-country-controlled parties).
quote: the technical and operational support or assistance related to the audited service, including subsequent sub-outsourcing arrangements, are initiated and performed exclusively within the Union;
conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

summary: Levels 2-3 require a European cybersecurity certificate of at least assurance level 'substantial' (level 4: 'high') under a Cybersecurity Act cloud scheme once established; until then national schemes, or else the highest cybersecurity standards under Union law.
quote: the audited service obtains a European cybersecurity certificate of at least assurance level ‘high’ under a European cybersecurity certification scheme covering cloud computing services
conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

summary: Levels 2-4: data generated by using the service may not be used to train or fine-tune any AI system operated by a third country or third-country entity, nor transferred outside the Union.
quote: the data generated by using the audited service are not used to train or fine-tune any AI system operated by a third country or a legal entity established in a third-country
conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

summary: Level 2: a third-country-controlled provider must show legal, technical and organisational measures preventing third-country control from restricting the service, accessing customer data, disrupting or degrading service, or imposing third-country restrictive measures.
quote: access by a third country or by a legal entity established in a third-country to customer data is prevented;
conditional_on: Recognition at level 2 by a provider subject to third-country control

summary: Levels 3-4: provider and involved subcontractors must not be subject to third-country control; at level 3 a derogation applies for providers controlled from a third country named by Commission implementing act (Art. 18), with separation safeguards and reasonable access to code.
quote: the audited provider and the subcontractors which are involved in the provision of the audited service are not subject to the control of a third country or a legal entity established in a third-country;
conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 3 or 4

summary: Levels 3-4: personnel (including subcontractors') involved in the service must be Union citizens, with Member State security clearance where handling classified information; at level 2 citizenship and screening apply only if the public sector body requires them.
quote: the personnel, including the personnel of the subcontractors , which are involved in the provision of the audited service are Union citizens and, where appropriate, the personnel must also have the necessary national security clearance
conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 3 or 4 (level 2 on request of the public body)

summary: Levels 2-4: software supply-chain measures (SBOM and dependency list for the auditor; controls blocking remote tamper features; source-code audits and migration plans for third-country components; level 4: effective control over software components) and controls on open-source software.
quote: a complete and up-to-date software bill of materials ( SBOM ) , as defined in Article 3 , point (39) , of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, and a list of identified dependencies
conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

summary: Levels 2-4: providers operating globally with a third-country subsidiary must ensure effective legal, technical and organisational separation between the Union parent and the subsidiary.
quote: the audited provider has implemented the necessary measures to ensure and enforce the effective legal, technical and organisational separation between the Union parent company and any such third-country subsidiary
conditional_on: Recognition at level 2, 3 or 4 by a provider with a third-country subsidiary

summary: The Commission must establish and maintain a public central repository of recognised cloud computing services, where revocations stay published for five years.
quote: The Commission shall establish and maintain a dedicated repository of cloud computing services that have been recogni sed in accordance with A rticle 1 7

summary: The national competent authority that recognised a service must register it in the central repository and, after notifications, assess and notify any amendment or revocation of its recognition.
quote: The national competent authority of establishment that recognised a cloud computing service under Article 1 7 shall register the cloud computing service in the central repository.

summary: Member States must lay down effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties for infringements of the cloud sovereignty Chapter, weighing the Art. 24(2) criteria, and notify them to the Commission.
quote: Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Chapter by cloud computing service providers within their competence

summary: Member States must designate national competent authorities, notify them to the Commission, and give them sufficient resources; the Member State of main establishment has exclusive enforcement competence.
quote: shall have exclusive competence for enforc ing this Chapter .

summary: Competent authorities must give mutual assistance and answer information requests within two months, and the authority of establishment must assess requests from authorities of destination or the Commission and report within two months.
quote: The competent authority receiving the request pursuant to paragraph 2 shall comply with such request

summary: Member States and Union entities must carry out risk assessments identifying public sector activities using cloud services that contribute to public order and the Union assurance level (2, 3 or 4) appropriate to each, considering data sensitivity, unlawful third-country access, disruption risk and multi-cloud strategies.
applies_from: entry into force + 1 year; then every two years
quote: determine which Union assurance level 2, 3, or 4 set out in Annex II of this Regulation is appropriate for the identified public sector activities .

summary: Member States must send risk-assessment results to the Commission within three months, flagging departures from the implementing-act methodology; the Commission may then specify required assurance levels.
quote: indicating where they depart from th e implementing acts referred to in paragraph 3 .

summary: Where a risk assessment requires migration to another cloud service, the Member State or Union entity must migrate within at most 12 months.
quote: Where the risk assessment requires the migration to another cloud computing service, the Member State or Union entity shall migrat e
conditional_on: Risk assessment requires migration

summary: Union entities and public sector bodies whose activities are not identified as public-order relevant must use cloud services recognised at Union assurance level 1 (when procuring for their exclusive use).
applies_from: date of application (entry into force + 1 year)
quote: shall use cloud computing services that have been recognised under Article 1 7 as having a Union assurance level 1 .
conditional_on: Contracting authority procures cloud services for its exclusive use; derogations in Art. 30(4)

summary: Contracting authorities whose activities are identified as contributing to public order (NIS2 Annex I/II sectors, national and internal security, border management, defence, justice, law enforcement) may only procure services recognised at levels 2, 3 or 4; exceptional, justified derogations apply if no recognised service exists, a recent tender failed, or costs are disproportionate.
applies_from: date of application (entry into force + 1 year)
quote: shall only procure cloud computing services that have been recognised as having a Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4 .
conditional_on: Activity identified under the Art. 29(1) risk assessment; derogations in Art. 30(4)

summary: In procurement of innovative cloud services and AI systems, contracting authorities must include ancillary, non-decisive non-price award criteria on the tenderer's contribution to a European cloud and AI ecosystem (Union supply chain, Union technologies, security of supply, Union-made hardware).
quote: contracting authorities shall include , as part of the quality evaluation of the tender, non-price award criteria

summary: Member States must monitor their procurement of innovation in cloud and AI and report yearly to the Commission on operator size, SME participation and measures to improve SME access; they must pursue a 25% innovative-SME objective and plan for it in national strategies.
quote: Member States shall inform the Commission, on a yearly basis , of the following information :

summary: The Commission must set up a EuroCloud Federation platform with a catalogue of public-sector data centre and cloud services and a service platform for exchanging compute, storage and network resources, and assess and admit sharing entities.
quote: The Commission shall establish a platform for the EuroCloud Federation providing at least:

summary: A EuroCloud Federation member may share services only if it owns (directly or via a controlled entity) the hardware and provides the service, has appropriate security and resilience measures, and has demonstrated this to the Commission; fees to users are capped at cost.
quote: Prior to sharing data centre services and cloud computing services within the EuroCloud Federation, the sharing entity shall demonstrate to the Commission that it fulfils the conditions
conditional_on: Member of the EuroCloud Federation acting as sharing entity

summary: Members of the EuroCloud Federation must jointly finance the Commission's administration costs through fees, reimbursing any Union-budget advance within three years.
quote: shall be jointly finance d by the member s of the EuroCloud Federation through fees levied by the Commission.
conditional_on: Membership of the EuroCloud Federation

summary: Before procuring for others under Art. 37, the Commission and at least two Member States must conclude an agreement setting practical arrangements and a Steering Committee; participating entities finance the costs through fees.
quote: The costs arising from the procurement activities carried out pursuant to this Chapter shall be jointly financed by the participating entities through fees levied by the Commission.

summary: Union entities and public sector bodies releasing software they own under an open source licence must do so through a catalogue or repository connected to the EU OSS Catalogue; the Union and Member States must encourage open-source use.
quote: a Union entity or public sector body shall do so using a catalogue or repository that is connected to, and made accessible through, the EU OSS Catalogue referred to in Article 43.
conditional_on: Making owned software available for reuse under an open source licence

summary: The Commission must provide the EU Open Source Solutions Catalogue, free of charge on the Interoperable Europe portal, and establish, support and chair (at least twice a year) a network of Open Source Programme Offices.
quote: The Commission shall convene and chair a meeting of the members of the OSPO Network at least twice a year.

summary: The Commission must evaluate the Regulation four years after entry into force and every five years, reporting to Parliament, Council and EESC, with attention to SMEs and new competitors.
quote: and shall pay specific attention to small and medium-sized enterprises and the position of new competitors.

summary: A coordinator, appointed by all members of a prospective ECIC, must submit the application to the Commission on behalf of the founding members, with the required contents listed in Art. 7(3).
quote: The coordinator of a potential ECIC shall, on behalf of all of the founding members, submit an application to the Commission in writing.
conditional_on: Application for establishment of an ECIC

summary: An ECIC must appoint a coordinator, which is the principal point of contact for the Commission (Art. 2(8)).
quote: appoint a coordinator.

summary: An ECIC must notify amendments to its statutes to the Commission within 10 days of adoption, with the amended text and consolidated statutes; the Commission may object within 60 days.
quote: The ECIC shall notify such amendments to the Commission within 10 days of adoption.
conditional_on: Adoption of amendments to the ECIC statutes

summary: An ECIC must produce an annual activity report with a technical description and financial statement, including an assessment of environmental and social impact, to be sent to the Commission and made publicly available.
quote: An ECIC shall produce an annual activity report, containing a technical description of its activities and a financial statement.

summary: Member States must designate candidate competence centres through an open and competitive process in accordance with national procedures; the Chips Joint Undertaking selects the network members.
quote: Member States shall designate candidate competence centres in accordance with their national procedures, administrative and institutional structures through an open and competitive process.

summary: Competence centres in the network must perform all or some of the listed activities (access to design services and pilot lines, awareness and know-how, knowledge transfer, and training) for the Union industry and other stakeholders.
quote: Competence centres shall perform all or some of the following activities to the benefit of and in close cooperation with the Union industry
conditional_on: Selection as a competence centre in the network

summary: An integrated production facility must meet listed requirements: clear positive spill-over impact, assurance against extraterritorial public service obligations, continued innovation investment, and support for the talent pipeline.
quote: An integrated production facility shall meet the following requirements:
conditional_on: Recognition as integrated production facility

summary: An integrated production facility must commit to informing the Commission when an extraterritorial public service obligation of a third country arises.
quote: commits to informing the Commission when such obligation arises
conditional_on: Arising of a third-country extraterritorial public service obligation

summary: An open EU foundry must meet the same listed requirements as an integrated production facility, including taking into account the extent of front-end or back-end capacity offered to unrelated undertakings.
quote: An open EU foundry shall meet the following requirements:
conditional_on: Recognition as open EU foundry

summary: An open EU foundry offering capacity to unrelated undertakings must establish and maintain functional separation of design and manufacturing processes to protect information obtained at each stage.
quote: it shall establish and maintain adequate and effective functional separation of the design and manufacturing processes
conditional_on: Open EU foundry offers production capacity to undertakings not related to its operator

summary: The Commission must assess applications for integrated production facility or open EU foundry status through a fair and transparent process, taking into account the European Semiconductor Board's views, on the listed elements.
quote: The Commission shall, taking into account the views of the European Semiconductor Board, assess the application through a fair and transparent process
conditional_on: Application under Art. 15(1)

summary: The Commission must process applications, adopt decisions and notify applicants within six months of receipt of a complete application, and must allow incomplete applications to be completed; it sets the status duration.
quote: The Commission shall process applications, adopt its decisions and notify the applicants within six months of receipt of a complete application.
conditional_on: Receipt of a complete application

summary: The Commission must monitor progress in establishing and operating integrated production facilities and open EU foundries and inform the European Semiconductor Board regularly.
quote: The Commission shall monitor the progress achieved in the establishment and operation of integrated production facilities and open EU foundries
conditional_on: Recognised facilities

summary: Where the Commission finds a facility no longer fulfils the requirements, it must give the operator the opportunity to comment and propose measures.
quote: it shall give the operator of the integrated production facility or open EU foundry the opportunity to comment and to propose appropriate measures.
conditional_on: Commission finding that a facility no longer meets Art. 13(3) or 14(3)

summary: Before repealing a facility's status, the Commission must consult the European Semiconductor Board after giving it the reasons; any withdrawal must be reasoned and subject to a right of appeal by the operator.
quote: Before taking such a decision, the Commission shall consult the European Semiconductor Board after providing it with the reasons for the proposed repeal.
conditional_on: Proposed repeal of recognised status

summary: Facilities whose status has been repealed remain subject to the priority-rated order obligation of Art. 26(1) for the period originally foreseen or the reviewed duration.
quote: such facilities shall remain subject to the obligation set out in Article 26(1) for a period equivalent
conditional_on: Repeal of status under Art. 15(7)

summary: The Commission must adopt delegated acts, under Art. 37, setting the procedure for applications and the requirements for granting, monitoring and withdrawing the design centre of excellence label.
quote: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 37, supplementing this Regulation

summary: Member States must ensure that permit applications for planning, construction and operation of integrated production facilities and open EU foundries are processed in an efficient, transparent and timely manner, with the most rapid treatment legally possible. Where national law has a status of highest national significance, these facilities receive it in permit-granting (Art. 18(2)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that administrative applications related to the planning, construction and operation of integrated production facilities and open EU foundries are processed in an efficient, transparent and timely manner.
conditional_on: Administrative applications for such facilities

summary: The Commission must carry out a strategic mapping of the Union's semiconductor sector in cooperation with the European Semiconductor Board, covering the factors listed in Art. 19(1)(a) to (f).
quote: The Commission shall carry out a strategic mapping of the Union’s semiconductor sector in cooperation with the European Semiconductor Board.

summary: The Commission must develop a list of early warning indicators after consulting the European Semiconductor Board, and review it at least every two years.
quote: The Commission shall, on the basis of the outcome of the strategic mapping carried out pursuant to paragraph 1 and after consulting the European Semiconductor Board, develop a list of early warning indicators.

summary: The Commission must carry out regular monitoring of the semiconductor value chain in consultation with the European Semiconductor Board, focusing on early warning indicators, key market actors and best practices.
quote: The Commission, in consultation with the European Semiconductor Board, shall carry out regular monitoring of the semiconductor value chain

summary: Member States must monitor the integrity of activities carried out by key market actors and report on major events that may hinder their regular operations.
quote: monitoring by Member States of the integrity of activities carried out by the key market actors

summary: National competent authorities must establish and maintain a list of contacts of all relevant undertakings along the semiconductor supply chain in their territory, transmitted to the Commission.
quote: national competent authorities shall establish and maintain a list of contacts of all relevant undertakings operating along the semiconductor supply chain established in their territory.

summary: Member States, in cooperation with the Commission, must identify key market actors along the semiconductor supply chains in their territory, taking account of the listed elements.
quote: Member States shall, in cooperation with the Commission in accordance with Article 19, identify key market actors along the semiconductor supply chains established in their territory

summary: A national competent authority that becomes aware of a risk of serious supply disruption or other relevant risk must alert the Commission without undue delay.
quote: it shall alert the Commission without undue delay.
conditional_on: Awareness of a risk of serious disruption in semiconductor supply or other relevant risk factor

summary: On becoming aware of a risk of serious disruption, the Commission must without undue delay convene an extraordinary meeting of the European Semiconductor Board, discuss joint procurement and stakeholder dialogue, consult third countries, and ask national authorities to assess key market actors' preparedness.
quote: it shall, without undue delay, carry out the following preventive actions:
conditional_on: Commission awareness of a risk of serious supply disruption or other relevant risk factor

summary: Any joint procurement following Art. 22(2)(a)(iii) must be carried out by Member States under the public procurement rules of Directives 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU.
quote: shall be carried out by Member States in accordance with the rules set out in Articles 38 and 39 of Directive 2014/24/EU
conditional_on: Joint procurement following discussions under Art. 22(2)(a)(iii)

summary: During the crisis stage the Commission must report at least every three months to the European Semiconductor Board and the European Parliament on the state of the crisis.
quote: The Commission shall report on a regular basis and in any event at least every three months to the European Semiconductor Board and to the European Parliament on the state of the crisis.
conditional_on: Crisis stage activated under Art. 23

summary: During the crisis stage, Member States must work closely with the Commission, inform it in a timely manner about, and coordinate, any national measures taken on the semiconductor supply chain within the European Semiconductor Board.
quote: Member States shall work closely with the Commission, inform in a timely manner about and coordinate any national measures taken with regard to the semiconductor supply chain
conditional_on: Crisis stage activated

summary: Upon expiry or early termination of the crisis stage, the measures under Arts. 25, 26 and 27 must cease to apply immediately; the Commission must update the mapping and monitoring within six months after the crisis stage expires.
quote: the measures taken in accordance with Articles 25, 26 and 27 shall cease to apply immediately.
conditional_on: Expiry or early termination of the crisis stage

summary: The Commission must regularly inform the European Parliament and the Council of any emergency measures taken and explain the reasons for its decision.
quote: The Commission shall regularly inform the European Parliament and the Council of any measures taken in accordance with paragraph 1 and explain the reasons for its decision.
conditional_on: Measures taken under Art. 24(1)

summary: Undertakings must supply the information the Commission requests on production capabilities, capacities and current primary disruptions, through the owners or legal representatives.
quote: shall supply the information requested on behalf of the undertaking
conditional_on: Information request by the Commission during the crisis stage

summary: An undertaking established in the Union that is subject to a third-country request for information on its semiconductor activities must inform the Commission in due time.
quote: it shall inform the Commission, in due time, in such a manner as to enable the Commission to request similar information
conditional_on: Third-country information request concerning semiconductor activities

summary: A Commission request for information must state its legal basis, be limited to the minimum necessary and proportionate, consider the undertaking's legitimate aims and costs, set a time limit, and state the penalties under Art. 33.
quote: The request for information shall state its legal basis
conditional_on: Information request under Art. 25(1)

summary: Integrated production facilities and open EU foundries, when required by the Commission, must accept and prioritise an order of crisis-relevant products (priority-rated order), taking precedence over any performance obligation under private or public law.
quote: to accept and prioritise an order of crisis-relevant products (priority-rated order)
conditional_on: Crisis stage activated and Commission requirement under Art. 26(1)

summary: A Union semiconductor undertaking subject to a third-country priority-rated order measure must inform the Commission.
quote: When a semiconductor undertaking established in the Union is subject to a third-country priority-rated order measure, it shall inform the Commission.
conditional_on: Third-country priority-rated order measure

summary: The Commission must give the envisaged recipient of a priority-rated order an opportunity to be heard on feasibility and details, and must not issue the order where listed conditions apply.
quote: the Commission shall give the envisaged recipient of a priority-rated order the opportunity to be heard on the feasibility and details of the order.
conditional_on: Before issuing a priority-rated order

summary: The Commission must enact priority-rated order obligations as a last resort by decision, after consulting the European Semiconductor Board, stating the legal basis, time limit, product and quantity, and price.
quote: The Commission shall take that decision after consulting the European Semiconductor Board
conditional_on: Use of priority-rated order obligations

summary: The Commission must adopt an implementing act laying down practical and operational arrangements for priority-rated orders, under the examination procedure.
quote: The Commission shall adopt an implementing act laying down the practical and operational arrangements for the functioning of priority-rated orders.

summary: For common purchasing, the Commission must draw up a proposal for an agreement to be signed by the participating Member States, organising the purchasing and the Commission's mandate.
quote: The Commission shall draw up a proposal for an agreement to be signed by the participating Member States.
conditional_on: Common purchasing during the crisis stage

summary: Each Member State must designate one or more national competent authorities for application and implementation of the Regulation, empowered and resourced accordingly, and notify the Commission of designations and the single point of contact.
quote: Each Member State shall designate one or more national competent authorities

summary: Each Member State must designate one national single point of contact for cross-border cooperation with other Member States, the Commission and the European Semiconductor Board.
quote: Each Member State shall designate one national single point of contact

summary: Each Member State must notify the Commission of the designation of its national competent authorities and single point of contact, including tasks, contact information and later changes.
quote: Each Member State shall notify the Commission of the designation of the national competent authority

summary: Information acquired while implementing the Regulation may be used only for its purposes and must be protected under Union and national law; the Commission and national authorities must ensure confidentiality of information obtained, protecting IP rights, sensitive business information and trade secrets.
quote: The Commission and the national authorities, their officials, servants and other persons working under the supervision of those authorities shall ensure the confidentiality of information and data

summary: The Commission must provide standardised and secure means for collecting, processing and storing information acquired under the Regulation.
quote: The Commission shall provide for standardised and secure means for the collection, processing and storage of the information acquired

summary: The Commission must hear the undertaking concerned, on preliminary findings and intended measures, before adopting a penalty decision.
quote: Before adopting a decision pursuant to Article 33, the Commission shall give the undertaking concerned the opportunity of being heard
conditional_on: Before adopting a penalty decision under Art. 33

summary: The European Semiconductor Board must hold ordinary meetings at least once a year.
quote: The European Semiconductor Board shall hold ordinary meetings at least once a year.

summary: The Commission must inform the European Semiconductor Board regularly on progress in implementing operational objective 5 (Chips Fund activities).
quote: The Commission shall inform the European Semiconductor Board on progress in the implementation of the Initiative’s operational objective 5

summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts to amend Annex I (actions) and Annex II (measurable indicators) under Art. 37.
quote: the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 37 to amend Annex I

summary: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission must consult experts designated by each Member State, under the Interinstitutional Agreement of 13 April 2016.
quote: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State
conditional_on: Adoption of a delegated act

summary: By 20 September 2026 and every four years thereafter, the Commission must submit a report on evaluation and review of the Regulation to the European Parliament and the Council, to be made public.
quote: the Commission shall submit a report on the evaluation and review of this Regulation to the European Parliament and to the Council

summary: For evaluation and review, the European Semiconductor Board, Member States and national competent authorities must provide the Commission with information on its request.
quote: the European Semiconductor Board, the Member States and national competent authorities shall provide the Commission with information on its request.
conditional_on: Commission request for information for evaluation and review

summary: Member States must require that information provided to consumers under the Directive is free of charge, regardless of the medium used.
quote: such information is provided without charge to the consumer regardless of the media used to provide it

summary: Conditions for granting credit must not discriminate against consumers legally resident in the Union on grounds of nationality or place of residence, subject to objectively justified differences.
