quote: do not discriminate against consumers legally resident in the Union on ground of their nationality or place of residence

summary: Advertising and marketing communications must be fair, clear and not misleading; wording that may create false expectations about availability, cost or total amount payable is prohibited.
quote: Wording in such advertising and marketing communications that may create false expectations for a consumer regarding the availability or the cost of credit or the total amount payable by the consumer shall be prohibited.

summary: Advertising of credit must include a clear and prominent warning that borrowing costs money; where interest rates or cost figures are shown, standard information (borrowing rate, total amount of credit, APR, duration, and others) must be given by a representative example.
quote: Member States shall require that advertising concerning credit agreements include a clear and prominent warning to make consumers aware that borrowing costs money
conditional_on: where advertising indicates an interest rate or any figures relating to any cost of credit

summary: Advertising for credit products that encourages credit to improve finances, says registered credit has little influence on assessment, or falsely suggests credit increases resources is prohibited.
quote: Member States shall prohibit advertising for credit products which:

summary: Clear and comprehensible general information about credit agreements must be made available at all times on paper or another durable medium, and must include the listed elements (issuer identity, purposes, duration, rate types, representative example, further costs, repayment options, early repayment, withdrawal, ancillary services, general warning).
quote: clear and comprehensible general information about credit agreements is made available to consumers by creditors or, where applicable, by credit intermediaries, at all times

summary: Pre-contractual information must be provided in good time on the Standard European Consumer Credit Information form, with the prescribed elements on one page (two at most) and additional elements in a separate section; Annex I form and related content and consistency requirements apply.
quote: provide the consumer with the clear and comprehensible pre-contractual information needed to compare different offers

summary: Where pre-contractual information is given less than one day before the consumer is bound, a reminder of the right to withdraw must be sent between one and seven days after conclusion or submission of the binding offer.
quote: send a reminder to the consumer of the possibility to withdraw from the credit agreement
conditional_on: where pre-contractual information is provided less than one day before the consumer is bound

summary: On request, and where the creditor is willing to conclude the agreement, a copy of the draft credit agreement must be provided free of charge on paper or another durable medium.
quote: provide the consumer free of charge with a copy of the draft credit agreement
conditional_on: upon consumer request

summary: Where payments build capital rather than amortise credit, pre-contractual information must state that such agreements do not guarantee repayment of the total amount drawn, unless guaranteed expressly.
quote: include a clear and concise statement that such credit agreements do not provide for a guarantee of repayment
conditional_on: credit agreements where payments constitute capital rather than immediate amortisation

summary: For credit agreements under Art. 2(6) or (7), pre-contractual information must be given on the European Consumer Credit Information form (Annex II) with prescribed elements.
quote: shall, by way of derogation from Article 10(2), be provided on paper or on another durable medium chosen by the consumer
conditional_on: credit agreements referred to in Art. 2(6) or (7)

summary: Creditors and, where applicable, credit intermediaries must provide adequate explanations, free of charge and before conclusion, enabling the consumer to assess suitability, and must adapt them to the circumstances (Member States may adapt in justified cases).
quote: are required to provide adequate explanations to the consumer on the proposed credit agreements

summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must inform consumers in a clear and comprehensible manner when presenting a personalised offer based on automated processing of personal data.
quote: inform consumers in a clear and comprehensible manner when they are presented with a personalised offer that is based on automated processing of personal data
conditional_on: personalised offers based on automated processing of personal data

summary: Member States must prohibit tying practices (credit offered only in a package where credit is not available separately) while allowing bundling practices.
quote: Member States shall allow bundling practices but shall prohibit tying practices.

summary: Where credit requires insurance, the creditor must accept an equivalent policy from a supplier chosen by the consumer; consumers must be given at least three days to compare insurance offers and are informed of this.
quote: the creditor is required to accept the insurance policy from a supplier different to his or her preferred supplier
conditional_on: where the creditor requires a relevant insurance policy related to the credit

summary: Personal data on consumers' oncological diagnoses must not be used for insurance policies related to credit after a period set by Member States, not exceeding 15 years after end of treatment.
quote: personal data concerning consumers’ diagnoses of oncological diseases are not used for the purpose of an insurance policy related to a credit agreement
conditional_on: after a period of time determined by Member States, not exceeding 15 years

summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must not infer consumer agreement to credit or ancillary services from default options such as pre-ticked boxes.
quote: do not infer the agreement of the consumer for the conclusion of any credit agreement or for the purchase of ancillary services presented through default options

summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must explicitly inform consumers whether advisory services are or can be provided, and before providing them give the listed information (basis of recommendation, fee) on paper or durable medium.
quote: explicitly inform the consumer, in the context of a given transaction, whether advisory services are being or can be provided to the consumer
conditional_on: where advisory services are provided

summary: Where advisory services are provided, creditors and credit intermediaries must obtain and update the consumer's financial information, assess needs, consider a sufficiently large number of agreements, act in the consumer's best interests, and give a record of the recommendation.
quote: obtain the necessary information regarding the consumer’s financial situation, preferences and objectives related to the credit agreement
conditional_on: where advisory services are provided to consumers

summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must warn a consumer when a credit agreement may induce a specific risk given the consumer's financial situation.
quote: warn a consumer when a credit agreement may induce a specific risk for the consumer considering the consumer’s financial situation
conditional_on: where a credit agreement may induce a specific risk for the consumer

summary: Member States must prohibit any granting of credit to consumers without their prior request and explicit agreement.
quote: Member States shall prohibit any granting of credit to consumers without their prior request and explicit agreement.

summary: Before concluding a credit agreement the creditor must carry out a thorough creditworthiness assessment in the consumer's interest, based on relevant and accurate information (including joint repayment capacity for joint applications) and verified where necessary.
quote: the creditor carry out a thorough assessment of the consumer’s creditworthiness
conditional_on: before concluding a credit agreement

summary: Credit intermediaries must accurately submit the necessary consumer information to the relevant creditor so that the creditworthiness assessment can be carried out.
quote: credit intermediaries accurately submit the necessary information obtained from the consumer to the relevant creditor

summary: Creditors must establish, document and maintain procedures for the creditworthiness assessment and document and maintain the information used in it.
quote: Member States shall require the creditor to establish procedures for the assessment referred to in paragraph 1 and to document and maintain such procedures.

summary: Creditors may make credit available only where the creditworthiness assessment indicates the obligations are likely to be met.
quote: the creditor only makes the credit available to the consumer where the result of the creditworthiness assessment indicates

summary: Creditors must not cancel or modify a concluded credit agreement to the consumer's detriment because the creditworthiness assessment was incorrectly conducted, unless the consumer knowingly withheld or falsified information.
quote: the creditor shall not subsequently cancel or modify the credit agreement to the detriment of the consumer on the grounds that the assessment of creditworthiness was incorrectly conducted

summary: Where automated processing is used in the creditworthiness assessment, the creditor must allow human intervention, an explanation, the consumer's point of view, and review of the assessment and decision; consumers must be informed of this right.
quote: the consumer has the right to request and obtain from the creditor human intervention
conditional_on: where the creditworthiness assessment involves automated processing of personal data

summary: Where a credit application is rejected, the creditor must inform the consumer without delay and refer them to debt advisory services; where automated processing was used, the creditor must also inform the consumer of that and of the right to human assessment.
quote: the creditor is required to inform the consumer without delay of the rejection
conditional_on: where the credit application is rejected

summary: Before any significant increase in the total amount of credit after conclusion, the creditor must reassess creditworthiness on updated information.
quote: the creditor is required to reassess the consumer’s creditworthiness on the basis of updated information
conditional_on: where the parties agree to change the total amount of credit after conclusion and before any significant increase

summary: Member States must ensure that creditors from other Member States have non-discriminatory access to domestic creditworthiness databases in cross-border credit cases, for both public and private databases.
quote: Each Member State shall, in the case of cross-border credit, ensure access for creditors from other Member States to databases used in that Member State for assessing the creditworthiness of consumers.
conditional_on: cross-border credit

summary: Databases holding consumer credit information must hold at least information on arrears, type of credit and identity of the creditor; database providers must keep their information up to date and accurate.
quote: shall hold at least information on consumers’ arrears in repayment of credit, the type of credit and the identity of the creditor

summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must not process special categories of personal data or personal data from social networks contained in creditworthiness databases.
quote: Creditors and credit intermediaries shall not process special categories of data as referred to in Article 9(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679

summary: Where a credit application is rejected on the basis of a database consultation, the creditor must inform the consumer without undue delay and free of charge of the result, the database consulted and the categories of data used.
quote: the creditor informs the consumer without undue delay and free of charge of the result of such consultation
conditional_on: where the credit application is rejected on the basis of a database consultation

summary: Member States must ensure consumers are informed within 30 days of registration of any credit repayment arrears in a database, and of their rights under the GDPR.
quote: within 30 days of the registration of any arrears in repayment of credit in a database
conditional_on: registration of arrears in a credit database

summary: Member States must ensure complaint procedures exist to allow consumers to challenge the content of credit databases.
quote: Member States shall ensure that complaint procedures are in place in order to facilitate consumers’ challenges to the content of databases

summary: Credit agreements and any modifications must be drawn up on paper or another durable medium, and all contracting parties must receive a copy.
quote: credit agreements and any modifications of such agreements are drawn up on paper or another durable medium and that all the contracting parties are provided with a copy

summary: Credit agreements must specify in a clear and concise manner the listed elements (e.g., type of credit, parties, amount, duration, borrowing rate, APR, payments, charges, withdrawal, early repayment, complaint mechanism, supervisory authority and debt advice contacts).
quote: the credit agreement specify in a clear and concise manner all of the following elements

summary: Where capital is amortised, the creditor must provide a free statement of account in the form of an amortisation table at any time; a statement that building capital does not guarantee repayment must be included where relevant.
quote: the creditor shall make available to the consumer, free of charge and at any time throughout the duration of the credit agreement, a statement of account in the form of an amortisation table
conditional_on: where capital amortisation of a credit agreement with a fixed duration is involved

summary: Before modifying the terms and conditions of a credit agreement, the creditor must communicate a description of the changes, timescale, complaint means and periods, and the competent authority for complaints.
quote: the creditor communicates on paper or another durable medium specified in the credit agreement the following information to the consumer
conditional_on: prior to modifying the terms and conditions of the credit agreement

summary: Where creditors may change borrowing rates of existing agreements, they must inform the consumer of any change in good time before it takes effect, including the resulting payment amounts.
quote: the creditor inform the consumer of any change in the borrowing rate on paper or another durable medium specified in the credit agreement, in good time before the change enters into force
conditional_on: where creditors are allowed to change borrowing rates of existing credit agreements

summary: For overdraft facilities, the creditor must send at least monthly statements of account with listed elements, inform the consumer in good time of rate or charge increases, and notify reductions or cancellations at least 30 days in advance.
quote: keeps the consumer regularly, at least once per month, informed by means of statements of account
conditional_on: where credit is granted as an overdraft facility

summary: Where an overdraft facility is reduced or cancelled, the creditor must offer, before enforcement proceedings, at no additional cost, repayment of the amount drawn in 12 equal monthly instalments unless the consumer repays earlier.
quote: the creditor offer the consumer, before the enforcement proceedings have been initiated, at no additional cost, the possibility to repay the amount actually drawn down
conditional_on: where the overdraft facility is reduced or cancelled

summary: For overrunning, the creditor must include information on the overrun possibility and rates in the current account agreement, inform the consumer without delay of significant overruns exceeding one month, and notify non-allowance or reduction at least 30 days prior.
quote: the creditor includes information on that possibility in that agreement
conditional_on: where there is a possibility that the consumer is allowed an overrun

summary: In cases of regular overrunning, the creditor must offer advisory services where available and redirect the consumer at no cost to debt advisory services.
quote: the creditor shall offer the consumer advisory services, where available, and redirect the consumer at no cost towards debt advisory services
conditional_on: in the case of regular overrunning

summary: Where overrunning is reduced or cancelled, the creditor must offer, before enforcement, at no additional cost, repayment of the amount drawn in 12 equal monthly instalments unless repaid earlier.
quote: Where the overrunning is reduced or cancelled, Member States shall require that the creditor offer the consumer
conditional_on: where the overrunning is reduced or cancelled

summary: Consumers may withdraw from a credit agreement without giving reasons within 14 calendar days, with the period extended or limited as set out in the Article (including a 12-month-and-14-day long-stop where terms were not received).
quote: the consumer may withdraw from the credit agreement without giving any reason within a period of 14 calendar days

summary: A consumer exercising withdrawal must notify the creditor in the manner specified, and pay the capital and accrued interest without undue delay and no later than 30 calendar days after notification.
quote: no later than 30 calendar days after the dispatch of the notification referred to in point (a)
conditional_on: if the consumer exercises the right of withdrawal

summary: A consumer who withdraws from a purchase contract under Union law must no longer be bound by the linked credit agreement.
quote: is no longer bound by a linked credit agreement
conditional_on: where the consumer has exercised the right of withdrawal, based on Union law, concerning a contract for the supply of goods or services

summary: For open-end credit, the consumer may terminate free of charge at any time (subject to notice not exceeding one month); the creditor may, where agreed, terminate with at least two months' notice.
quote: the consumer may effect standard termination of an open-end credit agreement free of charge at any time
conditional_on: open-end credit agreements; creditor termination only where agreed in the credit agreement

summary: Where the creditor terminates the consumer's right to draw down for objectively justified reasons, it must inform the consumer of the termination and reasons, where possible before and at the latest immediately after.
quote: The creditor shall inform the consumer of the termination and the reasons for it on paper or another durable medium specified in the credit agreement
conditional_on: where agreed in the credit agreement and for objectively justified reasons

summary: The consumer is entitled at any time to early repayment, with a reduction in the total cost of credit for the remaining duration that takes into account all costs imposed by the creditor.
quote: the consumer is at any time entitled to early repayment

summary: The annual percentage rate of charge must be calculated by the mathematical formula in Annex III Part I, as the present value of all commitments agreed.
quote: shall be calculated in accordance with the mathematical formula set out in Part I of Annex III

summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts to amend Article 30 and Annex III Part II by adding or modifying assumptions for calculating the APR.
quote: the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 45
conditional_on: where the assumptions do not suffice to calculate the APR in a uniform manner or are no longer adapted to market situations

summary: Member States must introduce measures to effectively prevent abuse and ensure consumers cannot be charged excessively high borrowing rates, APRs or total costs of credit, such as caps; the Commission must make these measures public by 20 November 2027, and Member States must report to the Commission by 20 November 2026.
quote: Member States shall introduce measures to effectively prevent abuse

summary: The European Banking Authority must publish a report on the implementation of the Article 31(1) measures, including methodologies for caps and their effectiveness, by 20 November 2029.
quote: By 20 November 2029 the European Banking Authority shall publish a report on the implementation of the measures referred to in paragraph 1

summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must act honestly, fairly, transparently and professionally in manufacturing, advertising, granting, advising, ancillary services and executing credit; staff remuneration must not impede this and must avoid conflicts of interest and sales-target incentives.
quote: act honestly, fairly, transparently and professionally

summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must require staff to possess and keep up to date an appropriate level of knowledge and competence in relation to credit products, intermediation, advisory services and consumer rights.
quote: creditors and credit intermediaries require their staff to possess and keep up-to-date an appropriate level of knowledge and competence

summary: Member States must establish minimum knowledge and competence requirements for staff of creditors and intermediaries and ensure competent authorities supervise compliance and can require evidence.
quote: Member States shall establish minimum knowledge and competence requirements for the staff of creditors and of credit intermediaries.

summary: Member States must promote consumer financial education on responsible borrowing and debt management; the Commission must assess and publish a report on financial education and best practices.
quote: Member States shall promote measures that support the education of consumers in relation to responsible borrowing and debt management

summary: Creditors must exercise, where appropriate, reasonable forbearance before enforcement proceedings, considering the consumer's individual circumstances, and need not offer forbearance repeatedly unless justified.
quote: Member States shall require creditors to exercise, where appropriate, reasonable forbearance before enforcement proceedings are initiated
conditional_on: where appropriate, before enforcement proceedings are initiated

summary: Where Member States allow creditors to impose additional charges on default, they must cap those charges.
quote: those Member States shall place a cap on those charges
conditional_on: where Member States allow creditors to impose additional charges in the event of default

summary: Member States must ensure independent debt advisory services are available to consumers in difficulty, with only limited charges; the Commission must present a report by 20 November 2028 and Member States must report by 20 November 2026 and annually thereafter.
quote: Member States shall ensure that independent debt advisory services are made available to consumers

summary: Creditors must have processes and policies to detect early consumers experiencing financial difficulties and must refer them to easily accessible debt advisory services.
quote: creditors shall have processes and policies in place for the early detection of consumers experiencing financial difficulties

summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must be subject to an adequate admission process, registration and supervision by an independent competent authority, subject to listed exemptions for credit institutions, payment and e-money institutions and ancillary micro and SME suppliers.
quote: creditors and credit intermediaries are subject to an adequate admission process, to registration and to supervision arrangements set up by an independent competent authority

summary: Credit intermediaries must indicate in consumer-facing advertising and documentation the extent of their powers and whether they work exclusively with one or more creditors; must disclose and agree fees with consumers before conclusion and communicate fees to the creditor for APR calculation.
quote: indicate, in advertising and documentation intended for consumers, the extent of their powers

summary: The original creditor must inform the consumer of an assignment of the credit agreement, except where it continues to service the credit with the assignee's agreement.
quote: Member States shall require that the original creditor inform the consumer of the assignment referred to in paragraph 1
conditional_on: assignment of creditor's rights, unless original creditor continues servicing the credit

summary: Member States must ensure consumers have access to adequate, prompt and effective out-of-court dispute resolution procedures and encourage cross-border cooperation between such entities.
quote: Member States shall ensure that consumers have access to adequate, prompt and effective out-of-court dispute resolution procedures

summary: Member States must designate national competent authorities with investigation and enforcement powers and adequate resources, and notify the Commission of designations by 20 November 2025.
quote: Member States shall designate the national competent authorities empowered to ensure the application and enforcement of this Directive

summary: Competent authorities and persons working for them, and auditors and experts instructed by them, are bound by professional secrecy, subject to exceptions in law.
quote: are bound by the obligation of professional secrecy

summary: The Commission must publish a list of competent authorities in the Official Journal at least once a year and update it on its website.
quote: The Commission shall publish a list of the competent authorities in the Official Journal of the European Union at least once a year

summary: Where the Directive contains harmonised provisions, Member States may not maintain or introduce national provisions diverging from them, unless the Directive provides otherwise.
quote: Member States may not maintain or introduce in their national law provisions diverging from those laid down in this Directive
conditional_on: insofar as the Directive contains harmonised provisions

summary: Where a Member State uses the listed regulatory choices, it must notify the Commission without delay and of subsequent changes.
quote: that Member State shall notify the Commission without delay thereof, as well as of any subsequent changes
conditional_on: where a Member State uses the regulatory choices listed in Article 42(2)

summary: Consumers may not waive the rights conferred by the national measures transposing the Directive.
quote: consumers may not waive the rights conferred on them by the national measures transposing this Directive

summary: Member States must ensure that transposing provisions cannot be circumvented through the way agreements are formulated.
quote: Member States shall ensure that the provisions adopted in order to transpose this Directive cannot be circumvented

summary: Member States must notify the Commission of their penalty rules and measures by 20 November 2026, and notify any subsequent amendment without delay.
quote: Member States shall, by 20 November 2026, notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures

summary: Power to adopt delegated acts under Article 30(5) is conferred on the Commission for five years from 19 November 2023, tacitly extended unless opposed; the Commission must draw up a report not later than nine months before the end of that period.
quote: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 30(5) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 19 November 2023.

summary: The Commission must evaluate the Directive by 20 November 2029 and every four years thereafter (scope, thresholds, compensation percentages, green-transition credit, penalties), and assess consumer protection for crowdfunding by 20 November 2025.
quote: The Commission shall undertake, by 20 November 2029 and every four years thereafter, an evaluation of this Directive.

summary: Member States must adopt and publish the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with the Directive, and immediately communicate their text to the Commission.
quote: Member States shall adopt and publish, by 20 November 2025, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.

summary: Member States must apply the transposing measures from 20 November 2026.
quote: They shall apply those measures from 20 November 2026.

summary: Member States must communicate to the Commission the text of the main national law measures they adopt in the field covered by the Directive.
quote: Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.

summary: Form note (1): the creditor (text term) must fill in each 'where applicable' box if the information is relevant to the credit type, or delete the information or row where it is not relevant. Applies to the Annex I form.
quote: the creditor must fill in the box if the information is relevant to the type of credit

summary: Creditor must inform the consumer immediately and without charge of the result of a database consultation where a credit application is rejected on that basis (Annex I, Part 3 form text).
provision: Annex I, Part 3, 'Consultation of a database'
quote: The creditor must inform you immediately and without charge of the result of consulting a database
conditional_on: Credit application rejected on the basis of a database consultation

summary: Consumer has the right, on request, to a copy of the draft credit agreement free of charge; applies if the creditor is willing at the time of the request to conclude the agreement. Text is framed as a consumer right, implying a creditor duty to supply it.
provision: Annex I, Part 3, 'Right to a draft credit agreement'
quote: You have the right, upon request, to obtain a copy of the draft credit agreement free of charge.
conditional_on: Upon consumer request; creditor willing to proceed to conclusion of the agreement

summary: Form note (1) to Annex II (debt conversion form): creditor must fill in boxes where information is relevant to the credit type, or delete information or rows where not relevant.
quote: the creditor must fill in the box if the information is relevant to the type of credit

summary: APR calculation method (Annex III, Part I, Remarks (d)): the calculation result is expressed with accuracy of at least one decimal place, rounded per the stated rule. Remarks (c) also fix day/year conventions for interval calculations.
quote: The result of the calculation shall be expressed with an accuracy of at least one decimal place.
conditional_on: Calculation of the annual percentage rate of charge

summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts to supplement the Regulation by specifying whether a limitation or exclusion for products covered by other Union rules is necessary, the products and rules concerned, and the scope of the limitation.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 61 to supplement this Regulation
conditional_on: Sectoral rules achieve the same or a higher level of protection as provided by this Regulation.

summary: Member States shall not impede, for matters covered by the Regulation, the making available on the market of products with digital elements that comply with the Regulation. Also covers trade fairs, prototypes and unfinished software under Art. 4(2) and (3).
quote: Member States shall not impede, for the matters covered by this Regulation, the making available on the market of products with digital elements which comply with this Regulation.
conditional_on: Products comply with this Regulation.

summary: Member States shall ensure that compliance with the essential cybersecurity requirements in Annex I, including the manufacturers' ability to handle vulnerabilities, is taken into consideration in public procurement of products with digital elements.
quote: Member States shall ensure that compliance with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Annex I to this Regulation
conditional_on: Products with digital elements within the scope of the Regulation are procured.

summary: Products with digital elements may be made available on the market only where they meet the Part I essential cybersecurity requirements of Annex I (when properly installed, maintained and used) and the manufacturer's processes comply with Part II requirements.
quote: Products with digital elements shall be made available on the market only where:
conditional_on: Products are properly installed, maintained, used for their intended purpose or under reasonably foreseeable conditions, and necessary security updates are installed.

summary: Products with the core functionality of an Annex III category are important products and are subject to the conformity assessment procedures in Art. 32(2) and (3); integration of such a product into another product does not in itself subject that product to those procedures.
quote: shall be considered to be important products with digital elements and shall be subject to the conformity assessment procedures referred to in Article 32(2) and (3)
conditional_on: Core functionality of a product category set out in Annex III.

summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts to amend Annex III by adding a category, specifying its definition, moving a category between classes or withdrawing a category; a minimum transitional period of 12 months applies where the text provides for one.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 61 to amend Annex III
conditional_on: Assessment against the criteria in Art. 7(2).

summary: The Commission shall adopt an implementing act specifying the technical description of the categories of products under classes I and II of Annex III and of the categories in Annex IV, in accordance with the examination procedure.
quote: By 11 December 2025, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act specifying the technical description of the categories of products with digital elements under classes I and II

summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts to determine which critical products (Annex IV categories) must obtain a European cybersecurity certificate at assurance level at least substantial, and to amend Annex IV by adding or withdrawing categories; a minimum transitional period of six months applies.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 61 to supplement this Regulation to determine which products with digital elements
conditional_on: A European cybersecurity certification scheme covering the categories has been adopted and is available, and an assessment of market impact has been carried out.

summary: The Commission shall consult and take into account the views of relevant stakeholders when preparing implementation measures, and shall organise consultation and information sessions at least once a year.
quote: the Commission shall consult and take into account the views of relevant stakeholders

summary: Member States, with the support of the Commission, ENISA and the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre where appropriate, shall promote measures and strategies to develop cybersecurity skills and increase collaboration on skills for the purposes of the Regulation.
quote: shall promote measures and strategies aiming to:

summary: For products with digital elements that are high-risk AI systems under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and fall within this Regulation, the conformity assessment procedure in Art. 43 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 applies; such products are deemed to comply with AI Act Art. 15 cybersecurity requirements when the Part I and Part II requirements are met.
quote: the relevant conformity assessment procedure provided for in Article 43 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 shall apply.
conditional_on: Product is classified as a high-risk AI system under Article 6 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and falls within the scope of this Regulation.

summary: Manufacturers shall ensure that products with digital elements are designed, developed and produced in accordance with the Part I essential cybersecurity requirements of Annex I.
quote: manufacturers shall ensure that it has been designed, developed and produced in accordance with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I

summary: Manufacturers shall assess cybersecurity risks, take the outcome into account across the product lifecycle, document and update the assessment during the support period, include it in the technical documentation, and justify any non-applicable essential requirements.
applies_from: When placing on the market; during the support period
quote: The cybersecurity risk assessment shall be documented and updated as appropriate during a support period

summary: Where a manufacturer fails the formal requirements (CE marking, EU declaration, technical documentation), the market surveillance authority requires it to end the non-compliance.
quote: it shall require the relevant manufacturer to put an end to the non-compliance concerned
conditional_on: Where a formal non-compliance finding under Art. 58(1)(a) to (f) is made

summary: If the formal non-compliance persists, the Member State takes measures to restrict or prohibit the product being made available or to recall or withdraw it.
quote: the Member State concerned shall take all appropriate measures to restrict or prohibit the product
conditional_on: Where the non-compliance referred to in Art. 58(1) persists

summary: Market surveillance authorities may agree joint activities with other authorities on specific products; the Commission or ENISA may propose joint compliance checks.
quote: Market surveillance authorities may agree with other relevant authorities to carry out joint activities

summary: The authority concerned and, where applicable, the Commission make the joint-activity agreement, including the names of parties, available to the public.
quote: shall make the agreement on joint activities, including the names of the parties involved, available to the public.

summary: Market surveillance authorities conduct simultaneous coordinated control actions (sweeps) of particular products to check compliance.
quote: Market surveillance authorities shall conduct simultaneous coordinated control actions (sweeps)

summary: The sweep coordinator publishes aggregated results where appropriate; ENISA proposes sweeps for categories identified from notifications.
quote: The coordinator of the sweep shall, where appropriate, make the aggregated results publicly available.

summary: The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission for five years from 10 December 2024, tacitly extended unless opposed.
quote: shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 10 December 2024
conditional_on: Subject to the conditions in Art. 61

summary: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission consults experts designated by each Member State.
quote: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State

summary: As soon as it adopts a delegated act, the Commission notifies it simultaneously to the European Parliament and the Council.
quote: As soon as it adopts a delegated act, the Commission shall notify it simultaneously to the European Parliament and to the Council.

summary: The Commission is assisted by a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.
quote: The Commission shall be assisted by a committee.

summary: All parties involved in applying the Regulation respect confidentiality of information, protecting trade secrets, security interests, and proceedings integrity.
quote: All parties involved in the application of this Regulation shall respect the confidentiality of information and data

summary: Confidential information exchanged between market surveillance authorities, and with the Commission, is not disclosed without prior agreement of the originating authority.
quote: shall not be disclosed without the prior agreement of the originating market surveillance authority

summary: The Commission reports by 11 December 2030 and every four years thereafter on evaluation and review of the Regulation.
quote: By 11 December 2030 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a report

summary: By 11 September 2028 the Commission, after consulting ENISA and the CSIRTs network, reports on the effectiveness of the single reporting platform and the impact of cybersecurity-related delays.
quote: By 11 September 2028, the Commission shall, after consulting ENISA and the CSIRTs network, submit a report

summary: Article 14 reporting obligations apply to all products placed on the market before 11 December 2027, notwithstanding the general exemption in Art. 69(2).
quote: the obligations laid down in Article 14 shall apply to all products with digital elements
conditional_on: Products placed on the market before 11 December 2027

summary: Products with digital elements are designed, developed and produced to ensure appropriate cybersecurity based on risks; Part I (2) lists requirements including no known exploitable vulnerabilities, secure default configuration, security updates, access control, encryption, data minimisation, resilience and data erasure.
quote: Products with digital elements shall be designed, developed and produced in such a way that they ensure an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks.

summary: Manufacturers identify and document vulnerabilities and components including an SBOM; address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay through security updates; apply effective tests and reviews; put in place a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy; provide a contact address; distribute updates securely and free of charge.
quote: Manufacturers of products with digital elements shall:

summary: After a security update is available, manufacturers share and publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities, with description, affected product, impacts, severity and remediation help; publication may be delayed in duly justified cases.
quote: share and publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities
conditional_on: After a security update has been made available

summary: The product is accompanied by manufacturer contact details, a single point of contact for vulnerability reports, identification, intended purpose, security information, support period end-date, and instructions for secure use, updates and decommissioning.
quote: At minimum, the product with digital elements shall be accompanied by:

summary: The manufacturer affixes the CE marking to each individual product satisfying the requirements under internal control (Annex VIII Part I).
quote: The manufacturer shall affix the CE marking to each individual product with digital elements that satisfies the applicable requirements

summary: Under internal control, the manufacturer keeps the written EU declaration of conformity with technical documentation for 10 years or the support period, whichever is longer.
quote: keep it together with the technical documentation at the disposal of the national authorities for 10 years

summary: Under EU-type examination, the notified body examines technical design and vulnerability handling processes, verifies specimens, and issues or refuses an EU-type examination certificate.
quote: Where the type and the vulnerability handling processes meet the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Annex I, the notified body shall issue an EU-type examination certificate

summary: The manufacturer informs the notified body holding the technical documentation of modifications to the approved type or vulnerability handling processes that may affect conformity.
quote: The manufacturer shall inform the notified body that holds the technical documentation relating to the EU-type examination certificate

summary: The notified body carries out periodic audits to ensure vulnerability handling processes are implemented adequately.
quote: The notified body shall carry out periodic audits to ensure that the vulnerability handling processes

summary: Each notified body informs its notifying authorities of EU-type examination certificates issued or withdrawn and makes lists of refused or restricted certificates available.
quote: Each notified body shall inform its notifying authorities concerning the EU-type examination certificates

summary: Under full quality assurance (module H), the manufacturer undertakes to fulfil the obligations of the approved quality system and maintain it, allowing notified body access and surveillance.
quote: The manufacturer shall undertake to fulfil the obligations arising out of the quality system as approved and to maintain it
conditional_on: Under full quality assurance (module H)

summary: Each Member State participating in the European Cybersecurity Alert System designates or establishes a National Cyber Hub.
quote: Where a Member State decides to participate in the European Cybersecurity Alert System, it shall designate or, where applicable, establish a National Cyber Hub
conditional_on: Where a Member State decides to participate in the European Cybersecurity Alert System

summary: A National Cyber Hub acts as a single entity under the authority of a Member State, as a reference point and gateway at national level, and must be capable of detecting, aggregating and analysing cyber threat data (Art. 4(2)(a)-(b)).
quote: The National Cyber Hub shall:

summary: A Member State selected under Art. 9(1) commits to applying for its National Cyber Hub to participate in a Cross-Border Cyber Hub.
quote: A Member State selected pursuant to Article 9(1) shall commit to applying for its National Cyber Hub to participate in a Cross-Border Cyber Hub.
conditional_on: Member State selected pursuant to Article 9(1)

summary: Members of a selected Hosting Consortium conclude a written consortium agreement that sets out internal arrangements, establishes the Cross-Border Cyber Hub and includes the clauses required by Art. 6(1) and (2).
quote: Where a Hosting Consortium is selected in accordance with Article 9(3), its members shall conclude a written consortium agreement which:
conditional_on: Where a Hosting Consortium is selected in accordance with Article 9(3)

summary: Members of a Hosting Consortium ensure that their National Cyber Hubs share relevant threat information within the Cross-Border Cyber Hub, as set out in the consortium agreement.
quote: Members of a Hosting Consortium shall ensure that their National Cyber Hubs share, in accordance with the written consortium agreement referred to in Article 5(3), relevant information

summary: The consortium agreement must establish a commitment to share information, a governance framework incentivising sharing, and targets for contribution to advanced tools and technologies.
quote: The written consortium agreement referred to in Article 5(3) shall establish:

summary: Cross-Border Cyber Hubs (multi-country platforms) conclude cooperation agreements with one another on interoperability and information-sharing principles, and inform the Commission of them.
quote: Cross-Border Cyber Hubs shall conclude cooperation agreements with one another, specifying interoperability and information-sharing principles among the Cross-Border Cyber Hubs.

summary: ENISA issues interoperability guidelines on information-sharing formats and protocols; cooperation agreement interoperability requirements must be based on them.
quote: ENISA shall, in close consultation with the Commission, without undue delay and in any event by 5 February 2026, issue interoperability guidelines

summary: Cross-Border Cyber Hubs and the CSIRTs network cooperate closely and agree procedural arrangements on sharing relevant information.
quote: Cross-Border Cyber Hubs and the CSIRTs network shall cooperate closely, in particular for the purpose of sharing information.

summary: Where Cross-Border Cyber Hubs obtain information on a potential or ongoing large-scale incident, they ensure relevant information and early warnings reach Member States' authorities and the Commission via EU-CyCLONe and the CSIRTs network.
quote: they shall ensure, for the purposes of common situational awareness, that relevant information as well as early warnings are provided to Member States’ authorities and the Commission
conditional_on: Where the Cross-Border Cyber Hubs obtain information relating to a potential or ongoing large-scale cybersecurity incident

summary: Participating Member States ensure a high level of cybersecurity, confidentiality, data security and physical security of the Alert System network, and that sharing with non-public entities does not negatively affect security interests of the Union or Member States.
quote: Member States participating in the European Cybersecurity Alert System shall ensure a high level of cybersecurity, including confidentiality and data security, as well as physical security
conditional_on: Member States participating in the European Cybersecurity Alert System

summary: The ECCC and selected Member States conclude a hosting and usage agreement before procurement; selected Member States cover the remaining costs.
quote: Before launching the procedure for the acquisition of tools, infrastructure or services, the ECCC and the selected Member States shall conclude a hosting and usage agreement regulating the usage of the tools, infrastructure or services.
conditional_on: Before launching the procedure for the acquisition of tools, infrastructure or services

summary: A Member State whose National Cyber Hub has not joined a Cross-Border Cyber Hub within 2 years of acquisition or grant funding is not eligible for additional Union support under the Chapter until it joins.
applies_from: within 2 years of the date the tools, infrastructure or services were acquired or grant funding received, whichever occurred sooner
quote: the Member State shall not be eligible for additional Union support under this Chapter until it has joined a Cross-Border Cyber Hub.
conditional_on: National Cyber Hub is not a participant in a Cross-Border Cyber Hub

summary: The ECCC and the selected Hosting Consortium conclude a hosting and usage agreement before procurement; the Hosting Consortium covers the remaining costs.
quote: the ECCC and the Hosting Consortium shall conclude a hosting and usage agreement regulating the usage of the tools, infrastructure or services.
conditional_on: Before launching the procedure for the acquisition of tools, infrastructure or services

summary: The ECCC prepares a mapping of necessary tools, infrastructure and services and their availability, consulting the CSIRTs network, Cross-Border Cyber Hubs, ENISA and the Commission.
quote: The ECCC shall prepare, at least every 2 years, a mapping of the tools, infrastructure or services necessary

summary: Actions implementing the EU Cybersecurity Reserve are implemented by the Commission and ENISA; other Cybersecurity Emergency Mechanism actions primarily through the ECCC.
quote: actions implementing the EU Cybersecurity Reserve as referred to in Article 11, point (b), of this Regulation shall be implemented by the Commission and ENISA.

summary: The Commission identifies the sectors or sub-sectors eligible for coordinated preparedness testing after consulting the NIS Cooperation Group, EU-CyCLONe and ENISA; the NIS Cooperation Group, Commission, High Representative and ENISA develop common risk scenarios; Member State authorities may review follow-up of testing recommendations.
quote: the Commission shall, after consulting the NIS Cooperation Group, EU-CyCLONe and ENISA, identify the sectors or sub-sectors concerned

summary: The Commission has overall responsibility for the EU Cybersecurity Reserve, sets its priorities with the NIS Cooperation Group, reviews them every 2 years and informs Parliament and Council; it may entrust operation to ENISA; ENISA prepares a mapping of services every 2 years.
quote: The Commission shall have overall responsibility for the implementation of the EU Cybersecurity Reserve.

summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts specifying the types and number of response services required for the EU Cybersecurity Reserve.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 23 to supplement this Regulation by specifying the types and the number of response services required

summary: Users of the EU Cybersecurity Reserve take all appropriate measures to mitigate the effects of the incident and assist recovery.
quote: the users referred to in Article 14(3) shall take all appropriate measures to mitigate the effects of the incident for which the support is requested

summary: Support requests are transmitted to the contracting authority by the route set per user type; requests must include the information listed in Art. 15(5), covering the affected entity, impact, requested service and mitigation measures.
quote: Requests for support shall be transmitted to the contracting authority as follows:

summary: For requests from Member State cyber crisis authorities and CSIRTs, Member States inform the CSIRTs network and, where appropriate, EU-CyCLONe about the requests.
quote: Member States shall inform the CSIRTs network
conditional_on: In the case of requests from the users referred to in Article 14(3), point (a)

summary: ENISA, in cooperation with the Commission and EU-CyCLONe, develops a template to facilitate requests for support.
quote: ENISA, in cooperation with the Commission and EU-CyCLONe, shall develop a template to facilitate the submission of requests for support

summary: The Commission may, by implementing acts, specify detailed procedural arrangements for requesting and responding to EU Cybersecurity Reserve support, under the examination procedure.
quote: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, specify further the detailed procedural arrangements

summary: The contracting authority assesses requests and transmits a response within 48 hours; it assesses duration and nature of support by stated criteria; where requests are concurrent, the contracting authority and ENISA prioritise them and ENISA uses ENISA-prepared templates for agreements.
quote: requests for support from the EU Cybersecurity Reserve shall be assessed by the contracting authority.
conditional_on: In the case of requests from users referred to in Article 14(3), points (a) and (b)

summary: All parties involved limit use and sharing of information received under the Reserve to what is necessary, handle confidential or classified information only in accordance with law, and use secure information-sharing protocols including TLP.
quote: limit the use and sharing of that information to what is necessary to discharge their obligations or functions under this Regulation

summary: Service agreements between trusted managed security service providers and users must include liability conditions.
quote: All agreements referred to in this paragraph shall include, inter alia, liability conditions.

summary: Users may use Reserve services only to support response to and recovery from significant, large-scale or large-scale-equivalent incidents, and only in respect of the entities listed in Art. 16(8)(a) and (b).
quote: They may use those services only in respect of:

summary: Users that received support provide a summary report on the service, results and lessons learned to the Commission, ENISA, and the relevant networks or institutions.
applies_from: Within 2 months of the end of a support
quote: Within 2 months of the end of a support, users that have received support shall provide a summary report about the service provided

summary: The contracting authority reports to the NIS Cooperation Group, and the Commission reports to the Council and informs the High Representative, on use and results of support, at least twice per year.
quote: the contracting authority shall report to the NIS Cooperation Group, on a regular basis and at least twice per year, about the use and the results of the support.

summary: Where operation is entrusted to ENISA, ENISA reports to and consults the Commission on a regular basis and immediately sends it requests received from third-country users.
quote: ENISA shall report to and consult the Commission on a regular basis in that respect.
conditional_on: Where the operation and administration of the EU Cybersecurity Reserve has been entrusted to ENISA

summary: In procuring Reserve services, the contracting authority acts under the Financial Regulation principles and includes the criteria and requirements in Art. 17(2) in the procurement documents.
quote: When procuring services for the EU Cybersecurity Reserve, the contracting authority shall include in the procurement documents the following criteria and requirements:
conditional_on: In procedures for establishing the EU Cybersecurity Reserve

summary: Selected providers must demonstrate personnel integrity and competence, comply with classified-information rules, have a transparent governance structure, hold adequate security clearance and IT security, use hardware and software without known exploitable vulnerabilities, and meet service-delivery, language and conversion requirements (Art. 17(2)(a)-(k)); certification under a future EU scheme must follow within 2 years of that scheme's application.
quote: the provider shall demonstrate that its personnel has the highest degree of professional integrity
conditional_on: Provider selected for the EU Cybersecurity Reserve

summary: The contracting authority in procuring Reserve services applies the principles of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 and the Art. 17(1) principles on deployability, essential security interests and Union added value.
quote: the contracting authority shall act in accordance with the principles laid down in Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509

summary: A DEP-associated third country's association agreement must include provisions requiring compliance with the obligations in Art. 19(2) and (9).
quote: That agreement shall include provisions requiring the DEP-associated third country concerned to comply with the obligations set out in paragraphs 2 and 9 of this Article.
conditional_on: Where the agreement through which the third country is associated to the DEP provides for participation in the EU Cybersecurity Reserve

summary: A DEP-associated third country provides the Commission information on its cyber resilience and risk management capabilities, updated at least once a year.
applies_from: Within 3 months of the conclusion of the agreement referred to in paragraph 1 and in any event prior to receiving any support
quote: the DEP-associated third country shall provide to the Commission information about its cyber resilience and risk management capabilities

summary: The Commission assesses at least once a year whether each DEP-associated third country complies with its agreement, has taken adequate preparedness steps, and whether support is consistent with Union policy; it consults the High Representative and, if all conditions are met, proposes a Council implementing act.
quote: The Commission shall assess regularly, and at least once a year, the following criteria in respect of each DEP-associated third country referred to in paragraph 1:

summary: The Council acts expeditiously and, as a rule, adopts implementing acts on support to third countries within eight weeks of the Commission proposal; implementing acts apply for at most one year and may be renewed.
applies_from: within eight weeks of the adoption of the relevant Commission proposal
quote: the Council shall act expeditiously and shall, as a rule, adopt the implementing acts referred to in this paragraph within eight weeks of the adoption of the relevant Commission proposal

summary: When acting under Art. 19, the Council applies the Art. 19(3) criteria and explains its assessment; where it acts on its own initiative, it explains the significant change.
quote: the Council shall apply the criteria referred to in paragraph 3, first subparagraph, and shall explain its assessment of those criteria.

summary: Support from the EU Cybersecurity Reserve to a DEP-associated third country complies with any specific conditions in the association agreement.
quote: Support from the EU Cybersecurity Reserve to a DEP-associated third country shall comply with any specific conditions laid down in the agreement referred to in paragraph 1.

summary: Each DEP-associated third country eligible for Reserve support designates an authority to act as single point of contact.
quote: shall designate an authority to act as a single point of contact for the purposes of this Regulation.
conditional_on: Each DEP-associated third country eligible for support from the EU Cybersecurity Reserve

summary: Support to a third country may be provided by the contracting authority only where, and for as long as, a Council implementing act authorising it is in force.
quote: The contracting authority may provide support to a third country only where, and for so long as, a Council implementing act authorising such support
conditional_on: Council implementing act authorising such support is in force

summary: Upon receiving a third-country support request, the Commission immediately informs the Council, keeps it informed of the assessment, and cooperates with the High Representative.
quote: the Commission shall immediately inform the Council.
conditional_on: Upon receipt of a request for support under this Article

summary: Support for a large-scale incident handled under the IPCR Arrangements is handled in accordance with their relevant procedures.
quote: shall be handled in accordance with the relevant procedures under the IPCR Arrangements.
conditional_on: Where the EU Integrated Political Crisis Response Arrangements under Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/1993 (IPCR Arrangements) are activated

summary: On request of the Commission or EU-CyCLONe, ENISA reviews and assesses a specific incident and delivers an incident review report to EU-CyCLONe, the CSIRTs network, Member States and the Commission; it gathers stakeholder feedback, ensures the report complies with protection rules and anonymises it on request; consulted representatives must disclose conflicts of interest.
quote: ENISA shall deliver an incident review report to EU-CyCLONe, the CSIRTs network, the Member States concerned and the Commission
conditional_on: At the request of the Commission or EU-CyCLONe

summary: The Commission ensures in the Reserve implementation that the Commission and ENISA carry out operation as set out in the amended Regulation 2021/694 (Art. 6(2) as replaced).
quote: However, the EU Cybersecurity Reserve shall be implemented by the Commission and, in accordance with Article 14(6) of Regulation (EU) 2025/38, by ENISA.

summary: Power to adopt delegated acts under Art. 14(7) is conferred on the Commission for 5 years from 5 February 2025, tacitly extended; the Commission reports on the delegation at least 9 months before the period ends.
quote: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 14(7) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of 5 years from 5 February 2025.

summary: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission consults experts designated by each Member State, and notifies each delegated act simultaneously to Parliament and Council.
quote: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State
conditional_on: Before adopting a delegated act, or upon its adoption

summary: The Commission evaluates the functioning of the measures and submits a report to Parliament and Council, repeated at least every 4 years.
applies_from: By 5 February 2027 and at least every 4 years thereafter
quote: By 5 February 2027 and at least every 4 years thereafter, the Commission shall evaluate the functioning of the measures provided for in this Regulation

summary: Where appropriate, the Commission submits a legislative proposal to amend the Regulation based on the evaluation reports.
quote: the Commission shall, where appropriate, submit a legislative proposal to the European Parliament and to the Council to amend this Regulation.
conditional_on: On the basis of the reports referred to in paragraph 1, where appropriate

summary: Exchange of confidential information under the Regulation is limited to what is relevant and proportionate, preserves confidentiality and does not supply information contrary to essential national interests.
quote: The sharing or exchange of information under this Regulation that is confidential pursuant to Union or national rules shall be limited to that which is relevant and proportionate

summary: Connected products must be designed and manufactured, and related services designed and provided, so that product data and related service data are by default easily, securely, free of charge and machine-readable, and directly accessible to the user where relevant and technically feasible.
quote: Connected products shall be designed and manufactured, and related services shall be designed and provided

summary: Before a contract for purchase, rent or lease of a connected product, the seller, rentor or lessor (which may be the manufacturer) must give the user pre-contract information on the product data, its format, volume, storage and access arrangements.
quote: Before concluding a contract for the purchase, rent or lease of a connected product, the seller, rentor or lessor, which may be the manufacturer, shall provide at least the following information to the user

summary: Before a related service contract, the provider must give the user pre-contract information on the related service data, the prospective data holder, trade secret holders, complaint right and contract duration and termination.
quote: Before concluding a contract for the provision of a related service, the provider of such related service shall provide at least the following information to the user

summary: Where data cannot be directly accessed by the user, the data holder must make readily available data and metadata accessible to the user without undue delay, free of charge, in machine-readable format, on a simple electronic request where technically feasible.
quote: data holders shall make readily available data, as well as the relevant metadata necessary to interpret and use those data, accessible to the user without undue delay
conditional_on: Where data cannot be directly accessed by the user from the connected product or related service

summary: A data holder that refuses to share data under Art. 4(2), withholds or suspends sharing of trade secret data under Art. 4(7), or refuses under Art. 4(8) must notify the designated competent authority.
quote: Where the data holder refuses to share data pursuant to this Article, it shall notify the competent authority designated pursuant to Article 37.
conditional_on: Where the data holder refuses, withholds or suspends data sharing

summary: Data holders must not make the exercise of user choices or rights under Art. 4 unduly difficult, including through non-neutral choices or manipulative user interface design.
quote: Data holders shall not make the exercise of choices or rights under this Article by the user unduly difficult

summary: Data holders must not require information beyond what is necessary to verify user status and must not keep information, including log data, on the user's access beyond what is necessary.
quote: Data holders shall not keep any information, in particular log data, on the user’s access to the data requested beyond what is necessary

summary: Trade secrets are to be preserved: the data holder (or trade secret holder) must identify protected data and agree proportionate confidentiality measures with the user before disclosure.
quote: The data holder or, where they are not the same person, the trade secret holder shall identify the data which are protected as trade secrets
conditional_on: Where trade secrets are contained in the data

summary: The user must not use data obtained under a request to develop a competing connected product, share such data for that intent, or use it to derive insights about the manufacturer or data holder.
quote: The user shall not use the data obtained pursuant to a request referred to in paragraph 1 to develop a connected product that competes with the connected product from which the data originate

summary: The user must not use coercive means or abuse gaps in a data holder's technical infrastructure to obtain data.
quote: The user shall not use coercive means or abuse gaps in the technical infrastructure of a data holder

summary: Where the user is not the data subject, personal data may be made available by the data holder only where a valid legal basis under GDPR Art. 6 (and Art. 9 and ePrivacy Art. 5(3) where relevant) exists.
quote: shall be made available by the data holder to the user only where there is a valid legal basis for processing under Article 6
conditional_on: Where the user is not the data subject whose personal data is requested

summary: A data holder may use readily available non-personal data only on the basis of a contract with the user and must not use it to derive insights that could undermine the user's commercial position.
quote: A data holder shall only use any readily available data that is non-personal data on the basis of a contract with the user.

summary: Data holders must not make non-personal product data available to third parties other than for fulfilling their contract with the user, and must contractually bind third parties not to further share it.
quote: Data holders shall not make available non-personal product data to third parties for commercial or non-commercial purposes other than the fulfilment of their contract with the user.

summary: Upon request by a user or a party acting on its behalf, the data holder must make readily available data and metadata available to a third party without undue delay, free of charge to the user, in machine-readable format.
quote: Upon request by a user, or by a party acting on behalf of a user, the data holder shall make available readily available data
conditional_on: Upon request by a user or a party acting on behalf of a user

summary: A gatekeeper designated under Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 is not an eligible third party and must not solicit or incentivise users to make data available to its services, or receive such data.
quote: Any undertaking designated as a gatekeeper, pursuant to Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2022/1925, shall not be an eligible third party under this Article
conditional_on: Where the undertaking is designated as a gatekeeper

summary: Data holders must not keep information on the third party's access to the requested data beyond what is necessary for executing the request and for security and maintenance.
quote: Data holders shall not keep any information on the third party’s access to the data requested beyond what is necessary

summary: The third party must not use coercive means or abuse gaps in a data holder's technical infrastructure to obtain data.
quote: The third party shall not use coercive means or abuse gaps in the technical infrastructure of a data holder

summary: The data holder must not use readily available data to derive insights about the third party's economic situation or production methods that could undermine its commercial position, unless permission is given and can be withdrawn.
quote: A data holder shall not use any readily available data to derive insights about the economic situation, assets and production methods of, or the use by, the third party

summary: Personal data generated by the use of a product may be made available to a third party by the data holder only where a valid legal basis under GDPR Art. 6 (and Art. 9 and ePrivacy Art. 5(3) where relevant) exists.
quote: shall be made available by the data holder to the third party only where there is a valid legal basis for processing under Article 6
conditional_on: Where the user is not the data subject whose personal data is requested

summary: Trade secrets are disclosed to third parties only as strictly necessary; the data holder (or trade secret holder) must identify protected data and agree proportionate confidentiality measures with the third party.
quote: shall agree with the third party all proportionate technical and organisational measures necessary to preserve the confidentiality of the shared data
conditional_on: Where data are trade secrets

summary: Where a data holder withholds or suspends sharing with a third party under Art. 5(10) or refuses under Art. 5(11), it must notify the designated competent authority.
quote: the data holder shall notify the competent authority designated pursuant to Article 37 that it has withheld or suspended data sharing
conditional_on: Where the data holder withholds, suspends or refuses data sharing

summary: A third party receiving data at a user's request must process it only for the agreed purposes and conditions, subject to data protection law, and erase it when no longer necessary for the agreed purpose.
quote: A third party shall process the data made available to it pursuant to Article 5 only for the purposes and under the conditions agreed with the user
conditional_on: Data made available at the request of the user under Art. 5

summary: A third party must not, among other things, unduly hinder user choices, profile the user (unless necessary for the requested service), pass data to another third party or to a gatekeeper, compete with the source product, adversely affect security, or disregard agreed trade secret measures.
quote: use the data it receives to develop a product that competes with the connected product from which the accessed data originate
conditional_on: Data made available at the request of the user under Art. 5

summary: Where a data holder must make data available to a data recipient under Union law, it must agree the arrangements with the recipient on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms, transparently.
quote: it shall agree with a data recipient the arrangements for making the data available and shall do so under fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms and conditions
conditional_on: Where a data holder is obliged to make data available to a data recipient under Art. 5 or other Union or national law

summary: A data holder must not discriminate in data-making-available arrangements between comparable categories of data recipients, including its partner or linked enterprises.
quote: A data holder shall not discriminate regarding the arrangements for making data available between comparable categories of data recipients
conditional_on: Where a data holder is obliged to make data available to a data recipient

summary: On a reasoned request from a data recipient alleging discrimination, the data holder must without undue delay provide information showing there has been no discrimination.
quote: the data holder shall without undue delay provide the data recipient, upon its reasoned request, with information showing that there has been no discrimination.
conditional_on: Upon the reasoned request of a data recipient who considers the conditions discriminatory

summary: A data holder must not make data available to a data recipient, including on an exclusive basis, unless requested to do so by the user under Chapter II.
quote: A data holder shall not make data available to a data recipient, including on an exclusive basis, unless requested to do so by the user under Chapter II.

summary: Compensation agreed for making data available in business-to-business relations must be non-discriminatory and reasonable, and may include a margin.
quote: shall be non- discriminatory and reasonable
conditional_on: Business-to-business compensation for making data available

summary: Where the data recipient is an SME or not-for-profit research organisation without larger partner or linked enterprises, agreed compensation must not exceed the costs of making the data available.
quote: any compensation agreed shall not exceed the costs referred to in paragraph 2, point (a).
conditional_on: Where the data recipient is an SME or a not-for-profit research organisation without partner or linked enterprises that are not SMEs

summary: The Commission must adopt guidelines on the calculation of reasonable compensation, taking into account the advice of the EDIB.
quote: The Commission shall adopt guidelines on the calculation of reasonable compensation

summary: The data holder must give the data recipient information setting out the basis for calculating the compensation in sufficient detail to assess compliance.
quote: The data holder shall provide the data recipient with information setting out the basis for the calculation of the compensation

summary: Dispute settlement bodies must make their fees, or the mechanisms used to determine them, known to the parties before a decision is requested.
quote: Dispute settlement bodies shall make the fees, or the mechanisms used to determine the fees, known to the parties concerned

summary: Where a dispute settlement body decides in favour of the user or data recipient, the data holder must bear all fees charged and reimburse other reasonable expenses.
quote: the data holder shall bear all the fees charged by the dispute settlement body
conditional_on: Where the dispute settlement body decides in favour of the user or data recipient

summary: The Member State where a dispute settlement body is established must certify that body on request where it meets the listed conditions; Member States notify certified bodies to the Commission, which publishes a list.
quote: The Member State where the dispute settlement body is established shall, at the request of that body, certify that body
conditional_on: Upon request of the dispute settlement body

summary: A dispute settlement body must adopt its decision within 90 days of receipt of a request, in writing or on a durable medium with reasons.
quote: A dispute settlement body shall adopt its decision on a matter referred to it within 90 days of receipt of a request

summary: Dispute settlement bodies must draw up and make publicly available annual activity reports, including aggregated outcomes, average resolution times and common dispute reasons.
quote: Dispute settlement bodies shall draw up and make publicly available annual activity reports.

summary: A data holder may apply appropriate technical protection measures, including smart contracts and encryption, to prevent unauthorised access, provided they do not discriminate between recipients or hinder user rights.
quote: A data holder may apply appropriate technical protection measures, including smart contracts and encryption

summary: Users, third parties and data recipients must not alter or remove technical protection measures applied by the data holder unless the data holder agrees.
