quote: Users, third parties and data recipients shall not alter or remove such technical protection measures unless agreed by the data holder.

summary: Where a third party or data recipient has infringed the listed conduct under Art. 11(3), it must without undue delay erase the data and copies, end infringing production or use of goods, inform the user, and compensate the affected party when requested.
quote: the third party or data recipient shall comply, without undue delay, with the requests of the data holder
conditional_on: Where a third party or data recipient has engaged in conduct listed in Art. 11(3)

summary: Parties to a contract covered by Art. 13(1) may not exclude, derogate from or vary the application of the unfair-terms rules in Art. 13.
quote: shall not exclude the application of this Article

summary: Data holders that are legal persons, other than public sector bodies, must make requested data available upon a duly reasoned request in exceptional need cases.
quote: shall make them available upon a duly reasoned request
conditional_on: A public sector body, the Commission, the ECB or a Union body demonstrates an exceptional need under Art. 15.

summary: When requesting data under Art. 14, the requesting body must specify the data, demonstrate the exceptional need, explain purpose and use, set deadlines, state the legal basis, and meet the other request conditions in Art. 17(1)-(2) and (4); the Commission must develop a model request template (Art. 17(6)).
quote: When requesting data pursuant to Article 14, a public sector body, the Commission, the European Central Bank or a Union body shall:
conditional_on: Requests made under Art. 14.

summary: Public sector bodies, the Commission, the ECB and Union bodies may not make data obtained under Chapter V available for reuse under Regulation (EU) 2022/868 or Directive (EU) 2019/1024.
quote: shall not make data obtained pursuant to this Chapter available for reuse

summary: A data holder receiving a request under Chapter V must make the data available without undue delay, taking necessary technical, organisational and legal measures; it may decline or seek modification within the periods in Art. 18(2).
quote: shall make the data available to the requesting public sector body
conditional_on: Request received under Chapter V.

summary: Where personal data are requested, the data holder must anonymise them, or pseudonymise them where disclosure of personal data is required.
quote: the data holder shall properly anonymise the data
conditional_on: Requested data include personal data.

summary: A public sector body, Commission, ECB or Union body receiving data under Art. 14 must implement measures preserving confidentiality and integrity, preserve trade secrets, and is responsible for the security of data received (Art. 19(1)(b), (3), (4)).
quote: have implemented technical and organisational measures that preserve the confidentiality and integrity of the requested data
conditional_on: Data received under a request made under Art. 14.

summary: Receiving public sector bodies must erase data once no longer necessary for the stated purpose and inform the data holder and recipients of the erasure.
quote: erase the data as soon as they are no longer necessary for the stated purpose
conditional_on: Data received under a request made under Art. 14.

summary: Receiving bodies (and third parties receiving data) may not use the data for purposes incompatible with the request, use it to develop competing products, or share it with third parties for such purposes (Art. 19(1)(a), 19(2)).
quote: use the data or insights about the economic situation
conditional_on: Data received under Chapter V.

summary: Data holders other than microenterprises and small enterprises must make data needed for a public emergency available free of charge.
quote: shall make available data necessary to respond to a public emergency pursuant to Article 15(1), point (a), free of charge
conditional_on: Public emergency under Art. 15(1)(a); data holder is not a microenterprise or small enterprise.

summary: The receiving public body, Commission, ECB or Union body must provide public acknowledgement to the data holder if the holder requests it.
quote: shall provide public acknowledgement to the data holder if requested by the data holder
conditional_on: Data holder requests acknowledgement.

summary: Individuals or organisations receiving shared data for research or statistics must act on a not-for-profit basis or in a recognised public-interest mission, and may not be under significant commercial influence.
quote: shall act on a not-for-profit basis or in the context of a public-interest mission
conditional_on: Receipt of data shared under Art. 21(1).

summary: Recipients of shared data must comply with the same obligations that apply to public sector bodies under Art. 17(3) and Art. 19.
quote: shall comply with the same obligations that are applicable to the public sector bodies
conditional_on: Receipt of data shared under Art. 21(1).

summary: A public body sharing data under Art. 21(1) must notify the data holder without undue delay, stating recipient identity, purpose, period of use and protection measures.
quote: shall notify without undue delay the data holder from whom the data was received
conditional_on: Transmission or making available of data under Art. 21(1).

summary: Public sector bodies, the Commission, the ECB and Union bodies must cooperate and assist one another to implement Chapter V consistently; before requesting data from a holder in another Member State, a public sector body must notify that Member State's competent authority.
quote: shall cooperate and assist one another, to implement this Chapter in a consistent manner

summary: Data exchanged in mutual assistance may not be used in a manner incompatible with the purpose for which it was requested.
quote: shall not be used in a manner incompatible with the purpose for which they were requested
conditional_on: Data exchanged under Art. 22(1).

summary: A public sector body intending to request data from a holder in another Member State must first notify that Member State's competent authority.
quote: it shall first notify the competent authority designated pursuant to Article 37 in that Member State of that intention
conditional_on: Request to a data holder established in another Member State.

summary: The competent authority of the data holder's Member State must, without undue delay, transmit the request to the holder (with advice) or reject it on substantiated grounds.
quote: the relevant competent authority shall, without undue delay, take one of the following actions
conditional_on: Cross-border request under Art. 22(3).

summary: Providers of data processing services must not impose, and must remove, pre-commercial, commercial, technical, contractual and organisational obstacles to customers switching services.
quote: providers of data processing services shall not impose and shall remove pre-commercial, commercial, technical, contractual and organisational obstacles
conditional_on: Switching of a data processing service covering the same service type.

summary: The rights and obligations on switching must be set out in a written contract, which the provider must make available to the customer before signing in a form allowing storage and reproduction.
quote: shall make that contract available to the customer prior to signing the contract

summary: The switching contract must include at least the clauses listed in Art. 25(2)(a)-(i), including a transitional period of not more than 30 calendar days, a maximum notice period of two months, a data retrieval period of at least 30 calendar days, erasure, and switching charges per Art. 29.
quote: the contract referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall include at least the following

summary: Where the mandatory transitional period is technically unfeasible, the provider must notify the customer within 14 working days of the switching request, justify the unfeasibility and indicate an alternative period not exceeding seven months.
quote: shall notify the customer within 14 working days of the making of the switching request
conditional_on: Mandatory maximum transitional period is technically unfeasible.

summary: The provider must give the customer information on switching and porting procedures, methods and formats, and a reference to an online register of data structures and formats.
quote: The provider of data processing services shall provide the customer with:

summary: All parties involved, including destination providers, must cooperate in good faith to make switching effective and maintain service continuity.
quote: shall cooperate in good faith to make the switching process effective

summary: Providers must publish on their websites, and keep up to date, the jurisdiction of the ICT infrastructure and a description of measures against international governmental access; these websites must be listed in contracts.
quote: Providers of data processing services shall make the following information available on their websites

summary: From 12 January 2027 providers may not impose any switching charges on the customer.
quote: From 12 January 2027, providers of data processing services shall not impose any switching charges

summary: Providers may impose reduced switching charges, not exceeding their directly linked switching costs (Art. 29(3)).
quote: From 11 January 2024 to 12 January 2027, providers of data processing services may impose reduced switching charges

summary: Before contracting, providers must give prospective customers clear information on standard fees, early termination penalties and reduced switching charges, and on highly complex or costly switching services, and publish it where applicable.
quote: Before entering into a contract with a customer, providers of data processing services shall provide the prospective customer with clear information

summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts establishing a monitoring mechanism for switching charges.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 45

summary: Infrastructure-only providers must take all reasonable measures to facilitate functional equivalence; other providers must make open interfaces available free of charge to all customers; on request and absent common specifications, providers must export all exportable data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
quote: take all reasonable measures in their power to facilitate that the customer
conditional_on: Export obligation applies where no common specifications or harmonised standards are published (Art. 30(5)).

summary: Providers (other than infrastructure-only ones) must ensure compatibility with common specifications or harmonised interoperability standards, and update their online register accordingly.
applies_from: At least 12 months after the references to the common specifications or harmonised standards are published in the central Union standards repository.
quote: shall ensure compatibility with common specifications

summary: Providers must inform prospective customers of the Chapter VI obligations that do not apply to custom-built or non-production services.
quote: the provider of data processing services shall inform the prospective customer of the obligations of this Chapter that do not apply
conditional_on: Custom-built services or non-production versions for testing (Art. 31).

summary: Providers must take adequate technical, organisational and legal measures, including contracts, to prevent international governmental access to or transfer of non-personal data held in the Union where this conflicts with Union or Member State law.
quote: shall take all adequate technical, organisational and legal measures, including contracts
conditional_on: Conflict with Union law or the national law of the relevant Member State.

summary: Where an international access request applies, the provider must provide the minimum amount of data permissible in response.
quote: the provider of data processing services shall provide the minimum amount of data permissible in response to a request
conditional_on: Conditions of Art. 32(2) or 32(3) are met.

summary: Before complying with a third-country authority's request for customer data, the provider must inform the customer of the request, except where the request serves law enforcement purposes and secrecy is necessary.
quote: shall inform the customer about the existence of a request of a third-country authority to access its data before complying with that request
conditional_on: Request of a third-country authority to access customer data, before compliance.

summary: Participants in data spaces offering data or data services must comply with essential interoperability requirements (described data, machine-readable descriptions, technical access means, and tools for data sharing agreements).
quote: Participants in data spaces that offer data or data services to other participants shall comply with the following essential requirements
conditional_on: Participants offering data or data services to other participants in data spaces.

summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts further specifying the essential interoperability requirements.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts, in accordance with Article 45 of this Regulation

summary: The Commission must request European standardisation organisations to draft harmonised standards for the essential requirements (Art. 33(4)); it must consult the EDIB and stakeholders, and repeal superseded implementing acts when a standard reference is published (Art. 33(6), (7), (9)).
quote: The Commission shall, pursuant to Article 10 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012, request one or more European standardisation organisations to draft harmonised standards

summary: Interoperability requirements applied mutatis mutandis to providers of data processing services for in-parallel use: the Art. 23, 24, 25(2) and 30(2)-(5) requirements apply.
quote: shall also apply mutatis mutandis to providers of data processing services to facilitate interoperability
conditional_on: In-parallel use of data processing services.

summary: Providers may impose data egress charges for parallel use, only to pass on egress costs without exceeding them.
quote: the providers of data processing services may impose data egress charges, but only for the purpose of passing on egress costs incurred
conditional_on: Data processing service used in parallel with another service.

summary: The Commission must publish references to harmonised standards and common specifications for data processing service interoperability in a central Union standards repository, after consulting the competent authorities and stakeholders.
quote: the Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, publish the references of harmonised standards and common specifications
conditional_on: For the purpose of Art. 30(3).

summary: Vendors of applications using smart contracts for making data available (or persons deploying them for others) must ensure the smart contracts meet the robustness, safe termination, archiving, access control and consistency requirements in Art. 36(1)(a)-(e).
quote: shall ensure that those smart contracts comply with the following essential requirements
conditional_on: Smart contracts used for executing a data sharing agreement.

summary: The smart contract vendor must perform a conformity assessment and, on fulfilment, issue an EU declaration of conformity, and is responsible for compliance (Art. 36(3)).
quote: shall perform a conformity assessment with a view to fulfilling the essential requirements laid down in paragraph 1
conditional_on: Smart contracts used for executing a data sharing agreement.

summary: Each Member State must designate one or more competent authorities for application and enforcement, notify the Commission of them and their tasks, and ensure they are impartial, independent and resourced (Art. 37(1), (2), (7), (8), (9)).
quote: Each Member State shall designate one or more competent authorities to be responsible for the application and enforcement of this Regulation

summary: Member States must ensure competent authority tasks and powers are clearly defined, including promoting data literacy, handling complaints, investigations and cooperation.
quote: Member States shall ensure that the tasks and powers of the competent authorities are clearly defined and include:

summary: Competent authorities must provide a response with actions taken or intended, without undue delay, to a reasoned assistance request from another Member State (Art. 37(15)); a designated data coordinator must act as single point of contact (Art. 37(6)).
quote: A competent authority shall, upon receiving such a request, provide a response
conditional_on: Request for assistance from another Member State's competent authority.

summary: Entities making connected products available or offering services in the Union without an EU establishment must designate a legal representative in one Member State.
quote: shall designate a legal representative in one of the Member States
conditional_on: Entity not established in the Union.

summary: The legal representative must cooperate with and demonstrate to competent authorities, on request, the actions and provisions taken to ensure compliance.
quote: That legal representative shall cooperate with and comprehensively demonstrate to the competent authorities, upon request
conditional_on: Entity not established in the Union has designated a legal representative.

summary: The data coordinator must, on request, provide information to natural and legal persons for lodging complaints; the competent authority must inform the complainant of progress and outcome, and cooperate to resolve complaints.
quote: The data coordinator shall, upon request, provide all the necessary information to natural and legal persons
conditional_on: Complaint lodged under Art. 38(1).

summary: The Commission must develop and recommend non-binding model contractual terms on data access and use and non-binding standard contractual clauses for cloud computing contracts.
quote: shall develop and recommend non-binding model contractual terms on data access and use

summary: The EDIB, an expert group in which competent authorities are represented, must support consistent application of the Regulation by advising the Commission and facilitating cooperation between authorities.
quote: shall support the consistent application of this Regulation by:

summary: The power to adopt delegated acts (Art. 29(7) and Art. 33(2)) is conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period from 11 January 2024, subject to revocation by Parliament or Council.
quote: shall be conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period of time from 11 January 2024

summary: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission must consult experts designated by each Member State, and must notify each delegated act simultaneously to Parliament and Council.
quote: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State
conditional_on: Adoption of a delegated act.

summary: The Commission must carry out and report on an evaluation of the Regulation, covering in particular exceptional need, the data economy, unfair terms, switching and governmental access (Art. 49(1)); a second evaluation covers Art. 23-31, 34 and 35 (Art. 49(2)).
quote: By 12 September 2028, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Regulation

summary: Member States must provide the Commission with the information necessary for the preparation of the evaluation reports.
quote: Member States shall provide the Commission with the information necessary for the preparation of the reports

summary: Prohibits agreements or practices that grant exclusive re-use rights, or restrict re-use by others, for data held by public sector bodies, subject to the derogation in Art. 4(2) and (3).
quote: Agreements or other practices pertaining to the re-use of data held by public sector bodies containing categories of data referred to in Article 3(1) which grant exclusive rights

summary: Exclusive re-use rights may last no longer than 12 months; where a contract is concluded, its duration must match the exclusive right.
quote: The duration of an exclusive right to re-use data shall not exceed 12 months.
conditional_on: exclusive right granted under Art. 4(2)

summary: Grants of exclusive re-use rights, with reasons, must be transparent and published online in a form compliant with EU public procurement law.
quote: shall be transparent and be made publicly available online, in a form that complies with relevant Union law on public procurement.
conditional_on: exclusive right granted under Art. 4(2), (3) and (4)

summary: Pre-existing agreements that fall within the Art. 4(1) prohibition and do not meet Art. 4(2) and (3) must be terminated at the end of the contract and at latest by 24 December 2024.
quote: shall be terminated at the end of the applicable contract and in any event by 24 December 2024.
conditional_on: agreements concluded before 23 June 2022

summary: Public sector bodies competent to grant or refuse re-use must publish the re-use conditions and the request procedure via the single information point.
quote: shall make publicly available the conditions for allowing such re-use and the procedure to request the re-use via the single information point
conditional_on: competent under national law to grant or refuse re-use access

summary: Member States must ensure public sector bodies have the resources needed to comply with Art. 5.
quote: Member States shall ensure that public sector bodies are equipped with the necessary resources to comply with this Article.

summary: Conditions for re-use must be non-discriminatory, transparent, proportionate and objectively justified, and must not be used to restrict competition.
quote: Conditions for re-use shall be non-discriminatory, transparent, proportionate and objectively justified

summary: Public sector bodies must ensure the protected nature of data is preserved, in accordance with Union and national law.
quote: Public sector bodies shall, in accordance with Union and national law, ensure that the protected nature of data is preserved.

summary: Public sector bodies may require anonymisation or modification of data, or access within a secure processing environment or on premises (Art. 5(3)(a) to (c)).
quote: They may provide for the following requirements:

summary: Where access is allowed within a secure processing environment, public sector bodies must impose conditions preserving the integrity of the technical systems and may verify processing and prohibit use of results.
quote: the public sector bodies shall impose conditions that preserve the integrity of the functioning of the technical systems of the secure processing environment used.
conditional_on: re-use allowed under Art. 5(3)(b) or (c)

summary: Re-users are prohibited from re-identifying data subjects and must take technical and operational measures to prevent re-identification; re-use is conditional on a confidentiality obligation.
quote: Re-users shall be prohibited from re-identifying any data subject to whom the data relates
conditional_on: data provided under Art. 5(3)

summary: Re-users must notify the public sector body of any data breach resulting in re-identification of data subjects.
quote: to notify any data breach resulting in the re-identification of the data subjects concerned to the public sector body.
conditional_on: data provided under Art. 5(3)

summary: In case of unauthorised re-use of non-personal data, the re-user must without delay inform the legal persons whose rights may be affected.
quote: the re-user shall, without delay, where appropriate with the assistance of the public sector body, inform the legal persons whose rights and interests may be affected.
conditional_on: unauthorised re-use of non-personal data

summary: Where re-use cannot be allowed and no legal basis for transmission exists, the public sector body must make best efforts to help re-users obtain consent or permission.
quote: the public sector body shall make best efforts, in accordance with Union and national law, to provide assistance to potential re-users
conditional_on: re-use cannot be allowed under Art. 5(3) and 5(4) and no legal basis under Regulation (EU) 2016/679

summary: Public sector bodies must ensure confidential data is not disclosed as a result of allowing re-use.
quote: the public sector bodies shall ensure that the confidential data is not disclosed as a result of allowing re-use
conditional_on: data considered confidential under Union or national law

summary: A re-user intending to transfer protected non-personal data to a third country must inform the public sector body of the intention and purpose at the time of requesting re-use.
quote: it shall inform the public sector body of its intention to transfer such data and the purpose of such transfer at the time of requesting the re-use of such data.
conditional_on: transfer of non-personal data protected under Art. 3(1) to a third country

summary: Public sector bodies may transmit protected non-personal or IP-protected data to a re-user intending third-country transfer only if the re-user contractually commits to continued compliance and to the jurisdiction of the transmitting Member State courts.
quote: only if the re-user contractually commits to:
conditional_on: re-user intends to transfer to a third country not designated under Art. 5(12)

summary: Public sector bodies must, where relevant and to the extent of their capabilities, provide guidance and assistance to re-users on complying with the Art. 5(10) obligations.
quote: Public sector bodies shall, where relevant and to the extent of their capabilities, provide guidance and assistance to re-users
conditional_on: where relevant and to the extent of their capabilities

summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts establishing model contractual clauses for the Art. 5(10) obligations.
quote: the Commission may adopt implementing acts establishing model contractual clauses for complying with the obligations referred to in paragraph 10

summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts declaring that a third country's legal, supervisory and enforcement arrangements meet specified protection standards.
quote: the Commission may adopt implementing acts declaring that the legal, supervisory and enforcement arrangements of a third country
conditional_on: justified by the substantial number of requests concerning re-use of non-personal data in a third country

summary: Where a specific Union legislative act deems certain non-personal data categories highly sensitive, the Commission must adopt delegated acts laying down special conditions for transfers to third countries.
quote: the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 32 supplementing this Regulation by laying down special conditions applicable to the transfers of such data to third countries.
conditional_on: a specific Union legislative act deems the data categories highly sensitive

summary: The re-user may transfer non-personal data only to third countries for which the Art. 5(10), (12) and (13) requirements are met.
quote: may transfer the data only to those third countries for which the requirements in paragraphs 10, 12 and 13 are met.

summary: Fees charged for re-use must be transparent, non-discriminatory, proportionate, objectively justified and not restrict competition; fees must be payable online across borders and limited to necessary costs (Art. 6(2), (3), (5)).
quote: Any fees charged pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be transparent, non-discriminatory, proportionate and objectively justified and shall not restrict competition.
conditional_on: public sector bodies charge fees

summary: Where public sector bodies charge fees, they must provide incentives for non-commercial re-use, including scientific research, and for SMEs and start-ups, in accordance with State aid rules.
quote: Where public sector bodies charge fees, they shall take measures to provide incentives for the re-use of the categories of data referred to in Article 3(1) for non-commercial purposes
conditional_on: public sector bodies charge fees

summary: The list of re-user categories eligible for discounted or free re-use, and the criteria for it, must be made public.
quote: That list, together with the criteria used to establish it, shall be made public.
conditional_on: public sector bodies establish a list under Art. 6(4)

summary: Member States must lay down and publish the criteria and methodology for calculating fees; public sector bodies must publish a description of main cost categories and allocation rules.
quote: The criteria and methodology for calculating fees shall be laid down by the Member States and published.

summary: Each Member State must designate one or more competent bodies to assist public sector bodies granting or refusing re-use access, and may designate sector-specific bodies.
quote: each Member State shall designate one or more competent bodies

summary: Competent bodies must have adequate legal, financial, technical and human resources and the necessary technical knowledge.
quote: The competent bodies shall have adequate legal, financial, technical and human resources to carry out the tasks assigned to them

summary: Competent bodies must provide, where necessary, secure processing environments, guidance on data structuring, pseudonymisation and anonymisation support, consent-seeking support and assessment of re-user contractual commitments.
quote: The assistance provided for in paragraph 1 shall include, where necessary:
conditional_on: where necessary

summary: Member States must notify the Commission of the identity of the competent bodies by 24 September 2023 and of any subsequent change.
quote: Each Member State shall notify the Commission of the identity of the competent bodies designated pursuant to paragraph 1 by 24 September 2023.

summary: Member States must ensure information on Arts. 5 and 6 is available through a single information point, which they must establish or designate.
quote: Member States shall ensure that all relevant information concerning the application of Articles 5 and 6 is available and easily accessible through a single information point.

summary: The single information point must receive and transmit re-use requests and make available by electronic means a searchable asset list of data resources, including format, size and re-use conditions.
quote: The single information point shall make available by electronic means a searchable asset list

summary: The Commission must establish a European single access point offering a searchable register of data available in national single information points.
quote: The Commission shall establish a European single access point

summary: Competent public sector bodies or competent bodies must decide on re-use requests within two months of receipt, extendable by up to 30 days for exceptionally extensive requests, with notice to the applicant.
applies_from: within two months of the date of receipt of the request
quote: shall adopt a decision on the request for the re-use of the categories of data referred to in Article 3(1) within two months of the date of receipt of the request.
conditional_on: unless shorter national time limits apply

summary: Member States must lay down in national law an effective right of redress against decisions on re-use requests, including review by an impartial body.
quote: Such a right of redress shall be laid down in national law
conditional_on: directly affected by a decision under Art. 9(1)

summary: Providers of data intermediation services must comply with Art. 12 and with the notification procedure.
quote: shall comply with Article 12 and shall be subject to a notification procedure
conditional_on: provision of services listed in Art. 10

summary: A data intermediation services provider intending to provide Art. 10 services must submit a notification to the competent authority; the notification must contain the Art. 11(6) information.
quote: shall submit a notification to the competent authority for data intermediation services.
conditional_on: intends to provide Art. 10 services

summary: A provider not established in the Union but offering services in the Union must designate a legal representative in one Member State.
quote: shall designate a legal representative in one of the Member States in which those services are offered.
conditional_on: not established in the Union but offers Art. 10 services within the Union

summary: The legal representative must cooperate with and demonstrate to competent authorities, on request, the actions taken to ensure compliance.
quote: The legal representative shall cooperate with and comprehensively demonstrate to the competent authorities for data intermediation services, upon request
conditional_on: provider not established in the Union

summary: The competent authority must ensure the notification procedure is non-discriminatory and does not distort competition, and must issue a standardised declaration within one week of a complete notification on request, and confirm compliance on request.
quote: shall, within one week of a duly and fully completed notification, issue a standardised declaration

summary: The Commission must keep and regularly update a public register of all data intermediation services providers in the Union.
quote: The Commission shall keep and regularly update a public register of all data intermediation services providers providing their services in the Union.

summary: Recognised data intermediation services providers must display the common logo clearly on every online and offline publication relating to their data intermediation activities.
quote: Data intermediation services providers recognised in the Union shall display the common logo clearly on every online and offline publication
conditional_on: recognised in the Union under Art. 11(9)

summary: Changes to the notified information must be notified to the competent authority within 14 days of the change.
quote: shall notify the competent authority for data intermediation services of any changes to the information provided pursuant to paragraph 6 within 14 days of the date of the change.

summary: A provider ceasing its activities must notify the relevant competent authority within 15 days.
quote: Where a data intermediation services provider ceases its activities, it shall notify the relevant competent authority
conditional_on: provider ceases its activities

summary: A data intermediation services provider must not use the data it intermediates for purposes other than making it available to data users, and must provide such services through a separate legal person.
quote: shall not use the data for which it provides data intermediation services for purposes other than to put them at the disposal of data users

summary: Commercial terms including pricing must not depend on whether a holder or user uses other services of the provider. Also covers format conversion with opt-out (12(d)), non-discriminatory access (12(f)), continuity on insolvency (12(h)) and interoperability (12(i)).
quote: the commercial terms, including pricing, for the provision of data intermediation services to a data holder or data user shall not be dependent upon

summary: Data collected about user activity for the intermediation service may be used only for developing that service (including fraud or cybersecurity detection) and must be made available to data holders on request.
quote: shall be used only for the development of that data intermediation service

summary: Must take necessary measures for an appropriate level of security for storage, processing and transmission of non-personal data and the highest level for competitively sensitive information; must put measures in place to prevent unlawful transfer or access to non-personal data (12(j), (l)).
quote: shall take necessary measures to ensure an appropriate level of security for the storage, processing and transmission of non-personal data

summary: Must without delay inform data holders of any unauthorised transfer, access or use of the non-personal data it has shared.
quote: shall without delay inform data holders in the event of an unauthorised transfer, access or use of the non-personal data that it has shared
conditional_on: unauthorised transfer, access or use of shared non-personal data

summary: A provider offering services to data subjects must act in their best interest, informing and advising them concisely about intended data uses before they consent.
quote: shall act in the data subjects’ best interest where it facilitates the exercise of their rights
conditional_on: offering services to data subjects

summary: Where providing consent or permission tools, must specify the third-country jurisdiction of intended use and provide tools to give and withdraw consent or permission.
quote: provide data subjects with tools to both give and withdraw consent and data holders with tools to both give and withdraw permissions
conditional_on: provides tools for obtaining consent or permissions

summary: Must maintain a log record of its data intermediation activity.
quote: shall maintain a log record of the data intermediation activity.

summary: Each Member State must designate one or more competent authorities for the data intermediation notification procedure and notify the Commission of their identity by 24 September 2023.
quote: Each Member State shall designate one or more competent authorities to carry out the tasks related to the notification procedure for data intermediation services

summary: Competent authorities for data intermediation services and other relevant authorities must establish strong cooperation and exchange information.
quote: those authorities shall establish strong cooperation and exchange information as is necessary

summary: Competent authorities must monitor and supervise compliance with the Chapter III requirements, request reasoned information, notify findings giving 30 days to respond, and notify measures with a period not longer than 30 days to comply.
quote: shall monitor and supervise compliance of data intermediation services providers with the requirements of this Chapter.

summary: Competent authorities in the Member State of main establishment or legal representative and in other Member States must cooperate and assist each other, and respond to assistance requests without delay.
quote: shall cooperate and assist each other.
conditional_on: provider has its main establishment or legal representative in a Member State but provides services in other Member States

summary: A Member State that develops national data altruism policies must notify the Commission.
quote: If a Member State develops such national policies, it shall notify the Commission thereof.
conditional_on: Member State develops national data altruism policies

summary: Each competent authority for registration of data altruism organisations must keep and regularly update a public national register of recognised organisations.
quote: shall keep and regularly update a public national register of recognised data altruism organisations.

summary: The Commission must maintain a public Union register of recognised data altruism organisations and establish the common logo design by implementing acts.
quote: The Commission shall maintain a public Union register of recognised data altruism organisations for information purposes.

summary: Recognised data altruism organisations must display the common logo, accompanied by a QR code linking to the Union register, on every online and offline publication on their data altruism activities.
quote: Recognised data altruism organisations shall display the common logo clearly on every online and offline publication that relates to their data altruism activities.
conditional_on: recognised under Art. 17(2)

summary: To qualify for registration, an entity must carry out data altruism activities, be a legal person meeting general-interest objectives, operate not-for-profit and be legally independent of for-profit entities, and carry out such activities through a functionally separate structure (Art. 18(a) to (d)).
quote: In order to qualify for registration in a public national register of recognised data altruism organisations, an entity shall:
conditional_on: application for registration in a public national register

summary: An entity must comply with the rulebook referred to in Art. 22(1) within the stated period.
applies_from: at the latest 18 months after the date of entry into force of the delegated acts referred to in Art. 22(1)
quote: comply with the rulebook referred to Article 22(1), at the latest 18 months after the date of entry into force of the delegated acts referred to in that paragraph.
conditional_on: registration as a recognised data altruism organisation

summary: An entity not established in the Union that seeks registration must designate a legal representative in one Member State.
quote: shall designate a legal representative in one of the Member States in which the data altruism services are offered.
conditional_on: not established in the Union

summary: Applications for registration must contain the listed information, including legal status, sources of income, objectives of general interest and nature of the data.
quote: Applications for registration referred to in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 shall contain the following information:
conditional_on: application under Art. 19(1), (2) or (3)

summary: Once the entity is found compliant, the competent authority must register it within 12 weeks of receiving the application; the registration is valid in all Member States.
applies_from: within 12 weeks after the receipt of the application for registration
quote: it shall register the entity in the public national register of recognised data altruism organisations within 12 weeks after the receipt of the application for registration.
conditional_on: entity has submitted all information and complies with Art. 18

summary: Specified registration information (name, legal status, website, objectives and contact details) must be published in the national register.
quote: shall be published in the relevant public national register of recognised data altruism organisations.

summary: A recognised organisation must notify the competent authority of any change to the registration information within 14 days.
quote: shall notify the relevant competent authority for the registration of data altruism organisations of any changes to the information provided pursuant to paragraph 4 within 14 days of the date of the change.

summary: Must keep full and accurate records of persons given access to data, processing dates or duration, declared purposes and fees paid.
quote: shall keep full and accurate records concerning:

summary: Must draw up and transmit an annual activity report to the competent authority with the listed contents.
quote: shall draw up and transmit to the relevant competent authority for the registration of data altruism organisations an annual activity report

summary: Must inform data subjects or data holders, before any processing, in a clear and comprehensible manner of the objectives and purposes and of any third-country processing.
quote: shall inform data subjects or data holders prior to any processing of their data in a clear and easily comprehensible manner
conditional_on: prior to any processing of their data

summary: Must not use the data for objectives other than those of general interest for which permission was given, and must not use misleading marketing practices to solicit data.
quote: The recognised data altruism organisation shall not use the data for other objectives than those of general interest

summary: Must provide tools for obtaining consent or permissions and for easy withdrawal of consent or permission.
quote: shall provide tools for obtaining consent from data subjects or permissions to process data made available by data holders.

summary: Must take measures to ensure an appropriate level of security for storage and processing of non-personal data collected on the basis of data altruism.
quote: shall take measures to ensure an appropriate level of security for the storage and processing of non-personal data

summary: Must without delay inform data holders of any unauthorised transfer, access or use of the non-personal data it has shared.
quote: shall, without delay, inform data holders in the event of any unauthorised transfer, access or use of the non-personal data that it has shared.
conditional_on: unauthorised transfer, access or use of shared non-personal data

summary: Where facilitating third-party processing, must specify the third-country jurisdiction in which the data use is intended to take place.
quote: it shall, where relevant, specify the third-country jurisdiction in which the data use is intended to take place.
conditional_on: facilitates data processing by third parties

summary: The Commission must adopt delegated acts establishing a rulebook on information, technical and security requirements, communication roadmaps and interoperability recommendations for data altruism organisations.
quote: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 32, supplementing this Regulation by establishing a rulebook

summary: The rulebook must be prepared in close cooperation with data altruism organisations and relevant stakeholders.
quote: The rulebook referred to in paragraph 1 shall be prepared in close cooperation with data altruism organisations and relevant stakeholders.

summary: Each Member State must designate one or more competent authorities for its national register of recognised data altruism organisations and notify the Commission by 24 September 2023.
quote: Each Member State shall designate one or more competent authorities responsible for its public national register of recognised data altruism organisations.

summary: Registration authorities must undertake tasks in cooperation with the relevant data protection authority and sectoral authorities.
quote: shall undertake its tasks in cooperation with the relevant data protection authority

summary: Registration authorities must monitor and supervise compliance of recognised organisations with the Chapter IV requirements, request reasoned information, and notify findings giving 30 days to respond.
quote: shall monitor and supervise compliance of recognised data altruism organisations with the requirements laid down in this Chapter.

summary: Registration authorities in the Member State of main establishment or legal representative and in other Member States must cooperate and assist each other.
quote: shall cooperate and assist each other.
conditional_on: organisation has main establishment or legal representative in a Member State but is active in other Member States

summary: The Commission must adopt implementing acts establishing and developing a European data altruism consent form, after consulting the European Data Protection Board.
quote: the Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing and developing a European data altruism consent form

summary: Competent authorities for data intermediation services and for data altruism registration must be legally distinct from and functionally independent of providers, and must act impartially, transparently, consistently, reliably and timely.
quote: shall be legally distinct from, and functionally independent of, any data intermediation services provider or recognised data altruism organisation.

summary: Top-level management and personnel of competent authorities must not be designers, manufacturers, suppliers, owners, users or maintainers of services they evaluate, nor engage in conflicting activities (Art. 26(3) and (4)).
quote: shall not be the designer, manufacturer, supplier, installer, purchaser, owner, user or maintainer of the services which they evaluate

summary: Competent authorities must have adequate financial and human resources, including technical knowledge.
quote: shall have at their disposal the adequate financial and human resources to carry out the tasks assigned to them

summary: On reasoned request and without delay, competent authorities must provide the Commission and other competent authorities with the information needed for their tasks, keeping confidential information confidential.
quote: shall provide the Commission and competent authorities for data intermediation services and the competent authorities
conditional_on: reasoned request from the Commission or another competent authority

summary: Competent authorities must inform the complainant of the progress and outcome of proceedings and of available judicial remedies.
quote: shall inform the complainant of:
conditional_on: complaint lodged under Art. 27(1)

summary: The Commission must establish the European Data Innovation Board as an expert group with at least three subgroups.
quote: The Commission shall establish a European Data Innovation Board in the form of an expert group

summary: The European Data Innovation Board must carry out the tasks listed in Art. 30 (consistent practice, guidelines, standards, data spaces, harmonised re-use conditions and international transfers).
quote: The European Data Innovation Board shall have the following tasks:

summary: Public sector bodies, re-users, intermediation providers and recognised altruism organisations must take all reasonable technical, legal and organisational measures to prevent international transfer or governmental access to non-personal data where this would conflict with Union or Member State law.
quote: shall take all reasonable technical, legal and organisational measures, including contractual arrangements, in order to prevent international transfer or governmental access to non-personal data held in the Union
conditional_on: transfer or access would create a conflict with Union law or national law

summary: Where the Art. 31(2) or (3) conditions are met, must provide the minimum amount of data permissible in response to a request.
quote: shall provide the minimum amount of data permissible in response to a request
conditional_on: Art. 31(2) or (3) conditions are met

summary: Must inform the data holder of a third-country administrative authority request for its data before complying, except for law-enforcement requests where secrecy is necessary.
quote: shall inform the data holder about the existence of a request of a third-country administrative authority to access its data before complying with that request
conditional_on: request from a third-country administrative authority, except law-enforcement requests while necessary

summary: Before adopting a delegated act the Commission must consult experts designated by each Member State, and must notify each delegated act simultaneously to the European Parliament and the Council.
quote: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State

summary: Member States must notify the Commission of their penalty rules and measures by 24 September 2023, and of any later amendment.
quote: Member States shall, by 24 September 2023, notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures

summary: The Commission must evaluate the Regulation and submit a report to Parliament, the Council and the EESC, with legislative proposals where necessary.
quote: By 24 September 2025, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Regulation and submit a report

summary: Member States must provide the Commission with the information necessary for the evaluation report.
quote: Member States shall provide the Commission with the information necessary for the preparation of that report.

summary: Providers of data intermediation services already operating on 23 June 2022 must comply with the Chapter III obligations by 24 September 2025.
quote: shall comply with the obligations set out in Chapter III by 24 September 2025.
conditional_on: provided Art. 10 services on 23 June 2022

summary: Commission shall adopt delegated acts under Art. 97 to specify high-risk AI systems, requirements or obligations that may be limited, conditions and scope of limitation.
quote: By 2 August 2027, the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97
conditional_on: Where Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I Section A provides an equivalent or higher level of protection

summary: Providers and deployers shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff and other persons operating AI systems on their behalf; no guarantee of any specific literacy level is required.
quote: Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy

summary: Commission and Member States shall support and facilitate provider and deployer AI literacy efforts, in particular SMEs; Commission shall publish practical examples on the single information platform.
quote: the Commission shall publish practical examples of how to comply with that obligation

summary: The Board shall adopt recommendations, taking into account European competence frameworks, to support AI literacy promotion, including common objectives.
quote: The Board shall adopt recommendations

summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction, subject to conditions (a) to (e), including deletion once bias is corrected or retention ends.
quote: providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data
conditional_on: Strictly necessary for bias detection and correction; other data (including synthetic or anonymised) cannot effectively achieve it; conditions in Art. 4a(1)(a) to (e) met

summary: Records of processing activities under GDPR, EUDPR and LED must include the reasons why processing special categories of personal data was strictly necessary for bias detection and correction.
quote: include the reasons why the processing of special categories of personal data was strictly necessary
conditional_on: Where special categories of personal data are processed under Art. 4a(1)

summary: Providers and deployers of other AI systems and models, and deployers of high-risk AI systems, may exceptionally process special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction under the Art. 4a(1) conditions; the paragraph creates no obligation to conduct such bias detection.
quote: Providers and deployers of other AI systems and models and deployers of high-risk AI systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data
conditional_on: Strictly necessary; likely to affect health and safety, impact fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination; Art. 4a(1) conditions and safeguards applied

summary: Prohibits placing on the market, putting into service or use of AI systems generating or manipulating realistic intimate images or sexually explicit depictions of identifiable persons without consent (ba), and AI systems generating child sexual abuse material or material under Directive 2011/93/EU (bb), except where a without-right defence applies; for providers only where such generation is intended or reasonably foreseeable and safeguards are lacking, for deployers only where used for that purpose.
quote: the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that generates or manipulates realistic images
conditional_on: Provider liability limited to intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without reasonable and adequate safeguards (Art. 5(1a)(a)); deployer use only where used for that purpose (Art. 5(1a)(b))

summary: High-risk AI systems using training of AI models must be developed on training, validation and testing data sets meeting the quality criteria of Art. 10(2) to (4) and Art. 4a(1); Art. 10(6) applies the same to testing data sets for systems not using model training.
quote: High-risk AI systems which make use of techniques involving the training of AI models with data shall be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets
conditional_on: Where such data sets are used

summary: Technical documentation must demonstrate compliance and contain at least the elements of Annex IV; SMEs and SMCs may provide the elements in a simplified manner using the Commission form.
quote: It shall contain, at a minimum, the elements set out in Annex IV.
conditional_on: SMEs and SMCs may opt for the simplified manner

summary: Commission shall establish a simplified technical documentation form targeted at SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs.
quote: the Commission shall establish a simplified technical documentation form

summary: Notified bodies shall accept the simplified technical documentation form for the purposes of conformity assessment.
quote: Notified bodies shall accept the form for the purposes of the conformity assessment.
conditional_on: Where an SME, start-up or SMC uses the simplified form

summary: Implementation of quality management aspects must be proportionate to provider size; providers must still respect the required degree of rigour and level of protection.
quote: Providers shall, in any event, respect the degree of rigour and the level of protection required

summary: Initial provider that is no longer treated as provider must closely cooperate with new providers, provide technical documentation, known limitations and targeted technical access; not applicable where initial provider has specified the system is not to become high-risk.
quote: That initial provider shall closely cooperate with new providers
conditional_on: Where the circumstances in Art. 25(1) occur; not applicable where initial provider clearly excluded high-risk change

summary: Provider of a high-risk AI system and third-party suppliers of AI models, tools, services, components or processes must specify by written agreement the necessary information, capabilities, technical access and assistance; not applicable to free and open-source tools made publicly accessible.
quote: shall, by written agreement, specify the necessary information, capabilities, technical access and other assistance
conditional_on: Not applicable to third parties making accessible to the public tools, services, processes or components, other than general-purpose AI models, under a free and open-source licence

summary: When conducting the fundamental rights impact assessment, the deployer may cross-reference or include relevant parts of an existing data protection impact assessment.
quote: the deployer may, when conducting the fundamental rights impact assessment referred to in paragraph 1
conditional_on: Where the obligations of Art. 27(1) are already met through a DPIA under GDPR Art. 35 or LED Art. 27

summary: AI Office shall develop a template questionnaire, possibly through an automated tool, to help deployers comply with Art. 27 in a simplified manner.
quote: The AI Office shall develop a template for a questionnaire

summary: Notifying authorities for AI systems under Annex I Section A shall ensure that conformity assessment bodies can submit a single application and undergo a unified assessment procedure; the notifying authority under Annex I legislation is also the notifying authority for this procedure unless the Member State designates another.
quote: shall ensure that the conformity assessment body that applies for designation
conditional_on: Where the relevant Union harmonisation legislation provides for such a single application and unified procedure

summary: Notified bodies undergoing the unified assessment procedure shall submit the single application to the notifying authority designated under the Annex I legislation.
quote: shall submit the single application for assessment to the notifying authority
conditional_on: Notified bodies designated under Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I Section A that undergo the unified assessment procedure

summary: Notified body shall update the documentation referred to in Art. 29(2) and (3) whenever relevant changes occur, to enable monitoring of continuous compliance with Art. 31.
quote: The notified body shall update the documentation referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3
conditional_on: Whenever relevant changes occur

summary: Notifying authorities shall notify the Commission and other Member States, using the Commission electronic notification tool, of each conformity assessment body, based on the list in Annex XIV.
quote: Notifying authorities shall notify the Commission and the other Member States

summary: Commission may amend Annex XIV by delegated act, adding, withdrawing or moving codes, categories or types of AI systems in light of technical progress or new scientific evidence.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 in order to amend Annex XIV

summary: Commission shall request European standardisation organisations, without undue delay, to develop standardisation deliverables including harmonised standards to facilitate joint compliance and presumption of conformity for Chapter III Sections 2 and 3 and Annex I legislation.
quote: The Commission shall request, in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012

summary: Provider of a high-risk AI system covered by Annex I Section A shall follow the relevant conformity assessment procedure under that legislation, including the Section 2 requirements and the quality management system assessment.
quote: the provider of the system shall follow the relevant conformity assessment procedure as required in accordance with the relevant Union harmonisation legislation
conditional_on: Where the high-risk AI system is covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A

summary: Notified bodies notified under Annex I Section A legislation shall apply for designation under Section 4 of Chapter III by 28 January 2028, without prejudice to Art. 28.
quote: shall apply for designation in accordance with Section 4 of this Chapter by 28 January 2028
conditional_on: Without prejudice to Article 28

summary: Commission shall encourage and facilitate codes of practice at Union level on detection, marking and labelling of artificially generated content, assess their adequacy, and may adopt an implementing act if a code is deemed inadequate.
quote: The Commission shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level

summary: Commission and Board shall regularly monitor and evaluate the achievement of codes of practice objectives; Commission shall assess whether codes cover Art. 53 and 55 obligations and publish its assessment.
quote: The Commission and the Board shall regularly monitor and evaluate the achievement of the objectives of the codes of practice

summary: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities establish at least one national AI regulatory sandbox, which shall be operational by 2 August 2027, possibly jointly with other Member States.
quote: which shall be operational by 2 August 2027

summary: Competent authorities shall associate data protection and other relevant authorities with sandbox operation; coordinate and cooperate within the Board, including the EDPS and AI Office; sandboxes shall provide a controlled environment; AI Office may establish a Union-level sandbox with priority access for SMEs and SMCs; EDPS may establish a sandbox for Union institutions.
quote: National competent authorities shall ensure that, to the extent the innovative AI systems involve the processing of personal data

summary: Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying detailed arrangements for establishment, development, implementation, operation, governance and supervision of AI regulatory sandboxes, including common principles and governance rules.
provision: Art. 1(23)(a) (replacing introductory part of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Art. 58(1), first subparagraph)
quote: the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying the detailed arrangements

summary: Providers or prospective providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III or covered by Annex I Section A may conduct real-world testing outside sandboxes under Art. 60 and its plan, at any time before placing on the market, alone or with deployers, without prejudice to Art. 5.
quote: Testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes may be conducted by providers or prospective providers
conditional_on: Without prejudice to the prohibitions under Article 5; in accordance with the real-world testing plan

summary: Member States may allow real-world testing outside sandboxes of AI-enabled products covered by Annex I Section B legislation, to assess and verify conformity with Articles 8 to 15.
quote: Member States may allow, in accordance with this Article, the testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes
conditional_on: Member States choose to allow such testing

summary: Member States that allow such testing shall adopt real-world testing frameworks, notify each framework to the Commission before implementation, cooperate closely and remove practical obstacles, and ensure frameworks include governance and accountability arrangements and protection of health, safety and fundamental rights.
quote: shall, individually or jointly, adopt frameworks for real-world testing
conditional_on: Member States that choose to allow testing

summary: Real-world testing under the Annex I Section B frameworks requires a mandatory real-world testing plan agreed between the provider and the national competent authority, and must comply with the applicable Section B legislation.
quote: a mandatory real-world testing plan to be agreed between the provider or prospective provider
conditional_on: Testing under a Member State framework adopted under Art. 60a

summary: SMEs, including start-ups, may comply with certain elements of the Art. 17 quality management system in a simplified manner, provided they have no partner or linked enterprises.
quote: SMEs, including start-ups, may comply with certain elements of the quality management system required by Article 17 in a simplified manner
conditional_on: Provided they do not have partner enterprises or linked enterprises within the meaning of Recommendation 2003/361/EC

summary: Commission shall develop guidelines on which elements of the quality management system may be complied with in a simplified manner for SMEs.
quote: the Commission shall develop guidelines on the elements of the quality management system

summary: AI Office shall be allocated adequate resources to perform its duties and exercise its powers under the Regulation, without prejudice to the budgetary procedure.
quote: the AI Office shall be allocated adequate resources to effectively perform its duties
conditional_on: Without prejudice to the budgetary procedure

summary: Member States may be required to pay fees to experts of the scientific panel for advice and support, at a rate equivalent to Commission remuneration.
quote: The Member States may be required to pay fees for the advice and support provided by the experts
conditional_on: Where Member States call upon the scientific panel's expertise

summary: National competent authorities may provide guidance and advice on implementation, in particular to SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs, taking into account Board and Commission guidance.
quote: National competent authorities may provide guidance and advice on the implementation of this Regulation

summary: Where guidance concerns AI systems in areas covered by other Union law, the national competent authorities under that Union law shall be consulted, as appropriate.
quote: the national competent authorities under that Union law shall be consulted, as appropriate
conditional_on: Where guidance on an AI system in areas covered by other Union law is intended

summary: The post-market monitoring system of high-risk AI system providers shall be based on a post-market monitoring plan forming part of the Annex IV technical documentation.
provision: Art. 1(30) (replacing Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Art. 72(3), first and second sentences)
quote: The post-market monitoring system shall be based on a post-market monitoring plan.

summary: Commission, taking utmost account of the Board opinion, shall adopt guidance including a template on the post-market monitoring plan.
quote: The Commission, taking utmost account of the opinion of the Board, shall adopt guidance, including a template, on the post-market monitoring plan by 2 September 2027.

summary: AI Office is exclusively competent for supervision and enforcement regarding AI systems based on general-purpose AI models of the same undertaking and AI systems in or integrated into very large online platforms or search engines; it conducts conformity assessments and tests of certain high-risk systems, notifies the national market surveillance authority before restricting or withdrawing a system, and transmits incident information to the national authority.
quote: The AI Office shall be exclusively competent for the supervision and enforcement of the obligations under this Regulation
conditional_on: Subject to the exceptions in Art. 75(1)(a)(i) to (iv)

summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems under AI Office competence shall report serious incidents to the AI Office, with Art. 73(2) to (9) applying mutatis mutandis.
quote: providers of high-risk AI systems subject to the competence of the AI Office pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article shall report any serious incidents to the AI Office
conditional_on: High-risk AI systems subject to AI Office competence under Art. 75(1)

summary: Authorities involved in applying the Regulation shall cooperate actively with the AI Office and provide necessary assistance for its powers, including inspections in Member States.
quote: The authorities involved in the application of this Regulation shall cooperate actively with the AI Office

summary: Provider of a high-risk AI system that applied for third-party conformity assessment by the Commission shall pay fees and, for costs of services entrusted to notified bodies, pay the notified body directly.
quote: The provider shall pay the costs related to the services entrusted by the Commission to the notified bodies
conditional_on: Where the provider has applied for a third-party conformity assessment under Art. 75(1e)

summary: A market surveillance authority with well-founded reasons to suspect an infringement shall cooperate actively with the AI Office and provide assistance for its powers when it requests assessment of a matter.
quote: the market surveillance authority shall cooperate actively and provide the AI Office the necessary assistance
conditional_on: Where the market surveillance authority requests the AI Office to assess a matter

summary: AI Office shall take utmost account of a market surveillance authority request and inform the single point of contact of its intention to exercise powers under Art. 75a or its reasons for not exercising them; if it exercises them it shall periodically inform the single point of contact of major developments.
applies_from: no later than four months following receipt of the request
quote: The AI Office shall, without undue delay and in any event no later than four months following receipt of the request, inform the single point of contact
conditional_on: Where a market surveillance authority submits a request under Art. 75(2a)

summary: When requesting information, the AI Office shall state the legal basis and purpose, specify the information required and set a period; for voluntary replies it shall indicate that information must be correct and not misleading. It shall notify the operator when starting an investigation, inform the provider before inspections, and use information collected only for the Regulation's purposes.
quote: When requesting information, the AI Office shall state the legal basis and the purpose of the request
conditional_on: Where the AI Office exercises its powers under Art. 75a

summary: Where the AI Office considers that an operator's commitments cannot ensure effective compliance, it shall reject them in a reasoned decision when concluding proceedings.
quote: it shall reject those commitments in a reasoned decision when concluding the proceedings
conditional_on: Where the operator has offered commitments under Art. 75b

summary: AI Office shall adopt a decision establishing non-compliance, communicate preliminary findings to the operator before deciding, order measures within a reasonable period where relevant, and close proceedings by decision where no grounds exist. Penalty provisions in Art. 75c(4) to (8) are excluded.
quote: Before adopting a decision pursuant to paragraph 1, the AI Office shall communicate its preliminary findings to the operator concerned
conditional_on: Where the AI Office finds non-compliance

summary: AI Office shall fully respect the rights of defence and access to the file of operators in proceedings, and shall publish the decisions it adopts under Art. 75b and 75c, stating the parties and main content.
quote: The rights of defence and of access to the file of operators falling within the scope of Article 75(1) shall be fully respected in proceedings.

summary: Market surveillance authorities shall grant public authorities protecting fundamental rights access to information or documentation held under the Regulation, including by requesting it from providers or deployers where necessary and without undue delay.
quote: the market surveillance authority shall grant the relevant public authority or body referred to in paragraph 1 access
conditional_on: Where access is necessary for the public authority to fulfil its mandate

summary: Market surveillance authorities and public authorities protecting fundamental rights shall cooperate closely and provide mutual assistance, including exchange of information, for coherent application of the Regulation.
quote: Market surveillance authorities and public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 shall cooperate closely

summary: AI Office and Member States shall take into account the specific interests and needs of SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs when encouraging and facilitating codes of conduct.
quote: The AI Office and the Member States shall take into account the specific interests and needs of SMEs

summary: Commission shall publish guidelines on practical implementation of Art. 8(2), 9(10) and 17(3) for complementarity and proportionality with Annex I legislation, involving the Board and paying attention to SMEs, SMCs, local public authorities and affected sectors.
quote: such guidelines shall be published by 1 August 2027

summary: Power to adopt delegated acts under Art. 2(13) and Art. 30(2) is conferred on the Commission for five years, tacitly extendable, revocable by Parliament or Council.
quote: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 2(13) and Article 30(2) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 27 July 2026

summary: Commission shall draw up a report on the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period.
quote: The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period

summary: Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended for use by public authorities shall take the necessary steps to comply with the Regulation, for systems placed on the market or put into service before the application date of Chapter III and only if significantly changed.
quote: the providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities shall take the necessary steps to comply
conditional_on: Systems placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III, subject to significant changes in design

summary: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content and placed on the market before 2 August 2026 shall take the necessary steps to comply with Art. 50(2).
quote: shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026
conditional_on: Systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026

summary: Conformity assessment bodies shall use the lists of codes, categories and types of AI systems in Annex XIV when specifying the types of AI systems in the application for designation under Art. 29.
quote: Conformity assessment bodies shall use the lists of codes, categories and corresponding types of AI systems set out in this Annex

summary: Under amended Regulation (EU) 2018/1139, when the Commission adopts implementing or delegated acts on AI safety components (Arts 27, 31, 32, 36, 39, 50 and 53), it shall take into account the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
quote: the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account.
conditional_on: When adopting implementing or delegated acts concerning AI systems that are safety components

summary: Commission shall adopt delegated acts under Art. 47 to amend Annex III of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 by adding health and safety requirements for high-risk AI systems that are safety components in machinery or are machinery, reflecting Chapter III, Section 2 and Articles 17, 19, 72 and 73 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
quote: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 47 of this Regulation to amend Annex III
conditional_on: Applies to AI systems classified as high-risk under Art. 6(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 due to being a safety component in a product covered by Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

summary: Data holder (coded data_controller) refusing user or third-party access on trade-secret grounds must substantiate the refusal in writing and notify the competent authority; new ground includes risk of disclosure to entities in third countries with weaker protection
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Where the data holder refuses to share data pursuant to this paragraph, it shall notify the competent authority designated pursuant to Article 37.

summary: Data holders that are legal persons (other than public sector bodies) must make data and metadata available on a duly reasoned request of a public sector body, the Commission, the ECB or a Union body showing an exceptional need linked to a public emergency (Arts. 14-15 replaced by Art. 15a)
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Upon such duly reasoned request, data holders shall make the data and metadata available to the requesting public sector body, the Commission, the European Central Bank or Union body.
conditional_on: Public emergency; for mitigation/recovery requests only non-personal data and not from micro or small enterprises
