summary: Data for responding to a public emergency must be supplied free of charge (micro and small enterprises may claim compensation); data for mitigation or recovery give a right to fair compensation (costs plus reasonable margin), except for official statistics where national law bars purchase
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Data holders shall make available data necessary to respond to a public emergency pursuant to Article 15a(2) free of charge.

summary: Requesting bodies must demonstrate the Art. 15a conditions, explain purpose, intended use, duration and any personal-data processing, and keep requests proportionate in granularity, volume and frequency
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: When requesting data pursuant to Article 15a, a public sector body, the Commission, the European Central Bank or a Union body shall:

summary: Receiving bodies may require disclosure of trade secrets only where strictly necessary and must protect their confidentiality; they must notify the data holder before passing data to research organisations or statistical bodies
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
provision: Art. 1(11) and (13), Data Act Arts. 19(3) and 21(5)
quote: Disclosure of trade secrets to a public sector body, the Commission, the European Central Bank or a Union body shall be required only to the extent that it is strictly necessary to achieve the purpose of a request under Article 15a.

summary: Lighter regime for legacy cloud contracts: custom-made data processing services and services of SME/SMC providers under contracts concluded by 12 September 2025 are exempt from Chapter VI (except Art. 29) and Art. 34, need not be renegotiated, but terms contrary to Art. 29(1)-(3) on switching charges are void; fixed-term contracts may include proportionate early termination penalties
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Any contractual provision contained in that contract that is contrary to Article 29(1), (2), or (3) shall be considered null and void.

summary: Providers of data processing services, public sector bodies and re-users of protected data, data intermediation services providers and recognised data altruism organisations must take technical, organisational and legal measures to prevent unlawful third-country governmental access to or transfer of non-personal data held in the Union
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: shall take all adequate technical, organisational and legal measures, including contracts, in order to prevent international and third-country governmental access and transfer of non-personal data held in the Union

summary: Before complying with a third-country authority request, the same entities must provide the minimum data permissible and inform the natural or legal person whose rights may be affected, except for law-enforcement requests while needed
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: shall inform the natural or legal person whose rights and interests might be affected about the existence of a request of a third-country authority to access its data before complying with that request

summary: Voluntary registration as a recognised data intermediation services provider requires: data used only to put at disposal of data users; service metadata used only for service development; extra tools only on request; conditions for value-added services (non-micro/small); acting in data subjects' best interest
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: In order to qualify for registration in the public Union register referred to in Article 32a paragraph 1 point (a), a data intermediation services provider shall meet all of the following requirements:

summary: Registration as a recognised data altruism organisation requires carrying out data altruism, being a legal person pursuing general-interest objectives, operating not-for-profit and independently of for-profit entities, and functional separation
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: In order to qualify for registration in the public Union register referred to in Art. 32a paragraph 1 point (b), a data altruism organisation shall meet all of the following requirements:

summary: Data intermediation services providers and data altruism organisations with no main establishment in the Union must designate a legal representative in a Member State, which determines jurisdiction
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Data intermediation services providers and data altruism organisations that have no main establishment in the Union shall designate a legal representative in one of the Member States.
conditional_on: Applying for registration in the public Union register

summary: Registered data intermediation services providers and data altruism organisations must notify the competent authority of changes to their information or cessation of activities
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Registered entities shall notify the competent authority of any subsequent changes to the information as provided during the application process

summary: Recognised data altruism organisations must inform data subjects or data holders before processing of the general-interest objectives, purposes, and location of any third-country processing, and specify the third country where they facilitate third-party use
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Recognised data altruism organisations shall inform data subjects or data holders prior to any processing of their data in a clear and easily comprehensible manner of the following:

summary: Recognised data altruism organisations may not use data for other objectives than those permitted and may not use misleading marketing to solicit data
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: The recognised data altruism organisation shall not use misleading marketing practices to solicit the provision of data.

summary: Recognised data altruism organisations must provide electronic means to give and withdraw consent or permission
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Recognised data altruism organisations shall provide electronic means for obtaining consent from data subjects or permissions to process data made available by data holders as well as for their withdrawal.

summary: Recognised data altruism organisations must inform data holders without delay of any unauthorised transfer, access or use of shared non-personal data
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Recognised data altruism organisations shall, without delay, inform data holders in the event of any unauthorised transfer, access or use of the non-personal data that it has shared.

summary: Commission keeps public Union registers of recognised data intermediation services providers and data altruism organisations; Member States designate independent competent authorities that decide on registration within 12 weeks and monitor compliance
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: The Commission shall keep and regularly update public Union registers of:

summary: Member States may not impose data localisation requirements for non-personal data unless justified on public-security grounds and proportionate, or based on Union law
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Data localisation requirements for non-personal data shall be prohibited, unless they are justified on grounds of public security in compliance with the principle of proportionality or laid down on the basis of Union law.

summary: Member States must immediately communicate to the Commission any draft act introducing or changing a data localisation requirement, under the Directive (EU) 2015/1535 procedure
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Member States shall immediately communicate to the Commission any draft act which introduces a new data localisation requirement or makes changes to an existing data localisation requirement

summary: Conditions for re-use of public sector data must be non-discriminatory, transparent, proportionate and objectively justified; a public sector body re-using its own data commercially must apply the same charges and conditions as to other re-users
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Any applicable conditions for the re-use of data or documents shall be non-discriminatory, transparent, proportionate and objectively justified

summary: Exclusive re-use arrangements are prohibited, except where necessary for a service of general interest (transparent, reviewed every three years) or digitisation of cultural resources; exclusive rights over protected data are limited to 12 months; arrangements restricting availability must be published two months in advance
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: which have as their objective or effect to grant exclusive rights or to restrict the availability of data or documents for re-use by entities other than the parties to such agreements, arrangements or practices, shall be prohibited.

summary: Charges for re-use must be transparent, non-discriminatory and proportionate; standard charges and their calculation basis published in advance; online cross-border payment possible; applicants informed of means of redress
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Any charges set out under Section 2 or Section 3 shall be transparent, non-discriminatory, proportionate and objectively justified and shall not restrict competition.

summary: Public sector bodies must process re-use requests for open government data (within 20 working days, extendable by 20, where no other time limits exist) and give grounds for refusal; Member States set practical arrangements and review by an impartial body
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Public sector bodies shall, through electronic means where possible and appropriate, process requests for re-use

summary: Public sector bodies and public undertakings must make data available in open, machine-readable formats with metadata where possible; dynamic data via APIs immediately after collection; high-value datasets machine-readable via APIs and bulk download
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Public sector bodies shall make dynamic data available for re-use immediately after collection, via suitable APIs and, where relevant, as a bulk download.

summary: Re-use of open government data is free of charge or limited to marginal costs (exceptions: revenue-dependent bodies, libraries/museums/archives, public undertakings, which may charge up to cost plus reasonable return); high-value datasets and research data free of charge
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: The re-use of data or documents within the scope of this Section shall be free of charge.

summary: Re-use conditions must be objective, proportionate and non-discriminatory; standard licences in digital format; Member States provide asset lists, portals and a single point of access
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: The re-use of data or documents shall not be subject to conditions, unless such conditions are objective, proportionate, non-discriminatory and justified on grounds of a public interest objective.

summary: Member States must adopt open access policies for publicly funded research data; such data already published in repositories become re-usable for commercial or non-commercial purposes
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Member States shall support the availability of research data by adopting national policies and relevant actions aiming at making publicly funded research data openly available

summary: Commission must adopt implementing acts listing specific high-value datasets (free of charge, machine-readable, via APIs, bulk download), after consultations and an impact assessment with cost-benefit analysis
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: The Commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down a list of specific high-value datasets belonging to the categories set out in Annex I

summary: Public sector bodies competent for protected data (commercial or statistical confidentiality, third-party IP, personal data) must publish re-use conditions and procedures, preserve the protected nature (anonymisation, secure processing environments), and may verify and prohibit results
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: shall make publicly available the conditions for allowing such re-use and the procedure to request the re-use via the single information point referred to in Article 32aa

summary: Re-users of protected data (coded data_controller) must accept a confidentiality obligation, inform affected persons of unauthorised re-use of non-personal data, notify intended third-country transfers, and contractually commit to IP and confidentiality obligations and EU jurisdiction for transfers outside designated countries
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Where a re-user intends to transfer certain categories of protected data that are non-personal to a third country, it shall inform the public sector body of its intention to transfer such data and the purpose of such transfer at the time of requesting the re-use of the data.

summary: Fees for protected-data re-use must be cost-based, with incentives for non-commercial use, start-ups, SMEs and SMCs; Member States publish fee criteria and methodology
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: The criteria and methodology for calculating fees shall be laid down by the Member States and published.

summary: Member States must designate competent bodies to assist public sector bodies (covering all sectors) and a single information point with a searchable asset list; the Commission establishes a European single access point
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Each Member State shall designate a single information point.

summary: Decisions on requests to re-use protected data within two months (extendable by up to 30 days), with an effective right of redress before an impartial body
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: Any natural or legal person directly affected by a decision as referred to in paragraph 1 shall have an effective right of redress in the Member State where the relevant body is located.

summary: Competent authorities must handle complaints, including against recognised data intermediation services providers and data altruism organisations, and inform complainants of progress and remedies; the data coordinator assists complainants
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: The competent authority with which the complaint has been lodged shall inform the complainant, in accordance with national law, of:

summary: Establishes the European Data Innovation Board (Member States, competent authorities, EDPB, EDPS, ENISA, SME Envoy), chaired by the Commission, to advise on consistent enforcement
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: The European Data Innovation Board is established as a means to advising and assisting the Commission in coordinating the enforcement of this Regulation

summary: Commission must evaluate Data Act Chapters II-VIII by 12 September 2028 and Chapters VIIa-VIIc five years after entry into force; Member States provide information
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of chapters VIIa, VIIb and VIIc of this Regulation and submit a report on its main findings to the European Parliament and to the Council

summary: Controllers processing special categories of data for the development and operation of AI systems or models (new Art. 9(2)(k)) must take measures to avoid collecting them, remove any identified in training, testing or validation data or in the system or model, or otherwise protect them from use in outputs or disclosure
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: the controller identifies special categories of personal data in the datasets used for training, testing or validation or in the AI system or AI model, the controller shall remove such data

summary: Processing of personal data for developing and operating AI systems or models may rely on legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)) unless other law requires consent or the data subject's interests override (in particular children), subject to safeguards: data minimisation in source selection, training and testing, protection of residual data, enhanced transparency and an unconditional right to object
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: providing data subjects with an unconditional right to object to the processing of their personal data

summary: Controllers may charge a reasonable fee or refuse manifestly unfounded or excessive requests, including access requests abused for purposes other than data protection; the controller bears the burden of proof
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: for requests under Article 15 because the data subject abuses the rights conferred by this regulation for purposes other than the protection of their data

summary: Information duties (Art. 13(1)-(3)) do not apply in clear, circumscribed, non-data-intensive relationships where the data subject likely has the information (unless data are shared, transferred, used for automated decisions or high risk) or where informing is impossible or disproportionate for scientific research, subject to safeguards including public information
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: a controller exercising an activity that is not data-intensive and there are reasonable grounds to assume that the data subject already has the information referred to in points (a) and (c) of paragraph 1

applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: is necessary for entering into, or performance of, a contract between the data subject and a data controller regardless of whether the decision could be taken otherwise than by solely automated means

summary: Controllers must notify personal data breaches likely to result in a high risk to natural persons within 96 hours via the single-entry point (until it exists, directly to the supervisory authority)
applies_from: 18 months after entry into force (24 months if the Commission finds the single-entry point not functioning; Art. 11)
quote: In the case of a personal data breach that is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall without undue delay

summary: EDPB must propose to the Commission a common breach-notification template and list of high-risk circumstances, DPIA required/not-required lists and a common DPIA template and methodology (within 9 months), reviewed at least every three years; Commission adopts them by implementing act; supervisory authorities' list-making task is deleted
applies_from: Art. 33(6)-(7) (breach template): 18 months after entry into force (Art. 11, Art. 3(8)(c)); Art. 35 and Art. 70 changes: entry into force
quote: The Board shall prepare and transmit to the Commission a proposal for a list of the kind of processing operations which are subject to the requirement for a data protection impact assessment pursuant to paragraph 1.

summary: Commission may adopt implementing acts on means and criteria to determine when pseudonymised data are no longer personal data for certain entities, assessing the state of the art and closely involving the EDPB (opinion within 8 weeks)
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: The Commission may adopt implementing acts to specify means and criteria to determine whether data resulting from pseudonymisation no longer constitutes personal data for certain entities.

applies_from: 6 months after entry into force (GDPR Art. 88a(5))
quote: Storing of personal data, or gaining of access to personal data already stored, in the terminal equipment of a natural person is only allowed when that person has given his or her consent, in accordance with this Regulation.

summary: Where terminal-equipment access relies on consent, refusal must be possible with a single click or equivalent; no new request for the same purpose while consent is valid, or for at least six months after a refusal
applies_from: 6 months after entry into force (GDPR Art. 88a(5))
quote: if the data subject declines a request for consent, the controller shall not make a new request for consent for the same purpose for a period of at least six months.

summary: Controllers' online interfaces must accept consent, refusal and objections given through automated, machine-readable means and respect those choices (media service providers excluded); conformity with harmonised standards gives a presumption of conformity
applies_from: 24 months after entry into force (GDPR Art. 88b(5))
quote: Controllers shall ensure that their online interfaces allow data subjects to:
conditional_on: Not a media service provider providing a media service

summary: Providers of web browsers that are not SMEs (coded platform_operator) must provide the technical means for data subjects to give or refuse consent and object through automated, machine-readable signals
applies_from: 48 months after entry into force (GDPR Art. 88b(7))
quote: Providers of web browsers, which are not SMEs, shall provide the technical means to allow data subjects to give their consent and to refuse a request for consent

summary: Commission must request European standardisation organisations to draft standards for interpreting machine-readable indications of data subjects' choices
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: request one or more European standardisation organisations to draft standards for the interpretation of machine-readable indications of data subjects' choices

summary: Union institutions and bodies processing special categories of data for AI development or operation (new EUDPR Art. 10(2)(k)) must avoid, remove or protect such data, as under the GDPR amendment
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: For processing referred to in point (k) of paragraph 2, appropriate organisational and technical measures shall be implemented to avoid the collection and otherwise processing of special categories of personal data.

summary: Union institution controllers may refuse manifestly unfounded or excessive requests, including abusive access requests, bearing the burden of proof; automated decisions limited to contract, Union law or explicit consent
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: the controller may refuse to act on the request. The controller shall bear the burden of demonstrating that the request is manifestly unfounded

summary: Union institution controllers must notify high-risk personal data breaches to the EDPS within 96 hours where feasible
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: notify the personal data breach to the European Data Protection Supervisor. Where the notification to the European Data Protection Supervisor is not made within 96 hours, it shall be accompanied by reasons for the delay.

summary: Union institution controllers may store or access personal data in terminal equipment only with consent or listed exceptions, with single-click refusal and a six-month bar on repeat requests
applies_from: 6 months after entry into force (EUDPR Art. 37(6))
quote: (a) the data subject shall be able to refuse requests for consent in an easy and intelligible manner with a single-click button or equivalent means

summary: Union institution online interfaces must accept and respect automated, machine-readable consent and refusal signals
applies_from: 24 months after entry into force (EUDPR Art. 37(10))
quote: (b) decline a request for consent through automated and machine-readable means.

summary: ENISA must develop, secure and maintain a single-entry point for incident reporting under Union acts (possibly building on the CRA single reporting platform), set its specifications, pilot it within 18 months and not access notifications unless provided for
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: ENISA shall develop and maintain a single-entry point to support the obligation to report incidents and related events under the Union legal acts where those Union legal acts provide so

summary: Commission must assess the single-entry point's functioning, reliability, integrity and confidentiality and publish an OJ notice before reporting through it is enabled; ENISA corrects deficiencies
applies_from: entry into force (third day following publication in the OJ; Art. 11 sets no other date for this provision)
quote: finds that the single-entry point ensures the proper functioning, reliability, integrity and confidentiality, it shall publish a notice to that effect in the Official Journal of the European Union

summary: Member States must ensure essential and important entities notify significant incidents to the CSIRT or competent authority via the single-entry point, and allow voluntary notifications of incidents, cyber threats and near misses through it; CRA Art. 14(3) reports count towards NIS2 Art. 23(4)
applies_from: 18 months after entry into force (24 months if the Commission finds the single-entry point not functioning; Art. 11)
quote: Each Member State shall ensure that essential and important entities notify, without undue delay, its CSIRT or, where applicable, its competent authority

summary: Notifications under Regulation (EU) 910/2014 Arts. 19a(1)(b), 24(2)(fb) and 45a(3) to supervisory bodies or the Commission must go through the single-entry point (addressees of those provisions coded platform_operator)
applies_from: 18 months after entry into force (24 months if the Commission finds the single-entry point not functioning; Art. 11)
quote: shall be made through the single-entry point pursuant to Article 23a of Directive (EU) 2022/2555

summary: Financial entities must report major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority via the single-entry point and may voluntarily notify significant cyber threats through it
applies_from: 18 months after entry into force (24 months if the Commission finds the single-entry point not functioning; Art. 11)
quote: Financial entities shall report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority as referred to in Article 46 via the single-entry point

summary: Member States must ensure critical entities notify significantly disruptive incidents to the competent authority via the single-entry point; Commission may specify type and format by implementing acts
applies_from: 18 months after entry into force (24 months if the Commission finds the single-entry point not functioning; Art. 11)
quote: Member States shall ensure that critical entities notify via the single-entry point established pursuant to Article 23a of Directive (EU) 2022/2555 the competent authority

summary: Undertaking providing core platform services that meets all Art. 3(2) thresholds must notify the Commission within 2 months with the threshold information for each qualifying service; a designated gatekeeper must also notify when a further service meets the thresholds.

conditional_on: Meeting all thresholds in Art. 3(2)

summary: An undertaking meeting the thresholds may present substantiated arguments with its notification that, exceptionally, it does not satisfy the qualitative requirements of Art. 3(1) (rebuttal of the presumption).
quote: may present, with its notification, sufficiently substantiated arguments to demonstrate that, exceptionally, although it meets all the thresholds in paragraph 2
conditional_on: Notification under Art. 3(3)

summary: Undertakings providing core platform services must not segment, divide or split services by any means to circumvent the Art. 3(2) quantitative thresholds.
quote: shall not segment, divide, subdivide, fragment or split those services through contractual, commercial, technical or any other means in order to circumvent the quantitative thresholds laid down in Article 3(2)

summary: When submitting user numbers, the undertaking must submit aggregate anonymised unique end-user data based on signed-in environments and, where the service is also used outside them, on an alternate metric (IP addresses, cookie or other identifiers).
quote: the undertaking shall submit aggregate anonymized data on the number of unique end users per respective core platform service based on signed-in or logged-in environments, if such data exists
conditional_on: Submission of user numbers under Art. 3(3)

summary: The undertaking is responsible for complete and accurate active-user information: it must avoid under- and over-counting, explain its methodology and the counting risks and solutions, and provide data on an alternative metric if the Commission has accuracy concerns.
quote: shall be responsible for ensuring the completeness and accuracy of that information
conditional_on: Submission of user numbers under Art. 3(3)

summary: In counting users, the undertaking must not treat services of the same category as distinct mainly because of different domain names or geographic attributes, and must treat as distinct those services used for different purposes or of different categories, even if offered in an integrated way.
quote: shall not identify core platform services that belong to the same category of core platform services pursuant to Article 2, point (2) as distinct mainly on the basis that they are provided using different domain names
conditional_on: Calculation of active end users and business users

summary: Gatekeeper must not process third-party end-user personal data for advertising, combine or cross-use personal data across its core platform and other services, or sign users into other services to combine data, unless the end user was given a specific choice and consented under GDPR (or GDPR Art. 6(1)(c)-(e) applies).
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: unless the end user has been presented with the specific choice and has given consent within the meaning of Article 4, point (11), and Article 7 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Where an end user refuses or withdraws consent, the gatekeeper must not repeat the consent request for the same purpose more than once within one year.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: the gatekeeper shall not repeat its request for consent for the same purpose more than once within a period of one year
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must not prevent business users from offering products or services through third-party intermediation services or their own direct channels at different prices or conditions (no parity clauses).
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not prevent business users from offering the same products or services to end users through third-party online intermediation services or through their own direct online sales channel at prices or conditions that are different
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must allow business users, free of charge, to communicate and promote offers to end users acquired via the platform or elsewhere and to contract with them, whether or not they use the gatekeeper's services (anti-steering).
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow business users, free of charge, to communicate and promote offers, including under different conditions, to end users acquired via its core platform service or through other channels
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must allow end users to access and use, through its core platform services, content, subscriptions and features via a business user's app, including items acquired outside the gatekeeper's services.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow end users to access and use, through its core platform services, content, subscriptions, features or other items, by using the software application of a business user
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must not prevent or restrict business or end users from raising non-compliance issues with public authorities or national courts.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not directly or indirectly prevent or restrict business users or end users from raising any issue of non-compliance with the relevant Union or national law by the gatekeeper with any relevant public authority
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must not require users to use, offer or interoperate with its identification service, web browser engine, payment service or in-app payment systems in the context of business users' services.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not require end users to use, or business users to use, to offer, or to interoperate with, an identification service, a web browser engine or a payment service
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must not make access to any of its listed core platform services conditional on subscribing to or registering with another of its listed or threshold-meeting core platform services.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not require business users or end users to subscribe to, or register with, any further core platform services listed in the designation decision
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper supplying online advertising services must give each advertiser, on request, daily free information per advertisement on prices and fees paid, publisher remuneration (subject to publisher consent, otherwise daily averages) and the underlying metrics.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall provide each advertiser to which it supplies online advertising services, or third parties authorised by advertisers, upon the advertiser’s request, with information on a daily basis free of charge
conditional_on: Designation with online advertising services listed

summary: Gatekeeper supplying online advertising services must give each publisher, on request, daily free information per advertisement on remuneration and fees, the advertiser's price (subject to consent, otherwise daily averages) and the metrics.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall provide each publisher to which it supplies online advertising services, or third parties authorised by publishers, upon the publisher’s request, with free of charge information on a daily basis
conditional_on: Designation with online advertising services listed

summary: Gatekeeper must not use, in competition with business users, non-public data generated or provided by those business users or their customers on its core platform services (including click, search, view and voice data).
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not use, in competition with business users, any data that is not publicly available that is generated or provided by those business users
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must let end users easily uninstall software applications on its operating system, except apps essential to the OS or device that third parties cannot offer standalone.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow and technically enable end users to easily un-install any software applications on the operating system of the gatekeeper
conditional_on: Designation with an operating system listed

summary: Gatekeeper must let end users easily change default settings on its OS, virtual assistant and web browser, and show a choice screen of main providers of search engines, virtual assistants and browsers at first use.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow and technically enable end users to easily change default settings on the operating system, virtual assistant and web browser of the gatekeeper
conditional_on: Designation with an operating system, virtual assistant, web browser or online search engine listed

summary: Gatekeeper must allow installation and effective use of third-party apps and app stores on its operating system, accessible by other means than its own services, and allow and enable them to be set as default.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow and technically enable the installation and effective use of third-party software applications or software application stores using, or interoperating with, its operating system
conditional_on: Designation with an operating system listed

summary: Gatekeeper may take strictly necessary, proportionate and duly justified measures so that third-party apps or app stores do not endanger hardware or OS integrity, and non-default settings for user security.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: measures to ensure that third-party software applications or software application stores do not endanger the integrity of the hardware or operating system provided by the gatekeeper, provided that such measures are duly justified by the gatekeeper
conditional_on: Designation with an operating system listed

summary: Gatekeeper must not favour its own services and products in ranking, indexing and crawling over similar third-party ones and must apply transparent, fair and non-discriminatory ranking conditions.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not treat more favourably, in ranking and related indexing and crawling, services and products offered by the gatekeeper itself than similar services or products of a third party.
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must not restrict end users' ability to switch between and subscribe to different apps and services accessed through its core platform services, including choice of internet access service.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not restrict technically or otherwise the ability of end users to switch between, and subscribe to, different software applications and services
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must give service and hardware providers, and business users and alternative providers of ancillary services, free and effective interoperability with the same OS, virtual assistant, hardware and software features available to its own services; strictly necessary, justified integrity measures are allowed.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow providers of services and providers of hardware, free of charge, effective interoperability with, and access for the purposes of interoperability to, the same hardware and software features
conditional_on: Designation with an operating system or virtual assistant listed

summary: Gatekeeper must give advertisers, publishers and authorised third parties, on request and free, access to its performance measuring tools and the data needed for independent verification of the ad inventory.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: with access to the performance measuring tools of the gatekeeper and the data necessary for advertisers and publishers to carry out their own independent verification of the advertisements inventory
conditional_on: Designation with online advertising services listed

summary: Gatekeeper must provide end users and authorised third parties, on request and free, effective portability of data provided or generated by the end user, including tools and continuous real-time access.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall provide end users and third parties authorised by an end user, at their request and free of charge, with effective portability of data
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must give business users and authorised third parties free, high-quality, continuous real-time access to aggregated and non-aggregated data generated through their use of the platform; personal data only where directly connected and end users opt in by consent.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: with effective, high-quality, continuous and real-time access to, and use of, aggregated and non-aggregated data, including personal data
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must give third-party online search engines, on request, access on FRAND terms to ranking, query, click and view data from free and paid search; personal data in such data must be anonymised.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: with access on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms to ranking, query, click and view data in relation to free and paid search generated by end users on its online search engines
conditional_on: Designation with an online search engine listed

summary: Gatekeeper must apply fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory general conditions of access for business users to its listed app stores, search engines and social networks and publish them, including an alternative dispute settlement mechanism (second character: complaint mechanism).
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall apply fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory general conditions of access for business users to its software application stores, online search engines and online social networking services
conditional_on: Designation with app store, search engine or social network listed

summary: Gatekeeper must not have disproportionate general conditions for terminating a core platform service and must ensure termination can be exercised without undue difficulty.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not have general conditions for terminating the provision of a core platform service that are disproportionate.
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper providing a listed number-independent interpersonal communications service must, on request and free, make basic functionalities interoperable with other providers' services: one-to-one end-to-end text messaging and file sharing.
applies_from: Following listing in the designation decision (Art. 7(2)(a)); requests after publication of the reference offer (Art. 7(5))
quote: it shall make the basic functionalities of its number-independent interpersonal communications services interoperable with the number-independent interpersonal communications services of another provider
conditional_on: Designation with a number-independent interpersonal communications service listed; functionality provided to own end users

summary: Interoperability of group end-to-end text messaging and group-to-individual file sharing.
quote: end-to-end text messaging within groups of individual end users
conditional_on: Designation with a NIICS listed; functionality provided to own end users

summary: Interoperability of one-to-one and group-to-individual end-to-end voice and video calls.
quote: end-to-end voice calls between two individual end users
conditional_on: Designation with a NIICS listed; functionality provided to own end users

summary: The security level, including end-to-end encryption, that the gatekeeper provides to its own users must be preserved across interoperable services.
quote: The level of security, including the end-to-end encryption, where applicable, that the gatekeeper provides to its own end users shall be preserved across the interoperable services.
conditional_on: Designation with a NIICS listed

summary: Gatekeeper must publish and update a reference offer with technical details and terms of NIICS interoperability, including security and encryption details, within the Art. 3(10) period.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall publish a reference offer laying down the technical details and general terms and conditions of interoperability
conditional_on: Designation with a NIICS listed

summary: Gatekeeper must comply with any reasonable interoperability request from a NIICS provider within 3 months by making the requested functionalities operational (Commission may extend time limits, Art. 7(6)).
applies_from: After publication of the reference offer
quote: The gatekeeper shall comply with any reasonable request for interoperability within 3 months after receiving that request by rendering the requested basic functionalities operational.
conditional_on: Request by a provider offering or intending to offer NIICS in the Union

summary: In interoperability, the gatekeeper may collect and exchange only end-user personal data strictly necessary for effective interoperability, in full compliance with the GDPR and ePrivacy Directive.
quote: only the personal data of end users that is strictly necessary to provide effective interoperability
conditional_on: Designation with a NIICS listed

summary: Gatekeeper may take strictly necessary, proportionate and justified measures so that requesting NIICS providers do not endanger the integrity, security and privacy of its services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not be prevented from taking measures to ensure that third-party providers of number-independent interpersonal communications services requesting interoperability do not endanger the integrity, security and privacy of its services
conditional_on: Designation with a NIICS listed

summary: Gatekeeper must ensure and demonstrate effective compliance with Arts 5-7, with measures that comply with the GDPR, ePrivacy, cybersecurity, consumer protection, product safety and accessibility law, and ensure the obligations are fully and effectively complied with (Art. 13(3)).
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall ensure and demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in Articles 5, 6 and 7 of this Regulation.
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper may ask the Commission to determine whether its intended or implemented measures under Arts 6 and 7 are effective, with a reasoned submission and a non-confidential version.
quote: A gatekeeper may request the Commission to engage in a process to determine whether the measures that that gatekeeper intends to implement or has implemented to ensure compliance with Articles 6 and 7 are effective
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper may request suspension of a specific obligation where exceptional circumstances beyond its control endanger the economic viability of its Union operation (provisional suspension in urgent cases).
quote: Where the gatekeeper demonstrates in a reasoned request that compliance with a specific obligation laid down in Article 5, 6 or 7 for a core platform service listed in the designation decision pursuant to Article 3(9) would endanger
conditional_on: Exceptional circumstances beyond the gatekeeper's control

summary: Gatekeeper may request exemption from a specific obligation on grounds of public health or public security only (the Commission may also act on its own initiative).
quote: An exemption pursuant to paragraph 1 may only be granted on grounds of public health or public security.
conditional_on: Grounds of public health or public security

summary: Within 6 months of designation the gatekeeper must give the Commission a detailed compliance report on measures for Arts 5-7, publish a non-confidential summary, and update both at least annually.
quote: the gatekeeper shall provide the Commission with a report describing in a detailed and transparent manner the measures it has implemented to ensure compliance with the obligations laid down in Articles 5, 6 and 7
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must not undermine compliance with Arts 5-7 by contractual, commercial, technical or behavioural means or interface design.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not engage in any behaviour that undermines effective compliance with the obligations of Articles 5, 6 and 7
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Where consent is needed for compliance, the gatekeeper must enable business users to obtain consent directly (or comply otherwise, e.g. with anonymised data) and not make obtaining consent harder for business users than for its own services.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not make the obtaining of that consent by the business user more burdensome than for its own services.
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must not degrade service conditions or quality for users exercising rights under Arts 5-7, or make their exercise unduly difficult, including through non-neutral choices or user-interface design.
applies_from: 6 months after the core platform service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)); Regulation applies from 2023-05-02
quote: The gatekeeper shall not degrade the conditions or quality of any of the core platform services provided to business users or end users who avail themselves of the rights or choices laid down in Articles 5, 6 and 7
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must inform the Commission, before implementation, of any intended concentration where the parties or target provide core platform or other digital services or enable data collection, whether or not notifiable under merger rules, with turnover, user numbers and transaction value.
quote: A gatekeeper shall inform the Commission of any intended concentration within the meaning of Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 139/2004
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must inform the Commission within 2 months of a concentration's implementation if additional core platform services then meet the Art. 3(2)(b) thresholds.
quote: If, following any concentration referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, additional core platform services individually meet the thresholds in Article 3(2), point (b)
conditional_on: Concentration after which further core platform services meet the user thresholds

summary: Within 6 months of designation the gatekeeper must submit an independently audited description of its consumer profiling techniques (forwarded to the EDPB), publish an overview, and update both at least annually (second character: disclosure).
quote: a gatekeeper shall submit to the Commission an independently audited description of any techniques for profiling of consumers
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: Gatekeeper must set up an independent compliance function with compliance officers and an independent senior head reporting to the management body, communicate the head's contact details, and have the management body oversee governance and review compliance strategies at least annually.
quote: Gatekeepers shall introduce a compliance function, which is independent from the operational functions of the gatekeeper and composed of one or more compliance officers, including the head of the compliance function.
conditional_on: Designation as gatekeeper (Art. 3) and listing of the core platform service (Art. 3(9))

summary: After a non-compliance decision, the gatekeeper must describe to the Commission the measures it has taken to comply.
quote: The gatekeeper shall provide the Commission with the description of the measures that it has taken to ensure compliance with the non-compliance decision.
conditional_on: Non-compliance decision under Art. 29

summary: Undertakings and associations must supply information requested by the Commission (including access to data, algorithms and testing information) and submit to inspections ordered by decision.
quote: Undertakings or associations of undertakings are required to submit to an inspection ordered by a Commission decision.
conditional_on: Commission request or decision

summary: Commission monitoring may impose on the gatekeeper an obligation to retain all documents relevant to assessing compliance.
quote: the imposition of an obligation on the gatekeeper to retain all documents deemed to be relevant to assess the implementation of, and compliance with, those obligations and decisions
conditional_on: Commission monitoring measure

summary: Member States must not impose further obligations on gatekeepers by law, regulation or administrative measure to ensure contestable and fair markets; obligations outside the Regulation's scope remain possible if not based on gatekeeper status.
quote: Member States shall not impose further obligations on gatekeepers by way of laws, regulations or administrative measures for the purpose of ensuring contestable and fair markets.

summary: National authorities must not take decisions running counter to a Commission decision under the Regulation; national courts must not give such decisions and should avoid conflict with contemplated Commission decisions.
quote: National authorities shall not take decisions which run counter to a decision adopted by the Commission under this Regulation.

summary: National competition authorities must inform the Commission of first formal investigative measures against gatekeepers under national law and communicate draft obligations at least 30 days before adoption (not for merger decisions).
quote: it shall inform the Commission in writing of the first formal investigative measure, before or immediately after the start of such measure

summary: A national competition authority may investigate possible non-compliance with Arts 5-7 on its territory, informing the Commission first; Commission proceedings relieve it of that possibility, and it must report its findings.
quote: may, on its own initiative, conduct an investigation into a case of possible non-compliance with Articles 5, 6 and 7 of this Regulation on its territory
conditional_on: Competence and investigative powers under national law

summary: A national competent authority that finds a possible non-compliance issue in third-party information must transfer that information to the Commission.
quote: it shall transfer that information to the Commission

summary: Member State authorities must provide the Commission with necessary information on request, and Member States must assist Commission inspections, including through police assistance where an undertaking opposes them.
quote: the Member State concerned shall afford them the necessary assistance, requesting, where appropriate, the assistance of the police or of an equivalent enforcement authority

summary: Member States must forward to the Commission, without delay, copies of written national court judgments applying the Regulation.
quote: Member States shall forward to the Commission a copy of any written judgment of national courts deciding on the application of this Regulation.

summary: The Commission, Member State authorities and others including appointed auditors and experts must not disclose information covered by professional secrecy; collected information may be used only for the stated purposes.
quote: shall not disclose information acquired or exchanged by them pursuant to this Regulation and of the kind covered by the obligation of professional secrecy

summary: Commission must designate as gatekeeper an undertaking meeting all thresholds within 45 working days of complete information (or after a market investigation where the presumption is credibly rebutted), and list each gateway core platform service in the decision.
quote: The Commission shall designate as a gatekeeper, without undue delay and at the latest within 45 working days after receiving the complete information

summary: Commission must designate, through a market investigation (Art. 17), undertakings meeting the qualitative requirements but not the thresholds, considering size, user numbers, network effects, data advantages, scale, lock-in and conglomerate structure; it may declare only some obligations applicable to emerging gatekeepers.
quote: any undertaking providing core platform services that meets each of the requirements of paragraph 1 of this Article, but does not satisfy each of the thresholds in paragraph 2 of this Article

summary: Commission must review gatekeeper status at least every 3 years and new undertakings at least yearly, may reconsider designations, and must publish and update the list of gatekeepers and their core platform services.
quote: The Commission shall publish and update a list of gatekeepers and the list of the core platform services for which they need to comply with the obligations laid down in Chapter III on an on-going basis.

summary: Commission may specify by implementing act the measures a gatekeeper must take to comply with Arts 6 and 7 (Arts 5-7 for circumvention), after preliminary findings within 3 months and publication of a summary for comment.
quote: The Commission may adopt an implementing act, specifying the measures that the gatekeeper concerned is to implement in order to effectively comply with the obligations laid down in Articles 6 and 7.

summary: Commission must inform Member State authorities of notified concentrations and publish annually the list of acquisitions notified by gatekeepers.
quote: The Commission shall inform the competent authorities of the Member States of any information received pursuant to paragraph 1

summary: Commission may conduct market investigations into new services and practices and must publish findings within 18 months, with a legislative proposal or draft delegated act where appropriate.
quote: The Commission shall publish its findings in a report within 18 months from the date referred to in Article 16(3), point (a).

summary: Commission must monitor effective implementation of and compliance with Arts 5-7 and its decisions, and may appoint independent external experts, auditors and national officials.
quote: The Commission shall take the necessary actions to monitor the effective implementation and compliance with the obligations laid down in Articles 5, 6 and 7

summary: Before adopting decisions the Commission must hear the gatekeeper or undertaking on its preliminary findings and grant access to the file subject to business secrets.
quote: the Commission shall give the gatekeeper or undertaking or association of undertakings concerned the opportunity of being heard

summary: Commission must submit an annual implementation report to the European Parliament and Council and publish it.
quote: The Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council an annual report on the implementation of this Regulation

summary: Commission must establish, chair and provide the secretariat for a high-level group of EU regulatory bodies and networks.
quote: The Commission shall establish a high-level group for the Digital Markets Act (‘the high-level group’).

summary: Commission must examine Member State requests for market investigations within 4 months and publish its assessment.
quote: The Commission shall publish the results of its assessment.

summary: Commission must publish its decisions under Arts 3, 4, 8(2), 9, 10, 16-20, 24, 25(1), 29, 30 and 31, naming the parties and stating penalties, with regard to confidentiality.
quote: Such publication shall state the names of the parties and the main content of the decision, including any penalties imposed.

summary: Commission must evaluate the Regulation by 3 May 2026 and every 3 years, including whether Art. 7 should extend to online social networking services, and report to the European Parliament, Council and EESC.
quote: Moreover, the Commission shall evaluate if the scope of Article 7 may be extended to online social networking services.

summary: Commission empowered to adopt delegated acts specifying and adjusting the threshold methodology and updating the Annex methodology and indicators.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 49 to amend this Regulation by updating the methodology and the list of indicators set out in the Annex.

summary: Commission empowered, after a market investigation, to adopt delegated acts updating the Art. 5 and 6 obligations within the listed scope and adding or removing Art. 7 basic functionalities or specifying how Art. 7 obligations are performed.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 49 to supplement this Regulation with regard to the obligations laid down in Articles 5 and 6.
conditional_on: Market investigation under Art. 19

summary: Commission may adopt implementing acts on notifications, technical compliance measures, interoperability arrangements, reports, the profiling-audit methodology, procedures, rights of defence, cooperation and deadlines, after publishing drafts for at least one month of comments.
quote: The Commission may adopt implementing acts laying down detailed arrangements for the application of the following:

summary: Commission may adopt guidelines on any aspect of the Regulation and may mandate European standardisation bodies to develop standards.
quote: the Commission may mandate European standardisation bodies to facilitate the implementation of the obligations set out in this Regulation by developing appropriate standards

summary: Member States that exclude entities under Art. 2(5)(4) to (23) of Directive 2013/36/EU from DORA must inform the Commission, and any later changes; the Commission must make that information publicly available.
quote: it shall inform the Commission thereof as well as of any subsequent changes thereto
conditional_on: Member State chooses to use the exclusion option under Art. 2(4)

summary: Financial entities must implement the Chapter II ICT risk management rules in accordance with the proportionality principle, taking account of size, risk profile, and nature, scale and complexity of services.
quote: Financial entities shall implement the rules laid down in Chapter II in accordance with the principle of proportionality

summary: Competent authorities must consider financial entities' application of the proportionality principle when reviewing the consistency of their ICT risk management framework.
quote: The competent authorities shall consider the application of the proportionality principle by financial entities

summary: Financial entities must have an internal governance and control framework ensuring effective and prudent management of ICT risk.
quote: Financial entities shall have in place an internal governance and control framework that ensures an effective and prudent management of ICT risk

summary: The management body defines, approves, oversees and is responsible for the ICT risk management framework; it bears ultimate responsibility, sets policies, roles, business continuity and response plans, internal audit plans, budget, ICT third-party policy and reporting channels (Art. 5(2)(a) to (i)).
quote: The management body of the financial entity shall define, approve, oversee and be responsible for the implementation of all arrangements related to the ICT risk management framework

summary: Members of the management body must keep up to date with sufficient ICT risk knowledge and skills, including regular specific training.
quote: Members of the management body of the financial entity shall actively keep up to date with sufficient knowledge and skills

summary: Financial entities other than microenterprises must establish a role, or designate a senior manager, to monitor ICT third-party service arrangements and related risk exposure.
quote: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall establish a role in order to monitor the arrangements concluded with ICT third-party service providers
conditional_on: Entity is not a microenterprise

summary: Financial entities must have a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework as part of overall risk management, documented and reviewed at least yearly (Art. 6(5)), with a control function, internal audit, a follow-up process for audit findings, and a digital operational resilience strategy (Art. 6(4), (6) to (8)); non-microenterprises have the control function and audit duties.
quote: Financial entities shall have a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework

summary: The ICT risk management framework must include strategies, policies, procedures, ICT protocols and tools to protect all information assets and ICT assets, including physical components.
quote: The ICT risk management framework shall include at least strategies, policies, procedures, ICT protocols and tools that are necessary to duly and adequately protect all information assets and ICT assets

summary: Financial entities must provide complete and updated information on ICT risk and their ICT risk management framework to competent authorities upon request, and a review report on request (Art. 6(3), (5)).
quote: They shall provide complete and updated information on ICT risk and on their ICT risk management framework to the competent authorities upon their request.
conditional_on: Upon request of the competent authority

summary: The ICT risk management framework of non-microenterprises must be subject to regular internal audit by auditors with sufficient ICT expertise and independence; a formal follow-up process for critical audit findings is also required (Art. 6(6), (7)).
quote: shall be subject to internal audit by auditors on a regular basis
conditional_on: Entity is not a microenterprise

summary: Financial entities must use and maintain updated ICT systems, protocols and tools that are appropriate, reliable, have sufficient capacity, and are technologically resilient.
quote: financial entities shall use and maintain updated ICT systems, protocols and tools that are

summary: Financial entities must identify, classify and document ICT-supported business functions, information and ICT assets, and maintain inventories of assets, configurations and third-party dependencies, updated periodically and on major change, reviewed at least yearly.
quote: financial entities shall identify, classify and adequately document all ICT supported business functions

summary: Financial entities must continuously identify all sources of ICT risk and assess cyber threats and vulnerabilities, review risk scenarios at least yearly; non-microenterprises must perform a risk assessment upon each major change (Art. 8(3)) and a yearly specific risk assessment on all legacy ICT systems (Art. 8(7)).
quote: Financial entities shall, on a continuous basis, identify all sources of ICT risk
conditional_on: Art. 8(3) and 8(7) apply to entities other than microenterprises

summary: Financial entities must continuously monitor and control ICT system security, design and implement ICT security policies that ensure resilience, availability and data integrity, use appropriate ICT solutions, and document information security, network segmentation, access control, authentication, encryption, change management and patch policies.
quote: financial entities shall continuously monitor and control the security and functioning of ICT systems and tools

summary: Mechanisms must promptly detect anomalous activities and ICT incidents, provide multiple layers of control and alert thresholds, and be regularly tested under Art. 25; sufficient resources must monitor user activity and cyber-attacks.
quote: Financial entities shall have in place mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities

summary: Data reporting service providers must have systems that check trade reports for completeness and errors and request re-transmission.
quote: Data reporting service providers shall, in addition, have in place systems that can effectively check trade reports
conditional_on: Entity is a data reporting service provider

summary: Financial entities must put in place a comprehensive ICT business continuity policy, implemented through documented arrangements, plans and procedures for continuity, incident response, containment, and impact estimation (Art. 11(1), (2)); a crisis management function is required for non-microenterprises (Art. 11(7)).
quote: financial entities shall put in place a comprehensive ICT business continuity policy

summary: ICT response and recovery plans of non-microenterprises are subject to independent internal audit reviews.
quote: shall be subject to independent internal audit reviews
conditional_on: Entity is not a microenterprise

summary: Financial entities must maintain and periodically test ICT business continuity plans, including for outsourced critical functions; business continuity and response and recovery plans must be tested at least yearly, and crisis communication plans tested (Art. 11(4), (6)).
quote: Financial entities shall put in place, maintain and periodically test appropriate ICT business continuity plans

summary: Financial entities must conduct a business impact analysis of exposures to severe business disruptions, using quantitative and qualitative criteria, and align ICT assets with it.
quote: financial entities shall conduct a business impact analysis (BIA) of their exposures to severe business disruptions

summary: Financial entities must keep readily accessible records of activities before and during disruption events when continuity and recovery plans are activated.
quote: Financial entities shall keep readily accessible records of activities before and during disruption events
conditional_on: Continuity or recovery plans are activated

summary: Central securities depositories must provide competent authorities with copies of ICT business continuity test results; non-microenterprises must report to competent authorities, on request, estimated aggregated annual costs and losses from major ICT-related incidents (Art. 11(9), (10)).
quote: Central securities depositories shall provide the competent authorities with copies of the results of the ICT business continuity tests
conditional_on: Art. 11(9) applies to central securities depositories; Art. 11(10) to non-microenterprises on request

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee, must develop common guidelines on the estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses from major ICT-related incidents.
quote: the ESAs, through the Joint Committee, shall by 17 July 2024 develop common guidelines on the estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses

summary: Financial entities must develop and document backup policies and restoration and recovery procedures, set up backup systems, and test them periodically; restoration must use segregated systems and recovery checks must maintain data integrity (Art. 12(1), (2), (3), (7)).
quote: financial entities shall develop and document

summary: Non-microenterprises must maintain redundant ICT capacities; microenterprises must assess the need for such capacity based on risk profile.
quote: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall maintain redundant ICT capacities
conditional_on: Entity is not a microenterprise

summary: Central securities depositories must maintain at least one secondary processing site at a geographic distance from the primary site, with equivalent continuity capability and immediate accessibility to staff.
quote: Central securities depositories shall maintain at least one secondary processing site
conditional_on: Entity is a central securities depository

summary: Financial entities must capture and analyse vulnerability and threat information; after major incidents disrupting core activities they must hold post-incident reviews (Art. 13(1), (2), (3)); senior ICT staff report yearly to the management body (Art. 13(5)).
quote: Financial entities shall put in place post ICT-related incident reviews after a major ICT-related incident disrupts their core activities

summary: Non-microenterprises must, on request, communicate to competent authorities the changes implemented after post-incident reviews.
quote: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall, upon request, communicate to the competent authorities, the changes that were implemented
