conditional_on: Entity is not a microenterprise; upon request

summary: Financial entities must develop ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules for all staff and senior management, and monitor technological developments on a continuous basis (Art. 13(6), (7)).
quote: Financial entities shall develop ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules in their staff training schemes.

summary: Financial entities must have crisis communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of at least major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts and the public, and communication policies for staff and external stakeholders; at least one person must implement the communication strategy (Art. 14(2), (3)).
quote: financial entities shall have in place crisis communication plans enabling a responsible disclosure of, at least, major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients and counterparts as well as to the public

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee and in consultation with ENISA, must develop common draft regulatory technical standards on ICT security policies, access controls, anomaly detection, business continuity, response and recovery plans, and reporting content, taking account of entity size and risk profile.
quote: develop common draft regulatory technical standards in order to

summary: Power is delegated to the Commission to supplement the Regulation by adopting the regulatory technical standards referred to in Art. 15.
quote: Power is delegated to the Commission to supplement this Regulation by adopting the regulatory technical standards referred to in the first paragraph

summary: Simplified-regime entities must maintain a sound documented ICT risk management framework, monitor systems, use resilient ICT tools, identify key ICT third-party dependencies, ensure continuity through business continuity plans, test them regularly, and provide awareness training (Art. 16(1)(a) to (h)).
quote: the entities listed in the first subparagraph shall:
conditional_on: Entity is a simplified-regime entity under Art. 16(1)

summary: The ICT risk management framework of simplified-regime entities must be documented and reviewed periodically and upon major ICT-related incidents, and a review report must be provided on request.
quote: shall be documented and reviewed periodically and upon the occurrence of major ICT-related incidents
conditional_on: Entity is a simplified-regime entity under Art. 16(1)

summary: The ESAs must develop common draft regulatory technical standards on the simplified ICT risk management framework and submit them to the Commission.
quote: The ESAs shall submit those draft regulatory technical standards to the Commission by 17 January 2024.

summary: Financial entities must define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify incidents, with early warning indicators, classification, roles, communication plans and response procedures (Art. 17(1), (3)).
quote: Financial entities shall define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents.

summary: Financial entities must record all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats, and establish procedures to identify root causes and address them.
quote: Financial entities shall record all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats.

summary: Financial entities must classify ICT-related incidents and determine their impact by criteria covering clients affected, duration, geographic spread, data losses, service criticality and economic impact; they must also classify significant cyber threats (Art. 18(1), (2)).
quote: Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and shall determine their impact based on the following criteria

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee and in consultation with the ECB and ENISA, must develop common draft regulatory technical standards on classification criteria, materiality thresholds for major incidents, and significant cyber threat thresholds, and submit them to the Commission.
quote: The ESAs shall, through the Joint Committee and in consultation with the ECB and ENISA, develop common draft regulatory technical standards further specifying

summary: Power is delegated to the Commission to supplement the Regulation by adopting the regulatory technical standards referred to in Art. 18(3).
quote: Power is delegated to the Commission to supplement this Regulation by adopting the regulatory technical standards referred to in paragraph 3

summary: Financial entities must report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority; significant credit institutions report to the national competent authority, which transmits the report to the ECB; Member States may require reporting to CSIRTs.
quote: Financial entities shall report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority as referred to in Article 46
conditional_on: Incident is major

summary: Financial entities must submit an initial notification, intermediate reports on significant status changes, and a final report after root cause analysis, using templates, within time limits set under Art. 20.
quote: Financial entities shall, within the time limits to be laid down in accordance with Article 20
conditional_on: Time limits to be laid down under Art. 20 RTS

summary: Where a major ICT-related incident affects the financial interests of clients, financial entities must inform clients without undue delay of the incident and mitigation measures; for significant cyber threats they inform potentially affected clients of protection measures (Art. 19(3)).
quote: financial entities shall, without undue delay as soon as they become aware of it, inform their clients about the major ICT-related incident
conditional_on: Major ICT-related incident has an impact on the financial interests of clients

summary: Financial entities may voluntarily notify significant cyber threats to the relevant competent authority when they deem the threat relevant to the financial system, service users or clients.
quote: Financial entities may, on a voluntary basis, notify significant cyber threats to the relevant competent authority
conditional_on: Voluntary

summary: The competent authority must in a timely manner pass details of major incidents to EBA, ESMA or EIOPA, the ECB, other competent authorities, single points of contact or CSIRTs, resolution authorities and other relevant public authorities; EBA, ESMA or EIOPA and the ECB assess cross-border relevance and notify other authorities (Art. 19(6), (7)).
quote: the competent authority shall, in a timely manner, provide details of the major ICT-related incident to the following recipients

summary: Financial entities may outsource incident reporting obligations to a third-party provider, remaining fully responsible for compliance.
quote: Financial entities may outsource, in accordance with Union and national sectoral law, the reporting obligations under this Article
conditional_on: In accordance with Union and national sectoral law

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee and in consultation with ENISA and the ECB, must develop common draft regulatory technical standards on the content of incident reports, reporting time limits and significant cyber threat notifications, and common draft implementing technical standards on forms and templates.
quote: The ESAs shall submit the common draft regulatory technical standards referred to in the first paragraph, point (a), and the common draft implementing technical standards referred to in the first paragraph, point (b), to the Commission by 17 July 2024.

summary: Power is delegated to the Commission to adopt the common regulatory technical standards, and conferred to adopt the common implementing technical standards, referred to in Art. 20.
quote: Power is delegated to the Commission to supplement this Regulation by adopting the common regulatory technical standards

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee and in consultation with the ECB and ENISA, must prepare a joint report on the feasibility of a single EU Hub for major ICT-related incident reporting and submit it to the Parliament, Council and Commission.
quote: The ESAs shall submit the report referred to in paragraph 1 to the European Parliament, to the Council and to the Commission by 17 January 2025.

summary: Upon receipt of an initial notification or report, the competent authority must acknowledge receipt and may provide feedback or guidance; the ESAs must report yearly on anonymised and aggregated major incidents (Art. 22(2)).
quote: the competent authority shall, upon receipt of the initial notification and of each report as referred to in Article 19(4), acknowledge receipt

summary: The Chapter III incident requirements also apply to operational or security payment-related incidents, and major such incidents, where they concern credit institutions, payment institutions, account information service providers and electronic money institutions.
quote: The requirements laid down in this Chapter shall also apply to operational or security payment-related incidents
conditional_on: Entity is a credit institution, payment institution, account information service provider or electronic money institution

summary: Non-microenterprises must establish, maintain and review a sound digital operational resilience testing programme as part of the ICT risk management framework, with independent testers, remediation procedures, and at least yearly tests on all ICT systems supporting critical or important functions (Art. 24(1), (4) to (6)).
quote: establish, maintain and review a sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme
conditional_on: Entity is not a microenterprise

summary: The testing programme must provide for appropriate tests such as vulnerability assessments, scenario-based tests, performance and end-to-end testing and penetration testing.
quote: The digital operational resilience testing programme referred to in Article 24 shall provide

summary: Central securities depositories and central counterparties must perform vulnerability assessments before any deployment or redeployment of applications, infrastructure components and ICT services supporting critical or important functions.
quote: Central securities depositories and central counterparties shall perform vulnerability assessments before any deployment or redeployment
conditional_on: Entity is a central securities depository or central counterparty

summary: Microenterprises must perform the Art. 25(1) tests using a risk-based approach and strategic planning of ICT testing, balancing resources against risk and criticality.
quote: Microenterprises shall perform the tests referred to in paragraph 1 by combining a risk-based approach
conditional_on: Entity is a microenterprise

summary: Financial entities identified as required to perform advanced testing must carry out TLPT at least every 3 years, covering several or all critical or important functions on live production systems, with the competent authority able to adjust frequency.
quote: shall carry out at least every 3 years advanced testing by means of TLPT
conditional_on: Entity is other than an Art. 16(1) entity and other than a microenterprise, and is identified by the competent authority under Art. 26(8)

summary: Each TLPT must cover several or all critical or important functions and be performed on live production systems supporting them; the financial entity identifies relevant underlying systems and determines TLPT scope, validated by competent authorities.
quote: Each threat-led penetration test shall cover several or all critical or important functions of a financial entity
conditional_on: Entity is required to perform TLPT

summary: Where ICT third-party providers are in TLPT scope, the financial entity must take measures and safeguards to ensure their participation and retain full responsibility for compliance; it must also apply effective risk management controls to mitigate testing risks.
quote: the financial entity shall take the necessary measures and safeguards to ensure the participation of such ICT third-party service providers in the TLPT
conditional_on: ICT third-party service providers included in TLPT scope

summary: Financial entities must apply effective risk management controls to mitigate risks of impact on data, damage to assets and disruption to critical functions from TLPT, with cooperation of providers and testers.
quote: apply effective risk management controls to mitigate the risks of any potential impact on data
conditional_on: Entity is required to perform TLPT

summary: After TLPT, the financial entity and external testers must provide the designated authority a summary of findings, remediation plans and documentation; the entity must notify the competent authority of the attestation, findings summary and remediation plans (Art. 26(6), (7)).
quote: shall provide to the authority, designated in accordance with paragraph 9 or 10, a summary of the relevant findings, the remediation plans and the documentation
conditional_on: Entity is required to perform TLPT

summary: Financial entities must contract testers for TLPT in accordance with Art. 27; where internal testers are used, they must contract external testers every three tests.
quote: When financial entities use internal testers for the purposes of undertaking TLPT, they shall contract external testers every three tests.
conditional_on: Entity is required to perform TLPT; second sentence applies to use of internal testers

summary: Competent authorities must identify financial entities required to perform TLPT, based on impact, financial stability and ICT risk profile criteria; significant credit institutions may use only external testers.
quote: Competent authorities shall identify financial entities that are required to perform TLPT

summary: Member States may designate a single public authority for TLPT matters in the financial sector; absent such designation, a competent authority may delegate TLPT tasks to another national financial authority.
quote: Member States may designate a single public authority in the financial sector to be responsible for TLPT-related matters
conditional_on: Member State or competent authority chooses to designate or delegate

summary: The ESAs, in agreement with the ECB, must develop joint draft regulatory technical standards in accordance with TIBER-EU on TLPT criteria, internal testers, scope, methodology and cooperation, and submit them to the Commission.
quote: The ESAs shall submit those draft regulatory technical standards to the Commission by 17 July 2024.

summary: Power is delegated to the Commission to supplement the Regulation by adopting the TLPT regulatory technical standards referred to in Art. 26(11).
quote: Power is delegated to the Commission to supplement this Regulation by adopting the regulatory technical standards referred to in the first subparagraph

summary: Financial entities may use only testers for TLPT that have the highest suitability and reputability, specific threat intelligence and red team expertise, accreditation or codes of conduct, independent assurance, and professional indemnity insurance.
quote: Financial entities shall only use testers for the carrying out of TLPT, that:
conditional_on: Carrying out TLPT

summary: When using internal testers, financial entities must ensure additional conditions: competent authority approval, verified sufficient dedicated resources and avoidance of conflicts of interest, and an external threat intelligence provider.
quote: When using internal testers, financial entities shall ensure that, in addition to the requirements in paragraph 1, the following conditions are met
conditional_on: Entity uses internal testers for TLPT

summary: Contracts with external testers must require sound management of TLPT results and data processing that does not create risks to the financial entity.
quote: Financial entities shall ensure that contracts concluded with external testers require a sound management of the TLPT results

summary: Financial entities remain fully responsible for compliance with all DORA obligations when using ICT third-party services; they must manage ICT third-party risk within the ICT risk management framework on a proportionate basis.
quote: remain fully responsible for compliance with, and the discharge of, all obligations under this Regulation

summary: Non-microenterprises must adopt and regularly review a strategy on ICT third-party risk, including a policy on ICT services supporting critical or important functions, reviewed by the management body.
quote: shall adopt, and regularly review, a strategy on ICT third-party risk
conditional_on: Entity is not a microenterprise and not an Art. 16(1) entity

summary: Financial entities must maintain and update at entity, sub-consolidated and consolidated levels a register of information on all ICT third-party contractual arrangements, distinguishing those supporting critical or important functions, and provide it to the competent authority on request.
quote: shall maintain and update at entity level, and at sub-consolidated and consolidated levels, a register of information

summary: Financial entities must report at least yearly to competent authorities on new ICT third-party arrangements, provider categories, contract types and services, and inform them in a timely manner of planned arrangements for critical or important functions.
quote: Financial entities shall report at least yearly to the competent authorities on the number of new arrangements on the use of ICT services

summary: Before entering a contractual arrangement on ICT services, financial entities must assess whether it supports critical or important functions, supervisory conditions, relevant risks including concentration risk, provider due diligence and conflicts of interest.
quote: Before entering into a contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services, financial entities shall:
conditional_on: Before entering into a contractual arrangement on ICT services

summary: Financial entities may only contract with ICT third-party providers that comply with appropriate information security standards, and for critical or important functions must consider the most up-to-date and highest information security standards.
quote: Financial entities may only enter into contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers that comply with appropriate information security standards.

summary: In exercising access, inspection and audit rights over ICT third-party providers, financial entities must pre-determine audit frequency and areas on a risk basis, using accepted audit standards, and verify auditor skills for high technical complexity.
quote: financial entities shall, on the basis of a risk-based approach, pre-determine the frequency of audits and inspections

summary: Financial entities must ensure that ICT third-party contractual arrangements may be terminated where there is significant breach, circumstances altering performance, evidenced ICT risk weaknesses, or where the competent authority can no longer supervise effectively.
quote: Financial entities shall ensure that contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services may be terminated in any of the following circumstances
conditional_on: Specified termination circumstances arise

summary: For ICT services supporting critical or important functions, financial entities must put in place exit strategies, alternative solutions and transition plans, tested and reviewed periodically, plus contingency measures.
quote: For ICT services supporting critical or important functions, financial entities shall put in place exit strategies.
conditional_on: ICT services support critical or important functions

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee, must develop draft implementing technical standards establishing standard templates for the register of information, and submit them to the Commission.
quote: The ESAs shall, through the Joint Committee, develop draft implementing technical standards to establish the standard templates for the purposes of the register of information

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee, must develop draft regulatory technical standards further specifying the content of the ICT third-party policy for critical or important functions, and submit them to the Commission by 17 January 2024.
quote: The ESAs shall, through the Joint Committee, develop draft regulatory technical standards to further specify the detailed content of the policy

summary: Power is conferred on the Commission to adopt the implementing technical standards on the register of information (Art. 28(9)) and delegated to adopt the regulatory technical standards on the ICT third-party policy (Art. 28(10)).
quote: Power is delegated to the Commission to supplement this Regulation by adopting the regulatory technical standards referred to in the first subparagraph

summary: When assessing ICT concentration risk, financial entities must also consider whether a planned contract for critical or important ICT services would involve a non-substitutable provider or multiple contracts with the same or closely connected providers, and weigh alternatives.
quote: financial entities shall also take into account whether the envisaged conclusion of a contractual arrangement
conditional_on: Envisaged contractual arrangement for ICT services supporting critical or important functions

summary: Financial entities must weigh risks of subcontracting, including third-country subcontractors, consider insolvency law and data recovery constraints, and for third-country providers consider Union data protection rules and enforcement; also assess whether subcontracting chains could impair monitoring and supervision.
quote: financial entities shall weigh benefits and risks that may arise in connection with such subcontracting
conditional_on: Contractual arrangements on ICT services supporting critical or important functions, including subcontracting or third-country providers

summary: Rights and obligations of the financial entity and the ICT third-party service provider must be clearly allocated and set out in writing in one document including service level agreements.
quote: The rights and obligations of the financial entity and of the ICT third-party service provider shall be clearly allocated and set out in writing.

summary: ICT contracts must include at least listed elements, including service descriptions and subcontracting conditions, locations of service and data processing, data availability and access and return on insolvency or termination, incident assistance, cooperation with authorities, termination rights, and participation in security awareness and resilience training.
quote: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least the following elements:

summary: Contracts for ICT services supporting critical or important functions must include, in addition to Art. 30(2) elements, full quantitative service level targets, notice and reporting duties of the provider, business contingency and security requirements, participation in TLPT, exit strategies with transition periods, and contract terms on monitoring, access and audit rights.
quote: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions shall include, in addition to the elements referred to in paragraph 2, at least the following:
conditional_on: ICT services supporting critical or important functions

summary: Contracts for critical or important ICT services must provide the financial entity, or an appointed third party, and the competent authority with unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit, including taking copies on-site, and define scope, procedures and frequency of inspections and audits.
quote: unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit by the financial entity, or an appointed third party, and by the competent authority
conditional_on: ICT services supporting critical or important functions; the microenterprise derogation in Art. 30(3) allows delegation of audit rights to an independent third party

summary: Contracts for critical or important ICT services must require the provider to implement and test business contingency plans and to have ICT security measures, tools and policies appropriate to the financial entity's regulatory framework.
quote: requirements for the ICT third-party service provider to implement and test business contingency plans
conditional_on: ICT services supporting critical or important functions

summary: When negotiating contractual arrangements, financial entities and ICT third-party providers must consider using standard contractual clauses developed by public authorities for specific services.
quote: shall consider the use of standard contractual clauses developed by public authorities

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee, must develop draft regulatory technical standards specifying elements a financial entity must determine and assess when subcontracting ICT services supporting critical or important functions, and submit them to the Commission by 17 July 2024.
quote: The ESAs shall, through the Joint Committee, develop draft regulatory technical standards to specify further the elements

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee and upon recommendation from the Oversight Forum, must designate ICT third-party service providers that are critical for financial entities after assessment against the Art. 31(2) criteria, and appoint a Lead Overseer for each.
quote: designate the ICT third-party service providers that are critical for financial entities
conditional_on: Designation may not be used until the Commission adopts the delegated act under Art. 31(6)

summary: The ESAs, through the Joint Committee, must establish, publish and update yearly the list of critical ICT third-party service providers at Union level.
quote: shall establish, publish and update yearly the list of critical ICT third-party service providers at Union level.

summary: Competent authorities must transmit yearly and in aggregated form the Art. 28(3) reports to the Oversight Forum.
quote: competent authorities shall, on a yearly and aggregated basis, transmit the reports referred to in Article 28(3)

summary: The ESAs must notify the designated provider of its designation and starting date of oversight; the Lead Overseer must notify the provider of the assessment outcome and consider any reasoned statement.
quote: The Lead Overseer shall notify the ICT third-party service provider of the outcome of the assessment
conditional_on: Designation under Art. 31(1)(a)

summary: A designated critical ICT third-party service provider must notify the financial entities to which it provides services of its designation as critical.
quote: The ICT third-party service provider shall notify the financial entities to which they provide services of their designation as critical.
conditional_on: Designation as critical under Art. 31(1)(a)

summary: Critical ICT third-party service providers in a group must designate one legal person as coordination point for communication with the Lead Overseer.
quote: Critical ICT third-party service providers which are part of a group shall designate one legal person as a coordination point
conditional_on: Provider belongs to a group

summary: Financial entities may use a third-country ICT provider designated as critical only if that provider has established a subsidiary in the Union within 12 months of designation.
quote: Financial entities shall only make use of the services of an ICT third-party service provider established in a third country
conditional_on: Third-country ICT third-party service provider designated as critical

summary: A critical third-country ICT provider that has established an EU subsidiary must notify the Lead Overseer of any changes to the management structure of that subsidiary.
quote: shall notify the Lead Overseer of any changes to the structure of the management of the subsidiary established in the Union.
conditional_on: Subsidiary established in the Union under Art. 31(12)

summary: The Joint Committee must establish the Oversight Forum as a sub-committee; the Oversight Forum must regularly discuss ICT risk developments, assess oversight results yearly, submit benchmarks, and the ESAs must issue cooperation guidelines by 17 July 2024 and submit a yearly report on the Section.
quote: shall establish the Oversight Forum as a sub-committee

summary: The ESAs must issue guidelines on cooperation and the allocation of oversight tasks by 17 July 2024 and submit a yearly report on the application of the oversight Section to Parliament, Council and Commission.
applies_from: 17 July 2024 for guidelines (Art. 32(7)); yearly thereafter for report (Art. 32(9))
quote: the ESAs shall by 17 July 2024 issue, for the purposes of this Section, guidelines on the cooperation between the ESAs and the competent authorities

summary: The Lead Overseer must assess whether each critical ICT third-party service provider has comprehensive, sound and effective ICT risk management rules, procedures and arrangements, covering the areas listed in Art. 33(3).
quote: the Lead Overseer shall assess whether each critical ICT third-party service provider has in place comprehensive, sound and effective rules
conditional_on: Critical ICT third-party service provider under its oversight

summary: The Lead Overseer must adopt a reasoned individual annual oversight plan for each critical provider, communicate a draft to the provider beforehand, and communicate the adopted plan yearly to the provider; the provider may submit a reasoned statement within 15 calendar days.
quote: the Lead Overseer shall adopt a clear, detailed and reasoned individual oversight plan
conditional_on: Assessment under Art. 33(2) completed

summary: Competent authorities may take measures concerning critical ICT third-party service providers only in agreement with the Lead Overseer, once annual oversight plans are adopted and notified.
quote: competent authorities may take measures concerning such critical ICT third-party service providers only in agreement with the Lead Overseer.
conditional_on: Annual oversight plans adopted and notified under Art. 33(4)

summary: The three Lead Overseers must set up a Joint Oversight Network (JON) to coordinate oversight, and draw up a common oversight protocol, revised periodically.
quote: the three Lead Overseers appointed in accordance with Article 31(1), point (b), shall set up a JON

summary: The Lead Overseer must ensure regular coordination within the JON and seek consistent oversight approaches, take account of Directive (EU) 2022/2555, and seek to minimise disruption to services to entities outside the Regulation's scope.
quote: ensure regular coordination within the JON
conditional_on: Exercise of Art. 35 powers

summary: Critical ICT third-party service providers must cooperate in good faith with the Lead Overseer and assist it in carrying out its tasks.
quote: Critical ICT third-party service providers shall cooperate in good faith with the Lead Overseer
conditional_on: Critical ICT third-party service provider designated under Art. 31

summary: The Lead Overseer must inform the JON of the outcome of its information-request and investigation powers and transmit reports to the JON and the competent authorities of the financial entities using the provider's services.
quote: The Lead Overseer shall inform the JON of the outcome of the exercise of the powers referred to in paragraph 1, points (a) and (b).

summary: The Lead Overseer must disclose to the public every periodic penalty payment imposed, unless disclosure would seriously jeopardise financial markets or cause disproportionate damage.
quote: The Lead Overseer shall disclose to the public every periodic penalty payment that has been imposed
conditional_on: Periodic penalty payment imposed under Art. 35(6); exception for serious jeopardy or disproportionate damage

summary: EBA, ESMA or EIOPA must conclude administrative cooperation arrangements with relevant third-country authorities to enable inspections outside the Union, and these must specify listed elements.
quote: EBA, ESMA or EIOPA shall conclude administrative cooperation arrangements with the relevant authority of the third country
conditional_on: Oversight outside the Union under Art. 36(1)

summary: Where the Lead Overseer cannot conduct oversight outside the Union, it must exercise its Art. 35 powers on the basis of available facts and document and explain the consequences of its inability.
quote: document and explain any consequence of its inability to conduct the envisaged oversight activities
conditional_on: Lead Overseer unable to conduct oversight activities outside the Union

summary: When sending a simple request for information, the Lead Overseer must cite Art. 37 as legal basis, state the purpose, specify the information, set a time limit and inform the provider that a voluntary reply must not be incorrect or misleading. A request by decision must contain the same elements plus the penalty payment reference and appeal rights, and a copy must go to competent authorities and the JON.
quote: When sending a simple request for information under paragraph 1, the Lead Overseer shall:
conditional_on: Request under Art. 37(1)

summary: Representatives of critical ICT third-party service providers must supply requested information and remain fully responsible if it is incomplete, incorrect or misleading.
quote: The representatives of the critical ICT third-party service providers shall supply the information requested.
conditional_on: Request under Art. 37(1)

summary: Officials conducting investigations must exercise powers only on production of a written authorisation; the Lead Overseer must inform competent authorities of financial entities in good time before an investigation.
quote: shall exercise their powers upon production of a written authorisation specifying the subject matter and purpose of the investigation
conditional_on: General investigation under Art. 38(1)

summary: Representatives of critical ICT third-party service providers are required to submit to investigations based on a decision of the Lead Overseer.
quote: The representatives of the critical ICT third-party service providers are required to submit to the investigations on the basis of a decision of the Lead Overseer.
conditional_on: Investigation ordered by decision of the Lead Overseer

summary: The Lead Overseer must inform competent authorities of the financial entities using the provider's services in good time before an inspection, and before any planned on-site inspection must give reasonable notice to the provider, unless an emergency or the inspection would be rendered ineffective.
quote: Before any planned on-site inspection, the Lead Overseer shall give reasonable notice to the critical ICT third-party service providers
conditional_on: On-site or off-site inspection under Art. 39(1)

summary: Critical ICT third-party service providers must submit to on-site inspections ordered by decision of the Lead Overseer.
quote: The critical ICT third-party service provider shall submit to on-site inspections ordered by decision of the Lead Overseer.
conditional_on: Inspection ordered by decision of the Lead Overseer

summary: After consulting the Oversight Forum, the Lead Overseer must adopt recommendations to the critical provider within 3 months of completing an investigation or inspection, and immediately communicate them to the provider and the relevant competent authorities.
applies_from: Within 3 months of completion of an investigation or inspection (Art. 40(3))
quote: Within 3 months of the completion of an investigation or inspection, the Lead Overseer, after consulting the Oversight Forum, shall adopt recommendations
conditional_on: Completion of an investigation or inspection

summary: The ESAs must develop draft regulatory technical standards on information for designation applications, provider reporting templates, joint examination team composition, and competent authorities' assessment of measures, and submit them to the Commission by 17 July 2024.
quote: The ESAs shall, through the Joint Committee, develop draft regulatory technical standards to specify

summary: The Commission is empowered to supplement the Regulation by adopting the regulatory technical standards referred to in Art. 41(1).
quote: Power is delegated to the Commission to supplement this Regulation by adopting the regulatory technical standards referred to in paragraph 1

summary: Within 60 calendar days of receiving the Lead Overseer's recommendations, critical ICT third-party service providers must either notify their intention to follow them or provide a reasoned explanation for not doing so.
applies_from: Within 60 calendar days of receipt of recommendations (Art. 42(1))
quote: critical ICT third-party service providers shall either notify the Lead Overseer of their intention to follow the recommendations or provide a reasoned explanation
conditional_on: Recommendations issued under Art. 35(1)(d)

summary: The Lead Overseer must publicly disclose where a critical provider fails to notify its intention or its explanation is insufficient, including the provider's identity and the type and nature of non-compliance, limited to what is relevant and proportionate.
