summary: Member States must ensure that orders to act against illegal content meet the listed minimum conditions when transmitted to providers; DSCs transmit copies of orders to other DSCs.
quote: Member States shall ensure that when an order referred to in paragraph 1 is transmitted to the provider, it meets at least the following conditions
conditional_on: Orders issued under Art. 9(1)

summary: Providers must inform the issuing authority, without undue delay, of any effect given to an order to act against illegal content.
quote: providers of intermediary services shall inform the authority issuing the order
conditional_on: Receipt of an order under Art. 9(1)

summary: Providers must inform the recipient of the service concerned of the order received and the effect given to it, including a statement of reasons and redress options.
applies_from: At the latest when effect is given to the order
quote: providers of intermediary services shall inform the recipient of the service concerned of the order received and to the effect given to it
conditional_on: Order under Art. 9(1)

summary: Member States must ensure that orders to provide information meet the listed minimum conditions; DSCs transmit copies of orders to other DSCs.
quote: Member States shall ensure that when an order referred to in paragraph 1 is transmitted to the provider, it meets at least the following conditions
conditional_on: Orders issued under Art. 10(1)

summary: Providers must inform the issuing authority, without undue delay, of receipt of an order to provide information and of the effect given to it.
quote: providers of intermediary services shall, without undue delay inform the authority issuing the order
conditional_on: Receipt of an order under Art. 10(1)

summary: Providers must inform the recipient of the service concerned of the order received and the effect given to it, with a statement of reasons and redress possibilities.
applies_from: At the latest when effect is given to the order
quote: providers of intermediary services shall inform the recipient of the service concerned of the order received and the effect given to it
conditional_on: Order under Art. 10(1)

summary: Providers must designate a single point of contact for communication with Member State authorities, the Commission and the Board.
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall designate a single point of contact

summary: Providers must make public the information needed to identify and communicate with their single points of contact, keep it up to date, and specify accepted languages.
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall make public the information necessary to easily identify and communicate with their single points of contact.

summary: Providers must designate a single point of contact enabling recipients of the service to communicate directly and rapidly with them.
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall designate a single point of contact to enable recipients of the service to communicate directly

summary: Providers must make public the information needed for recipients to identify and communicate with their single points of contact.
quote: providers of intermediary services shall make public the information necessary for the recipients of the service

summary: Providers without an EU establishment but offering services in the Union must designate a legal representative in writing in a Member State where they offer services.
quote: shall designate, in writing, a legal or natural person to act as their legal representative
conditional_on: Provider has no establishment in the Union but offers services in the Union

summary: Providers must mandate and empower their legal representatives with necessary powers and resources to cooperate with authorities and comply with decisions.
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall provide their legal representative with necessary powers and sufficient resources
conditional_on: Designation of a legal representative under Art. 13(1)

summary: Providers must notify the name, postal address, email address and telephone number of their legal representative to the DSC of the Member State where the representative resides, and keep it public and up to date.
quote: shall notify the name, postal address, email address and telephone number of their legal representative to the Digital Services Coordinator
conditional_on: Designation of a legal representative under Art. 13(1)

summary: Terms and conditions must set out restrictions on use, including content moderation policies, tools, algorithmic decision-making, human review and complaint rules, in clear language and machine-readable format.
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall include information on any restrictions that they impose in relation to the use of their service

summary: Providers must inform recipients of any significant change to the terms and conditions.
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall inform the recipients of the service of any significant change to the terms and conditions.

summary: Where a service is primarily directed at or used by minors, the provider must explain conditions and restrictions in a way minors can understand.
quote: the provider of that intermediary service shall explain the conditions for, and any restrictions on, the use of the service in a way that minors can understand.
conditional_on: Service primarily directed at minors or predominantly used by them

summary: Providers must apply and enforce content restrictions in a diligent, objective and proportionate manner, with due regard to fundamental rights.
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall act in a diligent, objective and proportionate manner in applying and enforcing the restrictions

summary: Very large online platforms and search engines must provide recipients a concise, machine-readable summary of their terms and conditions, including remedies and redress.
quote: shall provide recipients of services with a concise, easily-accessible and machine-readable summary of the terms and conditions
conditional_on: Very large online platform or very large search engine (Art. 33)

summary: Very large online platforms and search engines must publish their terms and conditions in the official languages of all Member States where they offer services.
quote: shall publish their terms and conditions in the official languages of all the Member States in which they offer their services.
conditional_on: Very large online platform or very large search engine (Art. 33)

summary: Providers must publish at least annually machine-readable reports on content moderation, covering orders received, notices, own-initiative moderation, complaints and automated means; micro and small enterprises are excluded under Art. 15(2).
quote: shall make publicly available, in a machine-readable format and in an easily accessible manner, at least once a year, clear, easily comprehensible reports

summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts laying down templates and harmonised reporting periods for transparency reports.
quote: The Commission may adopt implementing acts to lay down templates concerning the form, content and other details of reports

summary: Hosting providers must put in place easy-to-access electronic notice mechanisms for any individual or entity, with notices containing listed elements, and process notices in a timely, diligent, non-arbitrary and objective manner.
quote: Providers of hosting services shall put mechanisms in place to allow any individual or entity to notify them of the presence on their service

summary: Hosting providers must send confirmation of receipt of a notice and notify the notifier of their decision, with redress information.
quote: The provider shall also, without undue delay, notify that individual or entity of its decision in respect of the information to which the notice relates
conditional_on: Notice received under Art. 16(1)

summary: Hosting providers must give affected recipients a clear and specific statement of reasons for restrictions based on illegality or incompatibility with terms and conditions, with the listed content.
applies_from: From the date the restriction is imposed
quote: Providers of hosting services shall provide a clear and specific statement of reasons to any affected recipients of the service
conditional_on: Restriction on the ground that information is illegal content or incompatible with terms

summary: Hosting providers aware of information giving rise to suspicion of a criminal offence threatening life or safety must promptly inform law enforcement or judicial authorities.
quote: it shall promptly inform the law enforcement or judicial authorities of the Member State or Member States concerned of its suspicion
conditional_on: Awareness of information giving rise to suspicion of such an offence

summary: Online platforms must provide recipients, including notifiers, access for at least six months to a free electronic internal complaint-handling system against content and account decisions, handled in a timely, non-discriminatory and non-arbitrary manner.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall provide recipients of the service, including individuals or entities that have submitted a notice

summary: Online platforms must inform complainants without undue delay of their reasoned decision and of out-of-court dispute settlement and other redress options.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall inform complainants without undue delay of their reasoned decision
conditional_on: Complaint lodged under Art. 20(1)

summary: Online platforms must ensure that complaint decisions are taken under supervision of appropriately qualified staff and not solely on the basis of automated means.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall ensure that the decisions, referred to in paragraph 5, are taken under the supervision of appropriately qualified staff

summary: Online platforms must make information on out-of-court dispute settlement access easily accessible, clear and user-friendly on their online interface.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall ensure that information about the possibility for recipients of the service to have access to an out-of-court dispute settlement

summary: Online platforms must engage in good faith with the selected certified out-of-court dispute settlement body, may refuse only for already-resolved disputes, and bear the body's fees where the recipient prevails.
quote: Both parties shall engage, in good faith, with the selected certified out-of-court dispute settlement body
conditional_on: Dispute selected under Art. 21(1)

summary: Digital Services Coordinators certify out-of-court dispute settlement bodies for up to five years, draw up biennial reports on those bodies, and notify certified bodies to the Commission.
quote: The Digital Services Coordinator of the Member State where the out-of-court dispute settlement body is established shall, for a maximum period of five years, which may be renewed, certify the body

summary: Online platforms must take technical and organisational measures so that notices from trusted flaggers are given priority and decided without undue delay.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall take the necessary technical and organisational measures to ensure that notices submitted by trusted flaggers
conditional_on: Notices from trusted flaggers acting within their expertise

summary: Digital Services Coordinators award trusted flagger status on application to applicants meeting the listed conditions, and communicate names to the Commission and the Board.
quote: shall be awarded, upon application by any entity, by the Digital Services Coordinator
conditional_on: Application by an entity

summary: Trusted flaggers must publish at least annual reports on notices submitted, listing numbers by provider, content type and action taken, without personal data.
quote: Trusted flaggers shall publish, at least once a year easily comprehensible and detailed reports on notices submitted in accordance with Article 16
conditional_on: Entity holding trusted flagger status

summary: Online platforms must communicate to the awarding DSC information indicating that a trusted flagger submitted a significant number of insufficiently precise or unsubstantiated notices.
quote: it shall communicate that information to the Digital Services Coordinator that awarded the status of trusted flagger
conditional_on: Information indicating such notices by a trusted flagger

summary: Online platforms must suspend, after a prior warning, services to recipients frequently providing manifestly illegal content, and suspend processing of frequent manifestly unfounded notices or complaints, assessing misuse case by case.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall suspend, for a reasonable period of time and after having issued a prior warning
conditional_on: Frequent provision of manifestly illegal content or frequent manifestly unfounded notices or complaints

summary: Online platforms must set out in their terms and conditions their policy on misuse and examples of relevant circumstances and suspension duration.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall set out, in a clear and detailed manner, in their terms and conditions their policy in respect of the misuse

summary: Online platforms must include in their transparency reports information on out-of-court disputes and on suspensions under Art. 23, distinguishing the types of suspension.
quote: providers of online platforms shall include in the reports referred to in that Article information on the following

summary: Providers must publish, in a public section of their interface, average monthly active recipients in the Union, updated at least every six months.
applies_from: By 17 February 2023 and at least once every six months thereafter
quote: By 17 February 2023 and at least once every six months thereafter, providers shall publish for each online platform or online search engine

summary: Providers must communicate average monthly active recipient information to the DSC of establishment and the Commission on request, and submit decisions and statements of reasons under Art. 17(1) to the Commission database without undue delay.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall, without undue delay, submit to the Commission the decisions and the statements of reasons referred to in Article 17(1)
conditional_on: Request by DSC or Commission for Art. 24(3); submission of decisions under Art. 17(1) for Art. 24(5)

summary: The DSC of establishment must inform the Commission where it has reasons to consider a provider meets the 45 million recipient threshold.
quote: it shall inform the Commission thereof.
conditional_on: DSC has reasons to consider threshold met

summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts laying down templates for reports under Art. 24(1).
quote: The Commission may adopt implementing acts to lay down templates concerning the form, content and other details of reports

summary: Online platforms must not design, organise or operate interfaces in a way that deceives or manipulates recipients or materially distorts their free decisions.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall not design, organise or operate their online interfaces in a way that deceives or manipulates the recipients

summary: Online platforms presenting advertisements must ensure recipients can identify each advertisement, its sponsor and payer, and main targeting parameters in real time, and must provide a functionality for recipients to declare commercial communications.
quote: Providers of online platforms that present advertisements on their online interfaces shall ensure that, for each specific advertisement presented to each individual recipient
conditional_on: Platform presents advertisements on its interface

summary: Online platforms must not present advertisements based on profiling using special categories of personal data.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall not present advertisements to recipients of the service based on profiling

summary: Online platforms using recommender systems must set out in their terms and conditions the main parameters and any options to modify them, including the most significant criteria and reasons for their relative importance.
quote: Providers of online platforms that use recommender systems shall set out in their terms and conditions, in plain and intelligible language, the main parameters
conditional_on: Use of recommender systems

summary: Online platforms using recommender systems that rank content must offer a functionality to select and modify the preferred option at any time.
quote: providers of online platforms shall also make available a functionality that allows the recipient of the service to select and to modify at any time their preferred option.
conditional_on: Several options available for recommender systems determining relative order

summary: Online platforms accessible to minors must put in place appropriate and proportionate measures to ensure a high level of privacy, safety and security of minors.
quote: Providers of online platforms accessible to minors shall put in place appropriate and proportionate measures
conditional_on: Platform accessible to minors

summary: Online platforms must not present profiling-based advertisements using personal data when they are aware with reasonable certainty that the recipient is a minor.
quote: Providers of online platform shall not present advertisements on their interface based on profiling
conditional_on: Awareness with reasonable certainty that recipient is a minor

summary: The Commission, after consulting the Board, may issue guidelines to assist online platforms in applying Art. 28(1).
quote: The Commission, after consulting the Board, may issue guidelines to assist providers of online platforms in the application of paragraph 1.

summary: Online platforms allowing consumers to conclude distance contracts with traders must obtain listed trader identification and contact information before traders can use the platform, make best efforts to assess its reliability, and request correction or suspend traders whose information is inaccurate.
quote: Providers of online platforms allowing consumers to conclude distance contracts with traders shall ensure that traders can only use those online platforms
conditional_on: Trader seeks to promote messages or offer products or services to consumers located in the Union

summary: For traders already using the platform on 17 February 2024, platforms must make best efforts to obtain the Art. 30(1) information and suspend traders who fail to provide it.
applies_from: 17 February 2024 (existing traders); information to be obtained within 12 months
quote: the providers shall make best efforts to obtain the information listed from the traders concerned within 12 months.
conditional_on: Trader already using the platform for Art. 30(1) purposes on 17 February 2024

summary: Platforms must store trader information in a secure manner for six months after the end of the contractual relationship and then delete it.
quote: shall store the information obtained pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2 in a secure manner for a period of six months after the end of the contractual relationship

summary: Platforms may disclose trader information to third parties only where required by applicable law or orders.
quote: shall only disclose the information to third parties where so required in accordance with the applicable law

summary: Platforms must make trader identity, address and self-certification information available to recipients on the online platform and where products are presented.
quote: shall make the information referred to in paragraph 1, points (a), (d) and (e) available on its online platform to the recipients of the service

summary: Platforms must design their interface to enable traders to provide required pre-contractual, compliance and product safety information and identification details.
quote: shall ensure that its online interface is designed and organised in a way that enables traders to comply with their obligations

summary: Platforms must make best efforts to assess whether traders have provided the required information before allowing them to offer products, and make reasonable efforts to randomly check illegal product databases afterwards.
quote: shall make best efforts to assess whether such traders have provided the information referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2

summary: On becoming aware of an illegal product offered by a trader, platforms must inform consumers who purchased it within the prior six months of its illegality, the trader's identity and redress means, where contact details are available.
quote: that provider shall inform, insofar as it has their contact details, consumers who purchased the illegal product or service
conditional_on: Platform becomes aware that an illegal product or service was offered by a trader

summary: Where platforms lack contact details of all affected consumers, they must publish the illegal product information, trader identity and redress means on their interface.
quote: that provider shall make publicly available and easily accessible on its online interface the information concerning the illegal product
conditional_on: Platform does not have contact details of all affected consumers

summary: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts to adjust the 45 million recipient threshold when Union population changes by at least 5 percent; the Commission may adopt delegated acts laying down the calculation methodology.
quote: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 87 to adjust the number of average monthly active recipients
conditional_on: Union population increases or decreases by at least 5 %

summary: The Commission adopts decisions designating platforms and search engines as very large (45 million recipients), notifies them, and publishes and maintains the list in the Official Journal.
applies_from: Four months after notification to the provider
quote: The Commission shall take its decision on the basis of data reported by the provider
conditional_on: Average monthly active recipients equal to or above 45 million

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must diligently identify, analyse and assess systemic risks, including the listed categories, at least annually and before deploying functionalities likely to have critical impact.
applies_from: By the date of application referred to in Art. 33(6)
quote: Providers of very large online platforms and of very large online search engines shall diligently identify, analyse and assess any systemic risks
conditional_on: Very large online platform or very large search engine (Art. 33)

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must preserve supporting documents of risk assessments for at least three years and communicate them on request to the Commission and DSC of establishment.
quote: shall preserve the supporting documents of the risk assessments for at least three years after the performance of risk assessments
conditional_on: Very large online platform or very large search engine (Art. 33)

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must put in place reasonable, proportionate and effective mitigation measures tailored to identified systemic risks, which may include listed measures such as design adaptation, moderation changes, testing of algorithms and protection of minors.
quote: shall put in place reasonable, proportionate and effective mitigation measures, tailored to the specific systemic risks identified pursuant to Article 34
conditional_on: Systemic risks identified under Art. 34

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must ensure that generated or manipulated images, audio or video resembling existing persons and falsely appearing authentic are distinguishable through prominent markings, and provide a functionality for recipients to indicate such content.
quote: is distinguishable through prominent markings when presented on their online interfaces
conditional_on: Generated or manipulated content that falsely appears authentic

summary: The Board, with the Commission, publishes annual reports on systemic risks; the Commission may issue guidelines on mitigation measures after public consultation.
quote: The Board, in cooperation with the Commission, shall publish comprehensive reports, once a year.

summary: Under a Commission crisis decision, very large platforms and search engines must assess their contribution to serious threats and apply specified measures for up to three months.
quote: requiring one or more providers of very large online platforms or of very large online search engines to take one or more of the following actions
conditional_on: Commission decision under Art. 36(1) following a crisis under Art. 36(2)

summary: Providers subject to a crisis decision must report to the Commission on assessments and measures taken, by the date or at the intervals specified in the decision.
quote: report to the Commission by a certain date or at regular intervals specified in the decision
conditional_on: Commission decision under Art. 36(1)

summary: The Commission must, after adopting a crisis decision, notify it to the provider, make it publicly available and inform the Board; it must report to Parliament and Council yearly and three months after the crisis.
quote: After adopting the decision referred to in paragraph 1, the Commission shall, without undue delay, take the following steps
conditional_on: Adoption of a crisis decision under Art. 36(1)

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must be subject, at their own expense and at least annually, to independent audits of compliance with Chapter III and their codes and crisis protocol commitments, afford auditors full cooperation, and ensure each audit produces a substantiated report with a listed content and opinion.
quote: shall be subject, at their own expense and at least once a year, to independent audits to assess compliance with the following
conditional_on: Very large online platform or very large search engine (Art. 33)

summary: Audit organisations must be independent of the audited provider, meet listed conditions on non-audit services, tenure, fee structure, expertise and objectivity.
quote: Audits performed pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be performed by organisations which:
conditional_on: Audit performed under Art. 37(1)

summary: Providers must adopt an audit implementation report within one month of receiving a non-positive audit report, setting out measures or justifying non-implementation.
applies_from: Within one month from receiving the operational recommendations
quote: They shall, within one month from receiving those recommendations, adopt an audit implementation report
conditional_on: Audit report that is not positive

summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts setting rules for audit procedures, methodologies and templates.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 87 to supplement this Regulation by laying down the necessary rules for the performance of the audits

summary: Very large platforms and search engines using recommender systems must provide at least one option not based on profiling for each recommender system.
quote: shall provide at least one option for each of their recommender systems which is not based on profiling
conditional_on: Use of recommender systems

summary: Very large platforms and search engines presenting advertisements must compile and publish a searchable advertisement repository with listed information for the period of presentation and one year afterwards, without personal data.
quote: shall compile and make publicly available in a specific section of their online interface, through a searchable and reliable tool
conditional_on: Very large online platform or very large search engine presenting advertisements

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must provide data access to the DSC of establishment or the Commission on reasoned request, explain their algorithmic systems on request, and provide data access to vetted researchers on reasoned request.
applies_from: Within the period specified in the request
quote: shall provide the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment or the Commission, at their reasoned request and within a reasonable period specified in that request, access to data
conditional_on: Reasoned request by DSC of establishment or Commission

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must give researchers without undue delay access to publicly accessible real-time data where technically possible.
quote: shall give access without undue delay to data, including, where technically possible, to real-time data
conditional_on: Data publicly accessible in their interface; researchers meeting Art. 40(8) conditions

summary: DSCs of establishment grant vetted researcher status on application, issue reasoned data-access requests, may terminate access, and communicate researcher names to the Board.
quote: the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment shall grant such researchers the status of
conditional_on: Substantiated application from researchers

summary: The Commission, after consulting the Board, shall adopt delegated acts laying down technical conditions and purposes for data sharing under Art. 40(1) and (4).
quote: The Commission shall, after consulting the Board, adopt delegated acts supplementing this Regulation by laying down the technical conditions

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must establish an independent compliance function with compliance officers and a head reporting to the management body, with listed tasks, and the management body must define governance, approve risk strategies at least annually and devote time to risk management.
quote: shall establish a compliance function, which is independent from their operational functions and composed of one or more compliance officers
conditional_on: Very large online platform or very large search engine (Art. 33)

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must communicate the name and contact details of the head of the compliance function to the DSC of establishment and the Commission.
quote: shall communicate the name and contact details of the head of the compliance function to the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment and to the Commission.
conditional_on: Very large online platform or very large search engine (Art. 33)

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must publish transparency reports at least every six months, first within two months of the application date, including human resources for content moderation, staff qualifications and accuracy indicators by language.
applies_from: Within two months from the date of application referred to in Art. 33(6)
quote: shall publish the reports referred to in Article 15 at the latest by two months from the date of application
conditional_on: Very large online platform or very large search engine (Art. 33)

summary: Very large platforms and search engines must transmit to the DSC of establishment and the Commission, and publish within three months of each audit report, the risk assessment results, mitigation measures, audit report and audit implementation report.
quote: shall transmit to the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment and the Commission, without undue delay upon completion, and make publicly available
conditional_on: Completion of risk assessment or receipt of audit report

summary: The Commission charges very large platforms and search engines an annual supervisory fee upon designation, capped under the listed principles, and reports annually to Parliament and Council on costs.
quote: The Commission shall charge providers of very large online platforms and of very large online search engines an annual supervisory fee upon their designation
conditional_on: Designation under Art. 33

summary: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts laying down the methodology for estimating costs and individual supervisory fees.
quote: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts, in accordance with Article 87, laying down the detailed methodology and procedures for

summary: The Commission shall consult the Board and support and promote voluntary standards for listed areas, and update them in light of technological developments.
quote: The Commission shall consult the Board, and shall support and promote the development and implementation of voluntary standards

summary: The Commission and the Board encourage and facilitate voluntary codes of conduct at Union level and assess and monitor them.
quote: The Commission and the Board shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of voluntary codes of conduct at Union level

summary: The Commission encourages and facilitates voluntary codes of conduct for online advertising transparency beyond Arts. 26 and 39.
quote: The Commission shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of voluntary codes of conduct at Union level

summary: The Commission shall encourage development and application of advertising codes of conduct on the stated timetable.
applies_from: Development by 18 February 2025; application by 18 August 2025
quote: The Commission shall encourage the development of the codes of conduct by 18 February 2025 and their application by 18 August 2025.

summary: Actors in the online advertising value chain are encouraged to endorse and comply with the commitments in advertising codes of conduct.
quote: to endorse the commitments stated in the codes of conduct, and to comply with them.

summary: The Commission shall encourage and facilitate accessibility codes of conduct for online services addressing persons with disabilities.
quote: The Commission shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of conduct at Union level

summary: The Commission shall encourage development and application of accessibility codes of conduct on the stated timetable.
applies_from: Development by 18 February 2025; application by 18 August 2025
quote: The Commission shall encourage the development of the codes of conduct by 18 February 2025 and their application by 18 August 2025.

summary: The Commission shall encourage and facilitate providers of very large platforms and search engines to participate in crisis protocols, and may request revision of protocols that fail to address the crisis effectively.
quote: The Commission shall encourage and facilitate the providers of very large online platforms, of very large online search engines
conditional_on: Extraordinary circumstances affecting public security or public health

summary: Member States must designate one or more competent authorities responsible for supervising intermediary service providers and enforcing the Regulation, one of which is the Digital Services Coordinator.
quote: Member States shall designate one or more competent authorities to be responsible for the supervision of providers of intermediary services

summary: Member States must designate the Digital Services Coordinators and make the designated authority public, communicating it to the Commission and the Board.
quote: Member States shall designate the Digital Services Coordinators by 17 February 2024.

summary: Member States must ensure Digital Services Coordinators perform tasks impartially, transparently and timely with sufficient resources and act with complete independence.
quote: Member States shall ensure that their Digital Services Coordinators perform their tasks under this Regulation in an impartial, transparent and timely manner.

summary: Member States must lay down specific rules and procedures for exercise of DSC investigation and enforcement powers, with safeguards.
quote: Member States shall lay down specific rules and procedures for the exercise of the powers pursuant to paragraphs 1, 2 and 3

summary: Digital Services Coordinators must assess complaints lodged by recipients and transmit them to the DSC of establishment or another competent authority where appropriate.
quote: The Digital Services Coordinator shall assess the complaint and, where appropriate, transmit it to the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment
conditional_on: Complaint lodged under Art. 53

summary: Digital Services Coordinators must draw up annual public, machine-readable reports on their activities, including complaints received and orders under Arts. 9 and 10.
quote: Digital Services Coordinators shall draw up annual reports on their activities under this Regulation

summary: Member States and the Commission must supervise and enforce the Regulation in close cooperation.
quote: Member States and the Commission shall supervise and enforce the provisions of this Regulation in close cooperation.

summary: Digital Services Coordinators must cooperate and provide mutual assistance; a receiving coordinator must comply with information requests and inform the DSC of establishment within two months or give a reasoned refusal.
quote: shall comply with such request and inform the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment about the action taken, without undue delay and no later than two months after its receipt
conditional_on: Request for mutual assistance under Art. 57(2)

summary: The DSC of establishment must communicate its assessment and measures to the requesting DSC and the Board, not later than two months after the request.
quote: shall, without undue delay and in any event not later than two months following receipt of the request
conditional_on: Request under Art. 58(1) or (2)

summary: The Commission must assess a matter referred by the Board within two months and, where insufficient, request the DSC of establishment to review it.
provision: The Commission shall assess the matter within two months following the referral of the matter pursuant to paragraph 1.
quote: The Commission shall assess the matter within two months following the referral of the matter pursuant to paragraph 1
conditional_on: Referral under Art. 59(1)

summary: Joint investigations must be concluded within three months of launch unless otherwise agreed, and the DSC of establishment must communicate its preliminary position within one month after that deadline.
provision: The joint investigation shall be concluded within three months from its launch
quote: The joint investigation shall be concluded within three months from its launch, unless otherwise agreed amongst the participants.
conditional_on: Joint investigation launched under Art. 60(1)

summary: The Commission chairs the Board, convenes its meetings and prepares the agenda, provides administrative and analytical support, and the Board adopts rules of procedure with Commission consent.
provision: The Commission shall convene the meetings and prepare the agenda
quote: The Commission shall convene the meetings and prepare the agenda

summary: Digital Services Coordinators and other competent authorities that do not follow Board opinions, requests or recommendations must give reasons for that choice.
quote: shall provide the reasons for this choice, including an explanation on the investigations, actions and the measures
conditional_on: Non-following of Board opinions, requests or recommendations

summary: The Commission, with DSCs, must develop Union expertise and capabilities and coordinate assessment of systemic and emerging issues for very large platforms and search engines.
provision: The Commission, in cooperation with the Digital Services Coordinators and the Board, shall develop Union expertise and capabilities
quote: The Commission, in cooperation with the Digital Services Coordinators and the Board, shall develop Union expertise and capabilities

summary: The Commission must notify all DSCs and the Board when it initiates proceedings against a very large platform or search engine, and DSCs must transmit information they hold on the alleged infringement.
quote: it shall notify all Digital Services Coordinators and the Board through the information sharing system
conditional_on: Commission initiates proceedings under Art. 66(1)

summary: Providers of very large platforms and search engines must supply information requested by the Commission by simple request or decision, through their representatives or lawyers, remaining responsible for its completeness.
applies_from: Within the period set in the request
provision: shall supply the information requested on behalf of the provider of the very large online platform
quote: shall supply the information requested on behalf of the provider of the very large online platform or of the very large online search engine concerned
conditional_on: Request for information under Art. 67(1)

summary: The Commission must state the legal basis, purpose, information required and time limit in any request for information, including fines for incorrect information, and send copies of requests and decisions to DSCs.
quote: the Commission shall state the legal basis and the purpose of the request, specify what information is required
conditional_on: Request for information under Art. 67(1)

summary: Providers of very large platforms and search engines must submit to an inspection ordered by Commission decision.
provision: shall be required to submit to an inspection ordered by decision of the Commission
quote: shall be required to submit to an inspection ordered by decision of the Commission
conditional_on: Commission inspection decision under Art. 69(6)

summary: Before adopting decisions under Arts. 73, 74 or 76, the Commission must give the provider the opportunity to be heard on preliminary findings and intended measures.
provision: the Commission shall give the provider of the very large online platform or of the very large online search engine concerned
quote: the Commission shall give the provider of the very large online platform or of the very large online search engine concerned
conditional_on: Adoption of a decision under Art. 73(1), 74 or 76

summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts of general scope specifying electronic information-exchange arrangements between supervisory authorities and the Board, following the examination procedure.
quote: The Commission may adopt implementing acts of general scope in order to specify the arrangements for the exchange of information by electronic means

summary: The Board ensures consistent application of the Regulation, issues guidelines, recommendations and best practices (including on profiling, breach notification, transfers), consults interested parties, and forwards its opinions to the Commission and make them public.
quote: The Board shall ensure the consistent application of this Regulation.

summary: The Board draws up an annual report on the protection of natural persons in the Union, made public and transmitted to Parliament, Council and Commission, including review of guidelines and binding decisions.
quote: The Board shall draw up an annual report regarding the protection of natural persons with regard to processing in the Union

summary: The Board adopts its own rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority of its members and organises its operational arrangements.
quote: The Board shall adopt its own rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority of its members

summary: The Chair of the Board convenes its meetings and prepares the agenda, notifies decisions under Art. 65, and ensures timely performance of the Board's tasks.
quote: to convene the meetings of the Board and prepare its agenda;

summary: The Board's secretariat is provided by the European Data Protection Supervisor and performs its tasks under the Chair's instructions.
quote: The Board shall have a secretariat, which shall be provided by the European Data Protection Supervisor.

summary: The supervisory authority with which a complaint is lodged must inform the complainant of progress and outcome, including the possibility of judicial remedy under Art. 78.
quote: The supervisory authority with which the complaint has been lodged shall inform the complainant on the progress and the outcome of the complaint

summary: A court of a Member State that learns of parallel proceedings on the same subject matter in another Member State must contact that court to confirm them.
quote: it shall contact that court in the other Member State to confirm the existence of such proceedings.
conditional_on: Information on pending proceedings concerning the same processing in another Member State

summary: Member States must by law reconcile data protection with freedom of expression and information, including journalistic, academic, artistic or literary purposes, and provide exemptions or derogations where necessary.
quote: Member States shall by law reconcile the right to the protection of personal data pursuant to this Regulation with the right to freedom of expression and information
conditional_on: Processing for journalistic, academic, artistic or literary purposes (Art. 85(2))

summary: Employment-context rules adopted by Member States by law or collective agreement must include suitable and specific measures safeguarding dignity, legitimate interests and fundamental rights, and be notified to the Commission by 25 May 2018.
quote: Those rules shall include suitable and specific measures to safeguard the data subject's human dignity, legitimate interests and fundamental rights
conditional_on: Member States adopt more specific employment rules under Art. 88(1)

summary: Processing for archiving, scientific or historical research or statistical purposes must be subject to safeguards, including technical and organisational measures ensuring data minimisation, pseudonymisation where possible, and anonymisation where purposes can be met that way.
quote: Those safeguards shall ensure that technical and organisational measures are in place in particular in order to ensure respect for the principle of data minimisation.
conditional_on: Processing for archiving in the public interest, research or statistical purposes

summary: Each Member State notifies the Commission of the rules adopted under Art. 90(1) on supervisory powers over controllers or processors subject to professional secrecy, and of later amendments.
quote: Each Member State shall notify to the Commission the rules adopted pursuant to paragraph 1, by 25 May 2018
conditional_on: Member State adopts rules under Art. 90(1)

summary: Power to adopt delegated acts conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period from 24 May 2016 (for Art. 12(8) and Art. 43(8)); the Commission must notify each delegated act simultaneously to Parliament and Council.
quote: The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.
conditional_on: Subject to the conditions of Art. 92; revocable under Art. 92(3)

summary: The Commission submits a report on the evaluation and review of the Regulation to Parliament and Council by 25 May 2020 and every four years thereafter, examining Chapter V and Chapter VII and proposing amendments if necessary.
applies_from: By 25 May 2020 and every four years thereafter (Art. 97(1))
quote: By 25 May 2020 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a report on the evaluation and review of this Regulation

summary: The Commission submits legislative proposals, if appropriate, to amend other Union data protection legal acts for uniform and consistent protection.
quote: The Commission shall, if appropriate, submit legislative proposals with a view to amending other Union legal acts on the protection of personal data
conditional_on: If appropriate

summary: Entities, competent authorities, single points of contact and CSIRTs process personal data only to the extent necessary for the Directive and in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679.
quote: Entities, the competent authorities, the single points of contact and the CSIRTs shall process personal data to the extent necessary for the purposes of this Directive

summary: Confidential information is exchanged with the Commission and other authorities only where necessary for the application of the Directive, limited to what is relevant and proportionate, and its confidentiality is preserved.
quote: shall be exchanged with the Commission and other relevant authorities in accordance with this Directive only where that exchange is necessary for the application of this Directive

summary: Member States must adopt national cybersecurity strategies and designate or establish competent authorities, cyber crisis management authorities, single points of contact and CSIRTs (obligations stated in the scope of the Directive).
quote: obligations that require Member States to adopt national cybersecurity strategies

summary: Member States establish a list of essential and important entities and entities providing domain name registration services, and review and update it at least every two years thereafter.
quote: By 17 April 2025, Member States shall establish a list of essential and important entities

summary: Entities listed under Art. 3(3) submit to the competent authorities their name, address and up-to-date contact details, sector and subsector, and Member States where they provide services, and notify changes within two weeks of the change.
quote: Member States shall require the entities referred to in that paragraph to submit at least the following information to the competent authorities

summary: Competent authorities notify the Commission and the Cooperation Group of the number of essential and important entities per sector and subsector, and notify the Commission of further information on entities identified under Art. 2(2)(b) to (e).
quote: By 17 April 2025 and every two years thereafter, the competent authorities shall notify:

summary: The Commission provides guidelines clarifying the application of the sector-specific Union legal act provisions in Art. 4(1) and (2).
quote: The Commission shall, by 17 July 2023, provide guidelines clarifying the application of paragraphs 1 and 2.

summary: Each Member State adopts a national cybersecurity strategy with strategic objectives, resources, policy and regulatory measures, including the listed elements (governance, risk assessment, preparedness, policies on supply chain, procurement, vulnerabilities, education, active cyber protection); strategy is assessed on a regular basis and at least every five years.
quote: Each Member State shall adopt a national cybersecurity strategy that provides for the strategic objectives

summary: Member States notify their national cybersecurity strategies to the Commission within three months of their adoption, and may exclude national security information.
quote: Member States shall notify their national cybersecurity strategies to the Commission within three months of their adoption.

summary: Member States designate or establish one or more competent authorities for cybersecurity and supervisory tasks, and a single point of contact; they ensure adequate resources for these authorities and the single point of contact.
quote: Each Member State shall designate or establish one or more competent authorities responsible for cybersecurity

summary: Each Member State notifies the Commission without undue delay of the identity of the competent authority and single point of contact, their tasks and any changes, and makes the identity of its competent authority public.
quote: Each Member State shall notify the Commission without undue delay of the identity of the competent authority

summary: Each Member State designates or establishes one or more cyber crisis management authorities, ensures their adequate resources, identifies crisis capabilities, and adopts a national large-scale cybersecurity incident and crisis response plan with the elements listed.
quote: Each Member State shall designate or establish one or more competent authorities responsible for the management of large-scale cybersecurity incidents and crises

summary: Member States notify the Commission of the identity of the cyber crisis management authority within three months of its designation, and submit response plan information to the Commission and EU-CyCLONe within three months of adoption of the plans.
quote: Within three months of the designation or establishment of the cyber crisis management authority referred to in paragraph 1, each Member State shall notify the Commission

summary: Member States designate or establish one or more CSIRTs covering the sectors in Annexes I and II, ensure they have adequate resources and a secure communication and information infrastructure, and ensure their cooperation in the CSIRTs network and with entities and third-country CSIRTs.
quote: Each Member State shall designate or establish one or more CSIRTs.

summary: Each Member State notifies the Commission without undue delay of the identity of its CSIRTs and of the CSIRT designated as coordinator, and of their tasks and any changes.
quote: Each Member State shall notify the Commission without undue delay of the identity of the CSIRT referred to in paragraph 1

summary: CSIRTs comply with listed requirements (communication channels, secure sites, request routing, confidentiality, staffing, redundant systems) and jointly have the technical capabilities for the tasks listed in Art. 11(3), including monitoring, early warnings, incident response, forensic analysis and proactive scanning on request.
quote: The CSIRTs shall comply with the following requirements:

summary: Each Member State designates one of its CSIRTs as coordinator for coordinated vulnerability disclosure, which acts as trusted intermediary and enables anonymous vulnerability reporting, with follow-up and anonymity ensured.
quote: Each Member State shall designate one of its CSIRTs as a coordinator for the purposes of coordinated vulnerability disclosure.

summary: ENISA develops and maintains, after consulting the Cooperation Group, a European vulnerability database with the listed content and security measures.
quote: ENISA shall develop and maintain, after consulting the Cooperation Group, a European vulnerability database.

summary: Competent authorities, single points of contact and CSIRTs of the same Member State cooperate; CSIRTs or competent authorities receive significant incident notifications and incident, cyber threat and near-miss notifications, and inform the single points of contact; and cooperation with listed national authorities is ensured.
quote: Member States shall ensure that their CSIRTs or, where applicable, their competent authorities, receive notifications of significant incidents

summary: Member States simplify reporting through technical means for the notifications referred to in Art. 23 and Art. 30.
quote: Member States shall simplify the reporting through technical means for notifications referred to in Articles 23 and 30.

summary: The Cooperation Group, composed of Member State, Commission and ENISA representatives, carries out the listed tasks (guidance on transposition, information exchange, risk assessments of critical supply chains, mutual assistance discussion, peer review methodology, reports, state-of-play assessments); Member States ensure effective cooperation of their representatives.
quote: The Cooperation Group shall have the following tasks:

summary: The Cooperation Group establishes a biennial work programme on actions to implement its objectives and tasks.
quote: By 1 February 2024 and every two years thereafter, the Cooperation Group shall establish a work programme

summary: The Cooperation Group meets regularly and at least once a year with the Critical Entities Resilience Group established under Directive (EU) 2022/2557.
quote: The Cooperation Group shall meet on a regular basis and in any event at least once a year with the Critical Entities Resilience Group

summary: The CSIRTs network carries out the listed tasks (information exchange, coordinated response, mutual assistance support, cooperation with SOCs, guidelines), and adopts its rules of procedure and procedural arrangements with EU-CyCLONe.
quote: The CSIRTs network shall have the following tasks:

summary: The CSIRTs network assesses progress on operational cooperation and adopts a report, with conclusions and recommendations based on peer reviews, submitted to the Cooperation Group.
quote: By 17 January 2025, and every two years thereafter, the CSIRTs network shall, for the purpose of the review

summary: EU-CyCLONe carries out the listed tasks (preparedness, shared situational awareness, impact assessment, coordination of crisis management, discussion of response plans), adopts its rules of procedure, and reports regularly to the Cooperation Group.
quote: EU-CyCLONe shall have the following tasks:

summary: EU-CyCLONe submits to the European Parliament and the Council a report assessing its work every 18 months.
quote: By 17 July 2024 and every 18 months thereafter, EU-CyCLONe shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report

summary: International agreements concluded by the Union on participation of third countries or international organisations in the Cooperation Group, CSIRTs network and EU-CyCLONe must comply with Union data protection law.
quote: Such agreements shall comply with Union data protection law.

summary: ENISA adopts, with the Commission and the Cooperation Group, a biennial report on the state of cybersecurity in the Union, submits and presents it to the European Parliament, makes it available in machine-readable data, and develops the methodology for the aggregated assessment.
quote: ENISA shall adopt, in cooperation with the Commission and the Cooperation Group, a biennial report on the state of cybersecurity in the Union

summary: The Cooperation Group, with the Commission and ENISA, establishes the methodology and organisational aspects of peer reviews on 17 January 2025.
quote: The Cooperation Group shall, on 17 January 2025, establish, with the assistance of the Commission and ENISA

summary: Member States subject to a peer review notify participating Member States of its scope; peer review experts follow codes of conduct and confidentiality; expert reports are submitted to the Cooperation Group and CSIRTs network.
quote: Before commencing a peer review as referred to in paragraph 1, Member States shall notify the participating Member States of its scope

summary: Member States ensure that management bodies of essential and important entities approve the cybersecurity risk-management measures taken under Art. 21 and oversee their implementation.
quote: Member States shall ensure that the management bodies of essential and important entities approve the cybersecurity risk-management measures

summary: Members of the management bodies of essential and important entities are required to follow cybersecurity training; essential and important entities are encouraged to offer similar training to employees on a regular basis.
quote: Member States shall ensure that the members of the management bodies of essential and important entities are required to follow training

summary: Essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage risks to network and information systems, including the all-hazards measures listed in Art. 21(2) (policies on risk analysis, incident handling, business continuity, supply chain security, vulnerability handling, cryptography, access control, multi-factor authentication and similar); when assessing supplier measures they take into account supplier vulnerabilities and, under Art. 21(3), the results of coordinated supply chain risk assessments; and an entity that finds it does not comply takes without undue delay corrective measures (Art. 21(4)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures

summary: The Commission adopts implementing acts laying down the technical and methodological requirements of the Art. 21(2) measures for DNS service providers, TLD name registries, cloud computing, data centre, content delivery network, managed service, online marketplace, search engine, social networking and trust service providers.
quote: By 17 October 2024, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down the technical and the methodological requirements of the measures referred to in paragraph 2

summary: The Commission, after consulting the Cooperation Group, ENISA and relevant stakeholders, identifies the specific critical ICT services, ICT systems or ICT products that may be subject to coordinated security risk assessments.
quote: The Commission, after consulting the Cooperation Group and ENISA, and, where necessary, relevant stakeholders, shall identify the specific critical ICT services

summary: Essential and important entities must notify their CSIRT or competent authority without undue delay of any significant incident, and report information enabling cross-border impact to be determined. Where appropriate, they must also notify affected service recipients.
quote: Each Member State shall ensure that essential and important entities notify, without undue delay, its CSIRT or, where applicable, its competent authority
conditional_on: Incident has a significant impact on the provision of the entity's services (significant incident as defined in Art. 23(3))

summary: Staged reporting for significant incidents: early warning within 24 hours of awareness (indicating suspected unlawful or malicious acts and possible cross-border impact); incident notification within 72 hours with initial assessment; intermediate report on request; final report within one month of the incident notification. Trust service providers have a 24-hour notification under the derogation in the last subparagraph of Art. 23(4).
applies_from: 24 hours after becoming aware of the significant incident (early warning); 72 hours after becoming aware (incident notification); one month after the incident notification (final report)
quote: without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, an early warning
conditional_on: Significant incident under Art. 23(3); intermediate report only upon request of CSIRT or competent authority

summary: Essential and important entities must communicate to recipients of their services potentially affected by a significant cyber threat any measures or remedies those recipients can take, and where appropriate inform them of the threat itself.
quote: essential and important entities communicate, without undue delay, to the recipients of their services
conditional_on: Where applicable; significant cyber threat

summary: Member States must ensure that the CSIRT or competent authority responds to an early warning within 24 hours where possible, with initial feedback and guidance; that the CSIRT or competent authority informs other affected Member States and ENISA of cross-border incidents; and that the single point of contact forwards notifications to other affected single points of contact on request.
applies_from: Within 24 hours of receiving the early warning, where possible
quote: The CSIRT or the competent authority shall provide, without undue delay and where possible within 24 hours
conditional_on: Upon receipt of an early warning or notification under Art. 23(4)

summary: The single point of contact must submit a summary report on significant incidents, incidents, cyber threats and near misses to ENISA every three months; ENISA must inform the Cooperation Group and CSIRTs network every six months.
applies_from: Every three months (summary report); every six months (ENISA findings)
quote: The single point of contact shall submit to ENISA every three months a summary report

summary: The Commission must adopt implementing acts further specifying the criteria for a significant incident for DNS service providers, TLD name registries, cloud computing, data centre, content delivery network, managed service and managed security service providers, and online marketplace, search engine and social network providers. Under the same paragraph the Commission may adopt such acts for other essential and important entities.
quote: By 17 October 2024, the Commission shall, with regard to DNS service providers

summary: Member States may require essential and important entities to use particular ICT products, services and processes certified under European cybersecurity certification schemes, and shall encourage the use of qualified trust services.
quote: Member States may require essential and important entities to use particular ICT products
conditional_on: To demonstrate compliance with particular requirements of Art. 21

summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts specifying which categories of essential and important entities must use certified ICT products or obtain certificates; such acts require an impact assessment and consultations beforehand and must include an implementation period.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts, in accordance with Article 38
conditional_on: Where insufficient levels of cybersecurity have been identified

summary: Member States must encourage the use of European and international standards and technical specifications relevant to the security of network and information systems, without favouring a particular technology.
quote: Member States shall, without imposing or discriminating in favour of the use of a particular type of technology, encourage the use of European and international standards

summary: ENISA, in cooperation with Member States, must draw up advice and guidelines on technical areas relevant to standardisation and existing standards.
quote: ENISA, in cooperation with Member States, and, where appropriate, after consulting relevant stakeholders, shall draw up advice and guidelines
conditional_on: Where appropriate, after consulting relevant stakeholders

summary: Entities referred to in Art. 26(1)(b) (DNS, TLD, domain registration, cloud, data centre, CDN, managed service, online marketplace, search engine and social network providers) not established in the Union but offering services in the Union must designate a representative in one of the Member States where services are offered.
quote: it shall designate a representative in the Union
conditional_on: Entity not established in the Union but offers services within the Union

summary: Member States that receive a request for mutual assistance may take supervisory and enforcement measures within the limits of that request.
quote: may, within the limits of that request, take appropriate supervisory and enforcement measures
conditional_on: Request for mutual assistance in relation to an entity under Art. 26(1)(b)

summary: ENISA must create and maintain a registry of the entities listed in Art. 27(1) (DNS, TLD, domain registration, cloud, data centre, CDN, managed service, managed security service, online marketplace, search engine and social network providers) based on information from single points of contact.
quote: ENISA shall create and maintain a registry of DNS service providers

summary: Entities listed in Art. 27(1) (including DNS service providers, TLD registries, domain registration service providers, cloud, data centre, CDN, managed service, managed security service, online marketplace, search engine and social network providers) must submit to the competent authorities their name, sector, address, contact details, Member States served and IP ranges.
quote: Member States shall require entities referred to in paragraph 1 to submit the following information to the competent authorities by 17 January 2025

summary: Entities listed in Art. 27(1) must notify the competent authority of any change to the information submitted under Art. 27(2).
applies_from: Without delay and in any event within three months of the date of the change
quote: notify the competent authority about any changes to the information they submitted under paragraph 2 without delay and in any event within three months of the date of the change
conditional_on: Change to information previously submitted

summary: The single point of contact must forward registration information received under Art. 27(2) and (3), except IP ranges, to ENISA without undue delay.
quote: the single point of contact of the Member State concerned shall, without undue delay, forward it to ENISA
conditional_on: Upon receipt of information under Art. 27(2) and (3)

summary: TLD name registries and domain name registration service providers must collect and maintain accurate and complete domain name registration data in a dedicated database, with due diligence under Union data protection law; the database must contain the information listed in Art. 28(2).
quote: Member States shall require TLD name registries and entities providing domain name registration services to collect and maintain accurate and complete domain name registration data

summary: Member States must require TLD name registries and domain name registration service providers to collect and maintain the registration data in Art. 28(1) and (2) and to have policies and procedures, including verification procedures, for accuracy.
quote: have policies and procedures, including verification procedures, in place to ensure that the databases referred to in paragraph 1 include accurate and complete information

summary: TLD name registries and domain name registration service providers must make publicly available their verification policies and procedures, and the domain name registration data that is not personal data, without undue delay after registration.
applies_from: Without undue delay after the registration of a domain name
quote: make publicly available, without undue delay after the registration of a domain name, the domain name registration data which are not personal data
conditional_on: Registration data that is not personal data

summary: TLD name registries and domain name registration service providers must provide access to specific registration data on lawful and duly substantiated requests from legitimate access seekers, reply to such requests within 72 hours, and make disclosure policies publicly available.
applies_from: Within 72 hours of receipt of any request for access
quote: reply without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of receipt of any requests for access
conditional_on: Lawful and duly substantiated request by legitimate access seekers

summary: TLD name registries and domain name registration service providers must cooperate with each other to avoid duplicated collection of registration data.
quote: to that end, Member States shall require TLD name registries and entities providing domain name registration services to cooperate with each other

summary: Member States must facilitate the establishment of cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements among essential and important entities and their suppliers or service providers.
quote: Member States shall facilitate the establishment of cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements

summary: Essential and important entities must notify the competent authorities of their participation in cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements, upon entering them, and of their withdrawal once it takes effect.
applies_from: Upon entering into such arrangements, and upon withdrawal taking effect
quote: essential and important entities notify the competent authorities of their participation in the cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements
conditional_on: Participation in arrangements under Art. 29(2)

summary: Member States must process voluntary notifications under Art. 30(1) in accordance with the procedure in Art. 23, and may prioritise mandatory notifications over voluntary ones.
quote: Member States shall process the notifications referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 23
conditional_on: Voluntary notifications submitted to CSIRTs or competent authorities

summary: Competent authorities must effectively supervise and take the measures necessary to ensure compliance with the Directive, and may prioritise supervisory tasks on a risk-based approach.
quote: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities effectively supervise and take the measures necessary to ensure compliance with this Directive.

summary: Competent authorities must work in close cooperation with data protection supervisory authorities when addressing incidents resulting in personal data breaches.
quote: The competent authorities shall work in close cooperation with supervisory authorities under Regulation (EU) 2016/679
conditional_on: Incidents resulting in personal data breaches

summary: For essential entities, competent authorities must state the purpose of information requests and specify the information requested when using their powers under Art. 32(2)(e), (f) or (g); they must also set out detailed reasoning for enforcement measures and notify preliminary findings before adopting them.
quote: the competent authorities shall state the purpose of the request and specify the information requested
conditional_on: When exercising powers under Art. 32(2)(e), (f) or (g); before adopting enforcement measures

summary: Competent authorities for essential entities must inform the competent authorities under Directive (EU) 2022/2557 when acting on entities identified as critical entities, and must cooperate with the competent authorities under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, including informing the Oversight Forum.
quote: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive inform the relevant competent authorities within the same Member State under Directive (EU) 2022/2557
conditional_on: Entity identified as a critical entity under Directive (EU) 2022/2557, or designated as a critical ICT third-party service provider under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554

summary: Competent authorities must take action, where necessary, through ex post supervisory measures when provided with evidence that an important entity does not comply, and must state the purpose of information requests under Art. 33(2)(d), (e) or (f).
quote: Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities take action, where necessary, through ex post supervisory measures
conditional_on: When provided with evidence, indication or information of non-compliance by an important entity

summary: Competent authorities for important entities must cooperate with the competent authorities under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 and inform the Oversight Forum when acting on an important entity designated as a critical ICT third-party service provider.
quote: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive cooperate with the relevant competent authorities of the Member State concerned under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554
conditional_on: Important entity designated as a critical ICT third-party service provider under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554

summary: Member States must notify the Commission of the provisions of laws adopted for imposing fines on entities where no administrative fine system exists, and of any subsequent amending law.
quote: The Member State shall notify to the Commission the provisions of the laws which it adopts pursuant to this paragraph by 17 October 2024
conditional_on: Where the legal system of the Member State does not provide for administrative fines

summary: Where competent authorities become aware that an infringement of Art. 21 or 23 can entail a personal data breach, they must inform the data protection supervisory authorities without undue delay; where another Member State's authority is competent, they must inform it of the potential breach.
quote: they shall, without undue delay, inform the supervisory authorities
conditional_on: Infringement of Art. 21 or 23 that can entail a personal data breach

summary: Member States must lay down rules on penalties applicable to infringements of national measures adopted under the Directive, and notify the Commission of those rules and measures and of subsequent amendments.
quote: Member States shall, by 17 January 2025, notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures

summary: Competent authorities of Member States concerned must cooperate with and assist each other where an entity provides services in more than one Member State, including by informing and consulting each other on measures taken and responding to requests for assistance.
quote: the competent authorities of the Member States concerned shall cooperate with and assist each other as necessary
conditional_on: Entity provides services in more than one Member State, or its network and information systems are located in other Member States

summary: Competent authorities of various Member States may carry out joint supervisory actions where appropriate and by common agreement.
quote: the competent authorities of various Member States may carry out joint supervisory actions
conditional_on: Where appropriate and with common agreement

summary: The power to adopt delegated acts under Art. 24(2) is conferred on the Commission for five years; the delegation may be revoked by Parliament or Council, and delegated acts are subject to objection periods.
applies_from: For a period of five years from 16 January 2023
quote: shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 16 January 2023

summary: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission must consult experts designated by each Member State, and must notify each delegated act simultaneously to Parliament and Council.
quote: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State
conditional_on: Before adopting, or upon adopting, a delegated act

summary: The Commission is to be assisted by a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.
quote: The Commission shall be assisted by a committee.

summary: The Commission must review the functioning of the Directive and report to Parliament and Council, assessing in particular the size of entities and the sectors in Annexes I and II; the review repeats every 36 months.
applies_from: By 17 October 2027 and every 36 months thereafter
quote: By 17 October 2027 and every 36 months thereafter, the Commission shall review the functioning of this Directive

summary: Member States must adopt and publish the measures necessary to comply with the Directive and inform the Commission; they must apply those measures from 18 October 2024.
applies_from: By 17 October 2024 (adoption and publication); from 18 October 2024 (application)
quote: By 17 October 2024, Member States shall adopt and publish the measures necessary to comply with this Directive.

summary: Relevant entities (DNS service providers, TLD registries, cloud, data centre, CDN, managed and managed security service providers, online marketplaces, search engines, social networking platforms, trust service providers) must ensure a level of network and information system security appropriate to the risks, taking into account their exposure, size, incident likelihood and severity.
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall ensure a level of security of network and information systems appropriate to the risks posed
