summary: Where a relevant entity considers a technical or methodological requirement with 'where appropriate', 'where applicable' or 'to the extent feasible' not appropriate, not applicable or not feasible, it must document its reasoning in a comprehensible manner.
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entity shall in a comprehensible manner document its reasoning to that effect
conditional_on: where the entity considers a requirement not appropriate, not applicable or not feasible

summary: Relevant entities must consider the listed categories when counting users impacted by an incident (customers with access contracts, and natural and legal persons associated with business customers), for the purposes of Articles 7 and 9 to 14.
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall consider all of the following
conditional_on: when counting users impacted by an incident

summary: Annex point 1: the policy on the security of network and information systems must set out the approach, objectives, commitments, roles, documentation, indicators and approval date listed in point 1.1.1, be reviewed at least annually, and responsibilities must be assigned to roles and reported to management bodies (points 1.1-1.2).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the policy on the security of network and information systems shall:

summary: Relevant entities must require all personnel and third parties to apply network and information system security in accordance with the established security policy and procedures (point 1.2.2).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall require all personnel and third parties to apply network and information system security

summary: Annex point 2: relevant entities must establish and maintain a risk management framework, perform and document risk assessments, establish a risk treatment plan, follow a risk management process listed in point 2.1.2 and review it at least annually.
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall perform and document risk assessments

summary: Relevant entities must regularly review compliance with their security policies and operate an effective compliance reporting system to the management bodies (points 2.2.1-2.2.3).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall regularly review the compliance with their policies on network and information system security

summary: Relevant entities must independently review their approach to network and information system security at planned intervals, through individuals with appropriate audit competence, with results reported to management bodies (points 2.3.1-2.3.4).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall review independently their approach to managing network and information system security

summary: Relevant entities must establish and implement an incident handling policy covering detection, analysis, containment, response, recovery, documentation and reporting of incidents, coherent with the business continuity plan (points 3.1.1-3.1.3).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall establish and implement an incident handling policy

summary: Relevant entities must monitor and log activity on their network and information systems, maintain, document and review logs, keep logs for a predefined period, and protect them from unauthorised access (points 3.2.1-3.2.7).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall maintain, document, and review logs

summary: Relevant entities must put in place a simple mechanism for employees, suppliers and customers to report suspicious events, and train employees on its use (points 3.3.1-3.3.2).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall put in place a simple mechanism allowing their employees, suppliers, and customers to report suspicious events.

summary: Relevant entities must assess suspicious events to determine whether they are incidents and their nature and severity, using predefined criteria and triage, and reassess events when new information becomes available (points 3.4.1-3.4.2).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall assess suspicious events to determine whether they constitute incidents

summary: Relevant entities must establish communication plans and procedures with CSIRTs or, where applicable, competent authorities related to incident notification, and for internal and external communication (points 3.5.3-3.5.4).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall establish communication plans and procedures

summary: Relevant entities must test their incident response procedures at planned intervals (point 3.5.5); post-incident reviews are to be carried out where appropriate (point 3.6).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall test at planned intervals their incident response procedures.

summary: Annex point 4: relevant entities must lay down and maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan, and a crisis management process (points 4.1.1, 4.3.1-4.3.2).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall lay down and maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan

summary: Relevant entities must carry out a business impact analysis of severe disruptions and establish continuity requirements for network and information systems on that basis (point 4.1.3).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall carry out a business impact analysis

summary: Business continuity and disaster recovery plans must be tested, reviewed and updated at planned intervals and after significant incidents (point 4.1.4); backup recovery must be regularly tested and results documented (point 4.2.6).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The business continuity plan and disaster recovery plan shall be tested, reviewed and, where appropriate, updated at planned intervals

summary: Relevant entities must maintain backup copies of data and sufficient redundant resources, with backup plans, storage, access controls and integrity checks (points 4.2.1-4.2.5).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall maintain backup copies of data

summary: Relevant entities must implement a process for managing information received from CSIRTs or competent authorities on incidents, vulnerabilities, threats or mitigation measures (point 4.3.3).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall implement a process for managing and making use of information received from the CSIRTs

summary: Annex point 5: relevant entities must establish, implement and apply a supply chain security policy and criteria to select and contract suppliers and service providers, and review the policy at planned intervals (points 5.1.1-5.1.2, 5.1.6-5.1.7).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall establish, implement and apply a supply chain security policy

summary: Relevant entities must ensure that contracts with suppliers and service providers specify cybersecurity requirements, training, background verification, incident notification, audit rights, vulnerability handling, subcontracting and termination obligations, where appropriate (point 5.1.4).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall ensure that their contracts with the suppliers and service providers specify
conditional_on: where appropriate, including through service level agreements

summary: Relevant entities must maintain and keep up to date a registry of their direct suppliers and service providers, with contact points and a list of ICT products, services and processes provided (point 5.2).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: shall maintain and keep up to date a registry of their direct suppliers and service providers

summary: Annex point 6: relevant entities must manage risks from acquisition of ICT products and services, set secure development rules, configuration, change management, patch management, network security, segmentation, malicious software and vulnerability handling measures (points 6.1-6.4, 6.6-6.10).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall set and implement processes to manage risks stemming from the acquisition of ICT services or ICT products

summary: Relevant entities must establish, implement and apply a policy and procedures for security testing, including test need, scope, frequency, documentation and mitigation of critical findings (points 6.5.1-6.5.3).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall establish, implement and apply a policy and procedures for security testing.

summary: Relevant entities must establish, implement and apply a policy and procedures to assess whether cybersecurity risk-management measures are effectively implemented and maintained (points 7.1-7.3).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall establish, implement and apply a policy and procedures to assess whether the cybersecurity risk-management measures

summary: Annex point 8: relevant entities must ensure employees, management body members and direct suppliers are aware of risks and apply cyber hygiene, through a scheduled awareness programme, and must provide regular security training to staff with security-relevant roles (points 8.1-8.2).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall ensure that their employees, including members of management bodies, as well as direct suppliers and service providers are aware of risks

summary: Relevant entities must establish, implement and apply a policy and procedures on cryptography, covering cryptographic measures, algorithms and key management (points 9.1-9.3).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall establish, implement and apply a policy and procedures related to cryptography

summary: Annex point 10: relevant entities must ensure employees and direct suppliers understand and commit to security responsibilities and that mechanisms exist for qualified hiring, and must apply the background-verification and disciplinary and termination requirements in points 10.2-10.4.
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall ensure that their employees and direct suppliers and service providers, wherever applicable, understand and commit to their security responsibilities

summary: Relevant entities must ensure, to the extent feasible, background verification of employees (and where applicable direct suppliers) where necessary for their role, and verification before such persons exercise the relevant roles (points 10.2.1-10.2.2).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall ensure to the extent feasible verification of the background of their employees
conditional_on: to the extent feasible and if necessary for the role

summary: Relevant entities must contractually define post-employment security duties (point 10.3) and establish, communicate and maintain a disciplinary process for violations of security policies (point 10.4).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall establish, communicate and maintain a disciplinary process for handling violations

summary: Annex point 11: relevant entities must establish and implement logical and physical access control policies, manage access rights, privileged and administration accounts, identities, authentication and multi-factor authentication (points 11.1-11.7).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall establish, document and implement logical and physical access control policies

summary: Relevant entities must lay down classification levels for all assets and a policy for handling assets, removable media and asset disposal (points 12.1-12.3, 12.5).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall lay down classification levels of all assets

summary: Relevant entities must develop and maintain a complete, accurate, up-to-date and consistent inventory of their assets, with changes recorded in a traceable manner (points 12.4.1-12.4.3).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: The relevant entities shall develop and maintain a complete, accurate, up-to-date and consistent inventory of their assets.

summary: Annex point 13: relevant entities must prevent loss, damage or compromise of network and information systems from supporting utility failures and physical and environmental threats, and prevent and monitor unauthorised physical access (points 13.1-13.3).
applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
quote: the relevant entities shall prevent loss, damage or compromise of network and information systems

summary: Public sector bodies process re-use requests electronically where possible, within a reasonable time (no fixed time limits apply where none are set elsewhere: 20 working days, extendable by 20 working days for extensive or complex requests, with notice within three weeks); communicate grounds for refusal; include a reference to means of redress in re-use decisions; and establish practical arrangements to facilitate re-use.
quote: Public sector bodies shall, through electronic means where possible and appropriate, process requests for re-use
conditional_on: Applies to requests for re-use; Art. 4(6) exempts public undertakings and educational, research performing and research funding organisations.

summary: Public sector bodies and public undertakings make documents available in any pre-existing format or language, by electronic means where possible, in open, machine-readable, accessible, findable and re-usable formats together with metadata, complying with formal open standards where possible. Art. 5(7) applies this to existing documents held by public undertakings.
quote: public sector bodies and public undertakings shall make their documents available in any pre-existing format or language
conditional_on: Where possible and appropriate; no duty to create or adapt documents where this involves disproportionate effort (Art. 5(3)).

summary: Member States encourage public sector bodies and public undertakings to produce and make available documents in accordance with the principle of open by design and by default.
quote: Member States shall encourage public sector bodies and public undertakings to produce and make available documents

summary: Dynamic data is made available for re-use immediately after collection via suitable APIs and, where relevant, as a bulk download; Art. 5(6) allows time frames or temporary technical restrictions where this would exceed financial and technical capacities. Art. 5(7) applies this to public undertakings.
quote: Public sector bodies shall make dynamic data available for re-use immediately after collection, via suitable APIs
conditional_on: Subject to the disproportionate-effort limit in Art. 5(6).

summary: High-value datasets listed under Art. 14(1) are made available for re-use in machine-readable format, via suitable APIs and, where relevant, as a bulk download.
quote: The high-value datasets, as listed in accordance with Article 14(1) shall be made available for re-use in machine-readable format
conditional_on: Datasets as listed in accordance with Art. 14(1).

summary: Re-use of documents is free of charge; recovery of marginal costs for reproduction, provision, dissemination, anonymisation and protection of commercially confidential information may be allowed.
quote: The re-use of documents shall be free of charge.
conditional_on: Exceptions in Art. 6(2) (public bodies required to generate revenue, libraries, museums and archives, public undertakings).

summary: Member States publish online a list of the public sector bodies that are required to generate revenue to cover a substantial part of their costs relating to their public tasks.
quote: Member States shall publish online a list of the public sector bodies referred to in point (a) of paragraph 2.
conditional_on: Public sector bodies referred to in Art. 6(2)(a).

summary: For public bodies charging above marginal cost under Art. 6(2)(a) and (c), total charges are calculated on objective, transparent and verifiable criteria laid down by Member States, and total income may not exceed cost plus a reasonable return on investment; Art. 6(5) sets the same cost-based limit for libraries, museums and archives.
quote: Such criteria shall be laid down by Member States.
conditional_on: Cases in Art. 6(2)(a) and (c) for Art. 6(4); Art. 6(2)(b) for Art. 6(5).

summary: High-value datasets listed under Art. 14(1) and research data referred to in Art. 1(1)(c) are free of charge for the user, subject to Art. 14(3), (4) and (5).
quote: The re-use of the following shall be free of charge for the user:
conditional_on: Subject to Art. 14(3), (4) and (5).

summary: For standard charges, applicable conditions and actual amounts, including the calculation basis, are pre-established and published; for other charges, the calculation factors are indicated at the outset and, on request, the holder indicates how the charge was calculated for a specific request.
quote: shall be pre-established and published, through electronic means where possible and appropriate.
conditional_on: Standard charges (Art. 7(1)); other charges (Art. 7(2)).

summary: Public sector bodies ensure that applicants for re-use are informed of available means of redress relating to decisions or practices affecting them.
quote: Public sector bodies shall ensure that applicants for re-use of documents are informed of available means of redress

summary: Re-use is not subject to conditions unless the conditions are objective, proportionate, non-discriminatory and justified by a public interest objective; conditions shall not unnecessarily restrict re-use or be used to restrict competition.
quote: When re-use is subject to conditions, those conditions shall not unnecessarily restrict possibilities for re-use
conditional_on: Re-use is subject to conditions only where justified on grounds of a public interest objective.

summary: Member States ensure that standard licences for re-use of public sector documents are available in digital format and can be processed electronically, and encourage their use.
quote: Member States shall ensure that standard licences for the re-use of public sector documents
conditional_on: In Member States where licences are used.

summary: Member States make practical arrangements facilitating the search for re-usable documents (asset lists with metadata, portal sites, cross-linguistic search where possible) and encourage public sector bodies to facilitate preservation of documents.
quote: Member States shall make practical arrangements facilitating the search for documents available for re-use
conditional_on: Where possible and appropriate.

summary: Member States, in cooperation with the Commission, continue efforts to simplify access to datasets, including by providing a single point of access and progressively making suitable datasets available in accessible, findable and re-usable formats.
quote: Member States shall, in cooperation with the Commission, continue efforts to simplify access to datasets

summary: Member States support the availability of publicly funded research data by adopting open access policies (open by default, compatible with the FAIR principles), addressed to research performing organisations and research funding organisations.
quote: Member States shall support the availability of research data by adopting national policies
conditional_on: Publicly funded research data; concerns on IP, personal data, confidentiality, security and commercial interests are taken into account.

summary: Research data is re-usable for commercial or non-commercial purposes under Chapters III and IV, insofar as it is publicly funded and already made publicly available through an institutional or subject-based repository; legitimate commercial interests, knowledge transfer and pre-existing IP rights are taken into account.
quote: research data shall be re-usable for commercial or non-commercial purposes in accordance with Chapters III and IV
conditional_on: Publicly funded research data already made publicly available through an institutional or subject-based repository.

summary: Conditions for re-use are non-discriminatory for comparable categories of re-use, including cross-border re-use; where a public sector body re-uses documents for its own commercial activities outside its public tasks, the same charges and conditions apply as to other users (Art. 11(2)).
quote: Any applicable conditions for the re-use of documents shall be non-discriminatory for comparable categories of re-use
conditional_on: Art. 11(2) applies to re-use as input for commercial activities outside the public task.

summary: Contracts or other arrangements between public sector bodies or public undertakings holding documents and third parties shall not grant exclusive rights; the re-use of documents is open to all potential market actors.
quote: Contracts or other arrangements between the public sector bodies or public undertakings holding the documents and third parties shall not grant exclusive rights.
conditional_on: Exception for exclusive rights where necessary for a service in the public interest (Art. 12(2)) and for digitisation of cultural resources (Art. 12(3)).

summary: Where an exclusive right is necessary for a service in the public interest, the reason is reviewed regularly and at least every three years; exclusive arrangements established on or after 16 July 2019 are published online at least two months before they take effect, and their final terms are made public.
applies_from: Exclusive arrangements established on or after 16 July 2019.
quote: The exclusive arrangements established on or after 16 July 2019 shall be made publicly available online at least two months before they come into effect.
conditional_on: Exclusive right necessary for a service in the public interest (Art. 12(2)); does not apply to digitisation of cultural resources.

summary: For exclusive rights over digitisation of cultural resources, exclusivity in general does not exceed 10 years, with review in the 11th year and every seven years thereafter if longer; arrangements are transparent and public; the public sector body is provided free of charge with a copy of the digitised resources, available for re-use at the end of the exclusivity period.
quote: the period of exclusivity shall in general not exceed 10 years.
conditional_on: Exclusive right relating to digitisation of cultural resources.

summary: Legal or practical arrangements that without expressly granting an exclusive right could restrict availability for re-use are published online at least two months before taking effect; their effect is reviewed regularly and at least every three years, and their final terms are made public.
quote: shall be made publicly available online at least two months before their coming into effect.
conditional_on: Arrangements that aim at, or could reasonably be expected to lead to, restricted availability for re-use by entities other than the participating third party.

summary: Exclusive arrangements existing on 17 July 2013 entered into by public sector bodies, and not qualifying for the exceptions in Art. 12(2) and (3), are terminated at the end of the contract and in any event not later than the stated date.
applies_from: At the end of the contract and in any event not later than 18 July 2043.
quote: shall be terminated at the end of the contract and in any event not later than on 18 July 2043.
conditional_on: Exclusive arrangements existing on 17 July 2013 not qualifying for the exceptions in Art. 12(2) and (3).

summary: Exclusive arrangements existing on 16 July 2019 entered into by public undertakings, and not qualifying for the exceptions in Art. 12(2) and (3), are terminated at the end of the contract and in any event not later than the stated date.
applies_from: At the end of the contract and in any event not later than 17 July 2049.
quote: shall be terminated at the end of the contract and in any event not later than on 17 July 2049.
conditional_on: Exclusive arrangements existing on 16 July 2019 entered into by public undertakings not qualifying for the exceptions in Art. 12(2) and (3).

summary: Public sector bodies shall not exercise the database maker's right under Art. 7(1) of Directive 96/9/EC to prevent re-use of documents or to restrict re-use beyond the limits set by this Directive.
quote: The right for the maker of a database provided for in Article 7(1) of Directive 96/9/EC shall not be exercised by public sector bodies in order to prevent the re-use of documents

summary: Member States ensure that documents within the scope of the Directive, and documents held by public undertakings, are re-usable for commercial or non-commercial purposes in accordance with Chapters III and IV.
quote: Member States shall ensure that documents to which this Directive applies in accordance with Article 1 shall be re-usable
conditional_on: For documents held by public undertakings and IP-holding cultural establishments (Art. 3(2)), where re-use is allowed.

summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts to amend Annex I by adding thematic categories of high-value datasets.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 15
conditional_on: Subject to the conditions of Art. 15.

summary: The Commission adopts implementing acts laying down a list of specific high-value datasets belonging to the Annex I categories, which may specify publication and re-use arrangements compatible with open standard licences.
quote: The Commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down a list of specific high-value datasets
conditional_on: Adopted under the examination procedure in Art. 16(2).

summary: Specific high-value datasets listed under Art. 14(1) are available free of charge, machine readable, provided via APIs, and provided as a bulk download where relevant.
quote: available free of charge, subject to paragraphs 3, 4 and 5;
conditional_on: Subject to paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 of Art. 14.

summary: For identifying specific high-value datasets, the Commission carries out appropriate consultations including at expert level, conducts an impact assessment including a cost-benefit analysis, and ensures complementarity with existing legal acts.
quote: the Commission shall carry out appropriate consultations, including at expert level, conduct an impact assessment
conditional_on: For the purpose of identifying specific high-value datasets under Art. 14(1).

summary: Member States may exempt public sector bodies required to generate revenue from the requirement to make high-value datasets available free of charge for no more than two years after the implementing act enters into force, where this would substantially impact their budget.
quote: Member States may exempt those bodies from the requirement to make those high-value datasets available free of charge
conditional_on: Where free availability would lead to a substantial impact on the budget of the bodies involved; period of no more than two years following the entry into force of the relevant implementing act.

summary: Conditions of the delegation to the Commission: delegation for five years from 16 July 2019 with tacit extension; the Commission reports at least nine months before expiry; the Commission consults experts designated by each Member State before adopting a delegated act and notifies it simultaneously to Parliament and Council.
quote: The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period.
conditional_on: Delegation under Art. 13(2).

summary: Member States bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with the Directive, communicate them to the Commission, and communicate the text of the main provisions of national law adopted in the field.
quote: Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 17 July 2021.

summary: The Commission carries out an evaluation of the Directive and submits a report to Parliament, Council and the EESC; Member States provide the Commission with the information necessary for that report.
quote: No sooner than 17 July 2025, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Directive

summary: Terms and conditions must be drafted in plain and intelligible language, easily available at all stages including pre-contract, set out grounds for suspension, termination or restriction, and include information on additional distribution channels, affiliate programmes and effects on business users' IP rights (Art. 3(1)(a)-(e)).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall ensure that their terms and conditions:

summary: Notify proposed changes to terms and conditions to affected business users on a durable medium and do not implement them before a notice period of at least 15 days, longer where technical or commercial adaptations are needed (Art. 3(2)).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall notify, on a durable medium, to the business users concerned any proposed changes of their terms and conditions.

summary: Ensure that the identity of the business user providing goods or services on the platform is clearly visible (Art. 3(5)).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall ensure that the identity of the business user providing the goods or services on the online intermediation services is clearly visible.

summary: Give the business user a statement of reasons on a durable medium, before or at the time a restriction or suspension of individual goods or services takes effect; the statement must refer to the specific facts and the applicable grounds (Art. 4(1), (5)).
quote: it shall provide the business user concerned, prior to or at the time of the restriction or suspension taking effect, with a statement of reasons for that decision on a durable medium.
conditional_on: Restriction or suspension of the provision of services to a business user in relation to individual goods or services

summary: Give the business user a statement of reasons on a durable medium at least 30 days before termination of the provision of the whole of the services takes effect (Art. 4(2), (5)).
quote: it shall provide the business user concerned, at least 30 days prior to the termination taking effect, with a statement of reasons for that decision on a durable medium.
conditional_on: Decision to terminate the provision of the whole of the online intermediation services to a given business user

summary: Where the 30-day notice period does not apply, provide the business user with a statement of reasons without undue delay, on a durable medium (Art. 4(4), second subparagraph).
quote: In cases where the notice period in paragraph 2 does not apply, the provider of online intermediation services shall provide the business user concerned, without undue delay, with a statement of reasons for that decision on a durable medium.
conditional_on: Notice period in Art. 4(2) does not apply under Art. 4(4)

summary: In cases of restriction, suspension or termination, give the business user an opportunity to clarify facts through the internal complaint-handling process; reinstate the business user without undue delay where the decision is revoked, including access to its data (Art. 4(3)).
quote: the provider of online intermediation services shall give the business user the opportunity to clarify the facts and circumstances in the framework of the internal complaint-handling process referred to in Article 11.
conditional_on: Restriction, suspension or termination of services to a business user

summary: Set out in the terms and conditions the main parameters determining ranking and the reasons for their relative importance (Art. 5(1)).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall set out in their terms and conditions the main parameters determining ranking and the reasons for the relative importance of those main parameters as opposed to other parameters.

summary: Provide an easily and publicly available, plain-language description of the main parameters determining ranking and their relative importance, and keep it up to date (Art. 5(2)).
quote: Providers of online search engines shall set out the main parameters, which individually or collectively are most significant in determining ranking

summary: Where ranking can be influenced against remuneration, describe those possibilities and their effects on ranking (Art. 5(3)).
quote: that provider shall also set out a description of those possibilities and of the effects of such remuneration on ranking
conditional_on: Main parameters include the possibility to influence ranking against remuneration

summary: Offer the corporate website user the possibility to inspect the contents of a third-party notification that led to an altered ranking or delisting (Art. 5(4)).
quote: the provider shall offer the possibility for the corporate website user to inspect the contents of the notification.
conditional_on: Ranking altered in a specific case or website delisted following a third party notification

summary: The Commission shall accompany the ranking transparency requirements with guidelines (Art. 5(7)).
quote: the Commission shall accompany the transparency requirements set out in this Article with guidelines.

summary: Set out in the terms and conditions a description of the type of ancillary goods and services offered, and whether and under what conditions business users may offer their own ancillary goods and services (Art. 6).
quote: shall set out in its terms and conditions a description of the type of ancillary goods and services offered
conditional_on: Ancillary goods and services offered to consumers through the platform

summary: Describe in the terms and conditions any differentiated treatment given to the provider's own offers or controlled business users, with the main economic, commercial or legal considerations (Art. 7(1); Art. 7(2) imposes the equivalent description on search engine providers for corporate website users, and Art. 7(3) lists covered matters).
quote: shall include in their terms and conditions a description of any differentiated treatment which they give, or might give

summary: Do not impose retroactive changes to terms and conditions, except where required by a legal or regulatory obligation or beneficial to business users (Art. 8(a)).
quote: not impose retroactive changes to terms and conditions, except when they are required to respect a legal or regulatory obligation

summary: Include in the terms and conditions information on the conditions for business users to terminate the contractual relationship, and a description of post-expiry technical and contractual access to business user information (Art. 8(b)-(c)).
quote: ensure that their terms and conditions include information on the conditions under which business users can terminate the contractual relationship

summary: Include in the terms and conditions a description of business users' technical and contractual access to data provided or generated on the platform, and inform business users of whether the provider has access, what access business users have, and whether data is shared with third parties with purpose and opt-out information (Art. 9(1)-(2)).
quote: shall include in their terms and conditions a description of the technical and contractual access, or absence thereof, of business users to any personal data or other data

summary: Where business users are restricted from offering goods or services under different conditions through other means, include the grounds for the restriction in the terms and make them easily available to the public (Art. 10(1)).
quote: they shall include the grounds for that restriction in their terms and conditions and make those grounds easily available to the public.
conditional_on: Provider restricts business users from offering the same goods or services under different conditions through other means

summary: Provide an internal complaint-handling system that is easily accessible and free of charge for business users, handles complaints within a reasonable time, considers and processes them, and communicates outcomes individually in plain language (Art. 11(1)-(2)).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall provide for an internal system for handling the complaints of business users.
conditional_on: Provider is not a small enterprise within the meaning of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC (Art. 11(5))

summary: Provide in the terms and conditions all relevant information on access to and functioning of the internal complaint system; make information on its functioning and effectiveness publicly available, verify it at least annually and update it (Art. 11(3)-(4)).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall provide in their terms and conditions all relevant information relating to the access to and functioning of their internal complaint-handling system.
conditional_on: Provider is not a small enterprise within the meaning of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC (Art. 11(5))

summary: Identify in the terms and conditions two or more mediators willing to engage in out-of-court dispute settlement; engage in good faith throughout mediation (business users are also bound to engage in good faith, Art. 12(3)) (Art. 12(1), (3)).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall identify in their terms and conditions two or more mediators with which they are willing to engage
conditional_on: Provider is not a small enterprise within the meaning of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC (Art. 12(7))

summary: Bear a reasonable proportion of the total costs of mediation in each individual case, as suggested by the mediator (Art. 12(4)).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall bear a reasonable proportion of the total costs of mediation in each individual case.
conditional_on: Provider is not a small enterprise within the meaning of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC (Art. 12(7))

summary: On request of a business user, before or during mediation, make available information on the functioning and effectiveness of mediation related to the provider's activities (Art. 12(6)).
quote: the provider of online intermediation services shall make available, to the business user, information on the functioning and effectiveness of mediation related to its activities.
conditional_on: If requested by a business user, before entering into or during mediation

summary: The Commission, with Member States, shall encourage providers and their representative organisations to set up specialised mediation organisations.
quote: The Commission shall, in close cooperation with the Member States, encourage providers of online intermediation services

summary: The Commission shall encourage Member States to exchange best practices and information on registries of unlawful acts (Art. 14(2)), and draw up and publish a list of designated organisations, associations and public bodies, updated every six months (Art. 14(6)).
quote: The Commission shall draw up a list of the organisations, associations and public bodies designated in accordance with paragraph 5.

summary: Where concerns are raised about a designated organisation or public body, the designating Member State shall investigate and, where appropriate, revoke the designation.
quote: shall investigate the concerns and, where appropriate, revoke the designation if one or more of the criteria are not complied with.
conditional_on: Concerns raised by a Member State or the Commission about compliance with the criteria in Art. 14(3) or 14(4)

summary: Member States shall ensure adequate and effective enforcement of the Regulation and lay down effective, proportionate and dissuasive measures for infringements (Art. 15(1)-(2)).
quote: Each Member State shall ensure adequate and effective enforcement of this Regulation.

summary: The Commission, in close cooperation with Member States, shall closely monitor the Regulation's impact on relations between platforms and business users and between search engines and corporate website users, gather information, and Member States shall assist by providing information on request.
quote: The Commission, in close cooperation with Member States, shall closely monitor the impact of this Regulation

summary: The Commission shall encourage the drawing up of codes of conduct by providers, search engine providers and sector bodies, including sector-specific codes (Art. 17(1)-(3)).
quote: The Commission shall encourage the drawing up of codes of conduct by providers of online intermediation services

summary: The Commission shall evaluate the Regulation every three years, first by 13 January 2022, with a report to Parliament, Council and EESC, covering the matters listed in Art. 18(2), and take appropriate measures afterwards.
applies_from: By 13 January 2022, and subsequently every three years
quote: By 13 January 2022, and subsequently every three years, the Commission shall evaluate this Regulation and report to the European Parliament

summary: Member States shall provide any relevant information they have that the Commission requires for the review report.
quote: Member States shall provide any relevant information they have that the Commission may require

summary: Member States must take measures so that persons performing platform work who have a contract with an intermediary enjoy the same protection as those with a direct contract, including mechanisms that may include joint and several liability systems.
quote: Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that, where a digital labour platform makes use of intermediaries, persons performing platform work
conditional_on: where a digital labour platform makes use of intermediaries

summary: Member States must have procedures to verify and ensure the correct employment status of platform workers, using the legal presumption (Art. 5). Where an employment relationship is established, the party responsible for employer obligations must be clearly identified (Art. 4(3)).
quote: Member States shall have appropriate and effective procedures in place to verify and ensure the determination of the correct employment status of persons performing platform work

summary: Member States must establish an effective rebuttable legal presumption of employment for platform workers, ensure it does not increase the burden on workers, and apply it in all relevant administrative or judicial proceedings on employment status (excluding tax, criminal and social security matters unless national law provides otherwise).
applies_from: 2 December 2026 (Art. 5(6), applies only to the period from this date)
quote: Member States shall establish an effective rebuttable legal presumption of an employment relationship
conditional_on: where facts indicating direction and control are found

summary: Where a national competent authority considers that a person performing platform work might be wrongly classified, it must initiate appropriate actions or proceedings to determine the correct employment status.
quote: it shall initiate appropriate actions or proceedings
conditional_on: where a national competent authority considers that a person might be wrongly classified

summary: Member States must establish a framework of supporting measures: guidance for platforms, workers and social partners; guidance and procedures for authorities to identify and pursue non-compliant platforms; effective controls and inspections; and training and technical expertise on algorithmic management for authorities.
quote: Member States shall establish a framework of supporting measures in order to ensure the effective implementation of and compliance with the legal presumption.

summary: Digital labour platforms must not, by means of automated monitoring or decision-making systems, process personal data on emotional or psychological state, private conversations, or data collected while workers are not working; process data to predict exercise of fundamental rights; or infer protected characteristics. Biometric identification of workers in a database is also prohibited. Applies from the start of recruitment or selection.
quote: Digital labour platforms shall not, by means of automated monitoring systems or automated decision-making systems:

summary: In carrying out the data-protection impact assessment for automated monitoring or decision-making systems, platforms acting as controllers must seek the views of persons performing platform work and their representatives.
quote: shall seek the views of persons performing platform work and their representatives.

summary: Platforms must provide the data-protection impact assessment to workers’ representatives.
quote: Digital labour platforms shall provide the assessment as referred to in paragraph 1 to workers’ representatives.

summary: Platforms must inform persons performing platform work of the use of automated monitoring and decision-making systems, including the information categories listed in Art. 9(1)(a)-(c). Information is in written form, in clear language. Concise information on systems directly affecting a worker is due at the latest on the first working day, before changes, and on request; comprehensive information on all systems is due on request.
applies_from: 2 December 2026 (transposition deadline, Art. 29(1)); first working day at the latest (Art. 9(3)(a))
quote: Member States shall require digital labour platforms to inform persons performing platform work
conditional_on: for systems and features that directly affect the person; comprehensive form upon request

summary: Platforms must give workers’ representatives comprehensive and detailed information on all relevant systems prior to their use, before changes affecting working conditions or monitoring, and on request; national competent authorities receive the same information on request.
applies_from: prior to the use of those systems (Art. 9(4)(a)); 2 December 2026 (transposition deadline, Art. 29(1))
quote: Digital labour platforms shall provide workers’ representatives, in a comprehensive and detailed form, with the information referred to in paragraph 1

summary: Platforms must provide information on automated monitoring or decision-making systems used in a recruitment or selection procedure, concisely and before the procedure starts, limited to systems used in that procedure.
applies_from: before the start of the recruitment or selection procedure (Art. 9(5)); 2 December 2026 (transposition deadline, Art. 29(1))
quote: Digital labour platforms shall provide the information referred to in paragraph 1 to persons undergoing a recruitment or selection procedure.
conditional_on: persons undergoing a recruitment or selection procedure

summary: Platforms must provide persons performing platform work, free of charge, with tools to exercise data portability rights for personal data generated through their work, including ratings and reviews, and transmit that data directly to a third party on request.
quote: The digital labour platform shall provide persons performing platform work, free of charge, with tools to facilitate the effective exercise of their portability rights
conditional_on: where the person requests direct transmission to a third party

summary: Platforms must oversee automated monitoring and decision-making systems with workers’ involvement; ensure sufficient human resources, competence, training and authority for oversight staff, who are protected from dismissal and adverse treatment; and ensure that decisions to restrict, suspend or terminate an account or contract, or equivalent detrimental decisions, are taken by a human being.
quote: Any decision to restrict, suspend or terminate the contractual relationship or the account of a person performing platform work or any other decision of equivalent detriment shall be taken by a human being.

summary: Platforms must regularly, and in any event every two years, evaluate the impact of individual decisions taken or supported by automated systems on persons performing platform work, including working conditions and equal treatment, with workers’ representatives involved.
quote: Member States shall ensure that digital labour platforms oversee and, with the involvement of workers’ representatives, regularly and in any event every two years, carry out an evaluation of the impact of individual decisions

summary: Where an evaluation identifies a high risk of discrimination at work, or an infringement of rights caused by automated decisions, platforms must take necessary steps, including modifying or discontinuing the system, to avoid such decisions in the future.
quote: the digital labour platform shall take the steps necessary, including, if appropriate, the modification of the automated monitoring system
conditional_on: where oversight or evaluation identifies a high risk of discrimination or an infringement of rights

summary: Platforms must transmit information on the Art. 10(1) evaluation to platform workers’ representatives, and make it available to persons performing platform work and national competent authorities on request.
quote: Information on the evaluation pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be transmitted to platform workers’ representatives.

summary: Platforms must give persons performing platform work access to a designated contact person to clarify decisions taken or supported by automated decision-making systems, provide a written statement of reasons for listed decisions (account restriction, suspension or termination, refusal of payment, contractual status, and similar) no later than their effect date, and provide an explanation without undue delay.
quote: Member States shall ensure that digital labour platforms provide persons performing platform work with access to a contact person designated by the digital labour platform
conditional_on: decisions taken or supported by an automated decision-making system

summary: On request for review of an automated decision covered by Art. 11(1), platforms must reply in writing with a substantiated answer within two weeks of the request. Where a decision infringes rights, the platform must rectify it within two weeks of adoption, or offer adequate compensation, and modify or discontinue the system to avoid similar decisions.
quote: The digital labour platform shall respond to such request by providing the person performing platform work with a sufficiently precise and adequately substantiated reply
conditional_on: upon request by the person performing platform work or their representatives

summary: For platform workers, platforms must evaluate the risks of automated monitoring and decision-making systems to safety and health (including accidents, psychosocial and ergonomic risks), assess whether the safeguards are appropriate for those risks, and introduce appropriate preventive and protective measures.
quote: evaluate the risks of automated monitoring systems and automated decision-making systems to their safety and health

summary: Platforms must ensure effective information, consultation and participation of platform workers and/or their representatives on safety and health matters in accordance with Articles 10 and 11 of Directive 89/391/EEC, and introduce appropriate preventive and protective measures.
quote: digital labour platforms shall ensure effective information and consultation and the participation of platform workers and/or their representatives

summary: Platforms must not use automated monitoring or decision-making systems in a manner that puts undue pressure on platform workers or otherwise puts at risk their safety and physical and mental health.
quote: Digital labour platforms shall not use automated monitoring systems or automated decision-making systems in a manner that puts undue pressure on platform workers

summary: Platforms must take preventive measures against violence and harassment, including providing effective reporting channels, for platform workers.
quote: Member States shall ensure that digital labour platforms take preventive measures, including providing for effective reporting channels.

summary: Platforms must ensure that information and consultation of workers’ representatives also covers decisions likely to lead to the introduction of or substantial changes in automated monitoring or decision-making systems, under the arrangements of Directive 2002/14/EC.
quote: decisions likely to lead to the introduction of or to substantial changes in the use of automated monitoring systems

summary: Where the platform has more than 250 workers in the Member State concerned, it bears the expenses of an expert of the platform workers’ representatives’ choice, provided they are proportionate.
quote: the expenses of the expert shall be borne by the digital labour platform, provided that they are proportionate.
conditional_on: more than 250 workers in the Member State concerned; expenses proportionate

summary: Where there are no representatives of platform workers, platforms must directly inform the platform workers concerned, in writing, of decisions likely to introduce or substantially change automated monitoring or decision-making systems.
quote: Member States shall ensure that digital labour platforms directly inform the platform workers concerned of decisions likely to lead to the introduction of or to substantial changes
conditional_on: where there are no representatives of platform workers

summary: Platforms must declare work performed by platform workers to the competent authorities of the Member State in which the work is performed.
quote: Member States shall require digital labour platforms to declare work performed by platform workers to the competent authorities of the Member State in which the work is performed

summary: Platforms must make available to competent authorities and workers’ representatives: number of platform workers per level of activity and status; general terms and conditions (updated on substantive change); average activity duration, weekly hours and income (on request only); and intermediaries used. Information is provided per Member State and updated at least every six months (SMEs may update yearly). Platforms must also answer authority or representative requests for clarification without undue delay.
applies_from: 2 December 2026 (transposition deadline, Art. 29(1)); updated at least every six months (Art. 17(4))
quote: Member States shall ensure that digital labour platforms make the following information available to competent authorities and to representatives of persons performing platform work
conditional_on: item (c) average duration, hours and income only upon request (Art. 17(3))

summary: Platforms must provide persons performing platform work, through their digital infrastructure or similarly effective means, with the possibility to contact each other privately and securely and to be contacted by their representatives.
quote: Member States shall take the measures necessary to ensure that digital labour platforms provide persons performing platform work
conditional_on: while complying with Regulation (EU) 2016/679

summary: Platforms must refrain from accessing or monitoring communications between platform workers or with their representatives through the channels in Art. 20.
quote: Member States shall require digital labour platforms to refrain from accessing or monitoring those contacts and communications.

summary: In proceedings under the Directive, national courts or competent authorities must be able to order a platform to disclose relevant evidence within its control; courts must have power to order disclosure of confidential information with effective protective measures.
quote: national courts or competent authorities are able to order the digital labour platform to disclose any relevant evidence which lies in its control.
conditional_on: in proceedings concerning the provisions of this Directive

summary: Member States must introduce measures to protect persons performing platform work, including their representatives, from adverse treatment by the platform and from adverse consequences of complaints or proceedings.
quote: Member States shall introduce the measures necessary to protect persons performing platform work

summary: Member States must prohibit dismissal or termination of contract of persons performing platform work, or equivalent action, on the grounds that they exercised rights under the Directive.
quote: Member States shall take the measures necessary to prohibit the dismissal or termination of the contract of persons performing platform work
conditional_on: on the grounds that they have exercised the rights provided for in this Directive

summary: On request by a person who considers they were dismissed or subjected to equivalent action for exercising rights under the Directive, the platform must provide substantiated grounds in writing without undue delay.
quote: The digital labour platform shall provide those grounds in writing without undue delay.
conditional_on: upon request by a person who considers they were dismissed or subjected to equivalent action

summary: The data-protection supervisory authorities must monitor and enforce Articles 7 to 11 of the Directive as far as data-protection matters are concerned, under the procedural framework of Regulation (EU) 2016/679.
quote: shall also be responsible for monitoring and enforcing the application of Articles 7 to 11 of this Directive as far as data-protection matters are concerned

summary: Supervisory authorities and other national competent authorities must cooperate in enforcing the Directive, exchange relevant information, and exchange information on enforcement where workers perform platform work in another Member State; national authorities cooperate on the legal presumption with Commission support.
quote: shall, where relevant, cooperate in the enforcement of this Directive within the remit of their respective competences
conditional_on: where relevant

summary: Member States must take adequate measures to promote the role of social partners and encourage the exercise of collective bargaining in platform work, including on employment status and algorithmic management rights.
quote: Member States shall, without prejudice to the autonomy of the social partners and taking into account the diversity of national practices, take adequate measures to promote the role of the social partners
conditional_on: without prejudice to the autonomy of the social partners

summary: Member States must ensure that the national transposing measures, and the relevant existing provisions including on the legal presumption, are brought to the attention of platform workers, platforms (including SMEs) and the public, in a clear and accessible way, including for persons with disabilities.
quote: Member States shall ensure that the national measures transposing this Directive

summary: Member States must bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with the Directive by 2 December 2026, inform the Commission, and include a reference to the Directive on publication.
quote: Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 2 December 2026.

summary: Member States must communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law they adopt in the field covered by the Directive.
quote: Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.

summary: Member States must take adequate measures to ensure effective involvement of social partners and promote social dialogue in implementing the Directive.
quote: Member States shall, in accordance with their national law and practice, take adequate measures to ensure the effective involvement of the social partners
conditional_on: in accordance with national law and practice

summary: The Commission must, after consultations, review implementation of the Directive, including its impact on SMEs and the effectiveness of the legal presumption and the use of intermediaries, and propose amendments where appropriate.
quote: By 2 December 2029, the Commission shall, after consulting the Member States, the social partners at Union level and key stakeholders

summary: Member States shall not maintain or introduce transparency provisions diverging from the Regulation; under Art. 4(2) the provision of political advertising services shall not be prohibited or restricted on transparency grounds where the Regulation's requirements are complied with.
quote: Member States shall not maintain or introduce, on grounds related to the transparency of political advertising, provisions or measures diverging from those laid down in this Regulation.

summary: Providers of political advertising services shall not make provision of their services subject to discriminatory restrictions based solely on the sponsor's place of residence or establishment, and shall not restrict services to European political parties or EP political groups solely on their place of establishment.
applies_from: from the date of entry into force (Art. 30(2))
quote: Providers of political advertising services shall not make the provision of their services subject to discriminatory restrictions solely based on the place of residence or establishment of the sponsor.

summary: In the last three months before an election or referendum, political advertising services pertaining to it may only be provided to a sponsor (or agent) who declares it is an EU citizen, a permanently resident third-country national with voting rights, or an EU-established legal person not ultimately owned or controlled by a third-country national or third-country entity.
quote: political advertising services pertaining to that election or referendum shall only be provided to a sponsor, or service provider acting on behalf of a sponsor, who declares itself to be
conditional_on: last three months preceding an election or referendum organised at Union, national, regional or local level

summary: Political advertising services shall be provided in a transparent manner in accordance with Art. 6, Arts. 7 to 17 and Art. 21.
quote: Political advertising services shall be provided in a transparent manner in accordance with the obligations laid down in this Article, Articles 7 to 17 and Article 21.

summary: Providers of political advertising services shall ensure that contractual arrangements for the service enable compliance, including allocation of responsibility and completeness and accuracy of information.
quote: Providers of political advertising services shall ensure that the contractual arrangements concluded for the provision of a political advertising service enable compliance with the relevant provisions of this Regulation

summary: Sponsors, and providers of advertising services acting on behalf of sponsors, shall make declarations on whether the service is political advertising and on Art. 5(2) requirements truthfully and are responsible for their accuracy; providers of advertising services shall request such declarations from sponsors.
quote: Sponsors, and providers of advertising services acting on behalf of sponsors, shall make such declarations truthfully and shall be responsible for their accuracy.

summary: Providers of political advertising services shall ensure that contracts require sponsors (or agents) to provide the Art. 7(1) declaration and the information needed to comply with Arts. 9(1), 11(1) and 12(1).
quote: Providers of political advertising services shall ensure that the contractual arrangements concluded for the provision of a political advertising service require the sponsor

summary: Sponsors (and agents acting for them) shall provide and ensure the accuracy of information needed for Arts. 9(1), 11(1) and 12(1) before or during publication, update changed information, and correct incomplete or inaccurate information transmitted to publishers.
applies_from: before or during the period of publication, delivery or dissemination (Art. 7(3))
quote: Sponsors shall provide and ensure the accuracy of the information necessary for the providers of political advertising services to comply with Article 9(1)

summary: Providers of political advertising services shall require sponsors to correct declarations or information that are manifestly erroneous.
quote: Providers of political advertising services shall require sponsors, or providers of advertising services acting on behalf of sponsors
conditional_on: declaration or information is manifestly erroneous

summary: Providers of political advertising services using an online interface shall design and organise it to facilitate sponsors' compliance with their Art. 7(1) and Art. 9(1) obligations.
quote: Providers of political advertising services using an online interface shall ensure that that online interface is designed and organised in a way that facilitates compliance

summary: The Commission shall draw up common guidance on the application of the Art. 8 criteria for identifying political advertising.
quote: The Commission shall draw up common guidance intended to contribute to the proper application of this Article.

summary: Providers of political advertising services shall retain, to the extent necessary, information on the advertisement, services, amounts and benefits, origin of funds, and sponsor identity; make reasonable efforts to keep it complete and accurate; and retain it in machine-readable form for seven years. Art. 9(4) exempts certain micro-undertakings.
quote: Providers of political advertising services shall retain, to the extent necessary to comply with this Regulation, information they collect in the provision of their services

summary: Providers of political advertising services shall transmit the Art. 9(1) information in a timely, complete and accurate manner to political advertising publishers, during the service and by standardised automated process where technically possible; they shall transmit updated information when it changes.
quote: Providers of political advertising services shall ensure that the information referred to in Article 9(1) is transmitted in a timely, complete and accurate manner

summary: Where the publisher is the only provider of political advertising services, the sponsor shall transmit the relevant information to the publisher.
quote: When the political advertising publisher is the only provider of political advertising services, the sponsor shall transmit the relevant information
conditional_on: the political advertising publisher is the only provider of political advertising services

summary: Political advertising publishers shall make each political advertisement available with a statement that it is political, the sponsor identity and controlling entity, linked election or process, targeting disclosure, and a transparency notice or a clear indication where it can be retrieved; labels shall be prominent and remain in place when further disseminated; completeness and accuracy of the information shall be ensured.
quote: Political advertising publishers shall ensure that each political advertisement is made available together with the following information in a clear, salient and unambiguous way:
conditional_on: where applicable (Art. 11(1)(c) and (d))

summary: The Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing the format and template of the labels for political advertisements, adapted to the medium used.
quote: By 10 July 2025, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing the format and the template of the labels

summary: Member States, including competent authorities, and the Commission shall encourage voluntary codes of conduct for the application of Art. 11, taking account of micro, small and medium-sized undertakings.
quote: Member States, including competent authorities, and the Commission shall encourage the drawing up of voluntary codes of conduct

summary: Political advertising publishers shall ensure that the transparency notice includes the Art. 12(1) items (a) to (m), including sponsor identity, remuneration, period, aggregated amounts and value of benefits, methodology, links and reach/engagement data where applicable. Under Art. 12(3) notices shall be in each advertisement or easily retrievable, kept up to date, machine-readable when made available electronically, in the language of the advertisement, accessible and clearly visible.
quote: Political advertising publishers shall ensure that the transparency notice referred to in Article 11(1), point (e), includes the following information:
conditional_on: where applicable (Art. 12(1)(k) to (m))

summary: Political advertising publishers shall ensure completeness of the transparency notice information and accuracy of listed items before and during publication; make best efforts to correct incomplete or inaccurate information; and shall not make available, or shall discontinue, an advertisement that cannot be completed or corrected without undue delay, informing sponsors and providers concerned.
quote: Where the information cannot be completed or corrected without undue delay, the political advertising publisher shall not make the political advertisement available

summary: Political advertising publishers shall retain their transparency notices and modifications for seven years after the last publication, unless the micro-undertaking exemption in Art. 12(5) applies.
quote: Political advertising publishers shall retain their transparency notices together with any modifications thereto for a period of seven years after the last publication

summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts amending Art. 12, including the list of notice items in Art. 12(1) and point (f), in light of technological and market developments.
quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 28 to amend this Regulation

summary: The Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing the format of, and technical specifications for, the transparency notice, adapted to the medium used.
quote: By 10 July 2025, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts to establish the format of and provide technical specifications for the transparency notice

summary: The Commission shall establish and ensure the management of a public European repository for all online political advertisements, directly or through a management authority, with a single portal, machine-readable access and a hosting service for seven years after last presentation.
quote: The Commission shall establish and ensure, directly or by entrusting this responsibility to a management authority, the management of a European repository

summary: Political advertising publishers that are very large online platforms or very large online search engines shall make each political advertisement and its Art. 12(1) information available in a repository under Art. 39 DSA, and enable access through the European repository from publication for the presentation period and seven years after last presentation.
quote: Political advertising publishers that are very large online platforms and very large online search engines shall ensure that each political advertisement

summary: Where a publisher removes or disables access to an advertisement on grounds of illegality or terms incompatibility, it shall continue to provide the Art. 12(1) information for the period in Art. 9(3).
quote: they shall continue to provide access to the information required by Article 12(1) of this Regulation for the period referred to in Article 9(3)
conditional_on: removal or disabling of access to a specific political advertisement

summary: Political advertising publishers other than very large online platforms and search engines that publish through an online service shall make each advertisement and its Art. 12(1) information available in the European repository.
applies_from: no later than 72 hours after the first publication of the political advertisement
quote: shall make each such political advertisement and the information required under Article 12(1) available in the European repository no later than 72 hours after the first publication
conditional_on: publication through an online service

summary: The Commission (or management authority) shall adopt implementing acts on the repository's data structure, metadata, authentication, and common application programming interface.
quote: By 10 April 2026, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts in accordance with Article 29 to set out detailed arrangements

summary: Political advertising publishers shall include in their management report, under Art. 19 of Directive 2013/34/EU, information on amounts or value of benefits received for services, including use of targeting and ad-delivery techniques, aggregated by campaign, and make it available to competent authorities where established under national law.
quote: Political advertising publishers shall include information on the amounts or the value of other benefits received in part or full exchange for the services provided

summary: Political advertising publishers shall have free, easy-to-access mechanisms for natural or legal persons to notify non-compliant advertisements, accepting electronic notifications where possible and containing the Art. 15(3) elements; they shall send confirmation of receipt without undue delay, provide redress information and information on automated means, and (non-VLOP publishers) make best efforts to examine notifications and inform notifiers on request.
quote: Political advertising publishers shall have in place the necessary mechanisms to enable natural or legal persons to notify them

summary: Political advertising publishers that are very large online platforms or search engines shall examine and address notifications in a diligent, non-arbitrary and objective manner and inform the notifier of the follow-up, without undue delay.
quote: Political advertising publishers which are very large online platforms and very large online search engines shall without undue delay:

summary: In the last month before an election or referendum, publishers shall process notifications about linked advertisements within 48 hours where they can be processed completely on the information in the notification; micro, small and medium-sized publishers shall make best efforts to process them without undue delay.
applies_from: last month preceding an election or referendum
quote: In the last month preceding an election or a referendum, political advertising publishers shall process any notification they receive about a political advertisement linked to that election or referendum within 48 hours
conditional_on: notification can be processed completely on the basis of the information included in the notification

summary: Political advertising publishers shall inform the sponsors or providers concerned, without undue delay, of measures taken following notifications that affect the availability or presentation of the advertisement.
quote: Political advertising publishers shall without undue delay inform the sponsors or providers of political advertising services concerned of any measures they take following notifications
conditional_on: measures affect availability or presentation of the advertisement

summary: Political advertising publishers may respond collectively to multiple notifications about the same advertisement or campaign, including through automated tools or a website announcement.
quote: Political advertising publishers may respond to multiple notifications under paragraph 1 regarding the same advertisement or advertising campaign collectively

summary: The Commission, after consulting the network of national contact points, may issue guidelines on the application of Art. 15.
quote: The Commission, after consulting the network of national contact points referred to in Article 22(8), may issue guidelines

summary: When national competent authorities request information to verify compliance, providers of political advertising services shall transmit complete, accurate and trustworthy information in a clear and, where possible, machine-readable format; acknowledge requests within two working days; and provide the information within eight working days (12 working days for micro, small and medium-sized undertakings), or without undue delay and within 48 hours in the last month before an election or referendum.
quote: The transmitted information shall be complete, accurate and trustworthy
conditional_on: upon a request by a national competent authority
