conditional_on: License application for a foreign entity owned 50 percent or more by listed or MEU List entities or SDNs, or where ownership cannot be determined

summary: Exporters, reexporters and transferors are advised to act with caution, and should undertake due diligence, when transacting with non-listed foreign entities in which listed entities hold significant ownership interests below 50 percent or that are parent entities of listed entities.
quote: Exporters, reexporters, and transferors are advised to act with caution when considering a transaction
conditional_on: Transaction with a foreign entity in which listed parties hold a significant interest below 50 percent, or a parent of a listed entity

summary: Exports, reexports, transfers (in-country) and exports from abroad made under the Temporary General License in General Order No. 7 are subject to the recordkeeping requirements of part 762 of the EAR.
quote: are subject to the recordkeeping requirements of part 762 of the EAR.
conditional_on: Transactions made under the Temporary General License (General Order No. 7); the TGL expires December 1, 2025

summary: Persons using the Temporary General License in General Order No. 7 must comply with all provisions of the EAR, including any additional applicable license requirements; the TGL overcomes only the license requirements of §§ 744.11 and 744.21 for the non-listed affiliate.
quote: Persons must comply with all provisions of the EAR, including any additional applicable license requirements.
conditional_on: Use of the Temporary General License in General Order No. 7

summary: The Entity List in Supplement No. 4 to Part 744 is revised and updated on a periodic basis by adding new or amended notifications and deleting notifications no longer in effect.
provision: Supplement No. 4 to Part 744 (introductory text), as revised
quote: This list is revised and updated on a periodic basis in this supplement by adding new or amended notifications and deleting notifications no longer in effect.

summary: Licence required to export, reexport or transfer (in-country) advanced computing items (3A090.a, 4A090.a, the .a/.1 .z paragraphs of 3A001, 4A003, 4A004, 4A005, 5A002, 5A004, 5A992, 5D002, 5D992 and related 3D001, 3E001, 4D001, 4D090, 4E001, 5E002, 5E992 software and technology) to or within any destination worldwide.
quote: Worldwide license requirement. A license is required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) items specified in ECCNs 3A001.z.1.a, z.2.a, z.3.a, z.4.a; 3A090.a

summary: Licence required for the lower-performance 3A090.b, 4A090.b and corresponding .b/.2 .z items and related software and technology to or within Country Groups D:1, D:4 or D:5, excluding destinations also in A:5 or A:6.
quote: A license is required to export, reexport, or transfer (incountry) items specified in ECCNs 3A001.z.1.b, z.2.b, z.3.b, z.4.b; 3A090.b

summary: Licence required to export, reexport or transfer (in-country) AI model weights classified in ECCN 4E091 to all destinations; deemed exports to permanent regular employees of entities headquartered in Supplement No. 5(a) destinations are excluded.
quote: A license is required for the export, reexport, and transfer (in-country) of items specified in ECCN 4E091 to all destinations worldwide.

summary: Advanced computing foreign direct product rule: foreign-produced 3A090, 4A090 and .z items that are direct products of listed U.S. software or technology, or of plants that are such direct products, are subject to the EAR when destined anywhere (or for D:5/Macau-headquartered mask or wafer production), and thus to § 742.6(a)(6) licence requirements.
quote: (h) Advanced computing FDP rule. A foreign-produced item is subject to the EAR if it meets both the product scope in paragraph (h)(1) of this section and the destination scope in paragraph (h)(2) of this section.

summary: AI model weights FDP rule: foreign-produced 4E091 model weights (including fine-tuned or quantized versions) produced using advanced computing items subject to the EAR (3A090, 4A090, .z) are subject to the EAR when destined to any location, and thus to the § 742.6(a)(13) licence requirement.
quote: (l) AI Model weights FDP rule. A foreign-produced item is subject to the EAR if it meets both the product scope in paragraph (l)(1) of this section and the destination scope in paragraph (l)(2) of this section.

summary: End-use licence requirement for 3A090.b, 4A090.b and corresponding .b/.2 .z items destined outside D:1/D:4/D:5 for entities headquartered (or with ultimate parent headquartered) in Macau or D:5, and for 3A090.c high bandwidth memory destined outside Macau/D:5 for such entities.
quote: destined to any destination other than those specified in Country Groups D:1, D:4, or D:5 (excluding any destination also specified in Country Groups A:5 or A:6) for an entity that is headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is

summary: Advanced computing items and model weights (3A090, 4A090, 4E091 and related 3D001, 3E001, 4D090, 4E001) going to D:1, D:4 or D:5 (not A:5/A:6), or to Macau/D:5-headquartered entities anywhere, may use only the listed license exceptions (TMP, NAC/ACA, RPL, GOV, TSU, HBM, AIA for 4E091 in listed cases, ACM).
quote: and the license exception is other than: TMP, restricted to eligibility under the provisions of § 740.9(a)(6); NAC/ACA, under the provisions of § 740.8

summary: License Exception STA may not be used for ECCN 4E091 technology to Country Group A:5 or A:6, nor for .a-level 4E001 technology to A:5 or A:6 (.b-level: A:6); ACM is not available for 4E091.
provision: Supp. No. 1 to part 774, ECCN 4E091, License Exceptions; ECCN 4E001
quote: STA: License Exception STA may not be used to ship or transmit ‘‘technology’’ specified by ECCN 4E091 to any of the destinations listed in Country Group A:5 or A:6

summary: Licence applications for 3A090.a, 4A090.a and .z AI commodities must include a purchase order or equivalent contract (BIS will generally limit licensed quantity to it) and the total aggregated TPP of each item (block 22(j)); one licence per country for destinations subject to a per-country TPP allocation.
quote: require the submission of a purchase order or equivalent contractual agreement with the submission of the license application

summary: License Exception NAC (to Macau, D:5 or D:5/Macau-headquartered entities) requires prior notification via SNAP-R at least 25 calendar days before export, giving TPP, performance density, datacenter design/marketing, prior 12-month approvals, memory bandwidth and cluster size and use; NAC/ACA exclude datacenter items meeting 3A090.a.
quote: you must provide prior notification under License Exception NAC by submitting a completed application in SNAP–R in accordance with § 748.1 of the EAR

summary: License Exception AIA covers 3A090.a/4A090.a/.z items and related software and technology to entities located in, and headquartered (with ultimate parent) in, Supplement No. 5(a) destinations; it may not be used to provide such items to entities headquartered or located outside those destinations for training 4E091 models.
quote: This license exception cannot be used to provide items identified in paragraph (a)(1) of this section to entities headquartered outside of or located outside of paragraph (a) in supplement no. 5 to this part for training AI models specified in ECCN 4E091.

summary: License Exception AIA also authorizes export of 4E091 model weights to entities headquartered in Supplement No. 5(a) destinations, if the recipient is located outside Macau and D:5 and the weights are stored in a facility complying with paras. 14, 15 and 18 of Supplement No. 10 to part 748.
quote: These items will be stored in a facility that complies with paragraphs 14, 15 and 18 of the guidelines outlined in supplement no. 10 to part 748

summary: Under AIA, the exporter must furnish the ECCN of each item to the ultimate consignee (the entity owning the items) and, with each shipment, notify the consignee in writing that it is made under License Exception AIA.
quote: The exporter, reexporter, or transferor must furnish to the ultimate consignee the ECCN of each item to be exported, reexported, or transferred (incountry) pursuant to this section.

summary: Before using AIA for chips (§ 740.27(a)(1)), the exporter must obtain a one-time certification from each ultimate consignee (awareness of AIA, no Part 744 end uses, no IaaS for 4E091 training for non-listed entities, no onward transfer outside listed destinations without BIS authorization).
quote: Prior to use of this license exception for items identified in (a)(1) only, the exporter, reexporter, or transferor must obtain a certification from the ultimate consignee.

summary: AIA ultimate consignees undertake not to use the items to provide IaaS access for training 4E091 models for entities headquartered or located outside Supplement No. 5(a) destinations, and not to export or transfer them to such entities or to Part 744 end uses without BIS authorization.
quote: Agrees items received under this license exception are not, without prior authorization from the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), to be used to provide Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) access for training AI models specified in ECCN 4E091
conditional_on: Receipt of items under License Exception AIA

summary: The AIA ultimate-consignee certification must be submitted to BIS (EARReports@bis.doc.gov, 'AIA Certification') before the initial export when the consignee receives items with a cumulative TPP of 253,000,000.
quote: the exporter, reexporter, or transferor must submit the certification to EARReports@bis.doc.gov, with the subject line: AIA Certification.

summary: License Exception ACM authorizes advanced computing items to 'private sector end users' for development, production or warehouse storage of items ultimately destined to customers outside Macau and D:5; unavailable to Macau, D:5 or consignees headquartered there.
quote: License Exception ACM authorizes the export, reexport, and transfer (in-country) of eligible items specified in paragraph (b) to ‘private sector end users’ for the ‘‘development,’’ ‘‘production,’’ or storage

summary: ACM users must keep a distribution system accounting for controlled items moved into and out of each facility, with records updated at least every six months.
quote: Exporters, reexporters, and transferors must maintain a system of distribution that allows them to account for the number of controlled items transferred to, and ... subsequently out, of the facility.

summary: License Exception LPP authorizes export and reexport (not in-country transfer) of eligible chips up to 26,900,000 cumulative TPP per calendar year per ultimate consignee, except to Macau, D:5 or entities headquartered there, and not for Part 744 end uses.
quote: License Exception LPP authorizes the export and reexport of up to 26,900,000 cumulative total processing performance (TPP) of advanced computing integrated circuits per-calendar year directly to a single ultimate consignee.

summary: Before using LPP, the exporter must obtain a certification from the ultimate consignee (awareness of LPP, no Part 744 uses, not having received 26,900,000 cumulative TPP in the calendar year).
quote: Prior to use of this license exception the exporter or reexporter must obtain a certification from the ultimate consignee

summary: LPP exporters must send BIS a copy of the consignee certification within 30 days of export and notify BIS before any shipment with an aggregate TPP of 3,200,000.
quote: must provide a copy of that certification to BIS by email to EARReports@bis.doc.gov with subject line ‘‘LPP Shipment’’

summary: LPP ultimate consignees must notify BIS ('LPP TPP Limit Reached') as soon as they receive the shipment that exhausts the 26,900,000 TPP annual limit.
quote: Ultimate consignees receiving eligible commodities under this License Exception TPP must notify BIS by email to EARReports@bis.doc.gov with subject line ‘‘LPP TPP Limit Reached’’

summary: Records relating to License Exceptions AIA, ACM and LPP are added to the records that must be retained under § 762.2.
quote: (58) § 740.27, License Exception AIA. (59) § 740.28, License Exception ACM. (60) § 740.29, License Exception LPP.

summary: Know-your-customer red flag: IaaS providers helping train a 4E091 model for an entity headquartered outside Supplement No. 5(a) destinations should ask whether the customer intends to export the model and apply for a licence or inform the customer of its licence obligation.
provision: Supp. No. 3 to part 732, Red Flag 28
quote: In such cases, the IaaS provider should inquire if the customer intends to export the model and if so, apply for a license as required or inform the customer of their obligation to do so prior to export.

summary: Exporters may confirm that a model is outside 4E091 (below the capability-equivalent operations) by classification request to BIS or by self-classification relying on BIS guidance or U.S. AI Safety Institute/DOE technical opinions.
quote: Classification requests may be submitted to confirm that technology is not controlled under ECCN 4E091

summary: BIS reviews licence applications for § 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) advanced computing items under a presumption of denial for Macau, D:5 and entities headquartered there, and a presumption of approval for Supplement No. 5(a) destinations and entities headquartered there.
quote: will be reviewed under a presumption of denial

summary: For all other destinations, BIS approves applications up to a per-country allocation of 790,000,000 TPP (2025-2027) and denies them once it is met; allocations may rise up to 100% for Supplement No. 5(b) destinations with government assurances; BIS reviews allocations annually with State, Energy and Defense and posts progress online.
quote: After the country allocations above are met, applications will be reviewed under a policy of denial.

summary: BIS reviews applications for § 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(B) (.b-level) items under a presumption of approval except for Macau, D:5 and entities headquartered there (presumption of denial).
quote: Applications for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) will be reviewed with a presumption of approval to or within destinations not specified in Country Group D:5 or Macau

summary: BIS reviews applications for 4E091 model weights under a presumption of denial for end users headquartered (or with ultimate parent) outside Supplement No. 5(a) destinations.
quote: Applications to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) items classified under ECCN 4E091 will be reviewed under a presumption of denial

summary: BIS adjudicates complete UVEU applications within 30 days and updates the VEU list (Supplement No. 7) with new data-center locations; no requirements beyond Supplement No. 10 may be imposed as a condition of the original UVEU grant.
quote: No other requirements may be placed on the UVEU beyond those described in Supplement No. 10 to this part as a condition for granting the original UVEU application.

summary: UVEU: the owner of the advanced computing ICs applies and certifies it will follow Supplement No. 10 (paras. 14, 15, 18 by 2026-01-15), identifies and obtains certifications from other entities involved, and a distinct operator needs its own UVEU; UVEUs must be headquartered in Supplement No. 5(a) destinations and may place data centers anywhere except Macau/D:5.
quote: To qualify for UVEU authorization, the owner of the advanced computing ICs must certify that it will follow the guidelines in Supplement No. 10 to this part.
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: NVEU: a separate authorization per country; owner adheres to Supplement No. 10 and possibly other requirements, provides written assurances from other entities, may need government-to-government assurances; distinct operator needs its own NVEU; eligible if headquartered or located in Country Groups A, B or D:1-D:4 (not Macau/D:5).
quote: For every additional country in which the NVEU wants to operate, the owner of the advanced compute must obtain a separate NVEU authorization.
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU applications are advisory-opinion requests listing items by ECCN and the Supplement No. 8 information (D:5/Macau government or military ties, NVEU customer lists, supply-chain plan to keep PRC-origin equipment out, export compliance programme, NVEU ability to verify items have not left the country).
quote: applications for Authorization VEU must include the information described in Supplement No. 8 to this part
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: UVEUs must notify BIS 180 days before exporting to a datacenter in a new location (with its physical address), and 60 days in advance of inter-country chip transfers or data-center construction in countries not previously notified.
quote: A UVEU will need to file a notification with BIS when building a datacenter in a new location 180 days before any exports, reexports, or transfers (incountry) to the new datacenter.
conditional_on: UVEU status

summary: Items under Data Center VEU authorizations may not be used for Part 744 activities and may only be used or consumed at the end user's own facility in an authorized destination; reexports and in-country transfers are not permitted except to another location of the same VEU or with separate authorization.
quote: Items obtained under Data Center VEU Authorizations may not be used for any activities described in part 744 of the EAR.
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: Reexporters using VEU authorizations report to BIS (annually for General VEU, semi-annually for Data Center VEU) the name and address of each VEU, destination, quantity, value and ECCN of items.
quote: Reexporters who make use of Data Center VEU Authorizations are required to submit semi-annual reports to BIS.

summary: Data Center VEU end users report semi-annually their current inventory of eligible items, dates of receipt and (NVEUs) current customers.
quote: End users who make use of Data Center VEU Authorizations must submit reports to BIS semi-annually.
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: Exporters, reexporters, transferors and VEUs must allow BIS review of records, including on-site reviews, and VEUs must cooperate with BIS audits of records and facilities.
quote: Upon request by BIS, exporters, reexporters, transferors, and validated end-users must allow review of records, including on-site reviews
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU must have a credible plan or track record for physical, cyber and personnel security, export-control compliance and respect for human rights, and be free (with subsidiaries, parents and personnel) of ties, including R&D agreements, to military or military-intelligence end users.
quote: must be free of ties to any ‘military end users’
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU (including non-U.S. persons) must adhere to the U.S. outbound investment rules (31 CFR part 850, without the § 850.501(g) exception, submitting to BIS) and to ICTS determinations under 15 CFR part 791.
quote: must adhere to the U.S. rules on outbound investment at 31 CFR part 850 as applied to U.S. persons regardless of whether such VEU, entity, or individual is a U.S. person
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU must show it has eliminated supply-chain dependencies on advanced chips and networking equipment produced by Macau/D:5-headquartered entities and on equipment and services on the FCC covered list.
quote: the VEU must demonstrate that it has eliminated supply chain dependencies on advanced semiconductors
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU must notify the U.S. Government of cooperative activities (e.g., joint ventures) with Macau/D:5-headquartered or Entity List/SDN parties and report their equity, ownership or debt interests in the VEU, except investments under 1% or $1 million.
quote: The VEU must report to BIS all equity interests (including contingent equity interests) or ownership stakes in the VEU
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU may not, without BIS authorization, transfer chips, assemblies or computers meeting 3A090.a/4A090.a to Macau/D:5-located or -headquartered entities, persons working for listed parties (Entity List, ISN, SDN) or persons employed by Macau/D:5 governments or presenting a diversion risk.
quote: The VEU may not, without authorization from BIS, transfer chips, assemblies, or computers that meet or exceed the scope of ECCN 3A090.a, 4A090.a
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: UVEU geographic allocation caps: no more than 25% of total AI compute outside Supplement No. 5(a) countries and 7% in any single other country (UVEUs headquartered there); no more than 50% outside the United States (U.S.-headquartered UVEUs).
quote: UVEUs will be subject to the geographic allocations identified in paragraph 6 or Supplement No. 10 to this part.
conditional_on: UVEU status

summary: VEU (with subsidiaries and parents) may not, without BIS authorization, train a 4E091 model outside Supplement No. 5(a) countries or as IaaS for entities headquartered outside them; fine-tuning up to 25% of original training operations, API access and IaaS for inference remain allowed.
quote: may not, without authorization from BIS, train an AI model specified in ECCN 4E091, in whole or in part, in a location outside of, or as Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) for an entity headquartered outside of, countries listed in paragraph (a) to Supplement No. 5 to Part 740.
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU may store or transfer 4E091 model weights only to facilities in Supplement No. 5(a) countries, or elsewhere outside Macau/D:5 in facilities owned or operated by entities headquartered in those countries that comply with paras. 14, 15 and 18 by 2026-01-15.
quote: The VEU may only store or transfer the model weights of an advanced AI model specified in ECCN 4E091 to facilities located in countries listed in paragraph (a) to Supplement No. 5 to Part 740
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU must ensure no EAR items support Part 744 activities, military and intelligence entities of Macau/D:5 or flagged by BIS, or activities enabling human rights abuses or repression (censorship, arbitrary surveillance, abusive genetic collection).
quote: The VEU is responsible for ensuring that no items subject to the EAR are used to support any of the following
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU reports semi-annually (1 February, 1 August) a facility-specific chip accounting for itself and parents/subsidiaries: quantities and types of 3A090.a chips purchased, exported, transferred and installed, total aggregate compute and chip attrition.
quote: a complete facility-specific chip accounting for itself and all parent and subsidiary entities
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU must carry out ongoing monitoring, evaluation and end-user due diligence on all conditions, notify BIS whenever any requirement is not met, and keep all related records for five years, available to BIS on request.
quote: The VEU must perform ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and end user due diligence of all the vetting requirements, export restrictions, acceptable use policies, and security requirements herein.
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU certification follows Supplement No. 9; entities outside Supplement No. 5(a), Macau and D:5 qualify only if they meet Supplement No. 10 and, for NVEUs, a government-to-government arrangement exists; VEU must show no foreign ownership, control or influence (FOCI) factors related to Macau/D:5 under NISPOM 32 CFR 117.11(b) and additional factors.
quote: must meet ownership security standards to ensure there are no Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence (FOCI) factors related to Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5.
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU datacenters must comply with NIST 800-53 consistent with FedRAMP High plus listed controls; model weights and training techniques treated as FIPS-199 HIGH; anti-seizure and anti-tampering measures; defense-in-depth security planning (threat, vulnerability, probability, consequence analysis); UFC 4-010-05 physical security, no windows in server core areas, 24/7 guard patrol or PIDS with 15-minute response.
applies_from: 2026-01-15 (delayed compliance date for Supp. No. 10 paras. 14, 15 and 18)
quote: The VEU’s datacenters must be compliant with NIST 800–53 in a fashion certified as appropriate for compliance with these conditions and consistent with the security requirements associated with FedRAMP High
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: Compliance with the NIST 800-53 requirements must be attested annually by a FedRAMP-recognized Third-Party Assessment Organization (3PAO) and made available to BIS.
applies_from: 2026-01-15 (delayed compliance date for Supp. No. 10 paras. 14, 15 and 18)
quote: must be attested annually by a Third-Party Assessment Organization (3PAO) and made available to BIS
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: AI-specific cybersecurity: follow NSA 'Deploying AI Systems Securely' and CISA CPG 1.0 actions; log and monitor usage (including third-party APIs and fine-tuning); store 4E091 weights on dedicated devices; rate-limit every interface to its legitimate output rate; interfaces allowing extraction within six months must be narrow, secured APIs.
applies_from: 2026-01-15 (delayed compliance date for Supp. No. 10 paras. 14, 15 and 18)
quote: The VEU will establish and bear responsibility for the following additional practices for AI security
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU must develop with the chip provider a shipment security plan (validated shippers, chain of custody, anti-theft and anti-tampering, inspection on receipt), track chips in transit, and apply verifiable end-of-life sanitization and disposal procedures.
quote: The VEU must work with the chip provider to develop, implement, and maintain a shipment security plan
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: VEU must report theft, loss or tampering incidents to BIS within 30 days and report transit anomalies.
quote: reporting any theft, loss, or tampering incidents to BIS within 30 days
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: Personnel security: vetting plan for everyone with access; exclude individuals on SDN/sanctions lists or with employment history with Macau/D:5 governments, intelligence or military or listed parties; extra vetting for those with Macau/D:5-headquartered employers; insider-threat programme per the CISA guide.
applies_from: 2026-01-15 (delayed compliance date for Supp. No. 10 paras. 14, 15 and 18)
quote: The VEU must develop a plan to implement a personnel vetting model covering all individuals granted access to the VEU data center facility or corresponding systems.
conditional_on: Holding or applying for Data Center VEU authorization (UVEU or NVEU)

summary: Exports, reexports or transfers under General or Data Center VEU are limited to validated end-users listed in supplement no. 7 to part 748; other end-users may not receive eligible items under these authorizations.
quote: The only end-users to whom eligible items may be exported, reexported, or transferred under a General VEU Authorization

summary: Requests for VEU authorization must be made as an advisory opinion request under 748.3(c), list the items by ECCN, and include the information in supplement no. 8; requests may come from exporters, reexporters or end-users.
quote: requests for authorization must be submitted in the form of an advisory opinion request

summary: In evaluating an end user for VEU eligibility, the End-User Review Committee considers a range of listed factors, including compliance record, need for on-site review, technology control plan and relationships with U.S. and foreign companies.
quote: In evaluating an end user for eligibility under authorization VEU, the ERC will consider a range of information

summary: Information submitted in a VEU request is treated as continuing representations; any material or substantive change relating to the authorization must be promptly reported to BIS, whether or not authorization has been granted.
quote: Any material or substantive change relating to the authorization must be promptly reported to BIS

summary: Items controlled under the EAR for missile technology (MT) and crime control (CC) reasons may not be exported or reexported under General or Data Center VEU Authorizations.
quote: Items controlled under the EAR for missile technology (MT) and crime control (CC) reasons may not be exported or reexported under General or Data Center VEU Authorizations.

summary: Before an initial export or reexport to a validated end-user under either VEU authorization, exporters or reexporters must obtain certifications from the end-user regarding end use and compliance with VEU requirements, containing the contents set out in supplement no. 8.
quote: exporters or reexporters must obtain certifications

summary: Certifications and all records relating to VEU must be retained under the recordkeeping requirements of part 762 of the EAR.
quote: Certifications and all records relating to VEU must be retained by exporters or reexporters

summary: Reexporters using General VEU Authorization must file annual reports to BIS; reexporters using Data Center VEU Authorization must file semi-annual reports. Each report lists, per validated end-user, name and address, eligible destination, quantity, value and ECCNs.
quote: Reexporters who make use of General VEU Authorizations are required to submit annual reports to BIS.

summary: End users under Data Center VEU must submit semi-annual reports to BIS covering current inventory of eligible items, dates and recipients of receipt, description of current compute use, and a list of current customers with their utilization.
quote: End users who make use of Data Center VEU Authorizations must submit reports to BIS semi-annually.

summary: On BIS request, exporters, reexporters, transferors and validated end-users must allow review of records, including on-site reviews of the information covered by paragraphs (e) and (f)(1).
quote: Upon request by BIS, exporters, reexporters, transferors, and validated end-users must allow review of records
conditional_on: Upon request by BIS

summary: Exporters and reexporters shipping under either VEU authorization, and persons transferring in-country under General VEU, must give the receiving VEU written notice of the shipment or transfer listing VEU-authorized contents and ECCNs; notice timing is agreed in advance and the notices must be kept.
quote: are required to provide the VEUs to which they are shipping or transferring notice of the shipment or transfer

summary: A Data Center VEU application must describe physical and logical security requirements for each location housing controlled items, access policies, an information security plan (cybersecurity, logging and monitoring, technology control, personnel security, incident reporting), and a supply chain plan preventing PRC-origin equipment and PRC vendors in the data center environment.

conditional_on: shipments made under the authorization of the TGL

summary: Items controlled under the listed ECCNs (new SME controls) and associated software and technology are not eligible for license exceptions other than License Exception GOV, restricted to § 740.11(b), when exported to Macau or Country Group D:5.
quote: the license exception is other than License Exception GOV, restricted to eligibility under the provisions of § 740.11(b)
conditional_on: export, reexport or in-country transfer to or within Macau or Country Group D:5

summary: A license is required for exports, reexports and in-country transfers to or within Macau or Country Group D:5 of listed semiconductor manufacturing equipment, software and technology (ECCNs 3B001, 3B002, 3D001, 3D002, 3E001).
quote: A license is required for exports, reexports, and transfers (in-country) to or within either Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5
conditional_on: destination is Macau or a destination in Country Group D:5

summary: License applications for the items in § 742.4(a)(4) are reviewed under the license review policies of § 744.23(d), except that applications are reviewed case by case where no license would be required under part 744.
quote: License applications for items specified in paragraph (a)(4) of this section will be reviewed consistent with license review policies in § 744.23(d) of the EAR
conditional_on: license application for items in § 742.4(a)(4)

summary: Regional stability license requirements apply to exports, reexports and in-country transfers to or within Macau or Country Group D:5 of listed advanced computing and semiconductor manufacturing items and associated software and technology, and to exports from abroad originating in China or Macau of certain 3E001 technology; deemed exports are excluded.
quote: A license is required for items specified in ECCNs 3A090
conditional_on: destination is Macau or Country Group D:5, or export from abroad originating in China or Macau

summary: U.S. persons are informed that a license is required for shipping, transmitting, transferring, facilitating or servicing (including installation) listed items or end uses in China, Macau or Country Group D:5 when they know the activity is covered (advanced-node IC development or production, Category 3 items for advanced-node ICs, and listed SME).
quote: then a license is required for shipping, transmitting, or transferring (in-country)
conditional_on: the person knows the export, reexport or in-country transfer meets one of the activities in paragraphs (c)(2)(i) through (iii)

summary: License applications submitted under the notice in § 744.6(c)(2) are reviewed with a presumption of denial for Macau and Country Group D:5 destinations, except for foreign-made items not subject to the EAR that perform the same function (presumption of approval); other applications are reviewed case by case.
quote: Applications for licenses submitted pursuant to the notice of a license requirement set forth in paragraph (c)(2) of this section will be reviewed with a presumption of denial
conditional_on: license application submitted under the notice in § 744.6(c)(2)

summary: General prohibition on exporting, reexporting or transferring (in-country) without a license, when the exporter knows the item is destined for supercomputer, advanced-node IC or SME end uses in China, Macau or Country Group D:5 (including SME for front-end IC production equipment); back-end exclusion in paragraph (a)(5).
quote: you may not export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) without a license any item subject to the EAR described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (4) of this section
conditional_on: exporter has knowledge at the time of export, reexport or transfer that the item is destined for a listed destination, end use or end user; not excluded by paragraph (a)(5)

summary: Persons informed by BIS by specific notice or Federal Register amendment that a license is required for a specific export, reexport or transfer (in-country) to a certain end-user may not proceed without that license. Paragraph (c) adds that no license exception may overcome the prohibition in paragraph (a).
quote: that a license is required for a specific export, reexport, or transfer (in-country)
conditional_on: BIS has informed the person that a license is required for a specific end-user

summary: Specific notice under paragraph (b) is to be given only by, or at the direction of, the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Export Administration. Oral notice must be followed by a written notice within two working days signed by the Deputy Assistant Secretary or designee.
quote: Specific notice is to be given only by, or at the direction of, the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Export Administration.
conditional_on: BIS gives specific notice under paragraph (b)

summary: License applications are reviewed with a presumption of denial for Macau and Country Group D:5 destinations, with a presumption of approval in specified cases, and case-by-case review otherwise, taking into account technology level, customers, compliance plans and contract sanctity.
quote: Applications will be reviewed with a presumption of denial for Macau and destinations specified in Country Group D:5.

summary: Supplement No. 1 to Part 774 revises ECCNs 3B001, 3B002, 3D001, 3D002, 3D003 and 3E001, each with license requirements by reason for control (NS, RS, AT, MT, NP) and country chart columns. A License Requirements Note in 3D002 and 3E001 refers to additional requirements in § 744.17 for certain microprocessors.
provision: Supp. No. 1 to Part 774, ECCNs 3B001, 3D001, 3E001 (License Requirements)
quote: NS applies to ‘‘technology’’ for commodities controlled
conditional_on: export, reexport or transfer of the listed items to the specified destinations

summary: ECCN 3D001 refers to § 743.1 of the EAR for reporting requirements for exports under License Exceptions, Special Comprehensive Licenses and Validated End-User authorizations. The reporting duty itself is stated in § 743.1, not in this part.
provision: Supp. No. 1 to Part 774, ECCN 3D001 (Reporting Requirements)
quote: See § 743.1 of the EAR for reporting requirements for exports under License Exceptions, Special Comprehensive Licenses, and Validated End-User authorizations.
conditional_on: export under License Exceptions, Special Comprehensive Licenses or Validated End-User authorizations

summary: License Exception STA may not be used to ship or transmit software or technology specially designed for the development or production of listed equipment (e.g., 3A002.g.1 or 3B001.a.2) to Country Group A:6 destinations, and for certain items to Country Group A:5 or A:6 destinations.
provision: Supp. No. 1 to Part 774, ECCN 3D001 (Special Conditions for STA)
quote: License Exception STA may not be
conditional_on: shipment or transmission of listed software or technology to Country Group A:5 or A:6 destinations

summary: License Exception STA for exports, reexports and in-country transfers to or within the UAE is available only where the ultimate consignee and all end users are approved entities listed in supplement no. 8 to part 740. Footnote 5 to the UAE entry in Country Group A:5 states the same limit.
quote: is destined to or within the UAE and either the ultimate consignee or any end user is not an approved entity listed in supplement no. 8 to this part
conditional_on: item exported, reexported or transferred under License Exception STA

summary: Within 30 days of receiving an advisory opinion request from a UAE or U.S.-headquartered entity, the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State and the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, determines whether to approve the entity and the scope of authorization. BIS notifies the requester within 5 days of a determination.
applies_from: within 30 days of receiving a request
quote: shall determine whether the entity should be approved for addition to this supplement
conditional_on: request submitted under the § 748.3(c) process

summary: UAE government agencies, including the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces, are approved entities to receive advanced computing items license-free and to receive other eligible items under full use of License Exception STA. Approval excludes UAE state-owned corporations and contractors or grantees of UAE government agencies.
quote: are approved entities to receive advanced computing items license-free

summary: Ultimate consignees and end users in the UAE listed in the table to para. (b) may receive items license-free and/or under License Exception STA as specified. Para. (c) grants the same to listed U.S.-headquartered AI companies and their subsidiaries, and Note 1 states that listed entities may receive items at any of their UAE addresses.
quote: may receive items license-free consistent with § 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A)–(B) and/or under License Exception STA, as specified.
conditional_on: as specified in the supplement table for each entity

summary: The authorization for G42 and Core42 in supplement no. 8 expires automatically on April 6, 2027, unless BIS gives subsequent notice.
provision: Supplement no. 8 to part 740, Note 2 to paragraph (b)
quote: shall automatically expire on April 6, 2027
conditional_on: absent subsequent notice by BIS

summary: A license is required to export, reexport or transfer (in-country) listed ECCN items, including advanced computing items, to or within the UAE. The license requirement does not apply where the ultimate consignee and all end users are approved UAE entities listed in supplement no. 8 for the items concerned.
quote: A license is required to export, reexport, or transfer (incountry) items specified in ECCNs
conditional_on: not required where the ultimate consignee and all end users are approved entities in the UAE listed in supplement no. 8 to part 740

summary: The license requirement text for listed ECCNs in Supplement No. 1 to part 774 is revised to add the United Arab Emirates to the RS control destinations, with the same exclusion for Country Groups A:5 and A:6 and approved entities.
quote: To or within the United Arab Emirates or destinations specified in Country Groups D:1, D:4, and D:5
conditional_on: destinations other than Country Groups A:5 or A:6

summary: Operating system provider shall provide an accessible account-setup interface requiring the account holder to indicate the user's birth date or age, and shall provide a developer that requested it a real-time API signal of the user's age bracket (under 13, 13-15, 16-17, 18 or over).
quote: Provide an accessible interface at account setup that requires an account holder to indicate the birth date, age, or both, of the user of that device

summary: Operating system provider shall send only the minimum amount of information necessary to comply with the title and shall not share the digital signal information with a third party for a purpose not required by the title.
quote: Send only the minimum amount of information necessary to comply with this title

summary: Developer shall request an age signal for a particular user from an operating system provider or a covered application store when the application is downloaded and launched.
quote: A developer shall request a signal with respect to a particular user from an operating system provider or a covered application store when the application is downloaded and launched.

summary: Developer shall not willfully disregard internal clear and convincing information indicating that a user's age differs from the signal; the signal is the primary indicator of age unless the developer holds contrary clear and convincing information, which it shall then use.
quote: A developer shall not willfully disregard internal clear and convincing information

summary: Developer shall use the received signal to comply with applicable law, shall not request from an operating system provider or covered application store more information than the minimum necessary, and shall not share the signal with a third party for a purpose not required by the title.
quote: shall use that signal to comply with applicable law but shall not do either of the following

summary: For devices whose account setup was completed before January 1, 2027, operating system provider shall provide an accessible interface allowing the account holder to indicate the user's birth date or age.
quote: an operating system provider shall, before July 1, 2027, provide an accessible interface that allows an account holder to indicate the birth date, age, or both

summary: For applications last updated on or after January 1, 2026 and downloaded before January 1, 2027, where the developer has not requested a signal for that user, the developer shall request a signal from a covered application store.
quote: the developer shall request a signal from a covered application store with respect to that user before July 1, 2027

summary: Operating system provider or covered application store shall comply with the title in a nondiscriminatory manner, including by imposing at least the same restrictions and obligations on its own applications and distribution as on third-party applications or distributors.
quote: shall impose at least the same restrictions and obligations on its own applications

summary: Operating system provider or covered application store shall not use data collected from a third party in the course of compliance to compete against that third party, give its own store preference, or otherwise use such data or the consent mechanism anticompetitively.
quote: shall not use data collected from a third party in the course of compliance with this title to compete against that third party

summary: Research using personal information collected for other purposes must be compatible with the original business purpose, subsequently pseudonymized and deidentified, protected by technical safeguards and business processes against reidentification, used solely for compatible research purposes, and subject to additional security controls limiting access.
quote: Research with personal information that may have been collected from a consumer in the course of the consumer's interactions with a business' service or device for other purposes shall be:
conditional_on: Research with personal information collected from a consumer in the course of interactions with a business' service or device for other purposes

summary: Information is deidentified only if the business possessing it takes reasonable measures against association with a consumer or household, publicly commits to keep it deidentified and not reidentify it (except to test deidentification), and contractually obligates recipients to comply with the subdivision.
quote: Takes reasonable measures to ensure that the information cannot be associated with a consumer or household.
conditional_on: Information treated as deidentified under Civil Code 1798.140(m)

summary: A service provider's written contract must prohibit it from selling or sharing the personal information, from retaining, using or disclosing it for purposes other than the contracted business purposes, and from retaining, using or disclosing it outside the direct business relationship; the contract must also limit combining data; the contractor contract (1798.140(j)) includes a certification of compliance.
quote: provided that the contract prohibits the person from:
conditional_on: Person acting as a service provider or contractor processing personal information on behalf of a business under a written contract

summary: A service provider or contractor that engages another person to assist in processing personal information for a business purpose must notify the business and bind that person by a written contract to the same requirements.
quote: it shall notify the business of that engagement, and the engagement shall be pursuant to a written contract
conditional_on: Service provider or contractor engages another person to assist in processing personal information

summary: A third party that acquires personal information in a merger, acquisition, bankruptcy or similar transaction and materially alters use or sharing inconsistently with promises made at collection must give prior notice to the consumer; the same notice duty appears for the sharing definition in 1798.140(ah)(2)(C).
quote: it shall provide prior notice of the new or changed practice to the consumer
conditional_on: Third party materially alters how it uses or shares a consumer's personal information in a manner materially inconsistent with promises made at the time of collection

summary: The California Privacy Protection Agency (after the Attorney General handover) is empowered to issue regulations on many topics, including opt-out rights and procedures, verifiable requests, correction, business purposes, opt-out preference signals (including age-band signals), limits on sensitive personal information, and rules on how businesses respond to opt-out signals (no degraded functionality, fees, or coercion).
applies_from: Beginning the later of July 1, 2021, or six months after the agency provides notice to the Attorney General that it is prepared to begin rulemaking; final regulations timeline July 1, 2022 (Sec. 28 subd. (d))
quote: Issuing regulations governing access and opt-out rights with respect to a business' use of automated decisionmaking technology

summary: Under regulations to be issued, businesses whose processing of personal information presents significant risk to consumers' privacy or security must perform a cybersecurity audit annually, with scope and independence set by regulation.
quote: Perform a cybersecurity audit on an annual basis
conditional_on: Regulations issued under Civil Code 1798.185(a)(14) requiring businesses whose processing presents significant risk

summary: Under regulations to be issued, businesses whose processing presents significant risk must submit to the California Privacy Protection Agency on a regular basis a risk assessment of their processing, identifying benefits and risks, including whether sensitive personal information is involved.
quote: Submit to the California Privacy Protection Agency on a regular basis a risk assessment
conditional_on: Regulations issued under Civil Code 1798.185(a)(14) requiring businesses whose processing presents significant risk

summary: The agency must review Insurance Code provisions on consumer privacy and adopt a regulation applying only the more protective provisions of the Act to insurance companies; the Insurance Commissioner keeps jurisdiction over insurance rates and pricing.
quote: the agency shall adopt a regulation that applies only the more protective provisions of this title to insurance companies
conditional_on: Completion of the review under Civil Code 1798.185(a)(20)

summary: The Superintendent must convene a working group with the composition set out in subdivision (c) (teachers, staff, administrators, faculty, industry representatives, pupils; at least half teachers) which is subject to the Bagley-Keene Open Meeting Act.
quote: The Superintendent shall convene a working group for all of the following purposes:

summary: The working group must assess the current and future state of AI use in education (including cost, ownership, licensing and source-code access), hold at least three public meetings, detail current uses (human-centered and human replacement AI), and solicit input from educators and pupils, and identify ways for the state to support educators.
quote: Conduct at least three public meetings to incorporate feedback from pupils, families, and relevant stakeholders into the assessment required by subparagraph (A).

summary: The working group must develop guidance for local educational agencies and charter schools on the safe use of AI in education, covering academic integrity, acceptable uses, data privacy and security, parent access to pupil AI inputs, and software procurement.
quote: On or before January 1, 2026, develop guidance for local educational agencies and charter schools on the safe use of artificial intelligence in education

summary: The working group must develop a model policy for local educational agencies and charter schools on the safe and effective use of AI, covering topics listed in paragraph (4)(A) to (I), including academic integrity, data privacy, procurement, equity and professional development.
quote: On or before July 1, 2026, develop a model policy for local educational agencies and charter schools

summary: The department must post on its website the guidance and the model policy developed under paragraphs (3) and (4) of subdivision (d).
quote: The department shall post on its internet website the guidance developed pursuant to paragraph (3) of subdivision (d)

summary: The working group must submit a report to the policy and fiscal committees of the Legislature presenting the assessment and any findings or recommendations; the working group is dissolved upon submission.
quote: On or before January 1, 2027, submit a report to the appropriate policy and fiscal committees of the Legislature

summary: Before each release or substantial modification of a generative AI system or service made publicly available to Californians, the developer must post on its website documentation of training data, covering sources, purpose, data point counts, data types, copyright status, purchase or licence, personal and aggregate consumer information, cleaning, collection period, first-use dates and synthetic data use; exemptions apply for security and integrity, aircraft operation, and national security systems.
applies_from: On or before January 1, 2026, and before each time thereafter
quote: the developer of the system or service shall post on the developer's internet website documentation regarding the data used by the developer to train the generative artificial intelligence system or service
conditional_on: Generative AI system or service released on or after January 1, 2022, or a substantial modification of one, made publicly available to Californians

summary: Before testing in California, the manufacturer performing testing must hold insurance, a surety bond or proof of self-insurance of $5,000,000 and provide evidence to the department. The application certifications in subdivision (c)(3) repeat the same insurance requirement.
applies_from: Prior to the start of testing in this state
quote: the manufacturer performing the testing shall obtain an instrument of insurance, surety bond, or proof of self-insurance in the amount of five million dollars ($5,000,000)
conditional_on: Testing on public roads under subdivision (b)

summary: During testing, the driver (the operator) must sit in the driver's seat, monitor safe operation and be able to take immediate manual control. The vehicle may be operated for testing only by employees, contractors or persons designated by the manufacturer.
quote: The driver shall be seated in the driver’s seat, monitoring the safe operation of the autonomous vehicle
conditional_on: Autonomous vehicle operated on public roads for testing under subdivision (b)

summary: Outside testing, an autonomous vehicle may not operate on public roads until the manufacturer submits an application that the department approves under its regulations. The application must contain the certifications in subdivision (c)(1) to (c)(3).
quote: until the manufacturer submits an application to the department
conditional_on: Except as provided in subdivision (b)

summary: The manufacturer must certify that the vehicle has an easily accessible engage/disengage mechanism, a cabin indicator of engagement, and an alert system for technology failure, which requires operator takeover or a complete stop. It must also certify operator override by brake, accelerator or steering, and compliance with federal and state safety standards.
quote: The autonomous vehicle has a system to safely alert the operator if an autonomous technology failure is detected while the autonomous technology is engaged
conditional_on: Application under subdivision (c)

summary: The vehicle must have a separate read-only mechanism that captures and stores autonomous technology sensor data for at least 30 seconds before a collision, retained until extracted by an external device. The data must be preserved for three years after the collision.
quote: The data shall be preserved for three years after the date of the collision.
conditional_on: Application under subdivision (c)(1)(G)

summary: The application must certify that the manufacturer has tested the autonomous technology on public roads and complied with any testing standards the department has set.
quote: A certification that the manufacturer has tested the autonomous technology on public roads
conditional_on: Application under subdivision (c)

summary: The department must adopt regulations on evidence of insurance, the application process and notices of noncompliance. Under subdivisions (d)(2) and (d)(3) it must also set testing, equipment and performance standards, and may adopt further requirements such as deployment limits and license rules.
quote: The department shall adopt regulations setting forth requirements for the submission of evidence of insurance, surety bond, or self-insurance

summary: The department must hold public hearings before adopting any regulation on operating an autonomous vehicle without a driver inside the vehicle.
quote: The department shall hold public hearings on the adoption of any regulation applicable to the operation of an autonomous vehicle without the presence of a driver inside the vehicle.
conditional_on: Regulation applicable to operation of an autonomous vehicle without the presence of a driver inside the vehicle

summary: The department must approve a manufacturer's application if it finds that the applicant has submitted all required information and testing and complied with the regulations. For driverless vehicles, it may impose additional requirements or require a driver.
quote: The department shall approve an application submitted by a manufacturer pursuant to subdivision (c) if it finds that the applicant has submitted all information
conditional_on: Application submitted under subdivision (c) and the department finds that the applicant has complied with the requirements

summary: After adopting the regulations under subdivision (d), the department must post a public notice on its website. It may not approve an application under those regulations until 30 days after the notice.
quote: The department shall post a public notice on its internet website when it adopts the regulations required by subdivision (d).
conditional_on: Department adopts regulations required by subdivision (d)

summary: The manufacturer of the autonomous technology must give the purchaser of an autonomous vehicle a written disclosure describing what information the installed technology collects.
quote: shall provide a written disclosure to the purchaser of an autonomous vehicle

summary: The department may adopt regulations to charge manufacturers that apply to operate autonomous vehicles a fee sufficient to recover its reasonable costs.
quote: The department may promulgate regulations to assess a fee upon a manufacturer that submits an application
conditional_on: Manufacturer submits an application under subdivision (c)

summary: Certain light autonomous vehicles (model year 2031 or later, gross vehicle weight rating under 8,501 pounds) may operate only under a deployment permit, and only if they are zero-emission vehicles.
quote: shall only be operated pursuant to a deployment permit
conditional_on: To the extent authorized by federal law; model year 2031 or later; gross vehicle weight rating less than 8,501 pounds; zero-emission vehicle as defined in Health and Safety Code § 44258

summary: The department may not begin rulemaking to implement the zero-emission deployment permit requirement before January 1, 2027.
quote: The department shall not commence rulemaking for the adoption of regulations implementing this subdivision before January 1, 2027.
conditional_on: Implementation of subdivision (i)

summary: The manufacturer must keep a dedicated emergency telephone line staffed around the clock, answer calls within 30 seconds through a remote human operator who can immobilize or move the vehicle, and provide a two-way voice device that reaches that operator within 30 seconds. It must also give law enforcement and firefighters access to any override system and train them on it.
quote: shall maintain a dedicated emergency response telephone line that is available for emergency response officials during all hours when an autonomous vehicle is on a public road
conditional_on: Manufacturer operating under a testing or deployment permit issued by the department; applies only to vehicles operated without a human operator physically present (§ 38751(e))

summary: The department may not renew, reinstate or approve an expansion of a permit's operational design domain unless the manufacturer certifies full compliance with the emergency response requirements in subdivision (b).
quote: The department shall not renew, reinstate, or approve an expansion of the operational design domain of a permit unless the manufacturer certifies
conditional_on: Manufacturer certification of compliance with subdivision (b)

summary: Within two minutes of receiving an emergency geofencing message from an emergency response official, the manufacturer must direct its fleet to leave or avoid the identified area.
quote: Within two minutes of receiving an emergency geofencing message, a manufacturer shall issue direction to its fleet to leave or avoid the area identified.
conditional_on: Receipt of an emergency geofencing message under subdivision (d)(1); applies only to vehicles operated without a human operator physically present (§ 38751(e))

summary: Within 30 business days of notice that an emergency response official intends to issue geofencing messages, the manufacturer must provide that official with all information needed to issue messages and for the manufacturer to receive and respond to them.
applies_from: Within 30 business days of receiving the notice
quote: a manufacturer shall provide the emergency response official with all information necessary
conditional_on: Receipt of notice that an emergency response official wishes to begin issuing emergency geofencing messages; operative July 1, 2026 (§ 38751(g))

summary: The manufacturer must give the department any notice of autonomous vehicle noncompliance issued by a peace officer within 72 hours of issuance, or within another timeframe the department sets. The department must provide a means for submission.
quote: shall provide any issued notice of autonomous vehicle noncompliance to the department within 72 hours of issuance
conditional_on: Section operative only after the department issues regulations on notices of noncompliance (Vehicle Code § 38752(e))

summary: Counties must deposit revenue from fines collected under Penal Code § 311.12 into a county fund and allocate it one-third each to sexual assault investigator training, to shelters and services for trafficking victims, and to multidisciplinary teams; a county may transfer allocations to another county.
applies_from: Operative as set by Sec. 7 of this act
quote: Revenue from any fines collected pursuant to this section shall be deposited into a county fund established for that purpose and allocated as follows
conditional_on: Sec. 7: the act is operative only if Senate Bill 1381 of the 2023–24 Regular Session is enacted and takes effect on or before January 1, 2025.

summary: The Secretary of State must post filed successor-in-interest or licensee claims, together with the entire registry of such claims, on its internet website. The Secretary of State may also microfilm or reproduce filings, which is a permission and is not coded.
applies_from: Upon receipt and after filing of any document under this section
quote: the Secretary of State shall post the document along with the entire registry
conditional_on: A document is filed under Civil Code 3344.1 (successor or licensee claims)

summary: A person claiming to be a successor in interest to a deceased personality's rights, or a licensee, who chooses to register the claim must file a verified form with the Secretary of State containing the listed information and pay the fee. The text does not specify further addressee categories.
applies_from: On registering a claim with the Secretary of State
quote: The form shall be verified and shall include the name and date of death of the deceased personality
conditional_on: The claimant chooses to register a claim under Civil Code 3344.1(f)(2)

summary: Courts must place proceedings in actions under Chapter 7 (commencing with Section 20510) of Division 20 of the Elections Code on the calendar in filing order and give them precedence (amended Code of Civil Procedure § 35(a)).
applies_from: Sec. 1 version applies until January 1, 2027 (CCP § 35(b)); Sec. 2 version operative January 1, 2027 (CCP § 35(b))
quote: shall be placed on the calendar in the order of their date of filing and shall be given precedence.
conditional_on: Applies to actions under Chapter 7 of Division 20 of the Elections Code, which are added to the list of precedence actions by this bill.

summary: Large online platforms must develop and implement procedures to identify and remove materially deceptive election content meeting listed conditions, remove qualifying posts within 72 hours of a report, and remove identical or substantially similar previously removed content during the applicable period.
quote: Any large online platform shall develop and implement procedures for the use of state-of-the-art techniques to identify and remove materially deceptive content
conditional_on: Content reported under Section 20515(a); content posted during the period beginning 120 days before an election in California through election day (or through the 60th day after the election for content about elections officials); platform knows or acts with reckless disregard; content is about a candidate, elections official or elected official as specified.

summary: Candidates for elective office must include the disclosure "This _____ has been manipulated." (image, audio or video) when portraying themselves as doing or saying something they did not do or say, during the period beginning 120 days before an election through election day. Applies to candidates who publish such content; addressee role is the closest available.
quote: any candidate for elective office shall include the disclosure required by subdivision (d)
conditional_on: Applies during the period beginning 120 days before an election in California and through the day of the election; the disclosure requirement is the condition for the exception in Section 20513(d)(1).

summary: Large online platforms must develop and implement procedures to identify materially deceptive content and label it "This _____ has been manipulated and is not authentic." within 72 hours of a report, with a clickable explanation, for content outside the Section 20513 removal rules or within advertisements and election communications.
quote: Any large online platform shall develop and implement procedures for the use of state-of-the-art techniques to identify materially deceptive content and for labeling such content
conditional_on: Content reported under Section 20515(a); content outside the period in Section 20513(e) or within an advertisement or election communication not subject to Section 20513; labelling periods in Section 20514(e) (six months before the election through election day, or the 60th day after the election for specified content).

summary: Large online platforms must provide an easily accessible way for California residents to report content that should be removed or labelled, and must respond to the reporter within 36 hours describing action taken or not taken.
quote: A large online platform shall provide an easily accessible way for California residents to report to that platform content that should be removed pursuant to Section 20513 or labeled pursuant to Section 20514.
conditional_on: Applies to content that should be removed under Section 20513 or labelled under Section 20514.

summary: Where the content is not in English, the candidate disclosure under Section 20513(d) and the platform label under Section 20514 must appear in the language used as well as in English.
quote: the disclosure required by subdivision (d) of Section 20513 and the label required by Section 20514 must appear in the language used as well as in English.
conditional_on: Applies where the language of the materially deceptive content is not English.

summary: A person, committee or other entity may not, during the period in subdivision (c), with malice and knowingly, distribute an advertisement or other election communication containing materially deceptive content of the listed kinds. Under (b)(4), it may also not remove a required disclosure or knowingly republish covered content without the required disclosure.
applies_from: 120 days before any election in California (subd. (c)(1)); for items in (b)(1)(B) and (D), 120 days before through 60 days after the election (subd. (c)(2))
quote: A person, committee, or other entity shall not, during the time period set forth in subdivision (c), with malice, knowingly distribute an advertisement or other election communication containing materially deceptive content of any of the following:
conditional_on: Malice and knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard; content reasonably likely to harm a candidate's reputation or prospects or falsely undermine confidence in an election outcome, depending on the category; exemptions in (b)(2), (b)(3) and (e)

summary: Where a candidate portrays themself in covered content, or where content is satire or parody, the content must carry a disclosure reading "This ____ has been manipulated." (or "for purposes of satire or parody"), with the blank filled by Image, Audio or Video. Visual disclosures must meet size requirements, and audio disclosures must be read aloud at the beginning, end and at intervals of no more than two minutes. Under (g), the disclosure must be in the language used if that language is not English.
quote: the content includes a disclosure stating “This ____ has been manipulated.”
