summary: Creates the Data Brokers' Registry Fund in the State Treasury, administered by the California Privacy Protection Agency; moneys collected by the agency and the Department of Justice under the title are to be deposited into it, for expenditure upon appropriation.
quote: The fund shall be administered by the California Privacy Protection Agency.

summary: Annual registration with the agency, paying a registration fee not exceeding the reasonable costs of the website and deletion mechanism, and providing listed information (name and addresses, metrics, whether it collects minors' data, precise geolocation and reproductive health care data, a privacy-rights link that makes no use of dark patterns, and regulation status); a final item allows optional additional information.
applies_from: On or before January 31 following each year in which a business meets the definition of data broker
quote: the business shall register with the California Privacy Protection Agency
conditional_on: business meets the definition of data broker as provided in this title

summary: Registration information to include whether the data broker has undergone an audit under Section 1798.99.86(e) and the most recent year a report was submitted.
quote: Beginning January 1, 2029, whether the data broker has undergone an audit

summary: Agency creates a public web page on which registration information and the accessible deletion mechanism are accessible to the public.
quote: The California Privacy Protection Agency shall create a page on its internet website

summary: Compile for the previous calendar year the number of consumer requests received, complied with in whole or part, and denied, and the median and mean number of days to substantively respond.
applies_from: On or before July 1 following each calendar year in which a business meets the definition of a data broker as provided in this title
quote: Compile the number of requests pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 1798.99.86
conditional_on: business meets the definition of a data broker as provided in this title

summary: Disclose the compiled metrics in the privacy policy, with a link from the policy; for deletion requests, also disclose the number denied in whole or part by reason (not verifiable, not made by a consumer, exempt from deletion, other grounds) and the number of deletion-not-required cases under each provision of Sections 1798.145 or 1798.146.
applies_from: On or before July 1 following each calendar year in which a business meets the definition of a data broker as provided in this title
quote: Disclose the metrics compiled pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2) within the data broker’s privacy policy posted on their internet website
conditional_on: business meets the definition of a data broker as provided in this title

summary: Agency establishes the accessible deletion mechanism, which must include reasonable security safeguards, allow a single verifiable request to delete personal information held by all registered data brokers and their service providers or contractors, allow selective exclusion of brokers, be free, available in any language spoken by affected consumers, accessible to consumers with disabilities, usable by authorized agents, and provide status verification and descriptions.
quote: By January 1, 2026, the California Privacy Protection Agency shall establish an accessible deletion mechanism

summary: Access the deletion mechanism at least once every 45 days; within 45 days process all deletion requests and delete the consumers' personal information; treat requests denied as unverifiable as opt-outs of sale or sharing; direct associated service providers or contractors to delete or process requests accordingly; then delete the consumer's personal information at least once every 45 days absent a consumer request otherwise or an exception.
quote: Beginning August 1, 2026, a data broker shall access the accessible deletion mechanism established pursuant to subdivision (a) at least once every 45 days

summary: Personal information retained under the deletion exceptions may be used only for the exception purposes and not for other purposes, including marketing.
quote: Personal information described in paragraph (2) shall only be used for the purposes described in paragraph (2)
conditional_on: personal information retained under paragraph (2) of subdivision (c)

summary: After a consumer's deletion request has been processed, the data broker shall not sell or share new personal information of that consumer, unless the consumer requests otherwise or the sale or sharing is permitted under Section 1798.145 or 1798.146.
quote: the data broker shall not sell or share new personal information of the consumer unless the consumer requests otherwise
conditional_on: after a consumer has submitted a deletion request and the data broker has deleted the consumer's data

summary: Undergo an audit by an independent third party every three years to determine compliance with Section 1798.99.86.
quote: Beginning January 1, 2028, and every three years thereafter, a data broker shall undergo an audit by an independent third party

summary: Submit the audit report and related materials to the agency upon its written request.
applies_from: Within five business days of a written request from the California Privacy Protection Agency
quote: the data broker shall submit a report resulting from the audit and any related materials to the California Privacy Protection Agency within five business days of a written request
conditional_on: audit completed under subdivision (e)(1)

summary: Maintain the audit report and related materials for at least six years.
quote: A data broker shall maintain the report and materials described in paragraph (2) for at least six years.
conditional_on: audit completed under subdivision (e)(1)

summary: Agency may charge data brokers an access fee for accessing the deletion mechanism, not exceeding the reasonable costs of providing access; fees are deposited in the Data Brokers' Registry Fund.
quote: The California Privacy Protection Agency may charge an access fee to a data broker
conditional_on: data broker accesses the accessible deletion mechanism

summary: Agency may adopt regulations under the Administrative Procedure Act to implement and administer the title; regulations establishing fees are exempt from that Act.
quote: the California Privacy Protection Agency may adopt regulations pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Act

summary: Testing on public roads under subd. (b): the driver must be seated in the driver's seat, monitor safe operation and be able to take immediate manual control. Subd. (b)(1) limits operation to persons designated by the manufacturer.
quote: The driver shall be seated in the driver's seat, monitoring the safe operation of the autonomous vehicle
conditional_on: Operation for testing under subdivision (b), if all requirements of (b) are met

summary: Before testing in California, the manufacturer performing the testing must obtain insurance, a surety bond or proof of self-insurance of $5,000,000 and provide evidence to the department. Subd. (c)(3) requires the manufacturer to maintain the same coverage in its application certification.
applies_from: Prior to the start of testing in this state
quote: the manufacturer performing the testing shall obtain an instrument of insurance, surety bond, or proof of self-insurance in the amount of five million dollars ($5,000,000)
conditional_on: Testing under subdivision (b)

summary: An autonomous vehicle may not operate on public roads until the manufacturer submits an application that the department approves under subd. (d). The application must contain manufacturer certifications: (c)(1)(A)-(G) technical requirements (engage/disengage mechanism, cabin indicator, operator alert and takeover, FMVSS compliance, data capture), (c)(2) public-road testing, and (c)(3) insurance.
quote: Except as provided in subdivision (b), an autonomous vehicle shall not be operated on public roads until the manufacturer submits an application to the department
conditional_on: Except as provided in subdivision (b)

summary: Certified mechanism must capture and store autonomous technology sensor data for at least 30 seconds before a collision, in read-only format, separate from other required mechanisms. Data must be preserved for three years after the collision.
quote: The data shall be preserved for three years after the date of the collision.
conditional_on: Application under subdivision (c)(1)(G); the vehicle operating in autonomous mode

summary: The department must adopt regulations on evidence of insurance, the application and approval process, and notices of noncompliance. Regulations must include testing and performance standards. Under (d)(3) the department may adopt additional requirements, and under (d)(4) it must hold public hearings on regulations covering driverless operation.
quote: The department shall adopt regulations setting forth requirements for the submission of evidence of insurance

summary: The department must approve a manufacturer's application under subd. (c) if it finds the applicant has submitted all information and completed testing needed to show the vehicles are safe, and has complied with the regulations. Under (e)(2) the department may impose additional requirements for vehicles without a driver and may require a driver in the driver's seat.
quote: The department shall approve an application submitted by a manufacturer pursuant to subdivision (c) if it finds
conditional_on: Finding under subdivision (e)(1) that the applicant has submitted all information, completed testing and complied with the regulations

summary: When the department adopts the regulations under subd. (d), it must post a public notice on its website. It may not approve an application under those regulations until 30 days after the notice.
applies_from: 30 days after the public notice is provided
quote: The department shall post a public notice on its internet website when it adopts the regulations required by subdivision (d).
conditional_on: When the department adopts the regulations required by subdivision (d)

summary: The manufacturer of the autonomous technology installed on a vehicle must give the purchaser a written disclosure describing what information the autonomous technology collects.
quote: The manufacturer of the autonomous technology installed on a vehicle shall provide a written disclosure to the purchaser of an autonomous vehicle

summary: The department may adopt regulations to assess a fee on a manufacturer that applies under subd. (c), in an amount needed to recover its reasonably incurred costs.
quote: The department may promulgate regulations to assess a fee upon a manufacturer that submits an application pursuant to subdivision (c)

summary: From 2030, an autonomous vehicle of model year 2031 or later with a gross vehicle weight rating under 8,501 pounds may only be operated under a deployment permit under the California Code of Regulations, if it is a zero-emission vehicle. The text limits this to the extent authorized by federal law.
quote: any autonomous vehicle with a model year of 2031 or later and a gross vehicle weight rating of less than 8,501 pounds shall only be operated pursuant to a deployment permit
conditional_on: To the extent authorized by federal law; model year 2031 or later; gross vehicle weight rating under 8,501 pounds; zero-emission vehicle as defined in Health and Safety Code 44258

summary: The department may not begin rulemaking to implement subd. (j) before January 1, 2027.
quote: The department shall not commence rulemaking for the adoption of regulations implementing this subdivision before January 1, 2027.

summary: Driver during testing on public roads must sit in the driver's seat, monitor safe operation and be capable of taking immediate manual control; testing operation limited to persons designated by the manufacturer.
quote: The driver shall be seated in the driver's seat, monitoring the safe operation of the autonomous vehicle
conditional_on: Testing on public roads under subdivision (b)

summary: Manufacturer performing testing must obtain insurance, surety bond or proof of self-insurance of five million dollars ($5,000,000) and provide evidence to the department.
applies_from: Prior to the start of testing in this state
quote: the manufacturer performing the testing shall obtain an instrument of insurance, surety bond, or proof of self-insurance in the amount of five million dollars ($5,000,000)
conditional_on: Testing under subdivision (b)

summary: Manufacturer must submit an application to the department, approved under regulations, before an autonomous vehicle is operated on public roads (except as provided in subdivision (b)).
quote: an autonomous vehicle shall not be operated on public roads until the manufacturer submits an application to the department
conditional_on: Operation on public roads other than testing under subdivision (b)

summary: Application must contain certifications that the technology meets requirements in (c)(1)(A) to (G) (engage/disengage mechanism, cabin indicator, operator alert, FMVSS compliance, data capture), that public-road testing was done and complied with standards, and that insurance or bond of five million dollars is maintained.
quote: The application shall contain, at a minimum, all of the following certifications
conditional_on: Application under subdivision (c)

summary: Vehicle must have a separate mechanism that captures and stores autonomous technology sensor data for at least 30 seconds before a collision, in read-only format, retained until extracted.
quote: The data shall be preserved for three years after the date of the collision.
conditional_on: Application under subdivision (c)

summary: Vehicle must have an operator-accessible engage/disengage mechanism, a cabin indicator when engaged, an operator alert on failure that requires takeover or a complete stop, and allow operator control via brake, accelerator or steering wheel with a disengagement alert.
quote: The autonomous vehicle shall allow the operator to take control in multiple manners
conditional_on: Application under subdivision (c)

summary: Department must adopt regulations on requirements for submitting evidence of insurance, surety bond or self-insurance and for submitting and approving applications.
applies_from: As soon as practicable, but no later than January 1, 2015
quote: As soon as practicable, but no later than January 1, 2015, the department shall adopt regulations setting forth requirements for the submission of evidence of insurance

summary: Regulations shall include testing, equipment and performance standards necessary for safe operation; department may establish additional requirements, including on aggregate deployments, registration, new operator licence requirements and revocation, suspension or denial of licences or approvals.
quote: The regulations shall include any testing, equipment, and performance standards

summary: Department shall hold public hearings on the adoption of any regulation applicable to operation of an autonomous vehicle without a driver present inside the vehicle.
quote: The department shall hold public hearings on the adoption of any regulation applicable to the operation of an autonomous vehicle without the presence of a driver inside the vehicle.
conditional_on: Adoption of regulations on driverless operation

summary: Department shall approve a manufacturer application under subdivision (c) if it finds the vehicles safe and requirements complied with; for driverless vehicles it may impose additional requirements, including requiring a driver in the driver's seat.
quote: The department shall approve an application submitted by a manufacturer pursuant to subdivision (c) if it finds
conditional_on: Application under subdivision (c)

summary: Department must post a public notice on its website when it adopts regulations under subdivision (d), and may not approve applications under those regulations until 30 days after the notice.
applies_from: Not until 30 days after the public notice is provided
quote: The department shall post a public notice on its internet website when it adopts the regulations required by subdivision (d).
conditional_on: Adoption of regulations under subdivision (d)

summary: Manufacturer of the autonomous technology installed on a vehicle must give the purchaser a written disclosure describing what information the technology collects.
quote: The manufacturer of the autonomous technology installed on a vehicle shall provide a written disclosure to the purchaser of an autonomous vehicle

summary: Department may promulgate regulations to assess a fee on manufacturers applying to operate autonomous vehicles, in an amount to recover costs reasonably incurred.
quote: The department may promulgate regulations to assess a fee upon a manufacturer

summary: Autonomous vehicles with model year 2031 or later and gross vehicle weight rating under 8,501 pounds that are zero-emission vehicles may be operated only under a deployment permit under Title 13 regulations.
quote: any autonomous vehicle with a model year of 2031 or later and a gross vehicle weight rating of less than 8,501 pounds shall only be operated pursuant to a deployment permit
conditional_on: To the extent authorized by federal law; model year 2031 or later; gross vehicle weight rating under 8,501 pounds; zero-emission vehicle

summary: Department shall not commence rulemaking to implement subdivision (i) before January 1, 2027.
quote: The department shall not commence rulemaking for the adoption of regulations implementing this subdivision before January 1, 2027.

summary: Large frontier developers must write, implement, comply with and publish a frontier AI framework covering standards, capability thresholds, mitigations, deployment review, third-party assessment, updates, model-weight cybersecurity, incident response, internal governance and internal-use risk.
quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework that applies to the large frontier developer’s frontier models
conditional_on: Large frontier developer

summary: Large frontier developers must review the framework at least yearly and publish any materially modified framework with a justification within 30 days.
quote: If a large frontier developer makes a material modification to its frontier AI framework, the large frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish the modified frontier AI framework and a justification for that modification within 30 days.
conditional_on: Large frontier developer; publication on material modification

summary: Frontier developers must publish a transparency report (website, contact mechanism, release date, languages, output modalities, intended uses, use restrictions) before or when deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model; a system or model card can satisfy this.
quote: a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a transparency report containing all of the following
conditional_on: Deployment of a new or substantially modified frontier model

summary: Large frontier developers must add to the transparency report summaries of catastrophic-risk assessments under their framework, their results, third-party evaluator involvement and other framework steps.
quote: a large frontier developer shall include in the transparency report required by paragraph (1) summaries of all of the following
conditional_on: Large frontier developer; deployment of a new or substantially modified frontier model

summary: Large frontier developers must send OES summaries of any assessment of catastrophic risk from internal use of their frontier models every three months or on another reasonable schedule communicated in writing.
quote: frontier developer shall transmit to the Office of Emergency Services a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from internal use of its frontier models
conditional_on: Large frontier developer

summary: Frontier developers must not make materially false or misleading statements about catastrophic risk from their frontier models or their management of it; good-faith reasonable statements are excepted.
quote: developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk from its frontier models or its management of catastrophic risk.

summary: Large frontier developers must not make materially false or misleading statements about implementing or complying with their frontier AI framework; good-faith reasonable statements are excepted.
quote: A large frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about its implementation of, or compliance with, its frontier AI framework.
conditional_on: Large frontier developer

summary: Frontier developers that redact published documents (for trade secrets, cybersecurity, public safety, national security or legal compliance) must describe the character and justification of each redaction and keep the unredacted information for five years.
quote: the frontier developer shall describe the character and justification of the redaction in any published version of the document to the extent permitted by the concerns that justify redaction and shall retain the unredacted information for five years
conditional_on: Redaction of a document published under 22757.12

summary: Frontier developers must report any critical safety incident involving their frontier models to OES within 15 days of discovery; amended reports are allowed and reporting on non-frontier foundation models is encouraged.
quote: frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovering the critical safety incident
conditional_on: Discovery of a critical safety incident

summary: If a critical safety incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the frontier developer must disclose it within 24 hours to an appropriate authority, such as law enforcement or a public safety agency.
quote: If a frontier developer discovers that a critical safety incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority
conditional_on: Incident posing an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury

summary: A frontier developer that intends to meet the incident-reporting section through a federal law, regulation or guidance designated by OES must declare that intent to OES; it is then deemed compliant to that extent, and failing the federal standard is a violation of the chapter.
quote: A frontier developer that intends to comply with this section by complying with the requirements of, or meeting the standards stated by, a federal law, regulation, or guidance document designated pursuant to subdivision (h) shall declare its intent to do so to the Office of Emergency Services.
conditional_on: OES designation regulation under 22757.13(h) and the developer's election

summary: OES must set up a mechanism for frontier developers and the public to report critical safety incidents (date, reasons, description, internal-use link), and must review developers' reports.
quote: The Office of Emergency Services shall establish a mechanism to be used by a frontier developer or a member of the public to report a critical safety incident

summary: OES must set up a confidential channel for large frontier developers' internal-use risk summaries and limit access to internal-use reports to personnel with a need to know.
quote: The Office of Emergency Services shall establish a mechanism to be used by a large frontier developer to confidentially submit summaries of any assessments of the potential for catastrophic risk resulting from internal use of its frontier models.

summary: OES must publish an annual anonymized, aggregated report on reviewed critical safety incidents, from 1 January 2027, and send it to the Legislature and the Governor.
quote: the Office of Emergency Services shall produce a report with anonymized and aggregated information about critical safety incidents that have been reviewed by the Office of Emergency Services since the preceding report

summary: OES must revoke any regulation designating federal incident-reporting standards once the designation conditions are no longer met (designation itself is discretionary).
quote: The Office of Emergency Services shall revoke a regulation adopted under subdivision (h) if the requirements of subdivision (h) are no longer met.

summary: The Department of Technology must assess developments annually, from 1 January 2027, and recommend to the Legislature whether and how to update the definitions of frontier model, frontier developer and large frontier developer.
quote: shall make recommendations about whether and how to update any of the following definitions for the purposes of this chapter

summary: The Attorney General must publish an annual anonymized, aggregated report on reviewed covered-employee reports, from 1 January 2027, and send it to the Legislature and the Governor.
quote: the Attorney General shall produce a report with anonymized and aggregated information about reports from covered employees

summary: A 14-member consortium within the Government Operations Agency must develop a framework for CalCompute, a public cloud computing cluster, seeking to establish it within the University of California.
quote: There is hereby established within the Government Operations Agency a consortium that shall develop, pursuant to this section, a framework for the creation of a public cloud computing cluster to be known as “CalCompute.”
conditional_on: Appropriation in a budget act or other measure (11546.8(k))

summary: The Government Operations Agency must submit the consortium's CalCompute report (landscape, costs and funding, governance, use parameters, workforce, partnerships) to the Legislature by 1 January 2027.
quote: the Government Operations Agency shall submit, pursuant to Section 9795, a report from the consortium to the Legislature with the framework developed pursuant to subdivision (b) for the creation and operation of CalCompute
conditional_on: Appropriation in a budget act or other measure (11546.8(k))

summary: Frontier developers must not adopt or enforce rules, policies or contracts that prevent covered employees from disclosing, or retaliate against them for disclosing, catastrophic-risk dangers or violations of the TFAIA to the Attorney General, federal authorities or internal authorities.
quote: A frontier developer shall not make, adopt, enforce, or enter into a rule, regulation, policy, or contract that prevents a covered employee from disclosing, or retaliates against a covered employee for disclosing

quote: A frontier developer shall not enter into a contract that prevents a covered employee from making a disclosure protected under Section 1102.5.

summary: Frontier developers must give all covered employees clear notice of their whistleblower rights, by permanent workplace posting (with notice to new and remote employees) or yearly written notice that is acknowledged.
quote: A frontier developer shall provide a clear notice to all covered employees of their rights and responsibilities under this section

summary: Large frontier developers must run a reasonable internal anonymous disclosure process with monthly status updates to the discloser, and share disclosures and responses with officers and directors at least quarterly (except those accused).
quote: A large frontier developer shall provide a reasonable internal process through which a covered employee may anonymously disclose information to the large frontier developer
conditional_on: Large frontier developer

summary: Make available a free AI detection tool to users that assesses image, video or audio content for the provider's GenAI system, outputs system provenance data but not personal provenance data, is publicly accessible (reasonable access limits allowed), accepts uploads or URLs, and supports an API.
quote: A covered provider shall make available an AI detection tool at no cost to the user
conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

summary: Collect user feedback on the efficacy of the AI detection tool and incorporate relevant feedback into efforts to improve the tool's efficacy.
quote: A covered provider shall collect user feedback related to the efficacy of the covered provider’s AI detection tool
conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

summary: Not collect or retain personal information from users of the AI detection tool (except contact information of users opting in to feedback contact, used only to evaluate and improve the tool); not retain submitted content longer than necessary; not retain personal provenance data from submitted content.
quote: A covered provider shall not do any of the following:
conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

summary: Offer the user the option to include a manifest disclosure identifying image, video or audio content as AI-generated, clear and conspicuous, and permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove where technically feasible.
quote: A covered provider shall offer the user the option to include a manifest disclosure
conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

summary: Include a latent disclosure in AI-generated image, video or audio content, where technically feasible and reasonable, conveying the provider name, the GenAI system name and version, the time and date of creation or alteration, and a unique identifier (directly or via a link); the disclosure must be detectable by the AI detection tool, consistent with widely accepted industry standards, and permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove where technically feasible.
quote: A covered provider shall include a latent disclosure in AI-generated image, video, or audio content
conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

summary: Where the provider licenses its GenAI system to a third party, require by contract that the licensee maintain the system's capability to include the latent disclosure; if the provider knows a licensee modified the system so that it can no longer include the disclosure, revoke the license within 96 hours of discovering the action.
quote: the covered provider shall require by contract that the licensee maintain the system’s capability
conditional_on: Provider licenses its GenAI system to a third party (and, for revocation, knows of a modification by the licensee)

summary: Third-party licensee of a GenAI system shall cease using the licensed system after the provider has revoked the license under Sec. 22757.3(c)(2).
quote: A third-party licensee shall cease using a licensed GenAI system after the license for the system has been revoked
conditional_on: License revoked by the covered provider under Sec. 22757.3(c)(2)

summary: Notify the Department of implementation of its CIP and of the CIPs of its foreign resellers through a CIP certification form with the content listed in § 7.304(a)(1)-(3), including an attestation.

summary: Submit annual certifications of its CIPs, including updates and attestations on CIP review, updates, threat-landscape changes, compliance, and unverified-customer tracking and resolution (§ 7.304(b)(1)-(6)). Certifications may be submitted within one year of the previous notification, but no earlier than 60 calendar days before that date.
quote: U.S. IaaS providers must submit to the Department certifications of their CIPs on an annual basis

summary: Notify the Department of significant changes in business operations or corporate structure, and of material CIP changes, outside the normal reporting schedule; also notify changes of the Primary Contact.
quote: Each U.S. IaaS provider must notify the Department if, outside of the normal reporting schedule
conditional_on: Outside the normal reporting schedule, when such changes occur.

summary: A newly established provider notifies the Department of CIP implementation before furnishing any foreign customer an account; providers also notify the Department before providing products to a new foreign reseller.
applies_from: Prior to furnishing any foreign customer with an IaaS Account.
quote: Prior to furnishing any foreign customer with an IaaS Account, any newly established U.S. IaaS provider must notify the Department
conditional_on: Newly established U.S. IaaS provider; new foreign reseller.

summary: Collect from foreign resellers the information needed for the provider's initial and annual reporting.
quote: Each U.S. IaaS provider of U.S. IaaS products must collect from its foreign resellers the information necessary for the initial and annual reporting requirements

summary: Submit annually, in compiled format, CIP certification forms for all foreign resellers' CIPs, within one year of the previous notification and no earlier than 60 calendar days before that date.
quote: Each U.S. IaaS provider of U.S. IaaS products must submit on an annual basis CIP certification forms for all foreign resellers' CIPs

summary: On Department request, provide copies of its CIPs and those of its foreign resellers within ten calendar days. If inspection finds shortcomings, resolve them within a reasonable period set by the Department and resubmit the CIP.
applies_from: Within ten calendar days of a Department request.
quote: must provide any copy of these CIPs to the Department within ten calendar days of a request from the Department
conditional_on: Upon a Department request; resubmission follows a finding of shortcomings.

summary: Conduct compliance assessments of certain providers based on the Department's evaluation of risk; the Department may conduct follow-up assessments and request an audit of a provider's CIP processes (§ 7.305(b), (e)).
quote: The Department shall conduct compliance assessments of certain U.S. IaaS providers according to the Department's evaluation of risk
conditional_on: Based on the Department's evaluation of risk.

summary: After compliance assessments, the Department may recommend remediation measures to providers, including special measures under § 7.307 and transaction review under subpart B.
quote: Recommend remediation measures to be taken by the U.S. IaaS providers of U.S. IaaS products
conditional_on: Based on the results of compliance assessments.

summary: The Secretary may exempt a provider, an account type or lessee, or a foreign reseller from subpart requirements other than §§ 7.308 and 7.309, on a finding of security best practices to deter abuse.
quote: may exempt any U.S. IaaS provider, any specific type of Account or lessee
conditional_on: Finding that the provider or reseller implements security best practices to otherwise deter abuse of IaaS products (§ 7.306(a), (e)).

summary: A provider seeking a Secretary's finding exempting it or a foreign reseller from CIP requirements initiates the process by a written submission describing its ADP; the Secretary consults other agencies before making a finding.
quote: shall initiate the process by providing a written submission to the Secretary describing its establishment of an ADP
conditional_on: Request for exemption from CIP requirements (§ 7.306(e)).

summary: The Abuse of IaaS Products Deterrence Program must include policies and procedures to identify Red Flags (risk factors, sources, categories), detect and respond to them (including privacy-preserving data sharing where feasible), update them regularly, and administer the ADP with board or senior-management approval and oversight, staff training, and oversight of reseller arrangements.
quote: A U.S. IaaS provider or foreign reseller ADP must include reasonable policies and procedures to:
conditional_on: Relevant where the provider seeks a Secretary's finding exempting it from CIP requirements, which requires an established ADP and a request for a finding (§ 7.306(b)).

summary: Document within its ADP the process and capabilities for integrating insights and responding to intelligence generated through consortium interaction.
quote: IaaS providers must document their process and capabilities for integrating insights and responding to intelligence generated through consortium interaction
conditional_on: Paragraph (c) concerns providers participating in a consortium on privacy-preserving data sharing and analytics.

summary: Have a continuing obligation to update the ADP in response to the changing threat landscape; foreign resellers are to do the same.
quote: have a continuing obligation to update their ADPs in response to the changing threat landscape
conditional_on: Where the provider or its foreign reseller holds an exemption (§ 7.306(f), 'Maintenance of exemption').

summary: Notify the Secretary of any significant deviations or changes to the ADP, and submit annual notifications for the provider and its exempt foreign resellers.
quote: must notify the Secretary of any significant deviations or changes to their ADP
conditional_on: Exempt provider or exempt foreign reseller.

summary: The Secretary issues an unclassified written determination summarizing the evaluation and the reasonable-grounds findings, stating the special measure and its consistency with the Executive Order and subpart; the measure is imposed on issuance.
quote: Upon completion of the evaluation, the Secretary shall issue an unclassified written determination
conditional_on: Before imposing special measures under paragraph (b).

summary: The Secretary evaluates the relevant factors and consults other agencies before deciding whether to impose a special measure and which one.
quote: the Secretary will evaluate the relevant factors provided in paragraph (b) of this section
conditional_on: Upon the Secretary's own initiative or referral by other agencies or providers.

summary: The Secretary may prohibit or impose conditions on opening or maintaining accounts with U.S. IaaS providers by foreign persons in a jurisdiction found to have a significant number of foreign persons offering IaaS products used for malicious cyber-enabled activities, or by providers acting for such persons (§ 7.307(b)(1)-(2)).
quote: The Secretary may prohibit or impose conditions on the opening or maintaining with any U.S. IaaS provider of an Account
conditional_on: Reasonable-grounds determination under § 7.307(a) and the factors in § 7.307(b)(3).

summary: Notify in writing the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of any special measure invoked.
applies_from: Not later than 10 calendar days after the date of any determination under paragraph (a)(4) of this section.
quote: the Secretary shall notify, in writing, the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the U.S. House of Representatives
conditional_on: Any determination under § 7.307(a)(4).

summary: Each provider submits to the Department a report whenever it has knowledge of a covered transaction, with the content required by § 7.308(d)(1); the report is certified as true, correct and complete.
applies_from: Within 15 calendar days of a covered transaction occurring or the provider or reseller having “knowledge” that a covered transaction has occurred.
quote: each U.S. IaaS provider must submit a report to the Department whenever they have “knowledge” of a covered transaction
conditional_on: Covered transaction: a transaction by, for, or on behalf of a foreign person that results or could result in training a large AI model with potential capabilities that could be used in malicious cyber-enabled activity (§ 7.308(b)).

summary: Require foreign resellers to report covered transactions to the provider.
applies_from: Within 15 calendar days of a covered transaction occurring or the reseller having knowledge that one has occurred.
quote: U.S. IaaS providers must require their foreign resellers to file with the U.S. IaaS provider a report within 15 calendar days
conditional_on: Covered transaction (§ 7.308(b)).

summary: File with the Department the report on a foreign reseller's covered transaction.
applies_from: Within 30 calendar days of the covered transaction.
quote: The U.S. IaaS provider must file this report with the Department within 30 calendar days of the covered transaction.
conditional_on: Covered transaction involving a foreign reseller (§ 7.308(c)(2)).

summary: File a follow-up report responsive to a Department request for additional information.
applies_from: Within 15 calendar days of receiving the Department's request for additional information.
quote: will file a follow-up report responsive to the request within 15 calendar days of receiving the request for additional information
conditional_on: Department request for additional information under § 7.308(d).

summary: File a corrected report, in the form specified in paragraph (d), correcting all inaccuracies in a report found inaccurate when filed.
applies_from: Within 15 calendar days after the provider has knowledge of the inaccuracy.
quote: shall file a corrected report in the form and manner specified in paragraph (d) of this section within 15 calendar dates
conditional_on: A report found to have been inaccurate when filed.

summary: BIS may request additional information from a provider or foreign reseller on activities or risks of concern to U.S. national security, after receiving an initial, follow-up or corrected report.
quote: BIS may request that a U.S. IaaS provider or foreign reseller of U.S. IaaS products submit additional information
conditional_on: Upon receiving an initial, follow-up or corrected report.

summary: No provider may supply IaaS products to foreign resellers unless it has made all reasonable efforts to ensure reseller compliance. On evidence of non-compliance it notifies the reseller and requests evidence; if non-remediation is found it must suspend supply to the reseller until adequate assurances are provided.
quote: No U.S. IaaS provider shall provide U.S. IaaS products to foreign resellers, unless the U.S. IaaS provider has made all reasonable efforts
conditional_on: Absent reasonable efforts to ensure reseller compliance; on evidence or discovery of reseller non-compliance.

summary: Notify the Department of any material change to the CIP or to the provider's business that renders the CIP unnecessary, and of any material change to the ADP or business that may impact an ADP exemption.
quote: shall notify the Department of any material change to the CIP or to the IaaS provider's business
conditional_on: Persons who made CIP, exemption-request or ADP representations to the Department (§ 7.309(b)(1)-(2)).

summary: Any person who learns of facts or circumstances indicating a violation of the subpart may notify the Office of Information and Communications Technology and Services at the Bureau of Industry and Security.
quote: that person may notify
conditional_on: Person learns of facts or circumstances indicating that a violation may have occurred or is likely to occur.

summary: The Secretary periodically reviews the list of foreign adversaries in consultation with appropriate agency heads and may amend it. The Secretary's determination is based on multiple sources listed in paragraph (c).
quote: The Secretary will periodically review this list in consultation with appropriate agency heads

summary: In reviewing ICTS Transactions, the Secretary considers relevant information held by or available to the Federal Government, and determines in consultation with agency heads whether an ICTS Transaction involves foreign adversary-linked ICTS and whether a Covered ICTS Transaction poses an undue or unacceptable risk.
quote: Consider any and all relevant information held by, or otherwise made available to, the Federal Government

summary: A person required by the Secretary must furnish complete information, under oath, in reports or otherwise, including documents and records as the Secretary requires, relating to any act, transaction or property.
quote: the Secretary may require any person to furnish under oath, in the form of reports or otherwise
conditional_on: when the Secretary requires information from the person

summary: During a review the Secretary assesses whether the transaction is a Covered ICTS Transaction, involves ICTS linked to a foreign adversary, and poses an undue or unacceptable risk, and then either ends review or proceeds under the following sections.
quote: As part of the review, the Secretary will assess whether the transaction
conditional_on: when a review of an ICTS Transaction is under way

summary: The Secretary memorialises the assessment, provides it to the appropriate agency heads, and gives them twenty-one days to comment in writing. The Secretary may presume an agency has no comments if none are received within that period.
quote: the Secretary shall memorialize that assessment, provide the assessment to the appropriate agency heads, and offer the appropriate agency heads twenty-one (21) days to comment in writing
conditional_on: If the Secretary assesses that an ICTS Transaction meets the criteria under § 791.103(b)

summary: Where the Covered ICTS Transaction meets the criteria, the Secretary issues a dated and signed written Initial Determination stating the reasons, whether a prohibition or mitigation is proposed, and the factual basis. The Secretary gives agency heads at least twenty-one calendar days' notice and serves the Initial Determination on the parties, without classified information.
quote: Make a written Initial Determination, which shall be dated and signed by the Secretary
conditional_on: If the Secretary determines that the Covered ICTS Transaction meets the criteria set forth in § 791.103

summary: A notified person must retain records relating to the transaction for no less than ten years after a Final Determination, or as the Final Determination indicates. If no Initial Determination is made within ten years of notice of review, retention runs ten years from the initial notification.
quote: a notified person must immediately take steps to retain any and all records relating to such Transaction
conditional_on: Upon notification that an ICTS Transaction is under review

summary: Submissions by a party in response to an Initial Determination must be in writing, may not exceed fifty pages without prior approval, and must clearly mark any business confidential information. The party's response is due within thirty days of service of the Initial Determination.
quote: All submissions under this section must be made in writing.
conditional_on: When a party to a transaction responds to an Initial Determination under § 791.107

summary: The Secretary considers any party submission, gives written notice of the proposed Final Determination, and consults and seeks concurrence from all appropriate agency heads before issuing it. An agency objection must be submitted by its Deputy Secretary or equivalent within fourteen days.
quote: the Secretary shall provide notice in writing of the proposed Final Determination and consult with and seek concurrence from all appropriate agency heads
conditional_on: Upon receipt of a party submission under § 791.107

summary: For each Covered ICTS Transaction with an Initial Determination, the Secretary issues a written, signed and dated Final Determination (prohibited, not prohibited, or permitted with mitigation) within 180 days of serving the Initial Determination unless extended in writing. The Secretary directs necessary means where prohibited, sends the determination to parties and agency heads, and publishes notices in the Federal Register.
quote: the Secretary shall issue the Final Determination within 180 days of serving the Initial Determination
conditional_on: Unless the Secretary, at the Secretary's sole discretion, determines in writing that additional time is necessary

summary: No person may be a party to an ICTS Transaction prohibited by a Final Determination, aid or engage in conduct known to be prohibited, or be party to a transaction contrary to mitigation terms. Transactions made to evade prohibitions, conspiracies, US-person approval or financing of prohibited foreign transactions, and false or misleading statements to the Department are also prohibited.
quote: No person shall be a party to an ICTS Transaction that is prohibited by a Final Determination issued under this part, unless authorized by the Secretary.

summary: A person who has made a representation, statement or certification to the Department about an ICTS Transaction review must notify the Department in writing of any change of material fact or intention, immediately upon receiving information that would lead a reasonably prudent person to know of such a change. Earlier representations remain continuing until such notice.
quote: shall notify the Department, in writing, of any change of any material fact or intention from that previously represented
conditional_on: Upon receipt of information indicating a change of material fact or intention from a previous representation to the Department

summary: Adopted § 312.4(c)(1)(iv): the direct notice to parents must identify third-party disclosure recipients by name or category and the purposes of sharing, where the operator shares children's personal information with third parties.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16942-16943, Part II.C.1.c.iii (adoption of new § 312.4(c)(1)(iv))
quote: identify in the direct notice to parents for purposes of obtaining consent the third parties as well as the purposes for such sharing
conditional_on: operator shares personal information with third parties

summary: Adopted § 312.4(c)(1)(iii) and (iv): the direct notice to a parent must state how the operator intends to use the personal information it seeks to collect from the child, and the purposes of any third-party disclosure.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16959, Part II.E.b (discussing amended § 312.4(c)(1)(iii)-(iv))
quote: an operator’s direct notice to a parent for the purpose of obtaining verifiable parental consent must state, respectively, how the operator intends to use the personal information
conditional_on: operator seeks verifiable parental consent through direct notice

summary: Adopted § 312.4(d)(2): the online notice must include the identities and specific categories of any third-party disclosure recipients, by name and category.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16945, Part II.C.2.a.iii (amendment of § 312.4(d)(2))
quote: operators must include the identities and specific categories of
conditional_on: operator discloses personal information to third parties

summary: Adopted § 312.4(d)(2): the online notice must include the operator's written retention policy for children's personal information.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16945, Part II.C.2.a.ii (retention policy in online notice)
quote: an operator’s retention policy for children’s personal information must be included as part of the operator’s online notice

summary: Adopted § 312.4(d)(3): the online notice must describe, in general terms, internal operations uses of persistent identifiers under § 312.5(c)(7) and explain policies or practices to avoid unauthorized use of those identifiers.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16945-16946, Parts II.C.2.b.ii-iii (adoption of new § 312.4(d)(3))
quote: explain in their online notice what policies or practices are in place to avoid using persistent identifiers for unauthorized purposes
conditional_on: operator collects persistent identifiers under the support for internal operations exception

summary: Adopted § 312.4(d)(4): the online notice must describe how the operator uses audio files containing a child's voice and that the operator deletes them immediately after responding to the request.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16946, Part II.C.2.c.i (proposal and adoption of § 312.4(d)(4))
quote: a description of how the operator uses such audio files and that the operator deletes such audio files immediately after responding to the request for which they were collected
conditional_on: operator collects audio files containing a child's voice under § 312.5(c)(9)

summary: Amended § 312.5(a)(2): operators must obtain separate verifiable parental consent for disclosures of a child's personal information that are not integral to the website or online service.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16947, Part II.D.1.a (§ 312.5(a)(2) amendment as adopted in Part II.D.1.c)
quote: operators must obtain separate verifiable parental consent for disclosures of a child’s personal information
conditional_on: disclosure is not integral to the website or online service

summary: Adopted § 312.5(b)(2)(ix) text plus method: an operator using this method must provide notice that the parent can revoke any consent given in response to the earlier text message.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16956, Part II.D.7.c (adoption of new § 312.5(b)(2)(ix))
quote: An operator that uses this method must provide notice that the parent can revoke any consent given in response to the earlier text message
conditional_on: operator does not disclose children's personal information and uses the text plus method

summary: Amended § 312.5(c)(7): an operator collecting a persistent identifier under the internal operations exception must provide notice under § 312.4(d)(3) in its online notices.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16953, Part II.D.6.a (amendment of § 312.5(c)(7), adopted as originally proposed)
quote: the operator shall provide notice [in their online notices] under § 312.4(d)(3)
conditional_on: operator relies on the support for internal operations exception

summary: Proposed § 312.8(b), adopted in modified form: operators must establish, implement and maintain a written security program with safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of the information; the adopted text drops the term children's personal information security program and allows a general program that meets the requirements.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16960, Part II.F.a (proposed § 312.8(b)), modified in Part II.F.c
quote: operators must, at a minimum, establish, implement, and maintain a written children’s personal information security program

summary: Section 312.8(c): before releasing children's personal information to other operators, service providers or third parties, the operator must take reasonable steps to determine their capability and obtain written assurances that they will maintain confidentiality, security and integrity.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16960, Part II.F.a (proposed § 312.8(c)) and Part II.F.b (adopted written assurance requirement)
quote: obtain written assurances that the recipients will do so
conditional_on: operator releases children's personal information to other operators, service providers or third parties

summary: Amended § 312.10: an operator may retain children's personal information only for as long as reasonably necessary for the specific purposes for which it was collected, and not for any secondary purpose.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16959, Part II.E.c (amendment of § 312.10)
quote: an operator may retain children’s personal information only for as long as is reasonably necessary for the specific purposes for which it was collected

summary: Amended § 312.10: the operator must establish and maintain a written data retention policy specifying its business need for retaining children's personal information and its timeframe for deleting it.
provision: Federal Register 89 FR 16959, Part II.E.c (amendment of § 312.10)
quote: establish and maintain a written data retention policy specifying the operator’s business need for retaining children’s personal information

summary: Operators of mixed audience websites or online services must determine whether a visitor is a child in a neutral manner that does not default to a set age or encourage falsifying age information.
provision: § 312.2 (definition of Mixed audience website or online service)
quote: Any collection of age information, or other means of determining whether a visitor is a child, must be done in a neutral manner that does not default to a set age or encourage visitors to falsify age information.
conditional_on: Applies when an operator determines whether a visitor is a child, under the mixed audience definition.

summary: Operators of websites or online services directed to children, or with actual knowledge of collecting personal information from a child, may not collect such information in a manner that violates the regulations in this part.
quote: It shall be unlawful for any operator of a website or online service directed to children

summary: Operators must provide notice and obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting, using or disclosing children's personal information; the section also requires direct notice to parents, the content of direct and online notices, and posting of the online notice with the data retention policy.
quote: It shall be the obligation of the operator to provide notice and obtain verifiable parental consent prior to collecting, using, or disclosing personal information from children.

summary: Operators must obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting, using or disclosing children's personal information, including material changes; must make reasonable efforts using accepted consent methods; and must give parents the option to consent without consenting to third-party disclosure unless integral.
quote: An operator is required to obtain verifiable parental consent before any collection, use, or disclosure of personal information from children

summary: On a parent's request, operators must provide a description of the personal information collected from the child, the opportunity to refuse further use or collection and to direct deletion, and a means of reviewing the child's information, verifying the requestor is a parent.
quote: the operator of that website or online service is required to provide to that parent the following
conditional_on: Applies upon request of a parent whose child has provided personal information.

summary: Operators may not condition a child's participation in a game, prize or other activity on disclosing more personal information than is reasonably necessary to participate.
quote: prohibited from conditioning a child

summary: Operators must establish and maintain reasonable procedures and a written information security program with designated coordinators, at least annual risk assessments, safeguards, regular testing and at least annual evaluation; before sharing children's information with other operators, service providers or third parties, they must take reasonable steps and obtain written assurances.
quote: The operator must establish and maintain reasonable procedures to protect the confidentiality, security, and integrity of personal information collected from children.

summary: Operators must retain children's personal information online only as long as reasonably necessary for the specific purposes collected, must delete it when no longer reasonably necessary using reasonable measures, and may not retain it indefinitely.
quote: An operator of a website or online service shall retain personal information collected online from a child for only as long as is reasonably necessary

summary: Operators must establish, implement and maintain a written data retention policy setting out the purposes of collection, the business need for retention and a deletion timeframe, and must provide it in the online notice.
quote: At a minimum, the operator must establish, implement, and maintain a written data retention policy

summary: The Commission must issue a written determination on a safe harbor program application.
applies_from: within 180 days of the filing of the application
quote: The Commission shall issue a written determination within 180 days of the filing of the application.

summary: Industry groups or other persons applying for FTC-approved safe harbor programs must include a business model explanation, technological capabilities and mechanisms for assessing members, a copy of the guidelines, a comparison with the Rule and a statement on enforcement.
quote: shall be accompanied by the following
conditional_on: Applies to requests for Commission approval of safe harbor program guidelines.

summary: Approved safe harbor programs must maintain an effective, mandatory mechanism for at least annual comprehensive review of subject operators' privacy and security policies, practices and representations, impose disciplinary actions for non-compliance, and meet the other performance standards in paragraph (b).
quote: An effective, mandatory mechanism for the independent assessment
conditional_on: Applies to FTC-approved safe harbor programs.

summary: Approved safe harbor programs must submit an annual report identifying subject operators and approved services, the business model, consumer complaints, an aggregated summary of assessments, disciplinary actions and approvals of parental consent methods.
quote: By October 22, 2025, and annually thereafter, submit a report to the Commission
conditional_on: Applies to FTC-approved safe harbor programs.

summary: Approved safe harbor programs must promptly respond to Commission requests for additional information.
quote: Promptly respond to Commission requests for additional information
conditional_on: Applies upon Commission request.

summary: Approved safe harbor programs must maintain, for not less than three years, consumer complaints, disciplinary records and assessment results, and make them available to the Commission on request.
quote: Maintain for a period not less than three years, and upon request make available to the Commission

summary: Approved safe harbor programs must publicly post a list of all current subject operators and their certified websites or online services, and update the list every six months.
quote: No later than July 21, 2025, publicly post on each of the approved safe harbor program

summary: Approved safe harbor programs must submit proposed changes to their guidelines for Commission review and approval, with a statement on how the changes affect existing provisions.
quote: must submit proposed changes to their guidelines for review and approval by the Commission
conditional_on: Applies to post-approval modifications of guidelines.

summary: Approved safe harbor programs must submit a triennial report on their technological capabilities and mechanisms for assessing members' fitness for membership.
applies_from: No later than April 22, 2028, and every three years thereafter
quote: No later than April 22, 2028, and every three years thereafter, approved safe harbor programs shall submit to the Commission a report

summary: Safe harbor programs must submit proposed modifications to their guidelines to the Commission.
quote: Safe harbor programs shall, by October 22, 2025, submit proposed modifications to their guidelines.

summary: The Commission must issue a written determination on a request for approval of a parental consent method or of additional support-for-internal-operations activities.
applies_from: within 120 days of the filing of the request
quote: The Commission shall issue a written determination within 120 days of the filing of the request.

summary: Prohibits any person in or affecting commerce from materially and falsely posing as a government entity or officer, or materially misrepresenting affiliation with, endorsement or sponsorship by a government entity or officer (§ 461.2(a)-(b)); the rule applies to any actor in commerce, not only firms.
quote: materially and falsely pose as, directly or by implication, a government entity or officer thereof

summary: Prohibits any person in or affecting commerce from materially and falsely posing as a business or officer thereof, or materially misrepresenting affiliation with, endorsement or sponsorship by a business or officer thereof (§ 461.3(a)-(b)); 'business' includes not-for-profit entities (§ 461.1).
quote: materially and falsely pose as, directly or by implication, a business or officer thereof

summary: Clear and conspicuous disclosures (defined in § 465.1(c)) must use diction and syntax understandable to ordinary consumers, appear in each language of the representation, be unavoidable in interactive media, and not be contradicted by other content.
quote: The disclosure must use diction and syntax understandable to ordinary consumers
conditional_on: Applies where a disclosure is required under this part.

summary: A business may not write, create, sell, purchase, disseminate or procure fake or false consumer reviews, consumer testimonials or celebrity testimonials that materially misrepresent the reviewer's or testimonialist's existence or experience; the business-knowledge standard applies to purchase, dissemination and procurement.
quote: for a business to write, create, or sell a consumer review, consumer testimonial, or celebrity testimonial that materially misrepresents
conditional_on: For purchasing, disseminating and procuring (§ 465.2(b)-(c)), the business knew or should have known of the misrepresentation.

summary: A business may not provide compensation or other incentives in exchange for, or conditioned on, consumer reviews expressing a particular sentiment, whether positive or negative.
quote: for a business to provide compensation or other incentives in exchange for, or conditioned expressly or by implication on, the writing or creation of consumer reviews expressing a particular sentiment

summary: Officers and managers may not write insider reviews or testimonials without a clear and conspicuous disclosure of their material relationship (§ 465.5(a)); a business may not disseminate insider testimonials lacking such a disclosure where it knew or should have known of the relationship (§ 465.5(b)(1)); officers and managers may not solicit or demand reviews from relatives, employees or agents in the circumstances listed in § 465.5(c)(1), including failure to instruct disclosure or to take remedial steps.
quote: for an officer or manager of a business to write or create a consumer review or consumer testimonial about the business or one of the products or services it sells that fails to have a clear and conspicuous disclosure
conditional_on: § 465.5(b)(1) and § 465.5(c)(1) apply only where the business knew or should have known of the relationship, or the officer or manager acted as described in (c)(1)(ii).

summary: A business may not materially misrepresent that a website, organization or entity it controls, owns or operates provides independent reviews or opinions (other than consumer reviews) about a category of businesses, products or services including its own.
quote: purportedly independent websites, organizations, or entities to review or endorse their own products

summary: Anyone may not use an unfounded or groundless legal threat, a physical threat, intimidation, or a public false accusation (made knowingly or with reckless disregard) in response to a consumer review in an attempt to prevent a review from being written or to cause it to be removed or changed.
quote: For anyone to use an unfounded or groundless legal threat, a physical threat, intimidation, or a public false accusation
conditional_on: The threat or accusation is made in an attempt to prevent, remove or change a review.

summary: A business may not materially misrepresent that consumer reviews displayed in its review section represent most or all reviews submitted, where reviews are suppressed based on rating or negative sentiment; listed criteria applied equally to all reviews are not suppression based on sentiment.
quote: For a business to materially misrepresent, expressly or by implication, that the consumer reviews
conditional_on: Suppression based on rating or negative sentiment; criteria applied equally to all reviews fall outside the prohibition.

summary: Anyone may not sell or distribute fake indicators of social media influence, or purchase or procure them, where they knew or should have known the indicators were fake and they materially misrepresent influence or importance for a commercial purpose.
quote: Sell or distribute fake indicators of social media influence that they knew or should have known to be fake
conditional_on: Knew or should have known the indicators were fake; materially misrepresent influence for a commercial purpose.

summary: Any person making a sale or lease of high-technology data center equipment must collect the sales tax unless the purchaser furnishes a commissioner-issued exemption certificate.
quote: Any person making a sale or lease of high-technology data center equipment shall collect the tax imposed on such sale by this article
conditional_on: unless the purchaser furnishes the seller a certificate issued by the commissioner certifying the sale is exempt

summary: The commissioner may not issue an exemption certificate unless determining the data center will more likely than not meet the minimum investment threshold.
quote: The commissioner shall not issue a certificate of exemption from sales and use tax to a high-technology data center
conditional_on: commissioner determination that the data center will more likely than not meet the minimum investment threshold

summary: The commissioner may require information needed to determine whether the data center complies with its investment budgeting plan.
quote: The commissioner may require any information necessary to determine if such high-technology data center is in compliance with its investment budgeting plan

summary: File a final report with the commissioner listing expenditures counting toward the minimum investment threshold, new quality jobs, and other information the commissioner may reasonably require.
applies_from: Within 60 days after the end of the seventh year following its exemption start date

quote: A controller shall comply with an authenticated consumer request to exercise the right:

summary: Controllers must answer requests within 45 days (one 45-day extension with notice), explain any refusal with appeal instructions, and respond free of charge up to twice a year per consumer; controllers that obtained data from third parties may satisfy deletion by keeping a suppression record or opting the consumer out.
quote: a controller shall comply with a request by a consumer to exercise the consumer rights authorized pursuant to subsection A as follows:

quote: A controller shall establish a process for a consumer to appeal the controller's refusal to take action on a request within a reasonable period of time

summary: Controllers must offer, and describe in the privacy notice, secure and reliable means to submit rights requests, and may not require a new account to exercise rights.
quote: A controller shall establish, and shall describe in a privacy notice, one or more secure and reliable means for consumers to submit a request to exercise their consumer rights under this chapter.

summary: Controllers must limit collection to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary for the disclosed purposes, and may not process data for purposes neither necessary to nor compatible with those disclosed purposes without consent (consent as second character).
quote: Limit the collection of personal data to what is adequate, relevant, and reasonably necessary in relation to the purposes for which such data is processed, as disclosed to the consumer

summary: Controllers must establish, implement and maintain reasonable administrative, technical and physical data security practices appropriate to the volume and nature of the data.
quote: Establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and accessibility of personal data.

summary: Controllers may not process data in violation of anti-discrimination laws or discriminate (deny goods, charge different prices, lower quality) against consumers who exercise their rights; differential offers tied to opt-outs or bona fide loyalty programs remain allowed.
quote: A controller shall not discriminate against a consumer for exercising any of the consumer rights contained in this chapter, including denying goods or services, charging different prices or rates for goods or services, or providing a different level of quality of goods and services to the consumer.

summary: Controllers may not process sensitive data without the consumer's consent; sensitive data of a known child must be processed in accordance with COPPA.
quote: Not process sensitive data concerning a consumer without obtaining the consumer's consent

summary: Controllers may not sell or offer for sale a consumer's precise geolocation data (added by Acts 2026, c. 820, per text comparison).
quote: Not sell or offer for sale precise geolocation data concerning a consumer.

summary: Controllers must give consumers a reasonably accessible, clear and meaningful privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, how to exercise and appeal rights, data shared with third parties and the categories of those third parties.
quote: Controllers shall provide consumers with a reasonably accessible, clear, and meaningful privacy notice that includes:

summary: Controllers that sell personal data or process it for targeted advertising must clearly and conspicuously disclose this and how consumers can opt out.

conditional_on: Controller sells personal data to third parties or processes it for targeted advertising

summary: Without parental consent under COPPA, controllers may not process a known child's personal data for targeted advertising, sale or significant-decision profiling, beyond what is reasonably necessary for the online service, for undisclosed or incompatible purposes, or for longer than necessary.
quote: Subject to the consent requirement established by subdivision 3, no controller shall process any personal data collected from a known child:
conditional_on: Personal data collected from a known child (under 13); parental consent per COPPA (§ 59.1-578 F 3)

quote: no controller shall collect precise geolocation data from a known child unless (i) such precise geolocation data is reasonably necessary for the controller to provide an online service, product, or feature
conditional_on: Parental consent per COPPA (§ 59.1-578 F 3)

summary: Social media platform operators must limit minors' use to one hour per day per service or application, and let a parent give verifiable parental consent to raise or lower the limit (without extra parental access to the minor's data or accounts).
quote: limit a minor's use of such social media platform to one hour per day, per service or application

summary: Information collected to determine a user's age may be used only for age determination and age-appropriate experiences.
quote: Information collected for the purpose of determining a user's age shall not be used for any purpose other than age determination and provision of age-appropriate experiences.

summary: Social media platform operators may not withhold, degrade or raise the price of any online service, product or feature because they cannot provide use beyond the one-hour limit; offers reasonably related to compliance remain allowed.
quote: No controller or processor that operates a social media platform shall withhold, degrade, lower the quality of, or increase the price of any online service, product, or feature to a user

quote: A contract between a controller and a processor shall govern the processor's data processing procedures with respect to processing performed on behalf of the controller.

quote: A controller shall conduct and document a data protection assessment of each of the following processing activities involving personal data:

quote: Personal data processed by a controller pursuant to this section shall not be processed for any purpose other than those expressly listed in this section unless otherwise allowed by this chapter.

summary: Financial intermediation institutions and electronic money issuers are empowered to refrain from executing withdrawal or transfer orders on accounts that received funds from transactions declared unauthorised by the originating account holder; the freeze covers current balances and future inflows up to the disputed amount.
quote: Facúltase a las instituciones de intermediación financiera y a las entidades emisoras de dinero electrónico a la no ejecución de cualquier tipo de orden de retiro o transferencia de activos
conditional_on: when they have become aware, by reliable means, that funds from disputed transactions entered the accounts

summary: A fund freeze under Art. 11 must be communicated to the Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU) within one business day; the BCU may request additional information and may order the freeze lifted. The freeze must be lifted and the BCU notified where the conditions listed in literals A to D occur (no complaint filed within 48 hours, no judicial confirmation within 30 days, judicial lifting order, or convincing evidence from the account holder).
quote: deberá ser comunicada dentro del plazo de un día hábil al Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU)
conditional_on: when a fund freeze has been imposed under Art. 11

summary: Financial intermediation institutions and electronic money issuers must execute any order exceeding the limit of the disputed transaction amounts, unless the order fails to meet legal or contractual requirements.
quote: debiendo las instituciones de intermediación financiera y las entidades emisoras de dinero electrónico ejecutar toda orden que excediera dicho límite
conditional_on: for orders exceeding the amount of the disputed transactions, unless the orders do not meet legal or contractual requirements
